definition_zh: 成功者；有成就的人；学业优秀者；（高、低）成就者
definition_en: a person who reaches a goal or performs at a high level, especially in school, sport or work
core_image: 冲过终点线后仍站着记成绩的人
scene: 长跑比赛已经结束，人群里有个学生还在低头记下自己的成绩。Every achiever in the class set a goal and worked toward it.
sceneCN: 这里 achiever 是「有成就的人」（第 1 个义项：达成目标的人）；句意为班上每个有成就的学生都设定了目标并为之努力。

pos.zh: 名词：成功者；有成就的人；学业优秀者

collocations.zh: 成绩优异者；表现出色的人
成绩偏低者；表现欠佳的人

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉 -er 得到的动词，义为「达成；取得」
由动词加 -ment 构成的名词，义为「成就；达成」
由动词加 -able 构成的形容词，义为「可实现的」
由 over- 加本词构成，义为「过度追求成就的人」
由 under- 加本词构成，义为「表现低于自身潜力的人」

senses.title: A person who reaches a goal
senses.definition: someone who succeeds in reaching a goal they have set for themselves
senses.definitionCN: 成功达成自己设定目标的人
senses.example: She is an achiever who finishes every project she starts.
senses.exampleCN: 她是个有成就的人，开始做的每个项目都会完成。
senses.why: Achieve came from a phrase meaning to bring something to a head or an end, so an achiever is the one who brings a task to its end.
senses.whyCN: achieve 来自「把事情带到头、带到终点」的说法，所以 achiever 就是把任务做到终点的人。

senses.title: A successful person at work
senses.definition: a person who has built a successful career and is seen as successful by others
senses.definitionCN: 建立起成功事业、被他人视为成功者的人
senses.example: The firm prefers to hire proven achievers rather than talkers.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司更愿意聘用已被证明有成就的人，而不是空谈者。
senses.why: The same image of finishing a task moves from the race track into the office, where the finished task becomes a career.
senses.whyCN: 同一种「把事做完」的画面从跑道移到办公室，完成的任务就变成了事业成果。

senses.title: A high-achieving student
senses.definition: a student who consistently earns high marks or performs well in school
senses.definitionCN: 持续取得高分或在校表现良好的学生
senses.example: The school gives extra tutoring to both low and high achievers.
senses.exampleCN: 学校既给成绩偏低的学生补课，也给成绩优异的学生额外辅导。
senses.why: In education the word is used on a scale, so achiever picks up the school sense of measured results.
senses.whyCN: 在教育语境里这个词按高低分档使用，于是 achiever 带上了「用成绩衡量」的校园含义。

senses.title: A person driven by ambition
senses.definition: someone whose character is marked by ambition and a strong desire to accomplish things
senses.definitionCN: 性格中以雄心与强烈成事欲望为标志的人
senses.example: He is a natural achiever who cannot sit still for a whole afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个天生进取的人，整个下午都坐不住。
senses.why: When the word describes character rather than results, it names the inner drive that keeps producing finished tasks.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词描述性格而不是结果时，它指的是那股不断产出成果的内在驱动力。

senses.title: An overachiever
senses.definition: a person who pushes for success beyond what is expected, sometimes at a cost to health or balance
senses.definitionCN: 追求超出预期的成功、有时以健康或平衡为代价的人
senses.example: As an overachiever, she took on three jobs in one semester.
senses.exampleCN: 作为一个过度追求成就的人，她一学期接了三份工作。
senses.why: Adding over- to achiever pushes the core image past its normal limit, so the drive itself becomes excessive.
senses.whyCN: 在 achiever 前加 over-，把核心画面推过正常限度，于是那股驱动力本身变成了过度。

senses.title: A low achiever
senses.definition: a person, especially a student, whose measured results are below the usual level
senses.definitionCN: 尤其指学生，其被衡量的成绩低于通常水平
senses.example: Low achievers often need encouragement more than punishment.
senses.exampleCN: 成绩偏低的人往往更需要鼓励，而不是惩罚。
senses.why: The scale that produced high achiever also produces its opposite; the word alone does not name failure, only a low position on the scale.
senses.whyCN: 产生 high achiever 的那把尺子也产生它的反面；这个词本身并不等于失败，只表示在刻度上位置偏低。

senses.title: A winner in competition
senses.definition: a competitor who wins or places well in a contest or sporting event
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛或体育项目中获胜或名列前茅的参赛者
senses.example: The young achiever took first place in the regional spelling contest.
senses.exampleCN: 这位年轻的优胜者在地区拼写比赛中拿了第一。
senses.why: Competition is the clearest place where a goal has a visible finish line, so achiever fits the winner most literally.
senses.whyCN: 竞赛是目标有清晰终点线的地方，所以 achiever 用在获胜者身上最贴近字面。

senses.title: A model of effort and persistence
senses.definition: a person whose steady effort and persistence are held up as an example for others
senses.definitionCN: 以稳定努力与坚持被树立为他人榜样的人
senses.example: Teachers point to her as an achiever who never gave up on a difficult subject.
senses.exampleCN: 老师们把她当作榜样，说她从不放弃一门难学的科目。
senses.why: Because the word stresses bringing something to its end, it naturally honors the persistence that finishes the journey.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词强调把事情做到终点，它自然就褒扬那种把旅程走完的坚持。

intro.en: Achiever is a modern English agent noun built on achieve, a verb that entered English from Old French with a picture of arriving at a head or an end.
intro.cn: achiever 是建立在 achieve 之上的现代英语施事名词；achieve 从古法语进入英语，画面是抵达「头」或终点。

items.en: The Latin noun caput, meaning head, is generally traced to a reconstructed root *kaput-; the deeper history of that root is source uncertain.
items.cn: 拉丁语名词 caput 意为「头」，一般认为来自重构词根 *kaput-；该词根更早的历史来源不确定。

items.en: Caput meant head and also the top or the chief point of something, giving English capital and captain through other routes.
items.cn: caput 意为「头」，也指事物的顶端或首要之处，并经由其他路径生出英语 capital 与 captain。

items.en: The phrase ad caput, to the head, is thought to have produced a Vulgar Latin verb *accapare, to bring to a head; this form is reconstructed, not directly recorded.
items.cn: 一般认为 ad caput「到头」产生了俗拉丁语动词 *accapare「把事情带到头」；此形式属重构，未见直接记录。

items.en: Old French achever meant to finish or accomplish, and the phrase a chief kept the image of reaching the chief point.
items.cn: 古法语 achever 意为「完成、做成」，其中 a chief 的说法保留了「抵达首要之处」的画面。

items.en: English borrowed the verb as acheven; the modern spelling achieve settled later, and the exact first date is not certain.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入动词形式 acheven；现代拼写 achieve 更晚才固定，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The agent suffix -er was added to name the person, producing achiever alongside overachiever and underachiever.
items.cn: 加上施事后缀 -er 来指人，于是有了 achiever，并进一步产生 overachiever 与 underachiever。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words from the same achieve family; the near-meaning group collects people who succeed, with different degrees of praise.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 achieve 词族的词；近义组收获得成功的人，褒扬程度各不相同。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to reach a goal or accomplish something through effort.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「达成目标、通过努力完成某事」，是本词的核心动词。

entries.definition: The noun for a completed success or the act of accomplishing it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成就、达成」，指完成的成果或完成的过程。

entries.definition: A person who seeks success beyond expectations, often at a personal cost.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「过度追求成就的人」，常以个人代价换取超出预期的成绩。

entries.definition: A person who performs below the level their ability suggests.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「表现低于自身潜力的人」，即成绩低于能力所允许的水平。

entries.definition: A leader or the top person of a group; it shares the Latin caput root with achieve.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「首领、头目」，与 achieve 共享拉丁语 caput 词根。

entries.definition: A person who wins a contest; narrower than achiever because it needs a defeated opponent.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「获胜者」，比 achiever 窄，因为它必须有一个被击败的对手。

entries.definition: A person who acts rather than talks; stresses action, not measured success.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「实干者」，强调行动而非被衡量的成功。

entries.definition: The achievement of a goal; the abstract noun, while achiever names the person.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成功」，是抽象结果；achiever 则指取得结果的人。

entries.definition: An informal British term for an ambitious person who rises quickly.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，英式非正式用语，义为「飞黄腾达的人」，指上升很快的雄心者。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real caput root and the school and workplace phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的 caput 词根，以及这个词实际出现的校园与职场搭配。

normal.en: Achieve once meant to come to a head, from Latin caput, head.
normal.cn: achieve 曾表示「来到头的位置」，来自拉丁语 caput「头」。

normal.en: The same caput root gives capital, captain and chief, all about being at the top.
normal.cn: 同一 caput 词根还给出 capital、captain、chief，都与「处于顶端」有关。

normal.en: An achiever is simply the person who does the achieving; -er marks the doer.
normal.cn: achiever 就是完成 achieving 的那个人；-er 标记动作的执行者。

normal.en: Schools divide students into high achievers and low achievers, so the word works on a scale.
normal.cn: 学校把学生分成 high achiever 与 low achiever，可见这个词是按刻度使用的。

normal.en: Overachiever and underachiever show that the base word can be pushed above or below the expected line.
normal.cn: overachiever 与 underachiever 说明这个词可以被推到预期线之上或之下。

abstract.en: Picture a runner who crosses the line and then turns around to mark the distance on a board.
abstract.cn: 想象一名跑者冲过终点后转身，把跑过的距离记在板上。

abstract.en: The finish line is not a place but a habit: the achiever keeps setting a new head to reach.
abstract.cn: 终点线不是某个地点，而是一种习惯：有成就的人不断为自己设下新的「头」去抵达。

abstract.en: A head is both the top of the body and the top of a page; to achieve is to bring a matter to its own top.
abstract.cn: 「头」既是身体顶端，也是页面的顶端；achieve 就是把一件事带到它自己的顶端。

examples.en: Every achiever knows that a goal without a deadline is only a wish.
examples.cn: 每个有成就的人都明白，没有期限的目标只是愿望。

examples.en: The coach praised the young achiever for finishing the race despite the injury.
examples.cn: 教练表扬这位年轻的优胜者带伤跑完了全程。

examples.en: High achievers and low achievers often need different kinds of support.
examples.cn: 成绩优异者和成绩偏低者往往需要不同形式的支持。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿七婆」——她一路小跑冲到村头，事事都做到头：有成就的人

root: 英语 achieve 来自古法语 achever「完成」，源头是拉丁语 caput「头」的短语 ad caput「到头」，俗拉丁语重构为 *accapare；加施事后缀 -er 得到 achiever。caput 更早的印欧词根 *kaput- 属重构，来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all describe a person who brings something to an end: a personal goal, a career, school results, ambition itself, an excessive drive, a low score on the same scale, a contest, or the example of persistence.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述一种把事做到终点的人：个人目标、事业、学业成绩、进取心本身、过度的驱动力、同一刻度上的低分、竞赛，以及坚持的榜样。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a runner crosses the finish line and then turns to write the result on a board.
core.cn: 核心意象：跑者冲过终点线，转身把成绩写在板上。

branches.en: THE GOAL: the person is defined by reaching a self-set target.
branches.cn: 目标线：这个人由「达成自设目标」来定义。

branches.en: THE ARENA: work, school and sport each provide a visible finish line and a way to compare results.
branches.cn: 场域线：职场、学校与赛场都提供可见的终点线，并提供比较成绩的方式。

branches.en: THE DRIVE: the word can name the ambition inside the person, not only the result outside.
branches.cn: 驱动线：这个词可以指人内在的雄心，而不只是外在的结果。

branches.en: THE SCALE: over- and low- push the same image above or below the expected line.
branches.cn: 刻度线：over- 与 low- 把同一画面推到预期线之上或之下。

branches.en: THE EXAMPLE: persistence makes the person a model others point to.
branches.cn: 榜样线：坚持使这个人成为他人引用的榜样。

intro.en: The word is a verb stem plus an agent suffix; the verb itself grew from a Latin head noun and a preposition.
intro.cn: 这个词由动词词干加施事后缀构成；动词本身则从拉丁语「头」名词与介词生长出来。

latinIntro.en: Latin caput and ad are recorded, while the Vulgar Latin verb that joined them is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 caput 与 ad 均有文献记录，把它们组合起来的俗拉丁语动词则属重构形式。

items.example: The stem carries the whole action.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干承载整个动作。
它把 achieve 变成 achiever。

items.example: The prefix points the action toward a destination.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作指向一个目的地。

items.example: The head is the goal the action must reach.
items.exampleCN: 「头」就是动作必须抵达的目标。

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉施事后缀得到的动词，义为「达成；取得」
由动词加 -ment 构成，义为「成就；达成」
由动词加 -able 构成，义为「可实现的」
由 over- 加本词构成，义为「过度追求成就的人」
由 under- 加本词构成，义为「表现低于潜力的人」

definition_zh: 酸化；使变酸的过程；海洋酸化；土壤酸化
definition_en: the process of becoming acid or of making something acid, especially in water, soil or chemical systems
core_image: 一滴酸落进清水，整杯水的味道慢慢变酸
scene: 雨后的湖面看起来很平静，岸边的石头却被悄悄腐蚀了。Scientists measured the acidification of the lake after decades of acid rain.
sceneCN: 这里 acidification 是「酸化过程」（第 1 个义项：变成酸性的过程）；句意为科学家测量了数十年酸雨之后湖泊的酸化程度。

pos.zh: 名词：酸化；使变酸的过程

derivatives.zh: 由 acid 加 -ify 构成的动词，义为「使变酸；酸化」
基础名词，义为「酸；酸性物质」
由 acid 加 -ic 构成，义为「酸性的」
由 acid 加 -ity 构成，义为「酸度；酸性」
由动词加 -ed 构成，义为「已被酸化的」

senses.title: The process of becoming acid
senses.definition: the general process by which a substance or environment becomes more acid than before
senses.definitionCN: 某物质或环境变得比原先更具酸性的总体过程
senses.example: Acidification of the solution continued until the indicator turned red.
senses.exampleCN: 溶液的酸化持续到指示剂变红为止。
senses.why: Acid plus the -fication suffix means making acid, so the word names the process rather than the result.
senses.whyCN: acid 加上表示「造成」的 -fication 后缀，就是「使成酸」，所以这个词指过程而不是结果。

senses.title: Ocean acidification
senses.definition: the ongoing decrease in the pH of ocean water as it absorbs carbon dioxide from the atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 海水吸收大气中的二氧化碳而导致酸碱度持续下降的现象
senses.example: Ocean acidification threatens corals and shellfish that build calcium shells.
senses.exampleCN: 海洋酸化威胁着那些建造钙质外壳的珊瑚与贝类。
senses.why: The general chemical process is applied to the largest body of water, where dissolved carbon dioxide drives the change.
senses.whyCN: 一般化学过程被用到最大的水体上，溶解的二氧化碳推动了这一变化。

senses.title: Soil acidification
senses.definition: the gradual lowering of soil pH, often caused by heavy fertilizer use, acid rain or leaching
senses.definitionCN: 土壤酸碱度逐渐降低，常由大量施肥、酸雨或淋溶造成
senses.example: Years of ammonium fertilizer led to serious acidification of the farmland.
senses.exampleCN: 多年施用铵态氮肥导致这片农田严重酸化。
senses.why: Soil is treated as a chemical system, and the same making-acid process is measured in the field.
senses.whyCN: 土壤被当作一个化学系统看待，同一种「使成酸」的过程在田地里被测量。

senses.title: Acidification of lakes and rivers
senses.definition: the falling pH of freshwater bodies, often linked to acid deposition and poor buffering capacity
senses.definitionCN: 淡水水体酸碱度下降，常与酸性沉降和缓冲能力不足有关
senses.example: The acidification of the river killed several sensitive fish species.
senses.exampleCN: 河流的酸化使几种敏感的鱼类死亡。
senses.why: Fresh water has less capacity to resist acid than the sea, so the same process shows its effects faster.
senses.whyCN: 淡水抵抗酸的能力比海水弱，所以同一过程在淡水中更快显露后果。

senses.title: Industrial acidification
senses.definition: acidification caused by industrial emissions such as sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides
senses.definitionCN: 由二氧化硫、氮氧化物等工业排放引起的酸化
senses.example: Regulations cut the acidification caused by the old smelter.
senses.exampleCN: 新法规减少了旧冶炼厂造成的酸化。
senses.why: Industry adds acid-forming gases to the air, and the word names the downstream change in land and water.
senses.whyCN: 工业向空气排放成酸气体，这个词则指陆地和水中随之发生的变化。

senses.title: Acidification in a laboratory
senses.definition: the deliberate addition of acid to a sample or mixture in order to lower its pH
senses.definitionCN: 为降低酸碱度而向样品或混合物中人为加入酸的操作
senses.example: Acidification of the sample was needed before the metal could be measured.
senses.exampleCN: 在测定金属之前需要先对样品进行酸化处理。
senses.why: In the lab the process is intentional and controlled, so the word describes a step in a procedure.
senses.whyCN: 在实验室里这个过程是有意且受控的，所以这个词描述的是实验步骤。

senses.title: Food acidification
senses.definition: the controlled lowering of pH in food, used in pickling, fermentation or preservation
senses.definitionCN: 在腌制、发酵或保藏中受控地降低食品酸碱度
senses.example: The acidification of the cucumbers gives pickles their sharp taste.
senses.exampleCN: 黄瓜的酸化使腌菜带上尖锐的酸味。
senses.why: The same chemical change happens in a jar, where low pH both flavors food and slows spoilage.
senses.whyCN: 同一化学变化发生在罐子里，低酸碱度既给食物调味，也减缓腐败。

senses.title: Measured acidification
senses.definition: a quantified drop in pH or increase in acid content over a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 一段时间内酸碱度的量化下降或酸含量的上升
senses.example: The report recorded a steady acidification of the groundwater since the mine opened.
senses.exampleCN: 报告记录了自矿山开采以来地下水的持续酸化。
senses.why: Once the process is monitored, the word can name the measured trend itself, not only the invisible chemical change.
senses.whyCN: 一旦过程被监测，这个词就能指被测量出的趋势本身，而不只是看不见的化学变化。

intro.en: Acidification is a transparent scientific compound: acid, from a Latin word for sour, plus a suffix meaning making.
intro.cn: acidification 是一个透明的科学复合词：acid 来自拉丁语「酸」，加上表示「造成」的后缀。

items.en: The Latin root ac- meant sharp or sour; its wider connections are reconstructed and in part source uncertain.
items.cn: 拉丁词根 ac- 意为「尖、酸」，其更广的关联属重构，部分来源不确定。

items.en: Acidus meant sour or tart, and the verb acere meant to be sharp or sour.
items.cn: acidus 意为「酸的、尖酸的」，动词 acere 意为「是尖的、是酸的」。

items.en: Facere meant to make or do; in compounds it regularly appears as -ficare, as in acidificare.
items.cn: facere 意为「做、使」，在复合词中通常写作 -ficare，如 acidificare。

items.en: English acid entered through Old French acide; the exact first date is not certain, but it was established by the late Middle Ages.
items.cn: 英语 acid 经由古法语 acide 进入，确切首见年代不确定，但在中世纪末已确立。

items.en: The verb acidify and the noun acidification were formed in scientific English on Latin models, using -ify and -ification.
items.cn: 动词 acidify 与名词 acidification 是仿拉丁模型在科学英语中构成的，使用 -ify 与 -ification。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word became central to environmental science, especially for oceans and soils.
items.cn: 二十世纪这个词成为环境科学的核心术语，尤其用于海洋与土壤。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the acid family; the near-meaning group gathers related chemical changes with different directions or scales.
note.cn: 形近组收 acid 词族；近义组收方向或尺度不同的相关化学变化。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to make or become acid.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使变酸、酸化」，是本词对应的动作。

entries.definition: A substance that gives off hydrogen ions; the base noun of the family.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「酸」，指能释放氢离子的物质，是这一词族的基础名词。

entries.definition: An adjective describing something with a low pH or sour properties.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「酸性的」，形容低酸碱度或带酸味的物质。

entries.definition: The noun for the degree or quality of being acid.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「酸度、酸性」，指酸的程度或性质。

entries.definition: Rain made acidic by airborne pollutants; a cause of environmental acidification.
entries.definitionCN: 名词短语，义为「酸雨」，由空气污染物致酸，是环境酸化的成因之一。

entries.definition: The process of becoming more alkaline, the chemical opposite of acidification.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「碱化」，是酸化在化学方向上的相反过程。

entries.definition: The gradual destruction of material, often accelerated by acids; a consequence, not the pH change itself.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「腐蚀」，常被酸加速，是一种后果，而不是酸碱度变化本身。

entries.definition: The introduction of harmful substances into the environment; a broader cause of acidification.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「污染」，指有害物质进入环境，是酸化的更宽泛成因。

entries.definition: The removal of soluble substances from soil by water, often linked to acidification.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「淋溶」，指水把可溶物从土壤中带走，常与酸化相关。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real acid and facere roots plus the environmental phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的 acid 与 facere 词根，以及这个词实际出现的环境搭配。

normal.en: Acid plus -fication equals making acid; the suffix is the same one in purification.
normal.cn: acid 加 -fication 就是「使成酸」；这个后缀也出现在 purification 中。

normal.en: Facere, to make, is the verb behind -fication and also behind factory and manufacture.
normal.cn: facere「做」是 -fication 背后的动词，也藏在 factory 与 manufacture 里。

normal.en: Ocean acidification names the sea version of the same chemical change.
normal.cn: ocean acidification 就是同一化学变化在海洋中的版本。

normal.en: Soil acidification is measured as a falling pH in the field.
normal.cn: soil acidification 在田间表现为酸碱度不断下降。

normal.en: The opposite process is alkalinization, so the word has a clear chemical direction.
normal.cn: 相反的过程是 alkalinization，可见这个词有明确的化学方向。

abstract.en: Picture a drop of lemon juice falling into a bucket of clear water and a colour strip turning from blue to red.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴柠檬汁落进一桶清水，试纸由蓝变红。

abstract.en: The word is a slow-motion film: nothing visible happens, yet every measurement says the water is turning sour.
abstract.cn: 这个词像一段慢镜头：看不见什么发生，但每次测量都说水正在变酸。

abstract.en: Acidification is a direction, not a thing; it tells you which way a system is drifting.
abstract.cn: 酸化是一个方向而不是一件东西；它告诉你一个系统正在往哪边漂移。

examples.en: Ocean acidification is driven mainly by dissolved carbon dioxide.
examples.cn: 海洋酸化主要由溶解的二氧化碳推动。

examples.en: Farmers were warned about the acidification of their soil after years of over-fertilizing.
examples.cn: 农民被提醒，多年过量施肥已使土壤酸化。

examples.en: The acidification of the sample was completed before the test began.
examples.cn: 样品的酸化在测试开始前已经完成。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「酸一酸，飞一飞」——酸味一散开，整片水都变酸：酸化

root: 拉丁语 acidus「酸的」与 facere「做、使」组合成 acidificare「使成酸」；英语以 acid 加 -ify、-ification 构成 acidify 与 acidification。词根 ac-「尖、酸」的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses apply one direction of chemical change to different containers: a general solution, the ocean, soil, fresh water, industry, a lab sample, food, and a measured trend.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一个化学变化方向用到不同容器上：一般溶液、海洋、土壤、淡水、工业、实验样品、食物，以及被测量的趋势。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drop of acid falls into clear water, and a test strip slowly turns red.
core.cn: 核心意象：一滴酸落进清水，试纸慢慢变红。

branches.en: THE PROCESS: the general name for becoming more acid.
branches.cn: 过程线：泛指变得更酸的经过。

branches.en: THE ENVIRONMENT: ocean, soil and fresh water are three containers where the same change is observed.
branches.cn: 环境线：海洋、土壤与淡水是观察到同一变化的三个容器。

branches.en: THE SOURCE: industrial emissions supply the acid-forming gases behind the change.
branches.cn: 来源线：工业排放提供了推动变化的成酸气体。

branches.en: THE CONTROLLED SETTING: a lab sample or a food jar receives acid on purpose.
branches.cn: 受控场景线：实验样品或食品罐子被有意加入酸。

branches.en: THE RECORD: monitoring turns the invisible process into a measured trend.
branches.cn: 记录线：监测把看不见的过程变成可测量的趋势。

intro.en: Acidification joins a Latin sour root to a Latin making suffix, and English adds further suffixes to build the family.
intro.cn: acidification 把拉丁语「酸」词根与拉丁语「造成」后缀连接起来，英语再加后缀扩展出词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin acidus, acere and facere are recorded; the compound acidificare is attested in scientific Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 acidus、acere、facere 均有记录；复合形式 acidificare 见于科学拉丁语。

items.example: The root supplies the direction of the change.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供变化的方向。

items.example: It forms alkalinization, the opposite process.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 alkalinization，即相反过程。

items.example: It forms alkalinization and many process nouns.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 alkalinization 以及许多过程名词。

derivatives.zh: 由 acid 加 -ify 构成，义为「使变酸；酸化」
由 acid 加 -ic 构成，义为「酸性的」
由 acid 加 -ity 构成，义为「酸度；酸性」
由动词加 -ed 构成，义为「已被酸化的」
由动词加 -er 构成，义为「酸化剂；致酸物」

definition_zh: 橡子；橡树的果实；橡子形饰物；橡实
definition_en: the small oval nut of the oak tree, or something shaped like it
core_image: 一枚戴着小帽的橡实躺在落叶间
scene: 秋天的林子里，落叶堆得很厚，一只松鼠正忙着搬运食物。The squirrel buried an acorn under the old oak tree.
sceneCN: 这里 acorn 是「橡子」（第 1 个义项：橡树的果实）；句意为松鼠把一枚橡子埋在老橡树下。

pos.zh: 名词：橡子；橡实；橡子形物件

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 squash 构成的复合名词，指形状像橡子的小南瓜
由本词加 worm 构成的动物名，指一种海生蠕虫
由本词加 -ed 构成的少见形容词，义为「结满橡子的」

senses.title: The nut of an oak tree
senses.definition: the oval seed of an oak tree, enclosed in a woody cup at its base
senses.definitionCN: 橡树的椭圆形种子，基部包在木质壳斗中
senses.example: Each acorn holds a single seed that can grow into a new oak.
senses.exampleCN: 每枚橡子含一粒种子，可以长成一棵新橡树。
senses.why: The word is the oldest English name for this particular fruit, so the oak nut is the sense from which everything else grows.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是英语里对这类果实最古老的称呼，所以「橡树坚果」是其他义项生长的起点。

senses.title: The cup that holds the acorn
senses.definition: the woody cup-shaped base that surrounds the lower part of the acorn
senses.definitionCN: 包住橡子下部的木质杯状基部
senses.example: The empty acorn cup stayed on the branch after the nut fell.
senses.exampleCN: 坚果掉落后，空壳斗仍留在树枝上。
senses.why: The cup is so closely attached to the nut that English often uses the same word for the whole object, including its little cap.
senses.whyCN: 壳斗与坚果贴得太紧，英语常用同一个词指整个物件，连那顶小帽也算在内。

senses.title: Food for wildlife
senses.definition: acorns as a seasonal food source for squirrels, birds, deer and other animals
senses.definitionCN: 作为松鼠、鸟类、鹿等动物季节性食物的橡子
senses.example: A heavy acorn crop helps deer survive a hard winter.
senses.exampleCN: 橡子丰收能帮助鹿度过严冬。
senses.why: Because the nut is nutritious and stores well, whole food chains form around the acorn crop.
senses.whyCN: 因为这种坚果营养丰富又耐储存，整条食物链都围绕橡子收成形成。

senses.title: Acorn squash
senses.definition: a small winter squash with a shape and colour resembling an acorn
senses.definitionCN: 一种小型冬南瓜，形状与颜色都像橡子
senses.example: She roasted an acorn squash with butter and brown sugar.
senses.exampleCN: 她用黄油和红糖烤了一只橡子南瓜。
senses.why: The vegetable borrows the name because its outline copies the nut, showing how a concrete shape can be transferred to a new object.
senses.whyCN: 这种蔬菜借用了这个名字，因为外形模仿那枚坚果，说明具体形状可以被移植到新物件上。

senses.title: A symbol of small beginnings
senses.definition: the acorn as an emblem of great things growing from small, modest beginnings
senses.definitionCN: 作为「伟大事物由微小开端生长」的象征的橡子
senses.example: The proverb about tall oaks from little acorns is carved above the school door.
senses.exampleCN: 校门上方刻着那句关于小橡子长成高橡树的谚语。
senses.why: A tiny nut becoming a huge tree is a ready-made image of potential, so the object turns into a symbol.
senses.whyCN: 一枚小坚果长成大树，是现成的「潜力」画面，于是实物变成了象征。

senses.title: An emblem on flags and crests
senses.definition: the acorn used as a heraldic or institutional emblem representing growth or strength
senses.definitionCN: 作为纹章或机构标志的橡子，象征生长或力量
senses.example: The old town crest shows an acorn between two oak leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 这座古镇的纹章上，两片橡树叶之间有一枚橡子。
senses.why: Once the nut stands for growth, it can be drawn on a shield, where symbols speak instead of words.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这枚坚果代表生长，它就能被画上盾牌，在纹章里符号代替文字说话。

senses.title: An acorn-shaped object
senses.definition: any small object, ornament or fitting whose form imitates an acorn, such as a knob or pendant
senses.definitionCN: 任何模仿橡子外形的小物件、饰物或配件，如旋钮或坠饰
senses.example: The drawer handle ends in a brass acorn.
senses.exampleCN: 抽屉拉手的末端是一个黄铜橡子。
senses.why: Because the shape is easy to recognize, craft workers name the object after the nut it resembles.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个形状容易辨认，手艺人就用它模仿的坚果来命名物件。

senses.title: Acorns in forestry and seed collection
senses.definition: acorns treated as seed units in forestry, counted, graded and stored for replanting
senses.definitionCN: 林业中作为种子单位被计数、分级并储存用于再植的橡子
senses.example: The nursery stored the acorns in damp sand until spring.
senses.exampleCN: 苗圃把橡子存放在湿沙里直到春天。
senses.why: When forests are managed, the nut stops being a symbol and becomes a measured unit of seed.
senses.whyCN: 当森林被经营管理时，这枚坚果不再是象征，而成了被计量的种子单位。

intro.en: Acorn is an old English word whose earliest meaning was simply the fruit of the oak; its deeper origin is disputed.
intro.cn: acorn 是一个古老的英语词，最早只指橡树的果实；它更早的来源存在争议。

items.en: The word is often linked to a root for field or open land, but this connection is source uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词常被联系到一个表示「田地、开阔地」的词根，但这一关联来源不确定。

items.en: The reconstructed form *akran- meant fruit or acorn, and related forms appear across the Germanic languages.
items.cn: 重构形式 *akran- 意为「果实、橡子」，相关形式见于多种日耳曼语言。

items.en: Old English æcern meant the nut of the oak; the modern spelling with -orn is later and partly reshaped by oak.
items.cn: 古英语 æcern 指橡树的坚果；带 -orn 的现代拼写出现较晚，并部分受到 oak 的影响。

items.en: The form akern or acorn spread, and the word kept its single concrete sense through the Middle Ages.
items.cn: akern 或 acorn 的形式流行开来，这个词在中世纪一直保持单一的具体含义。

items.en: The acorn became a common shape name, giving acorn squash and acorn-shaped ornaments; exact first dates for these uses are uncertain.
items.cn: 橡子成为常见的形状名称，产生 acorn squash 与橡子形饰物；这些用法的确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The proverb about tall oaks from little acorns fixed the nut as a symbol of growth and potential.
items.cn: 「小橡子长成高橡树」的谚语把这枚坚果固定为生长与潜力的象征。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers oak and nut words; the near-meaning group gathers seeds and tree fruits with a different shape or role.
note.cn: 形近组收橡树与坚果类词；近义组收形状或作用不同的种子与树木果实。

entries.definition: The tree that produces acorns; the two words are historically linked in English.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「橡树」，是产生橡子的树；这两个词在英语史上相互关联。

entries.definition: A small winter squash named for its acorn-like shape.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「橡子南瓜」，因果实形状像橡子而得名。

entries.definition: A marine worm whose body resembles an acorn; unrelated to the oak nut.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「橡子蠕虫」，身体形似橡子，与橡树果实本身无关。

entries.definition: A rare adjective meaning bearing acorns.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，较少见，义为「结满橡子的」。

entries.definition: A hard-shelled fruit or seed; broader than acorn and covers many plant families.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「坚果」，范围比 acorn 宽，涵盖许多植物科属。

entries.definition: The unit of reproduction in plants; the acorn is one kind of seed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「种子」，是植物的繁殖单位，橡子正是其中一种。

entries.definition: The fruit of forest trees, especially acorns and beechnuts, used as animal feed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「林木果实」，尤指橡子与山毛榉果，用作动物饲料。

entries.definition: A tree or shrub with pods; the spelling resembles acorn but the plant is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「金合欢」，结荚果；拼写与 acorn 相似但植物无关，词源不同。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the old English history of the word and the real compounds it forms.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用这个词的英语早期历史，以及它实际构成的复合词。

normal.en: Old English æcern already meant the oak's nut, so the core sense is very old.
normal.cn: 古英语 æcern 已经指橡树的坚果，可见核心义项非常古老。

normal.en: The modern spelling was partly reshaped by the word oak, which is the tree that bears acorns.
normal.cn: 现代拼写部分受到 oak 影响，而 oak 正是结出橡子的树。

normal.en: Acorn squash borrows the name from the shape, not from any botanical relation.
normal.cn: acorn squash 借的是形状之名，并非植物学上的亲缘关系。

normal.en: Mast is the forestry term for acorns and similar nuts used as animal feed.
normal.cn: mast 是林业术语，指橡子等用作动物饲料的林木果实。

normal.en: The proverb tall oaks from little acorns grow turns the nut into a symbol of potential.
normal.cn: 谚语「小橡子长成高橡树」把这枚坚果变成潜力的象征。

abstract.en: Picture a tiny brown nut wearing a rough cap, sitting in a carpet of yellow leaves.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚戴粗壳小帽的棕色小坚果，坐在黄色落叶铺成的地毯上。

abstract.en: The acorn is a package: the cap is the lid, the shell is the box, and the seed inside is the future tree.
abstract.cn: 橡子像一个包裹：壳斗是盖子，硬壳是盒子，里面的种子是未来的树。

abstract.en: Every huge oak on a hill began as one small thing a squirrel could carry in its mouth.
abstract.cn: 山坡上每棵巨大的橡树，最初都是松鼠嘴里能叼走的一件小东西。

examples.en: The children collected acorns to feed the forest squirrels.
examples.cn: 孩子们收集橡子去喂林子里的松鼠。

examples.en: An acorn squash can be baked whole if you pierce its skin first.
examples.cn: 橡子南瓜只要先扎破表皮就可以整只烤。

examples.en: Foresters count the acorn crop to predict how many seedlings they can raise.
examples.cn: 林务人员清点橡子收成，以预测能培育多少幼苗。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一壳鬃」——一枚小果顶着壳帽、拖着小鬃毛：橡子

root: 古英语 æcern「橡树的果实」是这个词的最早记录形式，可追溯到日耳曼语重构形式 *akran-「果实、橡子」。它与表示「田地」的词根是否相关，来源不确定；现代拼写受 oak 影响。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses move from the oak nut itself through its cup, its role as wildlife food, its shape in vegetables and ornaments, its symbolic and heraldic use, to its place as measured forestry seed.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从橡树坚果本身出发，经过壳斗、野生动物食物、蔬菜与饰物中的形状、象征与纹章用途，最后到林业中被计量的种子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small brown nut with a rough cap lies among yellow autumn leaves.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚戴粗壳小帽的棕色坚果躺在黄色秋叶间。

branches.en: THE PLANT: the oak's fruit and the cup that holds it.
branches.cn: 植物线：橡树的果实与承托它的壳斗。

branches.en: THE HARVEST: animals eat the crop, and foresters measure and store it.
branches.cn: 收获线：动物取食这份收成，林务人员则计量并储存它。

branches.en: THE SHAPE: the outline of the nut is copied by a squash and by small ornaments.
branches.cn: 形状线：坚果的轮廓被一种南瓜和小饰物复制。

branches.en: THE SYMBOL: a small beginning that grows into something great.
branches.cn: 象征线：微小开端长成伟大事物。

branches.en: THE EMBLEM: the same symbol is drawn on crests and flags.
branches.cn: 纹章线：同一象征被画上盾徽与旗帜。

intro.en: Acorn is a native English word, not a Latin compound; its parts are historical forms rather than live affixes.
intro.cn: acorn 是英语本族词，不是拉丁语复合词；它的组成是历史形式而非现役词缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor of acorn, so no Latin family is listed here.
latinIntro.cn: acorn 没有拉丁语祖先，因此这里不列拉丁同族词。

items.example: It is the earliest recorded form of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这是这个词最早被记录的形式。

items.example: The form is reconstructed from related Germanic words.
items.exampleCN: 这一形式由相关日耳曼语词重构而来。

items.example: The modern spelling of acorn was partly influenced by oak.
items.exampleCN: acorn 的现代拼写部分受到 oak 影响。

items.meaning: not a live suffix; part of the modern form
items.meaningCN: 并非现役后缀，只是现代词形的一部分
items.example: The ending grew by reshaping, not by adding a suffix.
items.exampleCN: 词尾是经重新塑形形成的，不是添加后缀而来。

items.meaning: the woody base of the nut
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 acorn cup 中。
它出现在 acorn squash 中。
它出现在 acorn worm 中。

items.example: Acorns are a kind of mast.
items.exampleCN: 橡子属于林木坚果的一类。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 squash 构成，指形状像橡子的小南瓜
由本词加 worm 构成的动物名
由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「结满橡子的」

definition_zh: 声学专家；声学工程师；建筑声学顾问
definition_en: a specialist who studies or works with sound, especially in buildings, music or the environment
core_image: 一人拿着测声仪站在音乐厅空荡的座位间
scene: 音乐厅还没开门，空座之间已经有人拿着仪器走动。The acoustician measured how sound travelled through the hall.
sceneCN: 这里 acoustician 是「声学专家」（第 1 个义项：研究或处理声音的专门人才）；句意为这位声学专家测量声音在大厅中如何传播。

pos.zh: 名词：声学专家；声学工程师

derivatives.zh: 由希腊语「听觉」词根加 -ics 构成的学科名，义为「声学；音响效果」
由希腊语「听觉」词根加 -ic 构成，义为「声学的；原声的」
由形容词加 -ally 构成，义为「在声学上；从声音角度」
由 acoustic 加 -al 构成的形容词变体，义为「声学的」

senses.title: A specialist in acoustics
senses.definition: a person trained in the science of sound and vibration
senses.definitionCN: 受过声音与振动科学训练的人
senses.example: The acoustician explained why the room amplified every whisper.
senses.exampleCN: 这位声学专家解释了为什么这间屋子会放大每句耳语。
senses.why: Acoustics is the science of hearing, and -ician marks a practitioner, so the word names the person who works with sound as a science.
senses.whyCN: acoustics 是研究听觉的科学，-ician 标记从业者，所以这个词指把声音当作科学研究的人。

senses.title: An architectural acoustics consultant
senses.definition: a professional who advises architects on how a building will carry, absorb or isolate sound
senses.definitionCN: 就建筑如何传导、吸收或隔绝声音向建筑师提供建议的专业人士
senses.example: The acoustician recommended thicker walls around the rehearsal room.
senses.exampleCN: 声学顾问建议在排练室周围使用更厚的墙。
senses.why: Buildings are one of the largest practical problems in sound, so the specialist is often hired at the design stage.
senses.whyCN: 建筑是声音最大的实际问题之一，所以这位专家常在设计阶段就被聘用。

senses.title: A noise-control engineer
senses.definition: an engineer who reduces unwanted noise in machines, workplaces or cities
senses.definitionCN: 降低机器、工作场所或城市中不需要的噪声的工程师
senses.example: The acoustician traced the factory noise to a badly mounted fan.
senses.exampleCN: 这位噪声控制工程师把工厂噪声追查到一台安装不良的风扇。
senses.why: The same science is turned toward removing sound rather than designing it, which is the noise-control branch.
senses.whyCN: 同一门科学被用来消除声音而不是设计声音，这就是噪声控制分支。

senses.title: A researcher in musical acoustics
senses.definition: a scientist who studies how instruments and voices produce and shape sound
senses.definitionCN: 研究乐器与人声如何产生并塑造声音的科学家
senses.example: The acoustician built a model of how the violin body resonates.
senses.exampleCN: 这位声学专家建立了一个模型，说明小提琴琴身如何共振。
senses.why: Music gives sound a precise structure, so the specialist can measure pitch, resonance and timbre in controlled ways.
senses.whyCN: 音乐给声音提供了精确结构，所以专家能以受控方式测量音高、共振与音色。

senses.title: An underwater acoustics expert
senses.definition: a specialist in how sound travels through water, used in sonar and marine research
senses.definitionCN: 研究声音如何在水中传播的专家，应用于声呐与海洋研究
senses.example: The navy consulted an acoustician before changing its sonar frequency.
senses.exampleCN: 海军在改变声呐频率前咨询了一位水声学专家。
senses.why: Water carries sound very differently from air, so the general science grows a separate underwater branch.
senses.whyCN: 水传播声音的方式与空气很不同，所以这门总体科学分出了独立的水下分支。

senses.title: An environmental noise assessor
senses.definition: a person who measures and assesses noise impact on neighbourhoods and wildlife
senses.definitionCN: 测量并评估噪声对社区与野生动物影响的人
senses.example: The acoustician mapped the noise from the new motorway.
senses.exampleCN: 这位声学专家绘制了新高速公路的噪声分布图。
senses.why: Once noise is treated as pollution, the specialist is needed to measure it and argue about limits.
senses.whyCN: 一旦噪声被当作污染，就需要专家来测量它并讨论限值。

senses.title: A teacher of acoustics
senses.definition: a person who teaches acoustics to students of physics, engineering or music
senses.definitionCN: 向物理、工程或音乐专业学生教授声学的人
senses.example: As an acoustician, she taught a course on room design.
senses.exampleCN: 作为声学专家，她讲授一门关于房间设计的课程。
senses.why: A specialist can also be the one who passes the science on, so the word covers the teaching role.
senses.whyCN: 专家也可以是把这门科学传下去的人，所以这个词也涵盖教学角色。

senses.title: A sound-system designer
senses.definition: a person who designs or tunes sound systems and listening spaces for clear, even sound
senses.definitionCN: 设计或调试音响系统与聆听空间，使声音清晰均匀的人
senses.example: The acoustician tuned the concert hall speakers before the tour opened.
senses.exampleCN: 巡演开始前，这位声学专家调试了音乐厅的扬声器。
senses.why: The practical end of the science is making a space sound right, which joins measurement with design.
senses.whyCN: 这门科学的实践终点是让空间听起来正确，于是测量与设计在此汇合。

intro.en: Acoustician is a nineteenth-century English formation on the Greek verb for hearing, with the practitioner suffix -ician.
intro.cn: acoustician 是十九世纪在希腊语「听」动词基础上构成的英语词，加上表示从业者的后缀 -ician。

items.en: Greek akouein meant to hear; its deeper Indo-European connections are reconstructed and in part source uncertain.
items.cn: 希腊语 akouein 意为「听见」；其更早的印欧语关联属重构，部分来源不确定。

items.en: Akoustikos meant of or for hearing, and it was used of sounds and of the sense itself.
items.cn: akoustikos 意为「与听觉有关的、为听觉的」，用于声音也用于听觉本身。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek adjective as acusticus, keeping the hearing sense.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入这个希腊形容词作 acusticus，保留「听觉」之意。

items.en: French acoustique carried the word into modern European languages, where it also named the science.
items.cn: 法语 acoustique 把这个词带入现代欧洲语言，并同时用来指这门科学。

items.en: English acoustic is recorded from the seventeenth century; acoustics as a science name followed later.
items.cn: 英语 acoustic 在十七世纪已有记录；作为学科名的 acoustics 更晚出现。

items.en: Acoustician was formed with -ician on the model of musician and physician; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: acoustician 仿 musician、physician 等词加上 -ician 构成，确切首见年代不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the acoustics family; the near-meaning group gathers other sound professionals and hearing specialists.
note.cn: 形近组收 acoustics 词族；近义组收其他声音从业者与听觉专家。

entries.definition: The science of sound, or the sound properties of a room.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「声学」或「空间的音响效果」，是本词的学科基础。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning relating to sound, or describing an instrument that is not amplified.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「声音的」，也指不靠电声放大的原声乐器。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning in terms of sound or acoustics.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「从声学角度、在声音方面」。

entries.definition: An adjective variant of acoustic, common in engineering.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，是 acoustic 的变体，工程文献中常见。

entries.definition: A compound job title close in meaning to acoustician but marked as engineering.
entries.definitionCN: 复合职位名，意义接近 acoustician，但更强调工程身份。

entries.definition: A hearing-health professional who tests and treats human hearing, not building sound.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「听力师」，测试与治疗人的听力，不处理建筑声学。

entries.definition: A person who records, mixes or reproduces sound; practical rather than scientific.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「音响工程师」，负责录音、混音或重放，偏实操而非科研。

entries.definition: A scientist of matter and energy; acoustics is one branch of physics.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「物理学家」，研究物质与能量；声学是物理学的分支之一。

entries.definition: A person who operates underwater sound equipment rather than studying sound in general.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「声呐技师」，操作水下声学设备，而非研究一般声音。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Greek hearing root and the real job compounds the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用希腊语「听」词根，以及这个词实际出现的职业复合词。

normal.en: Greek akouein means to hear, so acoustics is literally the study of hearing.
normal.cn: 希腊语 akouein 意为「听见」，所以 acoustics 字面上就是研究听觉。

normal.en: The -ician ending marks a practitioner, as in musician and physician.
normal.cn: -ician 结尾标记从业者，如 musician 与 physician。

normal.en: An architectural acoustician is hired before a hall is built, not after.
normal.cn: 建筑声学专家在音乐厅建成之前就被聘用，而不是建成之后。

normal.en: Underwater acoustics is a separate branch because water carries sound differently.
normal.cn: 水声学是独立分支，因为水传播声音的方式不同。

normal.en: The opposite job is noise control, where the same science removes sound.
normal.cn: 相对的工作是噪声控制，用同一门科学去消除声音。

abstract.en: Picture an empty concert hall: one person walks the aisles with a meter while the seats stay silent.
abstract.cn: 想象一座空音乐厅：一个人拿着仪表走过走道，座位一片寂静。

abstract.en: The acoustician does not make music; they make the room behave so music can be heard.
abstract.cn: 声学专家不创作音乐；他们让房间规矩起来，好让音乐被听见。

abstract.en: Sound is invisible, so the specialist's real tool is measurement, not the ear alone.
abstract.cn: 声音看不见，所以专家真正的工具是测量，而不只是耳朵。

examples.en: The acoustician spent three days testing the new lecture hall.
examples.cn: 这位声学专家花了三天测试新的讲堂。

examples.en: Before the concert, an acoustician adjusted the ceiling panels.
examples.cn: 音乐会前，一位声学专家调整了天花板板件。

examples.en: The city hired an acoustician to study traffic noise near the school.
examples.cn: 市里聘请一位声学专家研究学校附近的交通噪声。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿库斯提申」——阿库斯提着仪器，一间间屋子听：声学专家

root: 希腊语 akouein「听见」派生出 akoustikos「与听觉有关的」，经拉丁语 acusticus 与法语 acoustique 进入英语；英语再加 -ician「从业者」构成 acoustician。更早的印欧语关联属重构，部分来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses follow one trained listener into different rooms: pure science, building design, noise control, music, underwater sound, environmental assessment, teaching, and sound-system tuning.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一位受过训练的「听者」走进不同场所：纯科学、建筑设计、噪声控制、音乐、水下声音、环境评估、教学，以及音响系统调试。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person with a sound meter stands in an empty hall, listening to how the room answers.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人拿着声级计站在空荡的大厅里，听房间如何回应。

branches.en: THE SCIENCE: the specialist knows the subject and can teach it.
branches.cn: 科学线：专家掌握这门学科，也能教授它。

branches.en: THE BUILDING: halls and sound systems are designed so that listening works.
branches.cn: 建筑线：大厅与音响系统被设计成让聆听成立。

branches.en: THE NUISANCE: the same knowledge is used to measure and reduce unwanted sound.
branches.cn: 扰民线：同样的知识被用来测量并减少不需要的声音。

branches.en: THE INSTRUMENT: music provides precise sound to study and tune.
branches.cn: 乐器线：音乐提供精确的声音供研究与调试。

branches.en: THE SEA: water turns sound into a separate technical branch.
branches.cn: 海洋线：水使声音分出一个独立的技术分支。

intro.en: The word joins a Greek hearing root with a Latin-derived practitioner suffix; the science name and the person name grew side by side.
intro.cn: 这个词把希腊语「听」词根与源自拉丁的从业者后缀连接起来；学科名与人名是并行长出的。

latinIntro.en: Greek akouein and akoustikos are recorded, and Latin acusticus borrowed the adjective; no native Latin root is involved.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 akouein 与 akoustikos 均有记录，拉丁语 acusticus 借入了这个形容词；不涉及拉丁本族词根。

items.example: It is the hearing element in the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这一词族中的「听」元素。

items.example: It appears in sonar, a related sound technology.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 sonar 这一相关声音技术中。

derivatives.zh: 由希腊语词根加 -ics 构成，义为「声学；音响效果」
由希腊语词根加 -ic 构成，义为「声学的；原声的」
由形容词加 -ally 构成，义为「在声学上」
由 acoustic 加 -al 构成的形容词变体

definition_zh: 贪得的；渴望获取的；占有欲强的；（犯罪）以获取财物为目的的
definition_en: strongly eager to acquire possessions, money or knowledge, sometimes to an excessive degree
core_image: 手不断伸向货架，车里越堆越满却仍不满足
scene: 商场大促，推着购物车的人一件接一件往里塞，轮子都快压弯了。An acquisitive shopper rarely leaves a sale empty-handed.
sceneCN: 这里 acquisitive 是「渴望获取的」（第 1 个义项：强烈想要得到财物）；句意为一个贪得的购物者很少空手离开促销现场。

pos.zh: 形容词：贪得的；渴望获取的；占有欲强的

collocations.zh: 以获取财物为目的的犯罪

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词基础，义为「获得；取得」
由动词加 -ition 构成，义为「获得；收购」
由本词加 -ness 构成，义为「贪得；占有欲」
由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「贪求地；以获取的方式」

senses.title: Eager to acquire possessions
senses.definition: strongly wanting to obtain money, goods or property, often more than one needs
senses.definitionCN: 强烈想要得到金钱、物品或财产，往往超出实际需要
senses.example: The acquisitive heir bought three houses in a single year.
senses.exampleCN: 这位贪得的继承人一年之内买了三栋房子。
senses.why: Acquire means to obtain, and the -itive suffix marks a tendency, so the word describes a person pulled toward obtaining things.
senses.whyCN: acquire 意为「获得」，-itive 后缀标记一种倾向，所以这个词描述被「获取」牵着走的人。

senses.title: Materialistic, as a society
senses.definition: describing a culture or group that measures worth by what people own and buy
senses.definitionCN: 形容以人们拥有和购买的东西衡量价值的文化或群体
senses.example: Critics call the city acquisitive because every advertisement promises more.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者称这座城市物质至上，因为每则广告都在许诺更多。
senses.why: When the tendency spreads from one person to a whole culture, the word becomes a judgement about shared values.
senses.whyCN: 当这种倾向从一个人扩散到整个文化，这个词就变成对共同价值观的判断。

senses.title: Acquisitive crime
senses.titleCN: 以获取财物为目的的犯罪
senses.definition: in law, a crime committed mainly to obtain money or property, such as theft or fraud
senses.definitionCN: 法律上指主要为取得金钱或财产而实施的犯罪，如盗窃或诈骗
senses.example: The report separates acquisitive crime from violent crime.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告把以获取财物为目的的犯罪与暴力犯罪区分开来。
senses.why: Law needs a label for motive rather than act, and acquisitive names the gain-seeking motive precisely.
senses.whyCN: 法律需要按动机而不是按行为分类的标签，acquisitive 恰好点明「为获取」的动机。

senses.title: An acquisitive instinct
senses.definition: in psychology, a natural drive to collect, hold and accumulate resources
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中指收集、持有并积累资源的天然驱动力
senses.example: Some researchers treat the acquisitive instinct as a survival mechanism.
senses.exampleCN: 一些研究者把获取本能视为一种生存机制。
senses.why: If obtaining is a tendency, it can also be described as an inborn drive rather than a moral failing.
senses.whyCN: 如果获取是一种倾向，它也可以被描述为先天的驱动力，而不只是道德缺陷。

senses.title: Growth by buying other companies
senses.definition: in business, describing a strategy of growing by purchasing other firms rather than by internal expansion
senses.definitionCN: 商业中指靠收购其他公司而非内部扩张来增长的策略
senses.example: The acquisitive group added two rivals to its portfolio last quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 这个靠收购扩张的集团上季度把两个竞争对手收入旗下。
senses.why: Companies acquire other companies, so the same word moves from personal greed to corporate strategy.
senses.whyCN: 公司收购其他公司，于是同一个词从个人贪欲转到了企业战略。

senses.title: Eager to acquire knowledge
senses.definition: strongly eager to learn, collect information or master new skills
senses.definitionCN: 强烈渴望学习、收集信息或掌握新技能
senses.example: Her acquisitive mind read every book on the reading list twice.
senses.exampleCN: 她那渴求知识的头脑把书单上的每本书读了两遍。
senses.why: The object of acquisition can be knowledge instead of goods, which turns a suspect trait into a praised one.
senses.whyCN: 获取的对象可以是知识而不是财物，这就把原本可疑的特质变成被称赞的品质。

senses.title: Hoarding behaviour in animals
senses.definition: in animal behaviour, the tendency to gather and store food beyond immediate need
senses.definitionCN: 动物行为学中指收集并储存超过当下所需食物的倾向
senses.example: The acquisitive squirrel filled every hollow in the old wall.
senses.exampleCN: 那只贪囤的松鼠把旧墙里的每个洞都塞满了。
senses.why: Hoarding is acquisition without immediate use, so the human word extends naturally to animal caching.
senses.whyCN: 囤积是获取而不立即使用，所以这个人类词汇自然延伸到动物的贮藏行为。

senses.title: Grasping attachment
senses.definition: in ethical and Buddhist contexts, the mental habit of grasping at things as if they could be permanently owned
senses.definitionCN: 在伦理与佛教语境中，指把事物当作可永久拥有而紧紧抓取的心理习惯
senses.example: Meditation aims to soften the acquisitive grip of the mind.
senses.exampleCN: 冥想旨在软化内心那种贪著不放的抓取。
senses.why: The word's image of a hand that will not let go becomes a moral and spiritual diagnosis of attachment.
senses.whyCN: 这个词「不肯松手」的画面，变成对执著的心理与精神诊断。

intro.en: Acquisitive comes from the Latin verb for seeking and obtaining, with a suffix that turns an action into a tendency.
intro.cn: acquisitive 来自拉丁语表示「寻求并获得」的动词，加上把动作变成倾向的后缀。

items.en: Quaerere meant to seek, ask or search for; it is also the source of question and inquiry.
items.cn: quaerere 意为「寻找、询问」，也是 question 与 inquiry 的来源。

items.en: Ad plus quaerere formed acquirere, to get in addition, to obtain; the past participle is acquisitus.
items.cn: ad 与 quaerere 构成 acquirere，意为「额外取得、获得」；其过去分词是 acquisitus。

items.en: Acquisitivus was used in medieval Latin for having the quality of acquiring.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语用 acquisitivus 表示「具有获取性质的」。

items.en: Old French acquerre carried the verb into English, while the adjective came later by a learned route.
items.cn: 古法语 acquerre 把动词带入英语，形容词则更晚经由学术路径进入。

items.en: The adjective acquisitive is recorded in English in the sixteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 形容词 acquisitive 在十六世纪见于英语记录，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The word split into a moral sense, a legal sense and a business sense, all keeping the idea of obtaining.
items.cn: 这个词分化出道德义、法律义与商业义，但都保留「获取」的核心理念。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the acquire family; the near-meaning group gathers words for greed and desire with different intensity.
note.cn: 形近组收 acquire 词族；近义组收表达贪欲与渴望的词，强度各不相同。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to obtain or gain something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「获得、取得」，是本词的核心动词。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of obtaining something, or a company that has been bought.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「获得」或「被收购的公司」。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being acquisitive.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「贪得、占有欲」，是本词的名词形式。

entries.definition: Necessary or required; it looks close to acquisitive but comes from requirere, to require.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「必需的」，拼写接近 acquisitive，但词源是 requirere「要求」，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Eager to ask questions and learn; it shares the quaerere root but aims at knowledge, not property.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「好奇好问的」，共享 quaerere 词根，但指向知识而非财产。

entries.definition: Wanting far more than one needs, especially food or money; harsher and more emotional than acquisitive.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「贪婪的」，尤指食物或金钱，语气比 acquisitive 更重、更情绪化。

entries.definition: Valuing possessions and money above other things; a judgement about values, not a drive.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「物质主义的」，是对价值观的判断，而不是描述驱动力。

entries.definition: Strongly desiring what belongs to someone else; formal and slightly old-fashioned.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「觊觎的」，强烈想得到别人所有之物，语气正式且略旧。

entries.definition: Wanting to keep and control what one already has; it points inward to existing belongings.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「占有欲强的」，强调守住已拥有之物，方向向内。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real quaerere root and the legal and business phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的 quaerere 词根，以及这个词实际出现的法律与商业搭配。

normal.en: Acquire is ad plus quaerere, to seek toward oneself; acquisitive is the habit of doing so.
normal.cn: acquire 是 ad 加 quaerere「朝自己寻求」，acquisitive 就是不断这样做的习惯。

normal.en: Inquisitive shares the same seeking root but seeks answers instead of things.
normal.cn: inquisitive 共享同一个「寻求」词根，但它寻求的是答案而不是东西。

normal.en: Acquisitive crime is a legal label for crimes committed for gain.
normal.cn: acquisitive crime 是法律标签，指为获利而实施的犯罪。

normal.en: An acquisitive company grows by buying other companies.
normal.cn: acquisitive 公司靠收购其他公司来扩张。

normal.en: The -itive ending, as in competitive, marks a tendency rather than a single act.
normal.cn: 与 competitive 相同的 -itive 结尾，标记的是一种倾向而非一次动作。

abstract.en: Picture a shopping cart that fills faster than it moves, because the hand keeps reaching.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆购物车装货比前进还快，因为那只手一直在伸。

abstract.en: The same hand can reach for books instead of goods, and then the word becomes praise.
abstract.cn: 同一只手也可以伸向书本而不是货物，这时这个词就变成赞美。

abstract.en: Acquisitive desire is a grip: the problem is not the object but the fingers that will not open.
abstract.cn: 贪求是一种抓握：问题不在物件，而在那几根不肯松开的手指。

examples.en: An acquisitive culture may confuse having more with being better.
examples.cn: 一个贪求的文化可能把「拥有更多」误当成「变得更好」。

examples.en: The court treated the theft as an acquisitive crime rather than a violent one.
examples.cn: 法院把这起盗窃视为以获取财物为目的的犯罪，而非暴力犯罪。

examples.en: Her acquisitive reading habits made her an expert in three fields.
examples.cn: 她渴求知识的阅读习惯使她成为三个领域的专家。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿奎西提夫」——阿奎的手总往货架上伸，拿到手还要再拿：贪得的

root: 拉丁语 quaerere「寻找、询问」加 ad- 构成 acquirere「取得」，过去分词 acquisitus；中世纪拉丁语 acquisitivus 加 -itive「倾向」构成形容词。quaerere 也是 question 与 inquiry 的词源。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all follow one reaching hand: it takes possessions, shapes a whole culture, supplies a legal motive, becomes an instinct, buys companies, reaches for knowledge, hoards food, or will not let go in a spiritual sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都跟着同一只伸出的手：它抓财物、塑造整个文化、构成法律动机、变成本能、收购公司、伸向知识、囤积食物，或在精神层面不肯松手。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand keeps reaching for more while the cart is already full.
core.cn: 核心意象：购物车已经装满，那只手仍在不断伸向更多。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the basic sense of wanting to obtain goods.
branches.cn: 个人线：想要获得财物的基本义。

branches.en: THE VALUE: the same drive becomes a judgement about society or a spiritual attachment.
branches.cn: 价值线：同一驱动力变成对社会价值的判断，或精神上的执著。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: law and business each give the drive an institutional name.
branches.cn: 制度线：法律与商业分别给这股驱动力一个制度化的名字。

branches.en: THE INSTINCT: psychology and animal behaviour describe it as inborn hoarding.
branches.cn: 本能线：心理学与动物行为学把它描述为先天的囤积倾向。

branches.en: THE MIND: when the object is knowledge, the tendency turns into a virtue.
branches.cn: 心智线：当对象是知识时，这种倾向就转为美德。

intro.en: Acquisitive joins a Latin prefix, a Latin seeking root and an adjective suffix that marks tendency.
intro.cn: acquisitive 由拉丁语前缀、表示「寻求」的拉丁词根，以及标记倾向的形容词后缀组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin quaerere, acquirere and acquisitus are recorded; the adjective acquisitivus is medieval.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 quaerere、acquirere、acquisitus 均有记录；形容词 acquisitivus 属中世纪拉丁语。

items.example: It directs seeking toward the self.
It is the seeking root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这一词族的「寻求」词根。

items.example: It joins the prefix and the root.
items.exampleCN: 它把前缀与词根结合起来。
它构成 inquisitive，指向寻求答案。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ition 构成，义为「获得；收购」
由本词加 -ness 构成，义为「贪得；占有欲」
由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「贪求地」
本词的动词基础，义为「获得；取得」

definition_zh: 恐高症；高处恐惧
definition_en: an unusually strong and persistent fear of heights
core_image: 站在高台边缘，双腿发软，不敢往下看
scene: 观景台的玻璃地板前，游客扶着栏杆，迟迟不敢迈出一步。Her acrophobia kept her far from the glass edge.
sceneCN: 这里 acrophobia 是「恐高症」（第 1 个义项：对高处的强烈恐惧）；句意为她的恐高症让她远离玻璃边缘。

pos.zh: 名词：恐高症；高处恐惧

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ic 构成，义为「恐高的；恐高症相关的」
由本词去掉 -ia 加 -e 构成，义为「恐高者」
由形容词加 -ally 构成，义为「以恐高的方式」

senses.title: Fear of heights
senses.definition: a strong fear of being high up or of looking down from a height
senses.definitionCN: 对身处高处或从高处向下看的强烈恐惧
senses.example: His acrophobia made the ferris wheel a trial rather than a treat.
senses.exampleCN: 他的恐高症让摩天轮成了一种折磨而不是享受。
senses.why: Greek akron means top or height and phobos means fear, so the word is literally height-fear.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 akron 意为「顶端、高处」，phobos 意为「恐惧」，所以这个词字面上就是「高处恐惧」。

senses.title: A clinical phobia
senses.definition: a diagnosable anxiety disorder in which the fear is out of proportion and leads to avoidance
senses.definitionCN: 一种可诊断的焦虑障碍，恐惧程度与危险不相称并导致回避
senses.example: The clinic treats acrophobia as an anxiety disorder, not a character flaw.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所把恐高症当作焦虑障碍来治疗，而不是性格缺陷。
senses.why: Once the fear is persistent and disabling, it moves from a common feeling into a clinical category.
senses.whyCN: 当恐惧持续并造成功能损害，它就从常见感受变成临床分类。

senses.title: Physical symptoms
senses.definition: the bodily reactions triggered by heights, such as dizziness, sweating, trembling and a racing heart
senses.definitionCN: 高处引发的身体反应，如头晕、出汗、发抖与心跳加快
senses.example: Her acrophobia showed itself as sweating palms before she even reached the balcony.
senses.exampleCN: 她的恐高症在她还没走到阳台时就表现为掌心出汗。
senses.why: Fear prepares the body to escape, so the word also names the physical alarm that comes with the height.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧让身体准备逃离，所以这个词也指随高处而来的身体警报。

senses.title: Trigger situations
senses.definition: places and activities that set off the fear, such as balconies, ladders, bridges and tall buildings
senses.definitionCN: 引发恐惧的场所与活动，如阳台、梯子、桥和高楼
senses.example: Glass floors are a common trigger for acrophobia.
senses.exampleCN: 玻璃地板是恐高症常见的触发情境。
senses.why: The fear needs a cue, and modern buildings supply many cues that make the height visible.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧需要一个线索，而现代建筑提供了许多让高度变得可见的线索。

senses.title: Exposure therapy
senses.definition: treatment that reduces the fear by gradual, controlled contact with heights
senses.definitionCN: 通过逐步、受控地接触高处来减轻恐惧的治疗
senses.example: The therapist used exposure therapy for her acrophobia, starting with a low step.
senses.exampleCN: 治疗师用暴露疗法治疗她的恐高症，从一级矮台阶开始。
senses.why: If avoidance keeps the fear alive, controlled approach is the treatment, so the word appears in therapy contexts.
senses.whyCN: 如果回避让恐惧持续，受控的接近就是治疗，所以这个词出现在治疗语境中。

senses.title: Virtual reality treatment
senses.definition: therapy that uses simulated heights in virtual reality to practise coping safely
senses.definitionCN: 利用虚拟现实中的模拟高处，在安全环境中练习应对的治疗
senses.example: The clinic offers acrophobia sessions in a virtual glass lift.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所在虚拟玻璃电梯里提供恐高症治疗课程。
senses.why: Simulation gives the height without the danger, which makes it a modern tool for the same old fear.
senses.whyCN: 模拟提供高度却不提供危险，于是它成了对付这种古老恐惧的现代工具。

senses.title: Distinction from vertigo
senses.definition: the difference between fear of heights and vertigo, which is a false sense of spinning
senses.definitionCN: 对高处的恐惧与眩晕的区别，后者是一种虚假的旋转感
senses.example: Acrophobia is about danger, while vertigo is about the room seeming to move.
senses.exampleCN: 恐高症关乎危险，而眩晕关乎房间似乎在移动。
senses.why: Two experiences can occur together, so clinical language keeps the fear and the spinning sensation separate.
senses.whyCN: 两种体验可能同时出现，所以临床语言把「恐惧」与「旋转感」分开命名。

senses.title: Everyday height anxiety
senses.definition: a mild, common unease around heights that does not amount to a disorder
senses.definitionCN: 在高处附近轻度而常见的紧张感，尚未达到障碍程度
senses.example: He calls it acrophobia, though he still climbs ladders when he must.
senses.exampleCN: 他称之为恐高症，尽管必要时他仍会爬梯子。
senses.why: People borrow the clinical word for ordinary unease, a common looseness in everyday speech.
senses.whyCN: 人们借临床词汇来形容普通的紧张感，这是日常语言中常见的宽松用法。

intro.en: Acrophobia is a Greek-derived compound made in modern medical English from words for height and fear.
intro.cn: acrophobia 是用希腊语「高处」与「恐惧」两词在现代医学英语中构成的复合词。

items.en: Akron meant the top, tip or highest point; it is also the source of acrobat and acropolis.
items.cn: akron 意为「顶端、尖端、最高点」，也是 acrobat 与 acropolis 的来源。

items.en: Phobos meant fear or panic and was also the name of a deity of fright.
items.cn: phobos 意为「恐惧、惊慌」，也是希腊神话中惊恐之神的名字。

items.en: The suffix -phobia formed words for abnormal fear in Greek medical writing.
items.cn: 后缀 -phobia 在希腊医学文献中构成表示异常恐惧的词。

items.en: Scientific Latin coined acrophobia from akron and -phobia; the exact first use is uncertain.
items.cn: 科学拉丁语用 akron 与 -phobia 造出 acrophobia，确切首次使用时间不确定。

items.en: The word entered English medical writing in the nineteenth century as phobias were being classified.
items.cn: 十九世纪恐惧症被分类时，这个词进入英语医学文献。

items.en: It now appears in everyday speech as well, often for mild unease rather than a diagnosis.
items.cn: 如今它也出现在日常口语中，常指轻度不适而非临床诊断。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other -phobia words built on Greek roots; the near-meaning group gathers balance and anxiety terms with different mechanisms.
note.cn: 形近组收其他以希腊词根构成的 -phobia 词；近义组收机制不同的平衡与焦虑类词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning afraid of heights or relating to acrophobia.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「恐高的」或「与恐高症相关的」。

entries.definition: A person who fears heights.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「恐高者」。

entries.definition: Fear of open or crowded places; it shares the -phobia suffix but a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「广场恐惧症」，共享 -phobia 后缀但词根不同。

entries.definition: Fear of enclosed spaces; a parallel formation with a different first element.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「幽闭恐惧症」，是替换首元素的平行构词。

entries.definition: A performer who moves high above the ground; it shares akron, height, but not phobos.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「杂技演员」，共享 akron「高处」词根，但不含 phobos。

entries.definition: A false sensation of spinning or movement; a balance symptom, not a fear.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「眩晕」，是虚假的旋转或移动感，属平衡症状而非恐惧。

entries.definition: The general emotion of danger; broad and not tied to heights.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「恐惧」，是一般危险情绪，范围宽泛且不限于高处。

entries.definition: A general state of worry; acrophobia is a focused, situation-specific form.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「焦虑」，是一般担忧状态；恐高症是聚焦于特定情境的形式。

entries.definition: A clinical phrase for discomfort at heights that may fall short of a full phobia.
entries.definitionCN: 名词短语，义为「高度不耐受」，指未达到完整恐惧症程度的高处不适。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real akron and phobos roots and the clinical phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的 akron 与 phobos 词根，以及这个词实际出现的临床搭配。

normal.en: Akron is the top or tip, so acro- words are about the highest point.
normal.cn: akron 是顶端或尖端，所以 acro- 开头的词都与最高点有关。

normal.en: Phobos is fear, the same element in agoraphobia and claustrophobia.
normal.cn: phobos 是恐惧，同一元素也出现在 agoraphobia 与 claustrophobia 中。

normal.en: Acrobat shares the height root but has no fear in it.
normal.cn: acrobat 共享「高处」词根，但其中没有「恐惧」。

normal.en: Acrophobia is a diagnosable anxiety disorder when the fear is persistent and disabling.
normal.cn: 当恐惧持续并造成功能损害时，acrophobia 是可诊断的焦虑障碍。

normal.en: Exposure therapy works by replacing avoidance with controlled approach.
normal.cn: 暴露疗法用受控接近取代回避，从而起作用。

abstract.en: Picture a glass floor: the eyes see solid surface, but the legs refuse to believe it.
abstract.cn: 想象一块玻璃地板：眼睛看见实心表面，双腿却拒绝相信。

abstract.en: The fear lives in the gap between the body and the drop, a gap the mind fills with falling.
abstract.cn: 恐惧住在身体与落差之间的缝隙里，而想象用「坠落」填满了这道缝隙。

abstract.en: Acrophobia is not the height itself but the story the body tells about the height.
abstract.cn: 恐高症不是高度本身，而是身体关于高度讲的那个故事。

examples.en: Acrophobia stopped her from taking the job on the twentieth floor.
examples.cn: 恐高症使她无法接受那份位于二十层的工作。

examples.en: The study found that virtual reality can reduce acrophobia in a few sessions.
examples.cn: 研究发现虚拟现实能在几次课程内减轻恐高症。

examples.en: He described his acrophobia as a sudden urge to step back from any edge.
examples.cn: 他把自己的恐高症描述为一种突然想从任何边缘退后的冲动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克罗福比阿」——阿克罗站在高处，福气比阿谁少，腿却先软：恐高症

root: 希腊语 akron「顶端、高处」与 phobos「恐惧」组合，经科学拉丁语构成 acrophobia；后缀 -phobia 表示异常恐惧。akron 也是 acrobat 与 acropolis 的词根。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses move from the plain fear of heights to its clinical status, bodily symptoms, triggers, treatments, its difference from vertigo, and its loose everyday use.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从对高处的直接恐惧，延伸到临床地位、身体症状、触发情境、治疗方式、与眩晕的区别，以及日常的宽泛用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person stands at a glass edge, legs trembling, unable to look down.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在玻璃边缘，双腿发抖，不敢向下看。

branches.en: THE FEELING: from a plain fear of heights to mild everyday unease.
branches.cn: 感受线：从直接的高处恐惧到日常轻度不适。

branches.en: THE CLINIC: persistent fear becomes a diagnosis with bodily symptoms.
branches.cn: 临床线：持续的恐惧变成带有身体症状的诊断。

branches.en: THE CUE: balconies, ladders and glass floors make height visible.
branches.cn: 线索线：阳台、梯子与玻璃地板让高度变得可见。

branches.en: THE CURE: exposure and simulation teach the body a safer story.
branches.cn: 治疗线：暴露与模拟教给身体一个更安全的故事。

branches.en: THE BOUNDARY: fear of heights is kept distinct from the spinning of vertigo.
branches.cn: 边界线：把高处恐惧与眩晕的旋转感区分开。

intro.en: The word is two Greek elements plus a Greek-derived suffix, assembled in scientific Latin.
intro.cn: 这个词由两个希腊语元素加一个源自希腊语的后缀组成，在科学拉丁语中装配。

latinIntro.en: Greek akron and phobos are recorded; the compound acrophobia belongs to modern scientific Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 akron 与 phobos 均有记录；复合词 acrophobia 属现代科学拉丁语。

items.example: It forms acrophobia and many clinical terms.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 acrophobia 以及许多临床术语。

items.example: It is the fear element behind -phobia.
items.exampleCN: 它是 -phobia 背后的「恐惧」元素。

items.example: It is the height element behind acro-.
items.exampleCN: 它是 acro- 背后的「高处」元素。

items.example: It forms agoraphobia, a parallel phobia.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 agoraphobia，一种平行的恐惧症。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ic 构成，义为「恐高的」
由本词去掉 -ia 加 -e 构成，义为「恐高者」
由形容词加 -ally 构成，义为「以恐高的方式」

definition_zh: 实际上；事实上；竟然；其实（用于纠正或补充）
definition_en: in fact, in reality, or used to correct, soften or emphasize what has just been said
core_image: 一人指着地图，另一人翻出照片说「其实是这样」
scene: 会上大家都以为预算够用，财务却翻出一叠账单放在桌上。The budget was actually much smaller than we thought.
sceneCN: 这里 actually 是「实际上」（第 1 个义项：与以为的情况相反的事实）；句意为预算实际上比我们想的小得多。

pos.zh: 副词：实际上；事实上；竟然；其实

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 actus 加 -al 构成，义为「实际的；真实的」
由 actual 加 -ity 构成，义为「现实性；实际情况」
由 actual 加 -ize 构成，义为「使实现；使成为现实」
由动词加 -ation 构成，义为「实现；现实化」

senses.title: In fact, contrary to belief
senses.definition: used to state what is true when it differs from what was believed or assumed
senses.definitionCN: 用于说明真实情况与原先相信或假设的不同
senses.example: The train was actually early for once.
senses.exampleCN: 火车这次竟然真的早到了。
senses.why: Actual comes from actus, a doing; what is actual is what has really been done, so actually points to the done fact.
senses.whyCN: actual 来自 actus「所做之事」；实际的就是真正做成的，所以 actually 指向「已经发生的事实」。

senses.title: In practice, not in theory
senses.definition: used to contrast real practice with a plan, rule or theory
senses.definitionCN: 用于把真实做法与计划、规则或理论相对照
senses.example: The system looks simple but actually takes ten steps to use.
senses.exampleCN: 这个系统看着简单，实际操作却要十步。
senses.why: If actual means done, then actually can mark the point where theory meets the work of doing.
senses.whyCN: 如果 actual 意为「做成的」，那么 actually 就可以标记理论与实际动手相交的那一点。

senses.title: A correction marker
senses.definition: used at the start of a reply to correct something someone has just said
senses.definitionCN: 用于回答开头，纠正对方刚说过的话
senses.example: Actually, the meeting is on Tuesday, not Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 其实会议是星期二，不是星期一。
senses.why: The word interrupts the previous statement and replaces it with the done fact, which is why it so often opens a correction.
senses.whyCN: 这个词打断前一句话，用「已发生的事实」替换它，所以常出现在纠正的开头。

senses.title: A softener for disagreement
senses.definition: used to make a disagreement or refusal sound less direct and less rude
senses.definitionCN: 用于让不同意见或拒绝听起来不那么直接、不那么无礼
senses.example: Actually, I think we should wait a little longer.
senses.exampleCN: 其实我觉得我们应该再等等。
senses.why: Because the word claims reality rather than personal opposition, it lets a speaker disagree without attacking the other person.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词诉诸现实而不是个人对立，说话者可以表示不同意却不攻击对方。

senses.title: Expressing surprise
senses.definition: used to show surprise that something really happened or is really true
senses.definitionCN: 用于表达对某事真的发生或真的如此感到惊讶
senses.example: She actually finished the whole marathon in the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 她竟然在雨中跑完了整个马拉松。
senses.why: Saying that something actually happened stresses the gap between expectation and the surprising done fact.
senses.whyCN: 说某事 actually 发生，强调了预期与令人惊讶的既成事实之间的落差。

senses.title: Emphasizing a strong claim
senses.definition: used before a strong word to insist that the statement is literally true
senses.definitionCN: 用在语气强烈的词前，强调该说法字面上确实成立
senses.example: The task is actually impossible without more staff.
senses.exampleCN: 没有更多人手，这项任务实际上不可能完成。
senses.why: The word appeals to reality, so placing it before a strong claim makes the claim sound measured rather than exaggerated.
senses.whyCN: 这个词诉诸现实，把它放在强烈断言前，会让断言听起来是有根据的而非夸张。

senses.title: A conversational hedge
senses.definition: used as a mild filler to hold the floor or soften a statement while the speaker thinks
senses.definitionCN: 用作轻微填充词，在思考时占住话轮或软化说法
senses.example: Actually, let me check the figures before I answer.
senses.exampleCN: 其实，让我先查一下数字再回答。
senses.why: Once the word marks a turn toward the real facts, it becomes a handy pause before the speaker produces them.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词标记「转向真实情况」，它就成了一种方便的停顿，等说话者把事实拿出来。

senses.title: Existing in reality
senses.definition: used in philosophical or careful writing to mean existing in reality rather than only in thought
senses.definitionCN: 在哲学或严谨写作中表示在现实中存在，而不只存在于思想中
senses.example: The plan describes a world that does not actually exist.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划描述的是一个并不真实存在的世界。
senses.why: The oldest sense of actual is real or done, so actually can still carry the plain meaning of existing in reality.
senses.whyCN: actual 最古老的意思是「真实的、做成的」，所以 actually 仍可承载「在现实中存在」这一朴素含义。

intro.en: Actually is an adverb built on actual, a word that came through Old French from Latin actus, a doing.
intro.cn: actually 是建立在 actual 之上的副词；actual 经由古法语来自拉丁语 actus「所做之事」。

items.en: Agere meant to do, drive or act; its past participle actus gave the noun for a deed.
items.cn: agere 意为「做、驱动、行动」，其过去分词 actus 给出表示「行为」的名词。

items.en: Late Latin actualis meant pertaining to action or practice, as opposed to mere possibility.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 actualis 意为「与行动或实践有关的」，相对于仅仅是可能性。

items.en: Old French actual carried the word toward English with the sense of real or existing.
items.cn: 古法语 actual 把这个词带向英语，带有「真实的、存在的」含义。

items.en: The adjective actual is recorded in Middle English; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 形容词 actual 在中古英语中已有记录，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The adverb actually appears later, first stressing reality and later gaining its conversational correcting role.
items.cn: 副词 actually 更晚出现，先强调现实，后来又获得口语中的纠正功能。

items.en: In modern speech actually is one of the most common markers of correction, surprise and polite disagreement.
items.cn: 在现代口语中，actually 是表示纠正、惊讶与礼貌异议的最常见标记之一。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the actual family; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of reality and contrast with different force.
note.cn: 形近组收 actual 词族；近义组收表示现实与对照的副词，语气强弱不同。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning real or existing, as opposed to imagined.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「实际的、真实的」，与想象相对。

entries.definition: The noun for the state of being real or for real conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「现实性」或「实际情况」。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to make something real or carry it out.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使实现、把……变为现实」。

entries.definition: A deed or the process of doing; it shares the Latin agere root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「行动、行为」，共享拉丁语 agere 词根。

entries.definition: A single deed or the process of doing something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「行为、行动」，与词根直接相关。

entries.definition: In fact or truly; more emotional and more common in surprise questions.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「真的、确实」，情绪更强，也更常用于惊讶疑问。

entries.definition: A phrase adding or correcting a fact; more formal and more explicit than actually.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「事实上」，用于补充或纠正事实，比 actually 更正式、更明确。

entries.definition: In the exact sense of the words; it stresses wording, while actually stresses reality.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「字面上、确实地」，强调字面意义，而 actually 强调现实。

entries.definition: At the present time; a time word, not a truth word.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「目前、当前」，是时间词而非真伪词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real actus root and the conversational positions the word actually occupies.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的 actus 词根，以及这个词实际占据的会话位置。

normal.en: Actual comes from actus, a deed, so actually means in the done fact.
normal.cn: actual 来自 actus「行为」，所以 actually 意为「在已完成的事实里」。

normal.en: Action, act and actual all trace back to the Latin verb agere, to do.
normal.cn: action、act、actual 都可追溯到拉丁语动词 agere「做」。

normal.en: Actually often opens a correction because it replaces a claim with the done fact.
normal.cn: actually 常用来开启纠正，因为它用一个既成事实替换原先说法。

normal.en: In British speech actually is a common way to soften disagreement.
normal.cn: 在英式口语中，actually 是缓和不同意见的常用方式。

normal.en: The word can also simply mean existing in reality, as in a plan that does not actually exist.
normal.cn: 这个词也可以只表示「在现实中存在」，如一个并不 actually 存在的计划。

abstract.en: Picture a map and a photograph side by side: the map is the claim, the photograph is the actual.
abstract.cn: 想象地图与照片并排：地图是说法，照片是实际。

abstract.en: Actually is a small lever that tilts the conversation from what we assumed to what was done.
abstract.cn: actually 是一根小杠杆，把对话从「我们以为什么」扳向「实际做了什么」。

abstract.en: The word does not shout; it simply puts the finished deed on the table.
abstract.cn: 这个词不大喊，它只是把已经完成的事情摆到桌上。

examples.en: The journey looks short on the map but actually takes five hours.
examples.cn: 这段路程在地图上看着短，实际却要五个小时。

examples.en: Actually, the shop closes at six, not seven.
examples.cn: 其实商店六点关门，不是七点。

examples.en: I was surprised that he actually apologized.
examples.cn: 我没想到他竟然真的道了歉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克戳阿利」——用手指戳着账本说：实际是这样

root: 拉丁语 agere「做、行动」的过去分词 actus 构成 actualis「与行动有关的」，经古法语进入英语为 actual；加 -ly 构成副词 actually。核心含义始终是「已做成的事实」。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all turn the conversation toward what is really done: a fact against belief, practice against theory, a correction, a soft disagreement, surprise, emphasis, a pause, or plain existence.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把对话转向「真正做成的事实」：与以为什么相反的事实、实践与理论之别、纠正、委婉异议、惊讶、强调、停顿，以及朴素的存在义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one person points at a map while another holds up a photograph of the real place.
core.cn: 核心意象：一人指着地图，另一人举着真实地点的照片。

branches.en: THE TRUTH: what is actual is what exists or has been done.
branches.cn: 真伪线：actual 就是存在或已做成的东西。

branches.en: THE PRACTICE: theory is tested by the work of doing.
branches.cn: 实践线：理论要由实际动手来检验。

branches.en: THE TURN: the word redirects a conversation, either correcting or softening.
branches.cn: 转折线：这个词把对话转向，或纠正或缓和。

branches.en: THE FORCE: surprise and emphasis both use the gap between expectation and fact.
branches.cn: 力度线：惊讶与强调都利用预期与事实之间的落差。

branches.en: THE PAUSE: the same marker can simply hold the floor while the speaker checks.
branches.cn: 停顿线：同一标记也可以只是占住话轮，让说话者核对。

intro.en: Actually is a Latin-root adjective turned into an adverb by a native English suffix.
intro.cn: actually 是一个拉丁词根形容词，靠英语本族后缀变成了副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin agere, actus and actualis are recorded; the English adverb is a later native formation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 agere、actus、actualis 均有记录；英语副词是更晚的本族构词。

items.example: It is the verb behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 它是整个词族背后的动词。

items.example: It is the direct source of actual.
items.exampleCN: 它是 actual 的直接来源。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 actualis 进入英语，义为「实际的；真实的」
由 actual 加 -ity 构成，义为「现实性；实际情况」
由 actual 加 -ize 构成，义为「使实现」
由动词加 -ation 构成，义为「实现；现实化」

definition_zh: 适应；改编；改写本；（生物）适应
definition_en: the process of adjusting to new conditions, or a version of a work changed for a new medium
core_image: 一件旧衣被改短，穿到了另一个身上
scene: 剧团把一本厚小说搬上舞台，台词删去大半，灯光也换了风格。The stage adaption cut the long novel into two hours.
sceneCN: 这里 adaption 是「改编」（第 1 个义项：把作品改成另一种表现形式）；句意为这次舞台改编把长篇小说压缩成两个小时。

pos.zh: 名词：适应；改编；改写本

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词基础，义为「适应；改编」
与本词同义的更常见拼写形式，义为「适应；改编」
由 adapt 加 -ive 构成，义为「适应性的」
由 adaptive 加 -ability 构成，义为「适应能力」
由 adapt 加 -er 构成，义为「改编者；适配器」

senses.title: The process of adjusting
senses.definition: the process of changing in order to fit new conditions or a new purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为适应新条件或新用途而作出改变的过程
senses.example: The adaption of the old team to the new software took a month.
senses.exampleCN: 旧团队适应新软件花了一个月。
senses.why: Adapt means to fit, and -ion names the process, so adaption is the act of making something fit.
senses.whyCN: adapt 意为「使适合」，-ion 表示过程，所以 adaption 就是「使某物适合」的行为。

senses.title: A changed version
senses.definition: a product that has been modified to suit a new use or audience
senses.definitionCN: 为适应新用途或新受众而修改过的成品
senses.example: The children's adaption keeps the story but simplifies the language.
senses.exampleCN: 儿童版改写保留了故事，但简化了语言。
senses.why: Once the process is finished, the word can name the finished thing, just as a translation names its result.
senses.whyCN: 过程完成后，这个词可以指完成的成品，就像 translation 也指译出的作品。

senses.title: Biological adaptation
senses.definition: an inherited feature or change that helps an organism survive in its environment
senses.definitionCN: 帮助生物在环境中存活的遗传特征或变化
senses.example: The thick coat is an adaption to the long northern winter.
senses.exampleCN: 厚皮毛是对漫长北方冬季的一种适应。
senses.why: Living things fit themselves to their surroundings over generations, so the general idea becomes a biological term.
senses.whyCN: 生物在世代之间使自己适合环境，于是这个一般概念成了生物学术语。

senses.title: A film or stage version
senses.definition: a play, film or television version of a novel, story or other source work
senses.definitionCN: 把小说、故事或其他原作改成戏剧、电影或电视的版本
senses.example: The film adaption moved the ending to a different city.
senses.exampleCN: 电影改编把结局搬到了另一座城市。
senses.why: A book must be fitted to a new medium, and the result is called by the same word as the fitting process.
senses.whyCN: 一本书必须被改造以适合新媒介，成品与改造过程共用同一个词。

senses.title: Sensory adaptation
senses.definition: the weakening of a sensation after continuous exposure to the same stimulus
senses.definitionCN: 持续接触同一刺激后感觉逐渐减弱的现象
senses.example: Sensory adaption explains why the noise seems quieter after an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 感觉适应解释了为什么一小时后噪声似乎变小了。
senses.why: The senses adjust their sensitivity to a steady input, which is a literal fitting of the body to conditions.
senses.whyCN: 感官会调整对稳定输入的敏感度，这是身体对条件的字面适应。

senses.title: Social or cultural adjustment
senses.definition: the process of adjusting to a new culture, community or way of life
senses.definitionCN: 适应新文化、新社区或新生活方式的过程
senses.example: Her adaption to the new school was helped by a host family.
senses.exampleCN: 寄宿家庭帮助她适应了新学校。
senses.why: People fit themselves to social surroundings, so the word covers the human version of fitting.
senses.whyCN: 人会让自己适合社会环境，所以这个词也涵盖「人适应环境」这一版本。

senses.title: A technical modification
senses.definition: a change made to a machine, system or device so it can serve a new purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为使机器、系统或装置服务新用途而作的改动
senses.example: The adaption of the pump for salt water required new seals.
senses.exampleCN: 把水泵改装用于海水需要新的密封件。
senses.why: Tools are fitted to new jobs by physical change, which is the engineering branch of the same idea.
senses.whyCN: 工具通过物理改动去适合新任务，这是同一理念在工程上的分支。

senses.title: A spelling variant
senses.definition: the less common spelling of adaptation, used chiefly in some technical and older texts
senses.definitionCN: adaptation 的较少见拼写，主要用于部分技术文献与较早文本
senses.example: Some journals use adaption, though adaptation is now the standard form.
senses.exampleCN: 有些期刊使用 adaption，不过 adaptation 现在是标准形式。
senses.why: English often drops or keeps a Latin suffix by fashion, so the shorter form survives as a recognized variant.
senses.whyCN: 英语常按习惯省略或保留拉丁后缀，于是较短的形式作为被承认的变体留存下来。

intro.en: Adaption and adaptation both rest on the Latin verb adaptare, to fit; the shorter form is an English variant.
intro.cn: adaption 与 adaptation 都建立在拉丁语动词 adaptare「使适合」之上；较短的形式是英语变体。

items.en: Aptus meant fit, suited or fastened; it is also the source of apt and aptitude.
items.cn: aptus 意为「合适的、贴合的」，也是 apt 与 aptitude 的来源。

items.en: Ad plus aptare formed adaptare, to fit something to something else.
items.cn: ad 与 aptare 构成 adaptare，意为「使某物适合另一物」。

items.en: The verb adapt entered English through French; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 动词 adapt 经由法语进入英语，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Adaptation was formed with -ation; the shorter adaption appeared as a variant spelling.
items.cn: adaptation 由 -ation 构成；较短的 adaption 作为变体拼写出现。

items.en: With evolutionary theory, adaptation became a central biological term for features that fit an environment.
items.cn: 随着进化论，adaptation 成为生物学的核心术语，指适合环境的特征。

items.en: Adaptation dominates standard usage, while adaption survives in technical and older writing.
items.cn: 现代标准用法以 adaptation 为主，adaption 则留存于技术文献与较早写作中。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the adapt family and its spelling double; the near-meaning group gathers words for change and versions of works.
note.cn: 形近组收 adapt 词族及其拼写双体；近义组收表示改变与作品版本的词。

entries.definition: The standard spelling of the same word, more common in modern English.
