entries.definitionCN: 同一词的标准化拼写，在现代英语中更常见。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to adjust or change to fit.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「适应；改编」，是本词的核心动词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning able to adjust to new conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「适应性的、能调整的」。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being able to adapt.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「适应能力」。

entries.definition: A person who adapts a work, or a device that connects different fittings.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「改编者」或「适配器」。

entries.definition: A change made to fit a new situation; often smaller and more mechanical than adaption.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「调整」，常指较小、更机械的改动，范围比 adaption 窄。

entries.definition: A form of something that differs from other forms; it does not imply fitting to a new medium.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「版本」，指与其他形式不同的形态，不必然暗示媒介转换。

entries.definition: A work moved from one language to another; a sibling idea to adaptation across media.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「翻译」，指把作品从一种语言搬到另一种语言，与跨媒介改编同类。

entries.definition: A partial change; broader than adaption and with no goal of fitting.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「修改」，指部分改动，范围更宽且不必然以适合为目的。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real aptus root and the media and biology phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的 aptus 词根，以及这个词实际出现的媒介与生物搭配。

normal.en: Adaptare is ad plus aptare, to fit one thing to another.
normal.cn: adaptare 是 ad 加 aptare，意为「把一物配到另一物上」。

normal.en: Apt and aptitude share the same fit root, so adapt is about fitting, not random change.
normal.cn: apt 与 aptitude 共享同一个「合适」词根，所以 adapt 讲的是贴合，不是随意改变。

normal.en: Adaptation is the standard spelling; adaption is the shorter variant.
normal.cn: adaptation 是标准拼写；adaption 是较短的变体。

normal.en: A film adaption fits a book to the screen.
normal.cn: film adaption 是把书「配到」银幕上。

normal.en: A biological adaption fits an organism to its habitat.
normal.cn: biological adaption 是让生物适合其栖息地。

abstract.en: Picture an old coat with the sleeves shortened, then handed to a smaller wearer.
abstract.cn: 想象一件旧外套被改短袖子，然后递给个子更小的人穿。

abstract.en: Adaption is not copying and not destroying: it keeps the material and changes the fit.
abstract.cn: 改编既不是复制也不是毁掉：它保留材料，只改变贴合方式。

abstract.en: A story moving from page to stage is the same coat worn in a different room.
abstract.cn: 故事从书页搬到舞台，就像同一件外套穿进另一间屋子。

examples.en: The radio adaption of the novel kept the narrator but cut two characters.
examples.cn: 这部小说的广播改编保留了叙述者，却删掉了两个人物。

examples.en: Her adaption to city life was slow but complete.
examples.cn: 她对城市生活的适应虽慢却彻底。

examples.en: The plant's adaption to dry soil is visible in its narrow leaves.
examples.cn: 这种植物对干燥土壤的适应体现在狭窄的叶片上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿达普申」——阿达把旧衣改一改，套到新身上：适应、改编

root: 拉丁语 aptus「合适的」派生动词 aptare，加 ad- 成 adaptare「使适合」；英语 adapt 加 -ation 成 adaptation，较短的 adaption 是其变体拼写。词根 aptus 的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all describe fitting one thing to another: a process, a finished version, a species to its habitat, a book to a screen, senses to a stimulus, a person to a culture, a machine to a job, and a spelling to fashion.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述「把一物配到另一物上」：过程、成品、物种与栖息地、书与银幕、感官与刺激、人与文化、机器与任务，以及拼写与习惯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coat is shortened at the sleeves and given to a smaller wearer.
core.cn: 核心意象：外套袖子被改短，交给个子更小的穿者。

branches.en: THE PROCESS: people, cultures and machines adjust to new conditions.
branches.cn: 过程线：人、文化与机器适应新条件。

branches.en: THE VERSION: a finished work or product made to fit a new medium.
branches.cn: 版本线：为适合新媒介而完成的成品。

branches.en: THE BODY: biology and the senses fit organisms to their surroundings.
branches.cn: 身体线：生物学与感官让生物适合环境。

branches.en: THE SPELLING: the shorter form survives beside the standard one.
branches.cn: 拼写线：较短形式与标准形式并存。

branches.en: THE NAME: process and product share one word, as in translation.
branches.cn: 命名线：过程与成品共用一个词，正如 translation。

intro.en: Adaption is a Latin verb turned into a process noun by an English suffix; a shorter suffix produced the variant.
intro.cn: adaption 是拉丁动词经英语后缀变成过程名词；较短的后缀造就了这个变体。

latinIntro.en: Latin aptus, aptare and adaptare are recorded; adaption itself is an English formation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 aptus、aptare、adaptare 均有记录；adaption 本身是英语构词。

items.example: It directs fitting toward a purpose.
items.exampleCN: 它把「贴合」指向某个用途。

items.example: It is the fit root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这一词族的「合适」词根。

items.example: It turns the adjective into an action.

items.meaning: to fit one thing to another
items.example: It is the direct source of adapt.
items.exampleCN: 它是 adapt 的直接来源。

latinEntries.meaning: to fit one thing to another

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词基础，义为「适应；改编」
与本词同义的更常见拼写
由 adapt 加 -ive 构成，义为「适应性的」
由 adaptive 加 -ability 构成，义为「适应能力」
由 adapt 加 -er 构成，义为「改编者；适配器」

definition_zh: 加法；增加；添加物；扩建部分；附加的人或物
definition_en: the act of adding something, the thing added, or the mathematical operation of combining numbers
core_image: 往已经装满的篮子里再放进一颗果子
scene: 孩子把最后几颗樱桃放进篮子，篮沿明显往下沉了一截。The addition of one more box made the stack unstable.
sceneCN: 这里 addition 是「添加」（第 1 个义项：把东西加进去的行为）；句意为再增加一个箱子使整摞变得不稳。

pos.zh: 名词：加法；增加；添加物；扩建部分

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词基础，义为「加；增加」
由本词加 -al 构成，义为「额外的；附加的」
由 additional 加 -ly 构成，义为「此外；另外」
由动词加 -itive 构成，义为「添加剂；添加物」
由动词加 -ed 构成，义为「附加的；额外的」

senses.title: The act of adding something
senses.definition: the act of putting something new into a group, mixture or place
senses.definitionCN: 把新东西放入一组事物、混合物或某处中的行为
senses.example: The addition of a little salt improved the soup.
senses.exampleCN: 加了一点盐使汤的味道更好。
senses.why: Latin addere meant to give to, and -tion names the act, so addition is literally the giving of one thing to another.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 addere 意为「给到……之上」，-tion 表示动作，所以 addition 字面上就是「把一物给到另一物」。

senses.title: The thing that is added
senses.definition: a new item, person or feature that is added to an existing set
senses.definitionCN: 被加入现有集合的新物品、人物或特征
senses.example: The new wing is a welcome addition to the museum.
senses.exampleCN: 新侧翼是博物馆一项受人欢迎的新增部分。
senses.why: When the act is finished, the word shifts from the action to the object that now sits inside the group.
senses.whyCN: 动作完成后，这个词从「动作」转到「现在留在群体里的那个物件」。

senses.title: The mathematical operation
senses.definition: the arithmetic operation of combining two or more numbers into a sum
senses.definitionCN: 把两个或多个数合成一个总和的算术运算
senses.example: Children learn addition before they learn multiplication.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们先学加法，再学乘法。
senses.why: Numbers are treated as objects put together, so the everyday act of adding becomes the name of a basic operation.
senses.whyCN: 数字被当作可以放在一起的物件，于是日常「添加」的动作成了基本运算的名称。

senses.title: The phrase in addition
senses.definition: used to introduce an extra point or item beyond what has already been said
senses.definitionCN: 用于在已说内容之外再引入一个额外要点或项目
senses.example: In addition, the hotel offers free breakfast.
senses.exampleCN: 此外，酒店还提供免费早餐。
senses.why: The literal act of adding becomes a discourse signal: another item is being put on the list.
senses.whyCN: 字面上的「添加」变成了话语信号：又有一样东西被放到清单上。

senses.title: Addition reaction in chemistry
senses.definition: a reaction in which two molecules combine into one without losing any atoms
senses.definitionCN: 两个分子结合成一个而不丢失任何原子的反应
senses.example: The addition of hydrogen to the double bond produced a saturated compound.
senses.exampleCN: 氢加成到双键上，生成了饱和化合物。
senses.why: Atoms are added across a bond, and nothing is removed, which is why chemistry borrows the plain word.
senses.whyCN: 原子被加到键的两端，且没有原子被移除，所以化学直接借用了这个普通词。

senses.title: An extension to a building
senses.definition: a new part built onto an existing structure
senses.definitionCN: 在现有建筑上新建的部分
senses.example: The kitchen addition doubled the size of the house.
senses.exampleCN: 厨房扩建使房子面积翻了一倍。
senses.why: A building grows by having new parts put onto it, so the physical act of adding becomes an architectural noun.
senses.whyCN: 建筑通过把新部分加上去而变大，所以物理上的「添加」成了建筑名词。

senses.title: A new member of a family
senses.definition: a baby or new family member welcomed into a household
senses.definitionCN: 被迎入家庭的新生儿或新成员
senses.example: The family announced the addition of a second child.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人宣布添了第二个孩子。
senses.why: People, like objects, can be spoken of as added to a group, which gives the word a warm domestic use.
senses.whyCN: 人也可以像物件一样被说成「加入某个群体」，这使这个词有了温暖的家庭用法。

senses.title: A new player on a team
senses.definition: a player or staff member newly added to a sports team or organization
senses.definitionCN: 新加入运动队或组织的新球员或工作人员
senses.example: The coach praised the latest addition to the squad.
senses.exampleCN: 教练称赞了队里最新加入的成员。
senses.why: Teams are lists of people, and a new name put on the list is an addition in the same literal sense.
senses.whyCN: 队伍是一份人的名单，新名字被写上去，就是同一字面意义上的 addition。

intro.en: Addition comes from the Latin verb for giving something to something else, with the noun suffix naming the act.
intro.cn: addition 来自拉丁语表示「把某物给到另一物」的动词，名词后缀表示这一动作。

items.en: Dare meant to give; it is also the source of data, something given, and of donate.
items.cn: dare 意为「给」，也是 data「给出的东西」与 donate 的来源。

items.en: Ad plus dare formed addere, to give to, to add; the past participle is additus.
items.cn: ad 与 dare 构成 addere，意为「给到……之上、添加」；过去分词是 additus。

items.en: Additio named the act of adding and also an addition made to a thing.
items.cn: additio 表示「添加的行为」，也表示「加到某物上的新增部分」。

items.en: Old French addition carried the word into English with both the act and the thing senses.
items.cn: 古法语 addition 把这个词带入英语，动作义与物件义同时进入。

items.en: The word is recorded in Middle English; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词在中古英语中已有记录，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Mathematics fixed addition as the name of one operation, while everyday speech kept the general sense of putting something new in.
items.cn: 数学把 addition 固定为一种运算的名称，日常口语则保留「放入新东西」的一般含义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the add family; the near-meaning group gathers words for extra things and joining with different scope.
note.cn: 形近组收 add 词族；近义组收表示额外事物与结合的词，范围各不相同。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to put something together with something else.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「加、添加」，是本词的核心动词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning extra or supplementary.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「额外的、附加的」。

entries.definition: A substance added, especially to food or fuel.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「添加剂」，尤指加入食物或燃料中的物质。

entries.definition: A number that is added to another in an addition; the word keeps the same giving root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「加数」，指加法中被加到另一个数上的数；保留同一「给」词根。

entries.definition: Something added at the end of a book or document; a Latin gerundive from the same verb.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「补遗、附录」，指书末或文末追加的内容；同一动词的拉丁语动形词。

entries.definition: A rise in amount or size; it stresses the result, while addition stresses the act.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「增加、增长」，强调结果，而 addition 强调动作。

entries.definition: Something added to complete or improve a whole; often an extra part rather than a new member.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「补充物」，指为使整体完整或更好而添加的东西。

entries.definition: An added part that continues something existing, especially a building.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「延伸部分」，指延续现有事物的新增部分，尤指建筑。

entries.definition: An additional item beyond what is usual or expected.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「额外的东西」，指超出通常或预期的事物。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real dare root and the everyday phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的 dare 词根，以及这个词实际出现的日常搭配。

normal.en: Addere is ad plus dare, to give to; an addition is something given onto a group.
normal.cn: addere 是 ad 加 dare「给到」，addition 就是加到群体之上的一样东西。

normal.en: Data and donate share the dare root, because both involve giving.
normal.cn: data 与 donate 共享 dare 词根，因为两者都涉及「给」。

normal.en: In addition is a phrase that puts one more item on the list.
normal.cn: in addition 这个短语就是把又一项放到清单上。

normal.en: An addition reaction adds atoms without removing any.
normal.cn: addition reaction 是加上原子而不移除任何原子的反应。

normal.en: A kitchen addition is a new part built onto an existing house.
normal.cn: kitchen addition 是加建在现有房子上的新部分。

abstract.en: Picture a basket already full, and one more fruit goes on top.
abstract.cn: 想象一只已经装满的篮子，顶上又放了一颗果子。

abstract.en: The word always looks at the edge of a group: what is outside is being brought inside.
abstract.cn: 这个词总是盯着群体的边缘：外面的东西正被带进里面。

abstract.en: Addition is a small door in the side of a set, through which a new member walks.
abstract.cn: addition 是集合侧面的一扇小门，新成员从那里走进来。

examples.en: The addition of two more lanes eased the morning traffic.
examples.cn: 增加两条车道缓解了早高峰的拥堵。

examples.en: In addition to the fee, students must pay for materials.
examples.cn: 除学费之外，学生还需支付材料费。

examples.en: She checked her addition twice before signing the sheet.
examples.cn: 她在表格上签字前把加法核对了两遍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿迪申」——阿迪往篮子里又塞了一颗，篮子更沉：增加

root: 拉丁语 dare「给」加 ad- 构成 addere「给到、添加」，名词 additio 表示添加行为与新增物；经古法语 addition 进入英语。dare 也是 data 与 donate 的词源。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all place something new at the edge of an existing group: an act, an object, a sum, a discourse phrase, a chemical bond, a building wing, a family member, or a team player.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把新东西放到现有群体的边缘：动作、物件、总和、话语短语、化学键、建筑侧翼、家庭成员，或队里的新球员。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a full basket receives one more fruit on top.
core.cn: 核心意象：装满的篮子顶上又接到一颗果子。

branches.en: THE ACT: the basic deed of putting something in.
branches.cn: 动作线：把东西放进去的基本行为。

branches.en: THE THING: the added object can be a feature, a building wing, a child or a player.
branches.cn: 物件线：被添加之物可以是功能、建筑侧翼、孩子或球员。

branches.en: THE NUMBER: arithmetic turns the act into a named operation.
branches.cn: 数字线：算术把这一动作变成有名称的运算。

branches.en: THE DISCOURSE: the same act becomes a phrase that adds a point.
branches.cn: 话语线：同一动作变成添加要点的短语。

branches.en: THE MOLECULE: chemistry adds atoms across a bond.
branches.cn: 分子线：化学把原子加到键上。

intro.en: Addition is a Latin verb plus a Latin noun suffix, with the same giving root behind several English words.
intro.cn: addition 是拉丁动词加拉丁名词后缀，同一个「给」词根还支撑着若干英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin dare, addere and additio are recorded; the English noun came through Old French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dare、addere、additio 均有记录；英语名词经由古法语进入。

items.example: It directs the giving toward a recipient.
It is the giving root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这一词族的「给」词根。

items.example: It joins the prefix and the root.
It survives in English as a book term.
items.exampleCN: 它作为书籍术语保留在英语中。

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词基础，义为「加；增加」
由本词加 -al 构成，义为「额外的；附加的」
由 additional 加 -ly 构成，义为「此外」
由动词加 -itive 构成，义为「添加剂」

definition_zh: 添加剂；添加物；附加的；加法的
definition_en: a substance added to something in small amounts, or an adjective meaning added or relating to addition
core_image: 一小勺粉末倒进面糊，颜色立刻变了
scene: 厨房里，面点师往面粉中倒进一小袋白色粉末，面团很快变得松软。The label lists every additive used in the bread.
sceneCN: 这里 additive 是「添加剂」（第 1 个义项：少量加入以改变性质的东西）；句意为标签列出了面包中使用的每一种添加剂。

pos.zh: 名词：添加剂；添加物
形容词：附加的；加法的

derivatives.zh: 本词对应的动词，义为「加；添加」
由动词加 -ition 构成，义为「加法；添加」
由 addition 加 -al 构成，义为「附加的；额外的」

senses.title: A food additive
senses.definition: a substance added to food in small amounts to preserve it, colour it or improve its texture
senses.definitionCN: 为防腐、着色或改善质地而少量加入食物中的物质
senses.example: The label warns that the drink contains several additives.
senses.exampleCN: 标签提示这种饮料含有多种添加剂。
senses.why: Addere means to give to, and -itive marks a thing that is added, so a food additive is literally a giving-into the recipe.
senses.whyCN: addere 意为「给到」，-itive 标记「被加入之物」，所以食品添加剂字面上就是「加进配方里的东西」。

senses.title: A fuel or oil additive
senses.definition: a chemical added to fuel or lubricant to improve performance or protect the engine
senses.definitionCN: 加入燃油或润滑油以改善性能或保护发动机的化学物质
senses.example: The mechanic recommended a cleaning additive for the old engine.
senses.exampleCN: 机修工建议给旧发动机加一种清洁添加剂。
senses.why: The same structure appears in machines: a small added substance changes how the main fluid behaves.
senses.whyCN: 同样的结构出现在机器里：少量加入的物质改变了主要液体的表现。

senses.title: Additive manufacturing
senses.definition: a production method that builds objects layer by layer instead of cutting material away
senses.definitionCN: 逐层堆积材料而非切削去除材料的制造方法
senses.example: Additive manufacturing made the custom part in a single day.
senses.exampleCN: 增材制造在一天之内就做出了这个定制零件。
senses.why: Material is added layer upon layer, so the adjective describes the direction of the build rather than a chemical ingredient.
senses.whyCN: 材料一层一层被加上去，所以这个形容词描述建造的方向，而不是化学配料。

senses.title: Additive colour
senses.definition: colour produced by mixing light, where added colours make the result brighter
senses.definitionCN: 通过混合光产生的颜色，加入颜色会使结果更亮
senses.example: Screens use additive colour, mixing red, green and blue light.
senses.exampleCN: 屏幕使用加色，把红、绿、蓝光混合起来。
senses.why: Light adds to light, unlike paint, so the adjective marks a mixing system that increases brightness.
senses.whyCN: 光加到光上，与颜料不同，所以这个形容词标记一种会增加亮度的混合系统。

senses.title: An additive effect
senses.definition: a combined effect equal to the simple sum of separate effects
senses.definitionCN: 等于各单独效应简单相加之和的合并效应
senses.example: The two drugs have an additive effect on blood pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 这两种药物对血压有叠加效应。
senses.why: If effects simply add, one plus one stays two, which is the mathematical meaning of the word applied to causes.
senses.whyCN: 如果效应只是相加，一加一仍等于二，这就是这个词的数学含义被用到原因上。

senses.title: Additive identity and inverse
senses.titleCN: 加法单位元与加法逆元
senses.definition: in mathematics, the number zero that leaves a sum unchanged, or the number that cancels another
senses.definitionCN: 数学中使总和不变的零，或使另一个数被抵消的数
senses.example: Zero is the additive identity because adding it changes nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 零是加法单位元，因为加上它不改变任何东西。
senses.why: These terms describe the rules of addition itself, so the adjective names a role inside the operation.
senses.whyCN: 这些术语描述加法本身的规则，所以这个形容词命名的是运算中的一种角色。

senses.title: Added as an extra
senses.definition: describing something added on top of what already exists, often as an extra charge or feature
senses.definitionCN: 形容在现有事物之上追加的东西，常指额外收费或额外功能
senses.example: The additive charge appears on a separate line of the bill.
senses.exampleCN: 附加费用出现在账单的单独一行。
senses.why: The adjective can simply describe anything extra, keeping the plain sense of something given in addition.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词也可以单纯描述任何额外之物，保留「额外加上」的朴素含义。

senses.title: An additive statistical model
senses.definition: a model in which the total value is the sum of separate components
senses.definitionCN: 总量等于各独立成分之和的模型
senses.example: The additive model assumes that each factor contributes independently.
senses.exampleCN: 加性模型假定每个因素独立地作出贡献。
senses.why: Statistics borrows the arithmetic sense to say that parts combine only by adding, with no interaction.
senses.whyCN: 统计学借用算术含义，表示各部分只通过相加结合，没有交互作用。

intro.en: Additive is the adjective and noun form of the Latin verb addere, to give to; English built it with -ive.
intro.cn: additive 是拉丁动词 addere「给到」的形容词与名词形式；英语用 -ive 构成。

items.en: Dare meant to give, and it also lies behind data and donate.
items.cn: dare 意为「给」，也藏在 data 与 donate 背后。

items.en: Ad plus dare formed addere, to give to or add; its participle additus means added.
items.cn: ad 与 dare 构成 addere「给到、添加」，其分词 additus 意为「被添加的」。

items.en: Late Latin additivus meant pertaining to adding; the exact first record is uncertain.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 additivus 意为「与添加有关的」，确切最早记录不确定。

items.en: The English adjective appears in scientific writing, first in mathematics and chemistry.
items.cn: 英语形容词先出现在科学写作中，最早用于数学与化学。

items.en: As industrial food and fuel grew, the noun additive became common for substances added in small amounts.
items.cn: 随着工业食品与燃料发展，名词 additive 常指少量加入的物质。

items.en: Additive manufacturing extended the word to a method of building objects layer by layer.
items.cn: additive manufacturing 把这个词扩展到逐层堆积物体的制造方法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers add-family words; the near-meaning group gathers substances and descriptors of extra things.
note.cn: 形近组收 add 词族；近义组收添加物与描述额外之物的词。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of adding or the thing added.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「添加的行为」或「被添加之物」。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to put something in addition.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「加、添加」。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning extra or supplementary.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「额外的、补充的」。

entries.definition: A thing added at the end of a text; a different noun from the same verb.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「补遗」，指文末追加之物，是同一动词的另一名词形式。

entries.definition: A number added to another; a precise cousin of additive in arithmetic.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「加数」，是 additive 在算术中的近亲。

entries.definition: One of the substances that make up a mixture; a normal component rather than a small extra.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成分、配料」，是混合物的正常组成部分，而非少量额外添加物。

entries.definition: A specific kind of additive that prevents food from spoiling.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「防腐剂」，是添加剂中专门防止食物变质的一类。

entries.definition: Something added to improve or complete, often a nutrient or extra dose.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「补充剂、补充物」，指为改善或补全而添加的东西。

entries.definition: An additional item beyond what is usual; broader and less technical.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「额外的」，范围更宽、技术性更弱。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real addere root and the food, fuel and manufacturing phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的 addere 词根，以及这个词实际出现的食品、燃料与制造搭配。

normal.en: Additive is the thing given into a mixture, from addere, to give to.
normal.cn: additive 是被加进混合物里的东西，来自 addere「给到」。

normal.en: A food additive is listed on the label because it was added in small amounts.
normal.cn: 食品添加剂会列在标签上，因为它是少量加入的。

normal.en: Additive manufacturing adds layers; subtractive manufacturing removes material.
normal.cn: additive manufacturing 是增加层，subtractive manufacturing 则是去除材料。

normal.en: Additive colour mixes light, so more colour means more brightness.
normal.cn: additive colour 混合的是光，所以颜色越多亮度越高。

normal.en: An additive effect is exactly the sum of the separate effects.
normal.cn: additive effect 正好等于各单独效应之和。

abstract.en: Picture a small spoon of white powder falling into a bowl of dough and changing it.
abstract.cn: 想象一小勺白色粉末落进一碗面团，把面团改变了。

abstract.en: The word is about small amounts with large effects: a little added, a lot changed.
abstract.cn: 这个词讲的是少量却有大效果：加了一点，变了很多。

abstract.en: Additive is the opposite of taking away; it builds by putting something on.
abstract.cn: additive 与「拿掉」相反；它靠往上加东西来建造。

examples.en: The bakery removed all artificial additives from its bread.
examples.cn: 这家面包店从面包中去掉了所有人工添加剂。

examples.en: Additive manufacturing can produce shapes that traditional cutting cannot.
examples.cn: 增材制造能做出传统切削做不到的形状。

examples.en: The additive effect of the two treatments was stronger than either alone.
examples.cn: 两种疗法的叠加效应比单独使用任何一种都强。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿迪提夫」——阿迪提着一小袋粉末，往面里一倒：添加剂

root: 拉丁语 dare「给」加 ad- 构成 addere「给到、添加」，分词 additus；晚期拉丁语 additivus 表示「与添加有关的」，英语据此构成 additive。dare 也是 data 与 donate 的词源。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all describe something added: a food or fuel substance, a layer-wise production method, a light-mixing system, a summed effect, a mathematical role, an extra charge, or a statistical assumption.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述「被加入之物」：食品或燃料物质、逐层制造方法、混光系统、相加效应、数学角色、额外收费，或统计假设。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small spoon of powder falls into dough and changes its texture.
core.cn: 核心意象：一小勺粉末落进面团，改变了它的质地。

branches.en: THE SUBSTANCE: food and fuel receive a small chemical that changes behaviour.
branches.cn: 物质线：食品与燃料接受少量改变其表现的化学物质。

branches.en: THE METHOD: layers or light are added rather than removed.
branches.cn: 方法线：增加的是层或光，而不是被去除。

branches.en: THE SUM: effects or model components combine by simple addition.
branches.cn: 总和线：效应或模型成分通过简单相加结合。

branches.en: THE RULE: mathematics names roles inside the operation.
branches.cn: 规则线：数学为运算内部的各种角色命名。

branches.en: THE EXTRA: the plain sense of something added on top.
branches.cn: 额外线：某物被追加在上面的朴素含义。

intro.en: Additive is a Latin participle stem plus an English adjective suffix; the noun use grew from the adjective.
intro.cn: additive 是拉丁分词词干加英语形容词后缀；名词用法从形容词生长出来。

latinIntro.en: Latin dare, addere and additivus are recorded; the English form follows the Latin adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dare、addere、additivus 均有记录；英语形式沿用拉丁形容词。

items.example: It supplies the stem for the adjective.
It contrasts with additive in subtractive manufacturing.
items.exampleCN: 它在 subtractive manufacturing 中与 additive 形成对照。

derivatives.zh: 本词对应的动词，义为「加；添加」
由动词加 -ition 构成，义为「加法；添加」
由 addition 加 -al 构成，义为「附加的；额外的」

definition_zh: 收件人；收信人；被称呼者；（语言学）受话人
definition_en: the person to whom a letter, message or speech is addressed
core_image: 信封正面写着「致某某」的那一行
scene: 邮局柜台上，信封正面只写了一个名字，寄件人地址落在背面。The addressee had moved, so the letter came back.
sceneCN: 这里 addressee 是「收件人」（第 1 个义项：信件寄送的对象）；句意为收件人已经搬走，所以信被退回。

pos.zh: 名词：收件人；收信人；受话人

derivatives.zh: 本词的基础词，义为「地址；致辞」，也可作动词「称呼；寄送」
由 address 加 -er 构成，义为「发件人；说话人」
由动词加 -ed 构成，义为「已写明地址的；被称呼的」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「称呼；地址填写」

senses.title: The recipient of a letter
senses.definition: the person named on an envelope or letter as the intended receiver
senses.definitionCN: 在信封或信件上被写明的预期接收者
senses.example: The addressee of the letter was a retired teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 这封信的收件人是一位退休教师。
senses.why: Address means to direct toward, and -ee marks the person receiving the action, so the addressee is the one the letter is directed to.
senses.whyCN: address 意为「指向」，-ee 标记接受动作的人，所以 addressee 就是信被指向的那个人。

senses.title: The recipient of an email
senses.definition: the person whose address appears in the recipient field of an electronic message
senses.definitionCN: 电子邮件的收件人栏中出现的那个地址所对应的人
senses.example: She checked the addressee before hitting send.
senses.exampleCN: 她在按下发送前核对了收件人。
senses.why: Electronic mail keeps the envelope structure, so the old word moves directly into the new medium.
senses.whyCN: 电子邮件保留了信封结构，于是这个旧词直接搬进了新媒介。

senses.title: The person spoken to
senses.definition: in linguistics, the person or group a speaker is directing an utterance to
senses.definitionCN: 语言学中说话者把话语指向的那个人或群体
senses.example: In the dialogue, the addressee answers only once.
senses.exampleCN: 在这段对话中，受话人只回答了一次。
senses.why: Speech also has a direction, so the receiver of an utterance is named by the same -ee pattern.
senses.whyCN: 言语也有方向，所以话语的接收者用同一个 -ee 模式来命名。

senses.title: The person a formal speech is meant for
senses.definition: the individual or audience for whom a formal speech or dedication is intended
senses.definitionCN: 正式演讲或献词所针对的个人或听众
senses.example: The dedication named the addressee as his late mentor.
senses.exampleCN: 献词把受献者指名为他已故的导师。
senses.why: A dedication directs words toward one person, which is the ceremonial version of addressing.
senses.whyCN: 献词把文字指向某一个人，这是「致意」的仪式版本。

senses.title: The recipient of a legal notice
senses.definition: the party to whom a formal legal notice or summons is directed
senses.definitionCN: 正式法律通知或传票所指向的当事方
senses.example: The court required proof that the addressee had received the notice.
senses.exampleCN: 法院要求证明该接收人已收到通知。
senses.why: Law depends on knowing exactly who received a document, so the word becomes a precise procedural label.
senses.whyCN: 法律要求确切知道是谁收到了文件，所以这个词成了精确的程序标签。

senses.title: The recipient of a parcel
senses.definition: the person to whom a package or delivery is sent
senses.definitionCN: 包裹或投递物被送往的那个人
senses.example: The courier asked the addressee to sign beside the box.
senses.exampleCN: 快递员请收件人在箱子旁签字。
senses.why: Parcels repeat the postal model, so the same word covers any delivered object.
senses.whyCN: 包裹重复了邮政模式，所以同一个词涵盖任何被投递的物件。

senses.title: The receiver in a communication model
senses.definition: in communication theory, the endpoint that receives and interprets a message
senses.definitionCN: 传播理论中接收并解释信息的终点
senses.example: The model labels the sender and the addressee at opposite ends of the arrow.
senses.exampleCN: 这个模型把发送者与接收者标在箭头的两端。
senses.why: Once communication is drawn as a channel, the old postal roles become abstract positions in a diagram.
senses.whyCN: 一旦传播被画成一条通道，古老的邮政角色就变成图表中的抽象位置。

senses.title: The intended audience of a work
senses.definition: the reader, viewer or listener a text or artwork is designed to reach
senses.definitionCN: 文本或艺术作品设计上要抵达的读者、观众或听众
senses.example: The novelist wrote with a young addressee in mind.
senses.exampleCN: 这位小说家写作时心里装着年轻的受众。
senses.why: Art also directs itself toward someone, so the word extends from mail to the imagined receiver of a work.
senses.whyCN: 艺术也把自己指向某个人，于是这个词从邮件延伸到作品的想象接收者。

intro.en: Addressee is address plus the French-derived -ee suffix that marks the receiver of an action.
intro.cn: addressee 是 address 加上源自法语的 -ee 后缀，后者标记动作的接受者。

items.en: Directus meant straight or direct, the past participle of dirigere, to set in a line.
items.cn: directus 意为「直的、直接的」，是 dirigere「排成一线」的过去分词。

items.en: A verb *directiare, to make straight, is reconstructed as the source of the French family.
items.cn: 重构动词 *directiare「使变直」被认为是法语词族的来源。

items.en: Old French adresser meant to straighten, prepare or direct something toward a person.
items.cn: 古法语 adresser 意为「弄直、准备、把某物指向某人」。

items.en: English address is recorded in the fifteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 address 在十五世纪已有记录，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The suffix -ee comes from the French past-participle ending used for the recipient of an action.
items.cn: 后缀 -ee 来自法语过去分词词尾，用于表示动作的接受者。

items.en: Addressee extended from letters to email, law, parcels, linguistics and the audience of a work.
items.cn: addressee 从信件扩展到电子邮件、法律、包裹、语言学以及作品的受众。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers address-family words and other -ee nouns; the near-meaning group gathers receivers and audiences.
note.cn: 形近组收 address 词族与其他 -ee 名词；近义组收接收者与受众类词。

entries.definition: The noun or verb meaning location details or to direct words toward someone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「地址」或「向某人致辞、寄送」。

entries.definition: The sender or speaker, the counterpart of the addressee.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「发件人、说话人」，是收件人的对应角色。

entries.definition: A person employed; it shares the -ee pattern for the receiver of an action.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「雇员」，共享 -ee 模式，表示动作的接受者。

entries.definition: The person to whom money is paid, formed on the same -ee model.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「收款人」，按同一 -ee 模式构成。

entries.definition: A person who has escaped; another -ee noun for the person affected.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「逃脱者」，也是表示受影响者的 -ee 名词。

entries.definition: A person who receives something; broader than addressee and common for awards and messages.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「接受者」，范围比 addressee 宽，常用于奖项与信息。

entries.definition: A person or device that receives; also used of phones and radios.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「接收者、接收器」，也用于电话与无线电。

entries.definition: The group listening or watching; collective rather than a single named person.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「观众、听众」，是集体而非单个被指名的人。

entries.definition: The person who sends; the opposite role to the addressee.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「发送者」，与收件人角色相反。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real -ee receiver suffix and the postal and linguistic phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的 -ee 接受者后缀，以及这个词实际出现的邮政与语言搭配。

normal.en: The -ee ending marks the receiver, as in employee and payee.
normal.cn: -ee 结尾标记接受者，如 employee 与 payee。

normal.en: Address means to direct toward, so the addressee is the one being directed to.
normal.cn: address 意为「指向」，所以 addressee 就是被指向的那个人。

normal.en: The sender and the addressee sit at opposite ends of the same arrow.
normal.cn: 发送者与收件人坐在同一支箭头的两端。

normal.en: Email kept the envelope, so it kept the word addressee.
normal.cn: 电子邮件保留了信封，也就保留了这个词。

normal.en: In law, proof of the addressee matters because delivery must be shown.
normal.cn: 在法律上，收件人身份很重要，因为必须证明已经送达。

abstract.en: Picture an envelope with one clean name on the front and everything else on the back.
abstract.cn: 想象一只信封，正面只有一个干净的名字，其余都写在背面。

abstract.en: The addressee is the person the arrow lands on, not the hand that shot it.
abstract.cn: 收件人是箭头落下处的那个人，而不是放箭的手。

abstract.en: Every message has a doorway, and the addressee is the room on the other side.
abstract.cn: 每条信息都有一扇门，收件人就是门另一边的房间。

examples.en: Please write the addressee's full name on the envelope.
examples.cn: 请在信封上写全收件人的姓名。

examples.en: The email was sent to the wrong addressee by mistake.
examples.cn: 这封邮件被误发给了错误的收件人。

examples.en: In the transcript, the addressee never speaks.
examples.cn: 在逐字稿中，受话人始终没有开口。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德瑞西」——阿德在信封正面写下收信人的名字：收件人

root: 拉丁语 dirigere「排成一线」的过去分词 directus「直的」经俗拉丁语 *directiare 与古法语 adresser 进入英语为 address；再加源自法语过去分词词尾的 -ee「动作接受者」构成 addressee。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all name the person an arrow of communication lands on: a letter reader, email recipient, spoken-to listener, dedication target, legal party, parcel receiver, model endpoint, or intended audience.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在命名「传播之箭落下的那个人」：读信人、邮件收件人、被说话的对象、献词目标、法律当事方、包裹接收者、模型终点，或预期受众。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an envelope with one name written cleanly on the front.
core.cn: 核心意象：信封正面干净地写着一个名字。

branches.en: THE POST: letters, email and parcels all name a receiver.
branches.cn: 邮政线：信件、邮件与包裹都指定一位接收者。

branches.en: THE VOICE: speech and dedication direct words toward a listener.
branches.cn: 声音线：演讲与献词把话语指向听者。

branches.en: THE LAW: procedure needs to know exactly who received the notice.
branches.cn: 法律线：程序需要确切知道是谁收到了通知。

branches.en: THE MODEL: communication theory turns the role into a diagram position.
branches.cn: 模型线：传播理论把这个角色变成图表中的位置。

branches.en: THE WORK: a text or artwork imagines the one it is written for.
branches.cn: 作品线：文本或艺术作品想象它所写给的对象。

intro.en: Addressee is an English noun plus a French-derived suffix that consistently marks the receiver of an action.
intro.cn: addressee 是英语名词加一个源自法语的后缀，该后缀稳定地标记动作的接受者。

latinIntro.en: Latin dirigere and directus are recorded; the -ee suffix reached English through French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dirigere 与 directus 均有记录；-ee 后缀经法语进入英语。

items.example: It directs the action toward someone.
It is the source of address.

items.meaning: to direct words or mail to someone
items.example: It is the base of this word.
It forms readdress, to address again.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 readdress，义为「再次处理地址或再次致辞」。

latinEntries.meaning: to set in a line, direct

derivatives.zh: 本词的基础词，义为「地址；致辞」
由 address 加 -er 构成，义为「发件人；说话人」
由动词加 -ed 构成，义为「已写明地址的」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「称呼；地址填写」

definition_zh: 拥护者；信徒；黏附的；附着物
definition_en: a supporter of a cause, person or belief, or something that sticks firmly to a surface
core_image: 标签紧紧贴在玻璃上，怎么撕都撕不下来
scene: 新贴的标签粘在瓶身上，冲洗几次也没有脱落。The adherent refused to abandon the movement.
sceneCN: 这里 adherent 是「拥护者」（第 1 个义项：坚定支持某项事业的人）；句意为这名拥护者拒绝放弃这项运动。

pos.zh: 名词：拥护者；信徒；附着物
形容词：黏附的；附着的

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词基础，义为「黏附；坚持」
由动词加 -ence 构成，义为「黏附；坚持；遵奉」
由拉丁分词加 -ion 构成，义为「黏附；附着力」
由动词加 -ive 构成，义为「黏合剂；胶带」

senses.title: A supporter of a cause
senses.definition: a person who supports a movement, leader or idea and remains loyal to it
senses.definitionCN: 支持某项运动、某位领袖或某种理念并保持忠诚的人
senses.example: The movement gained adherents in every large city.
senses.exampleCN: 这场运动在每座大城市都赢得了拥护者。
senses.why: Adhere means to stick to, and a supporter sticks to a cause, so the physical image becomes a political one.
senses.whyCN: adhere 意为「黏住」，支持者会「黏」在一项事业上，于是物理画面变成了政治画面。

senses.title: A follower of a religion
senses.definition: a person who follows a particular faith, teacher or religious tradition
senses.definitionCN: 追随某一信仰、导师或宗教传统的人
senses.example: Adherents of the tradition gather there each spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这一传统的信徒每年春天在那里聚会。
senses.why: Faith is something a person holds fast to, so the word for sticking becomes the word for religious belonging.
senses.whyCN: 信仰是人紧紧抓住的东西，所以表示「黏附」的词变成了表示宗教归属的词。

senses.title: Sticking firmly to a surface
senses.definition: describing a layer or substance that remains firmly attached to a surface
senses.definitionCN: 形容某层物质牢固附着在表面上
senses.example: The adherent film survived repeated washing.
senses.exampleCN: 这层附着膜经受了反复冲洗。
senses.why: The literal physical sense is the root image: two surfaces held together by contact.
senses.whyCN: 字面上的物理义是根本画面：两个表面靠接触被粘在一起。

senses.title: Adherent cells in biology
senses.definition: cells that attach to the surface of a culture vessel in order to grow
senses.definitionCN: 为生长而附着在培养容器表面的细胞
senses.example: The lab studies adherent cells that need a surface to spread.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室研究需要表面才能铺展的贴壁细胞。
senses.why: Cells that must stick to a dish are literally adherent, so biology borrows the everyday adjective.
senses.whyCN: 必须粘在培养皿上的细胞字面上就是「附着的」，所以生物学借用了这个日常形容词。

senses.title: A strict follower of rules
senses.definition: a person who keeps closely to a rule, principle or doctrine
senses.definitionCN: 紧密遵循某项规则、原则或教义的人
senses.example: He is an adherent of the old method and will not change.
senses.exampleCN: 他是旧方法的坚定遵循者，不愿改变。
senses.why: To adhere to a rule is to stay attached to it, which produces the sense of strict loyalty.
senses.whyCN: adhere to a rule 就是「黏在规则上」，于是产生了严格忠诚的含义。

senses.title: A political loyalist
senses.definition: a person who remains loyal to a party or political leader through difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 在困难时期仍忠于某政党或政治领袖的人
senses.example: The senator's adherents defended him after the scandal.
senses.exampleCN: 丑闻之后，这位参议员的追随者仍为他辩护。
senses.why: Politics tests loyalty, so the sticking image is used for those who do not peel away.
senses.whyCN: 政治考验忠诚，所以「黏住」的画面被用来指那些没有脱落的人。

senses.title: Attached by adhesion
senses.definition: in engineering, describing parts joined by molecular attraction rather than by bolts
senses.definitionCN: 工程中指靠分子吸引力而非螺栓连接的部件
senses.example: The adherent joint failed when the surface was wet.
senses.exampleCN: 表面潮湿时，这个黏附连接失效了。
senses.why: Engineering needs a word for contact-based joining, and adherent supplies it directly.
senses.whyCN: 工程需要为「靠接触连接」命名，adherent 正好直接提供这个词。

senses.title: An attached layer in materials
senses.definition: a thin layer that stays bonded to a substrate, as in coatings or films
senses.definitionCN: 保持在基底上的薄层，如涂层或薄膜
senses.example: The adherent layer protects the metal beneath.
senses.exampleCN: 这层附着层保护下面的金属。
senses.why: Coating work speaks of layers that must not peel, which extends the physical sense to materials science.
senses.whyCN: 涂装工艺讲的是不能剥落的层，这把物理义延伸到材料科学。

intro.en: Adherent comes from the Latin verb for sticking to something, and its two senses grew from one physical image.
intro.cn: adherent 来自拉丁语表示「黏在……上」的动词，它的两个义项都从同一个物理画面长出。

items.en: Haerere meant to stick, cling or remain fixed; its deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: haerere 意为「黏住、附着、固定不动」，其更早来源不确定。

items.en: Ad plus haerere formed adhaerere, to stick to or cleave to something.
items.cn: ad 与 haerere 构成 adhaerere，意为「黏到、附着于某物」。

items.en: The present participle adhaerens meant sticking to, and it is the direct source of the English word.
items.cn: 现在分词 adhaerens 意为「黏着的」，是英语词的直接来源。

items.en: Old French adherent carried the word into English with both the physical and the loyal senses.
items.cn: 古法语 adherent 把这个词带入英语，物理义与忠诚义同时进入。

items.en: The word is recorded in Middle English; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词在中古英语中已有记录，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Science added the technical senses for cells, joints and coatings, all keeping the idea of staying attached.
items.cn: 科学增加了细胞、接头与涂层等技术义项，但都保留「保持附着」的理念。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the adhere family; the near-meaning group gathers supporters and sticky terms with different focus.
note.cn: 形近组收 adhere 词族；近义组收支持者与黏性词，侧重点不同。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to stick to a surface or to follow a rule closely.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「黏附」或「坚持遵循」。

entries.definition: The noun for sticking to something or following a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「黏附」或「遵循」。

entries.definition: The physical force by which surfaces stay attached.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「黏附、附着力」，指表面保持贴合的力量。

entries.definition: A substance that sticks things together, such as glue or tape.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「黏合剂、胶带」或「黏性的」。

entries.definition: Logically connected; it comes from cohaerere, to stick together, so it shares the sticking root with adherent.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「连贯的」，来自 cohaerere「粘在一起」，与 adherent 共享「黏住」词根。

entries.definition: A person who helps or backs a cause; broader than adherent and less tied to loyalty.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「支持者」，范围比 adherent 宽，与忠诚的绑定较弱。

entries.definition: A person who follows a leader or idea; it stresses following, not sticking.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「追随者」，强调「跟随」而不是「黏附」。

entries.definition: A devoted follower of a teacher, especially religious; more personal and more formal.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「门徒」，尤指宗教导师的忠实追随者，更个人化也更正式。

entries.definition: An enthusiastic follower of a person, activity or faith.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「热衷者、信徒」，指对某人、某活动或某信仰充满热情的人。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real haerere root and the political, religious and laboratory phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的 haerere 词根，以及这个词实际出现的政治、宗教与实验室搭配。

normal.en: Adhaerere is ad plus haerere, to stick to; an adherent is one who sticks.
normal.cn: adhaerere 是 ad 加 haerere「黏住」，adherent 就是黏住的人。

normal.en: Adhesion is the physical force; adherence is the act or habit of sticking.
normal.cn: adhesion 是物理上的附着力；adherence 是黏附的动作或习惯。

normal.en: Adhesive is the substance that makes things stick.
normal.cn: adhesive 是让东西粘住的物质。

normal.en: An adherent of a policy keeps close to it and does not peel away.
normal.cn: 政策的 adherent 紧紧贴着它，不会脱落。

normal.en: Adherent cells must attach to a surface before they can grow.
normal.cn: 贴壁细胞必须先附着在表面才能生长。

abstract.en: Picture a label on glass that stays through every wash, still legible.
abstract.cn: 想象玻璃上的标签经过每次冲洗都还在，字迹仍然清楚。

abstract.en: The same stickiness explains loyalty: a person held to an idea by conviction.
abstract.cn: 同一种「黏性」解释了忠诚：一个人被信念粘在一个理念上。

abstract.en: An adherent does not stand near a cause; they are attached to it and move with it.
abstract.cn: 拥护者不是站在事业旁边，而是附着于它并随它移动。

examples.en: The reform attracted adherents from both parties.
examples.cn: 这项改革吸引了两党的拥护者。

examples.en: An adherent coating must survive heat and moisture.
examples.cn: 附着涂层必须经受高温与潮湿。

examples.en: The scientist cultured adherent cells on a treated dish.
examples.cn: 科学家在处理过的培养皿上培养贴壁细胞。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿希伦特」——阿希把标签贴在瓶上，冲了十次还粘着：拥护者、黏附的

root: 拉丁语 haerere「黏住」加 ad- 构成 adhaerere「黏附于」，现在分词 adhaerens 意为「黏着的」，经古法语进入英语为 adherent。haerere 的更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all describe something or someone that stays attached: to a cause, a faith, a surface, a dish, a rule, a party, a joint, or a substrate.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述「保持附着」的人或物：附着于事业、信仰、表面、培养皿、规则、政党、接头或基底。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a label stays stuck to glass and will not peel off.
core.cn: 核心意象：标签牢牢粘在玻璃上，怎么也不脱落。

branches.en: THE CAUSE: a person stays attached to a movement or party.
branches.cn: 事业线：一个人黏附于某项运动或政党。

branches.en: THE BELIEF: faith and rules are held fast, not lightly followed.
branches.cn: 信念线：信仰与规则被紧紧抓住，而非轻率跟随。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL BOND: a film, joint or layer remains attached.
branches.cn: 物理结合线：薄膜、接头或层保持附着。

branches.en: THE CELL: biology uses the same word for cells that must stick to a dish.
branches.cn: 细胞线：生物学用同一个词指必须贴住培养皿的细胞。

branches.en: THE PERSON: supporter and believer are both named by the sticking image.
branches.cn: 人物线：支持者与信徒都由「黏住」的画面来命名。

intro.en: Adherent is a Latin prefix plus a sticking root, shaped into a present participle and carried into English through French.
intro.cn: adherent 是拉丁语前缀加「黏住」词根，构成现在分词，再经法语进入英语。

latinIntro.en: Latin haerere, adhaerere and adhaerens are recorded; haesum supplies the participle stem behind adhesion.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 haerere、adhaerere、adhaerens 均有记录；haesum 提供 adhesion 背后的分词词干。

items.example: It directs the sticking toward a surface.
items.exampleCN: 它把「黏附」指向某个表面。

items.example: It is the sticking root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这一词族的「黏住」词根。

items.example: It joins the prefix and the root.

items.meaning: tending to, or a thing that

items.example: It forms cohesion, a related sticking-together term.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 cohesion，一个相关的「粘在一起」术语。

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词基础，义为「黏附；坚持」
由动词加 -ence 构成，义为「黏附；遵循」
由拉丁分词加 -ion 构成，义为「黏附；附着力」
由动词加 -ive 构成，义为「黏合剂」

definition_zh: 黏合剂；胶带；黏性的；有附着力的
definition_en: a substance that sticks things together, or an adjective describing something that sticks firmly
core_image: 两条彩纸被一段透明胶带牢牢粘住
scene: 手工课上，两条彩纸被一小段胶带牢牢粘住，两个孩子拉了半天也没拉开。The adhesive held the broken handle together for another year.
sceneCN: 这里 adhesive 是「黏合剂」（第 1 个义项：把物体粘在一起的材料）；句意为这种黏合剂让断裂的把手又撑了一年。

pos.zh: 名词：黏合剂；胶带；黏性材料
形容词：黏性的；有附着力的

derivatives.zh: 本词对应的动词，义为「黏附；坚持」
由拉丁分词加 -ion 构成，义为「黏附；附着力」
由动词加 -ence 构成，义为「黏附；遵循」
由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「以黏附方式地」
由本词加 -ness 构成，义为「黏性」

senses.title: A substance that sticks things together
senses.definition: a material such as glue or cement that bonds two surfaces into contact
senses.definitionCN: 如胶水或黏结剂那样把两个表面结合成接触状态的材料
senses.example: The carpenter used a strong adhesive instead of nails.
senses.exampleCN: 木匠用强力黏合剂代替钉子。
senses.why: Adhaerere means to stick to, and -ive marks a thing with that power, so the adhesive is the substance that makes sticking happen.
senses.whyCN: adhaerere 意为「黏附于」，-ive 标记具有该能力的物体，所以 adhesive 就是让「黏住」发生的物质。

senses.title: Adhesive tape
senses.definition: a thin strip of plastic or paper coated with glue, used to join or seal things
senses.definitionCN: 涂有胶层、用于连接或封口的塑料或纸条
senses.example: She sealed the box with a strip of adhesive tape.
senses.exampleCN: 她用一条胶带封住了箱子。
senses.why: Tape is adhesive in a portable form, so the adjective becomes a household noun for the whole product.
senses.whyCN: 胶带是「黏性」的便携形式，于是这个形容词成了整个日用品的名词。

senses.title: A medical adhesive
senses.definition: a safe bonding substance used to close wounds or attach medical devices to skin
senses.definitionCN: 用于闭合伤口或把医疗器械贴到皮肤上的安全黏合材料
senses.example: The surgeon used a medical adhesive instead of stitches.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生用医用黏合剂代替缝合线。
senses.why: Medicine needs materials that hold tissue without damaging it, which is a highly controlled kind of sticking.
senses.whyCN: 医学需要不损伤组织又能固定组织的材料，这是高度受控的「黏附」。

senses.title: The strength of an adhesive bond
senses.definition: in engineering, the force needed to separate two surfaces joined by an adhesive
senses.definitionCN: 工程中指分开两个由黏合剂连接的表面所需的力
senses.example: The adhesive bond failed only after the joint reached high heat.
senses.exampleCN: 接头达到高温后，黏结才失效。
senses.why: Once bonding is measured, the word names the joint and its strength, not only the glue itself.
senses.whyCN: 一旦黏合被测量，这个词就指接头及其强度，而不只是胶本身。

senses.title: Adhesive wear
senses.definition: a form of wear in which contacting surfaces tear material from each other
senses.definitionCN: 相互接触的表面从彼此撕下材料的一种磨损形式
senses.example: Adhesive wear shortened the life of the gearbox.
senses.exampleCN: 黏着磨损缩短了齿轮箱的寿命。
senses.why: The same sticking force that joins surfaces can, under sliding, pull material away, which is the failure mode's name.
senses.whyCN: 使表面结合的同一股黏附力，在滑动条件下会把材料撕走，这就是该失效模式的名称。

senses.title: Sticky in texture
senses.definition: describing a surface or substance that tends to cling to whatever touches it
senses.definitionCN: 形容容易粘住接触物的表面或物质
senses.example: The adhesive side of the label would not come off her fingers.
senses.exampleCN: 标签有黏性的一面粘在她手指上，甩不掉。
senses.why: The adjective keeps the plain physical quality that the noun was built from.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词保留了名词由之而来的朴素物理性质。

senses.title: An adhesive label or stamp
senses.definition: a label, stamp or sticker that carries its own glue and can be pressed into place
senses.definitionCN: 自带胶层、可按压贴上的标签、邮票或贴纸
senses.example: The parcel carried an adhesive label with the new address.
senses.exampleCN: 包裹上贴着一张写有新地址的不干胶标签。
senses.why: Self-sticking paper is named by its adhesive side, a very concrete everyday application.
senses.whyCN: 自粘纸张按它「有黏性的一面」来命名，这是非常具体的日常应用。

senses.title: Natural attachment structures
senses.definition: in biology, a substance or structure by which an organism fixes itself to a surface
senses.definitionCN: 生物学中生物把自身固定在某个表面上的物质或结构
senses.example: The barnacle's adhesive is one of the strongest natural glues.
senses.exampleCN: 藤壶的黏附物是自然界最强的胶之一。
senses.why: Organisms also need to stick, and their secretions are described with the same industrial word.
senses.whyCN: 生物也需要黏住，它们的分泌物就用同一个工业词汇来描述。

intro.en: Adhesive is the adjective from the Latin verb adhaerere, to stick to, later used as a noun for the sticking substance.
intro.cn: adhesive 是拉丁动词 adhaerere「黏附于」的形容词形式，后来又被用作表示黏合物质的名词。

items.en: Haerere meant to stick or cling; its deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: haerere 意为「黏住、附着」，其更早来源不确定。

items.en: Ad plus haerere formed adhaerere, to stick to, with the participle stem adhaes-.
items.cn: ad 与 haerere 构成 adhaerere「黏附于」，分词词干为 adhaes-。

items.en: Late Latin adhaesivus meant tending to stick; the exact first record is uncertain.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 adhaesivus 意为「有黏附倾向的」，确切最早记录不确定。

items.en: French adhésif carried the adjective toward English in the scientific and technical register.
items.cn: 法语 adhésif 把这个形容词以科学与技术的语体带向英语。

items.en: The adjective is recorded in English in the seventeenth century; the noun use for glue came later.
items.cn: 形容词在十七世纪见于英语记录；表示胶的名词用法更晚出现。

items.en: Industry created tapes, labels and surgical glues, and adhesive became the general word for all of them.
items.cn: 工业造出胶带、标签与医用胶，adhesive 成了统称这些事物的通用词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the adhere family; the near-meaning group gathers glues and joining materials with different scope.
note.cn: 形近组收 adhere 词族；近义组收胶类与连接材料，范围不同。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to stick or to follow closely.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「黏附」或「坚持遵循」。

entries.definition: The noun for the physical force of sticking.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「黏附、附着力」。

entries.definition: A supporter, or something that sticks to a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「拥护者」或「黏附的」。

entries.definition: The noun for sticking to a rule or surface.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「遵循」或「黏附状态」。

entries.definition: Holding together as a unit; it uses the same haerere root with the prefix co-.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有凝聚力的」，以 co- 前缀与同一 haerere 词根构成。

entries.definition: The everyday word for a sticky substance used to join materials.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「胶水」，是日常表示黏合材料的词。

entries.definition: A building material that hardens to join bricks or stones; a heavy-duty adhesive.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「水泥、黏结剂」，指硬化后连接砖石的重型黏合材料。

entries.definition: A narrow strip used for sticking or binding; the carrier, not the glue itself.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「胶带」，是承载胶层的条带，而非胶本身。

entries.definition: A force or connection holding things together; broader than adhesive.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「结合、黏结」，范围比 adhesive 宽。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real haerere root and the tape, medical and engineering phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的 haerere 词根，以及这个词实际出现的胶带、医用与工程搭配。

normal.en: Adhesive is the -ive form of adhaerere, the thing that sticks.
normal.cn: adhesive 是 adhaerere 的 -ive 形式，即「黏住的东西」。

normal.en: Adhesion is the force, adhesive is the material, adhere is the action.
normal.cn: adhesion 是力，adhesive 是材料，adhere 是动作。

normal.en: Adhesive tape is the portable version of the same idea.
normal.cn: 胶带是同一理念的便携版本。

normal.en: A surgical adhesive must hold tissue without harming it.
normal.cn: 医用黏合剂必须固定组织又不伤害组织。

normal.en: Adhesive wear is the failure mode where sticking surfaces tear material away.
normal.cn: 黏着磨损是黏附表面把材料撕走的失效模式。

abstract.en: Picture two paper strips joined by one clear strip, impossible to pull apart cleanly.
abstract.cn: 想象两条彩纸由一条透明胶带连在一起，无法干净地拉开。

abstract.en: Adhesive is contact that refuses to end: the surfaces touch and stay touching.
abstract.cn: 黏合剂是拒绝结束的接触：表面碰上，并且一直贴着。

abstract.en: The same force that holds a label on a jar also holds a barnacle to a rock.
abstract.cn: 把标签固定在罐子上的同一股力，也把藤壶固定在岩石上。

examples.en: The adhesive on the envelope had dried out and would not seal.
examples.cn: 信封上的胶已经干了，封不住口。

examples.en: Engineers tested the adhesive bond under freezing conditions.
examples.cn: 工程师在冷冻条件下测试黏结强度。

examples.en: A strong adhesive can replace nails in some furniture joints.
examples.cn: 强力黏合剂在某些家具接合处可以代替钉子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德希西夫」——阿德把纸条粘在一起，拉也拉不开：黏合剂

root: 拉丁语 haerere「黏住」加 ad- 构成 adhaerere「黏附于」，分词词干 adhaes-；晚期拉丁语 adhaesivus 意为「有黏附倾向的」，经法语 adhésif 进入英语为 adhesive。haerere 更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all describe holding surfaces together: a bonding substance, tape, a medical glue, a measured bond, a wear failure, a sticky texture, a self-stick label, or a natural attachment.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述「把表面固定在一起」：黏合物质、胶带、医用胶、可测量的黏结、磨损失效、黏性质地、不干胶标签，或自然附着结构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two paper strips are joined by one clear tape and will not pull apart.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条彩纸由一段透明胶带连住，拉不开。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL: the substance and its sticky quality.
branches.cn: 材料线：黏合物质及其黏性。

branches.en: THE PRODUCT: tape and self-stick labels carry glue into daily use.
branches.cn: 产品线：胶带与不干胶标签把胶带入日常使用。

branches.en: THE BODY: a medical adhesive must hold tissue safely.
branches.cn: 身体线：医用黏合剂必须安全地固定组织。

branches.en: THE ENGINEERING: the bond has measurable strength and a failure mode.
branches.cn: 工程线：黏结有可测量的强度，也有失效模式。

branches.en: THE NATURE: organisms make their own adhesives.
branches.cn: 自然线：生物会制造自己的黏附物。

intro.en: Adhesive is a Latin participle stem plus an adjective suffix, with the noun use added later.
intro.cn: adhesive 是拉丁分词词干加形容词后缀，名词用法是后来加上的。

latinIntro.en: Latin haerere, adhaerere and adhaesivus are recorded; haesum supplies the participle stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 haerere、adhaerere、adhaesivus 均有记录；haesum 提供分词词干。

items.example: It directs the sticking toward a surface.
items.exampleCN: 它把黏附指向某个表面。

items.example: It supplies the stem for adhesion and adhesive.
items.exampleCN: 它为 adhesion 与 adhesive 提供词干。
它构成 cohesive，义为「粘在一起的」。

derivatives.zh: 本词对应的动词，义为「黏附；坚持」
由拉丁分词加 -ion 构成，义为「黏附；附着力」
由动词加 -ence 构成，义为「黏附；遵循」
由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「以黏附方式地」
由本词加 -ness 构成，义为「黏性」

definition_zh: 毗邻；邻接；紧挨；附加
definition_en: to be next to or touching something, or to attach something to another
core_image: 两间房共用同一堵墙
scene: 旅店老板把两间相邻的房间一起租给同一家人，钥匙只给了一把。The garden adjoins the old chapel wall.
sceneCN: 这里 adjoin 是「毗邻」（第 1 个义项：紧挨着某物）；句意为花园紧挨着老教堂的墙。

pos.zh: 动词：毗邻；邻接；附加

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「相邻的；毗连的」
由拉丁语 adjacere 加 -ent 构成，义为「邻近的」，与本词语义接近但词源词不同
由 adjacent 加 -cy 构成，义为「邻接；相邻关系」
由拉丁语 adjungere 加 -ion 构成，义为「附加；添加」

senses.title: To be next to something
senses.definition: to lie next to or share a boundary with another place or object
senses.definitionCN: 位于另一地点或物体旁边，或与其共享边界
senses.example: The library adjoins the main lecture hall.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆紧挨着主讲堂。
senses.why: Adjungere means to join to, so two things that adjoin are joined at their edge without becoming one.
senses.whyCN: adjungere 意为「连接到」，所以 adjoin 的两样东西在边缘相接，却不会合为一体。

senses.title: Rooms that share a wall
senses.definition: describing hotel or house rooms connected by a shared wall or door
senses.definitionCN: 指旅馆或住宅中由共用墙壁或门相连的房间
senses.example: We asked for two rooms that adjoin so the children could sleep nearby.
senses.exampleCN: 我们要求两间相邻的房间，好让孩子睡在附近。
senses.why: The most familiar adjoining things are rooms, where a shared wall is easy to see and easy to use.
senses.whyCN: 最常见的「相邻物」是房间，共用的墙既看得见也方便使用。

senses.title: Land that borders another property
senses.titleCN: 与另一处地产相邻的土地
senses.definition: describing land or a building plot that shares a boundary with another property
senses.definitionCN: 指与另一处地产共享边界的土地或建筑地块
senses.example: The new field adjoins the school grounds.
senses.exampleCN: 这块新田地与学校校园相邻。
senses.why: Land boundaries are the clearest legal case of touching without merging, so property language relies on the word.
senses.whyCN: 土地边界是「接触但不合并」最清楚的法律情形，所以地产语言依赖这个词。

senses.title: Adjoining in property law
senses.definition: in law, describing properties that share a boundary and therefore create rights and duties
senses.definitionCN: 法律上指共享边界、因而产生权利与义务的房产
senses.example: The adjoining owners disagreed about the fence line.
senses.exampleCN: 相邻的业主对围栏界线产生了分歧。
senses.why: When neighbours share an edge, law must decide who may do what there, which turns a spatial word into a legal one.
senses.whyCN: 当邻居共享一条边，法律必须决定谁能在那里做什么，于是空间词变成法律词。

senses.title: To attach or annex
senses.definition: in older usage, to attach something to another thing or add it formally
senses.definitionCN: 较旧用法中指把某物附着到另一物上，或正式归并
senses.example: The estate adjoined the smaller farm to its accounts.
senses.exampleCN: 庄园把较小的农场归并进自己的账目。
senses.why: The original Latin verb meant to join to, and this administrative sense keeps the joining action rather than mere touching.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁原动词意为「连接到」，这个行政义保留的是「连接动作」而非单纯相邻。

senses.title: Neighbouring regions
senses.definition: describing counties, districts or countries that border one another
senses.definitionCN: 指彼此接壤的郡、区或国家
senses.example: The two adjoining counties share a river authority.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个相邻的郡共用一个河流管理机构。
senses.why: Regions also touch at edges, so maps and administration use the same joining word at a larger scale.
senses.whyCN: 地区也在边缘相接，所以地图与行政在更大尺度上使用同一个「连接」词。

senses.title: Ideas that touch
senses.definition: in abstract use, describing ideas or fields that are closely connected without being identical
senses.definitionCN: 抽象用法中指紧密相关但并不相同的观念或领域
senses.example: The two subjects adjoin, yet each keeps its own methods.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个学科彼此衔接，却各自保留自己的方法。
senses.why: Abstract fields can be imagined as plots of land, so the spatial idea of sharing a border transfers to thought.
senses.whyCN: 抽象领域可以被想象成地块，于是「共享边界」的空间观念转移到了思想上。

senses.title: Natural features that meet
senses.definition: describing a river, forest or shore that runs alongside another natural feature
senses.definitionCN: 指与另一自然地貌并排相接的河流、森林或岸线
senses.example: The meadow adjoins the river where the path begins.
senses.exampleCN: 草地在小路起点处与河流相接。
senses.why: Landscape features meet along lines, which is the most literal picture of adjoining in nature.
senses.whyCN: 地貌沿界线相接，这是自然界中最字面的「毗邻」画面。

intro.en: Adjoin comes from a Latin verb meaning to join to, built from a prefix and the root for joining.
intro.cn: adjoin 来自拉丁语表示「连接到」的动词，由前缀与表示「连接」的词根构成。

items.en: Iungere meant to join or yoke; it is also the source of junction, join and conjugate.
items.cn: iungere 意为「连接、套上轭」，也是 junction、join、conjugate 的来源。

items.en: Ad plus iungere formed adiungere, to join to or attach.
items.cn: ad 与 iungere 构成 adiungere，意为「连接到、附加」。

items.en: Old French ajoindre carried the verb into English, with the spelling later reshaped toward Latin.
items.cn: 古法语 ajoindre 把这个动词带入英语，拼写后来又被拉回拉丁形式。

items.en: The verb is recorded in Middle English; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个动词在中古英语中已有记录，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Property law fixed adjoining as a standard description of neighbouring land.
items.cn: 财产法把 adjoining 固定为描述相邻土地的标准用语。

items.en: The word now ranges from hotel rooms and gardens to counties and academic fields.
items.cn: 如今这个词从旅馆房间与花园，扩展到郡县与学术领域。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the join family and near-spelling words; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of touching and bordering.
note.cn: 形近组收 join 词族与拼写相近的词；近义组收表示接触与接壤的动词。

entries.definition: The basic verb meaning to connect or become part of.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「连接」或「加入」，是本词的核心。

entries.definition: A place where things meet, such as a road or railway crossing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「交叉点、接头」，指道路或铁路交汇处。

entries.definition: Next to something; it comes from a different Latin verb, adjacere, to lie near.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「邻近的」，来自另一个拉丁动词 adjacere「位于附近」，与本词语源不同。

entries.definition: To suspend a meeting until another time; it looks like adjoin but comes from a different French phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「休会、延期」，拼写像 adjoin，但来自不同的法语短语，词源不同。

entries.definition: The participial adjective meaning next to or sharing a boundary.
entries.definitionCN: 分词形容词，义为「相邻的、共享边界的」。

entries.definition: To touch along a boundary; it stresses the line rather than the joining.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「接壤」，强调边界线而非连接动作。

entries.definition: To be in contact; broader and can describe any physical contact, including a point.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「接触」，范围更宽，可指任何物理接触，包括一个点。

entries.definition: To be located near something; British spelling and less precise than adjoin.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「邻近」，为英式拼写，精确度低于 adjoin。

entries.definition: To touch at an end or edge, common in building and property descriptions.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「紧靠、抵接」，常用于建筑与地产描述。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real iungere root and the room, land and legal phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的 iungere 词根，以及这个词实际出现的房间、土地与法律搭配。

normal.en: Adiungere is ad plus iungere, to join to; adjoin keeps the joining but stops at the edge.
normal.cn: adiungere 是 ad 加 iungere「连接」，adjoin 保留了连接，却停在边缘。

normal.en: Join, junction and conjugate all share the yoke root iungere.
normal.cn: join、junction、conjugate 都共享「套轭」词根 iungere。

normal.en: Adjoining rooms share a wall but remain two rooms.
normal.cn: 相邻房间共用一堵墙，却仍是两间房。

normal.en: Adjacent comes from adjacere, to lie near, so it is a different Latin verb.
normal.cn: adjacent 来自 adjacere「位于附近」，是另一个拉丁动词，词源不同。

normal.en: In property law, adjoining owners have rights along a shared boundary.
normal.cn: 在财产法中，相邻业主在共享边界上拥有权利。

abstract.en: Picture two rooms with one wall between them and a single door in that wall.
abstract.cn: 想象两间房之间只有一堵墙，墙上只有一扇门。

abstract.en: Adjoin is closeness with a line down the middle: together at the edge, separate inside.
abstract.cn: adjoin 是中间画一条线的接近：边缘相连，内部各自独立。

abstract.en: Two academic fields can adjoin like two gardens sharing a fence.
abstract.cn: 两个学术领域可以像两座花园共用一道篱笆那样彼此衔接。

examples.en: The kitchen adjoins the dining room through a narrow door.
examples.cn: 厨房通过一扇窄门与餐厅相连。

examples.en: Their farm adjoins the forest reserve.
examples.cn: 他们的农场与森林保护区相邻。

examples.en: The two adjoining counties agreed to share the bridge.
examples.cn: 这两个相邻的郡同意共用这座桥。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿卓因」——阿卓把两间房用一堵墙连起来：毗邻

root: 拉丁语 iungere「连接、套轭」加 ad- 构成 adiungere「连接到」，经古法语 ajoindre 进入英语为 adjoin；拼写后来向拉丁形式靠拢。注意 adjacent 来自另一个动词 adjacere，词源不同。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all put two things edge to edge: a general neighbour, rooms, land, legal property, an annexation, counties, ideas, or natural features.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把两样东西放到边缘相接：一般邻居、房间、土地、法律地产、归并、郡县、观念，或自然地貌。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two rooms separated by one shared wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：两间房被一堵共用的墙隔开。

branches.en: THE GENERAL CASE: one thing lies next to another, and rooms share a wall.
branches.cn: 一般情形线：一物位于另一物旁，房间共用一堵墙。

branches.en: THE PROPERTY: land and legal rights meet along a shared line.
branches.cn: 地产线：土地与法律权利沿共享界线相接。

branches.en: THE ANNEXATION: older usage joins something formally to another.
branches.cn: 归并线：较旧用法把某物正式并入另一物。

branches.en: THE REGION: counties and countries border each other.
branches.cn: 区域线：郡县与国家彼此接壤。

branches.en: THE EXTENSION: ideas and landscapes can share an edge too.
branches.cn: 延伸线：观念与地貌也能共享边缘。

intro.en: Adjoin is a Latin prefix plus a joining root, reshaped in French and then partly re-Latinized in English.
intro.cn: adjoin 是拉丁语前缀加「连接」词根，在法语中变形，又在英语中部分回归拉丁拼写。

latinIntro.en: Latin iungere and adiungere are recorded; the English spelling reflects both French and Latin influence.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 iungere 与 adiungere 均有记录；英语拼写同时反映法语与拉丁语影响。

items.example: It directs the joining toward an object.
items.exampleCN: 它把「连接」指向某个对象。

items.example: It is the direct Latin source.
It appears in junction and juncture.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 junction 与 juncture 中。

items.example: It appears in adjacent, from a different verb.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 adjacent 中，但来自不同的动词。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「相邻的」
由 adjacent 加 -cy 构成，义为「邻接；相邻关系」
由拉丁语 adjacere 加 -ent 构成，义为「邻近的」，词源与本词不同
由拉丁语 adjungere 加 -ion 构成，义为「附加；添加」

definition_zh: 调整；调节；适应；校准；理算
definition_en: to change something slightly so that it fits, works better or matches a new situation
core_image: 把歪了的画框扶正，左右量一量
scene: 墙上那幅画有点歪，主人搬来梯子，把它重新扶正。He adjusted the mirror until the reflection lined up.
sceneCN: 这里 adjust 是「调整」（第 1 个义项：稍作改动使合适）；句意为他把镜子调整到影像对齐为止。

pos.zh: 动词：调整；调节；适应；校准

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ment 构成，义为「调整；调节」
由动词加 -able 构成，义为「可调整的」
由动词加 -er 构成，义为「理算员；调整器」
由 re- 加本词构成，义为「重新调整」
由动词加 -ed 构成，义为「调整过的；经调整的」

senses.title: To change slightly for a better fit
senses.definition: to make a small change so that something fits, sits or works correctly
senses.definitionCN: 作小幅改动，使某物合适、摆正或正常运作
senses.example: She adjusted the chair until her feet reached the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 她调整椅子，直到双脚能够落地。
senses.why: Adjust came from a word meaning to bring near or set right, so the core act is a small correction rather than a total remake.
senses.whyCN: adjust 来自表示「靠近、摆正」的词，所以核心动作是小幅校正，而不是彻底重做。

senses.title: To adapt to a new situation
senses.definition: to change one's habits or expectations in order to cope with new conditions
senses.definitionCN: 改变习惯或预期以应对新条件
senses.example: It took him a month to adjust to working nights.
senses.exampleCN: 他花了一个月才适应上夜班。
senses.why: People also set themselves right for a new circumstance, which turns a physical correction into an inner one.
senses.whyCN: 人也会为新的处境「摆正自己」，这把物理校正变成了内在调整。

senses.title: To adjust a device or setting
senses.definition: to move a control so that a machine, instrument or system works at the desired level
senses.definitionCN: 移动控制装置，使机器、仪器或系统达到所需水平
senses.example: Please adjust the thermostat before the guests arrive.
senses.exampleCN: 请在客人到达前调好恒温器。
senses.why: Machines have settings that must be brought into line, the most literal modern use of the word.
senses.whyCN: 机器有需要被「调到线上」的设置，这是这个词最字面的现代用法。

senses.title: To adjust prices or accounts
senses.definition: to change a price, figure or account in order to correct or update it
senses.definitionCN: 为纠正或更新而改动价格、数字或账目
senses.example: The shop adjusted its prices after the new tax.
senses.exampleCN: 新税出台后，商店调整了价格。
senses.why: Numbers can be brought into line with reality, so commerce uses the same correction image.
senses.whyCN: 数字可以被「调得与事实一致」，所以商业使用同一种校正画面。

senses.title: To settle an insurance claim
senses.definition: to assess and settle the amount payable on an insurance claim
senses.definitionCN: 评估并确定保险索赔应支付的金额
senses.example: The company adjusted the claim within two weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 公司在两周内理算了这笔索赔。
senses.why: An insurance adjuster brings the claim into an exact figure, which is a specialised financial correction.
senses.whyCN: 保险理算员把索赔调成一个准确数字，这是专门化的财务校正。

senses.title: To adjust expectations
senses.definition: to make one's hopes or plans more realistic in the light of new facts
senses.definitionCN: 根据新事实使希望或计划更符合现实
senses.example: After the test results, they adjusted their expectations for the season.
senses.exampleCN: 测试结果出来后，他们调低了对本赛季的预期。
senses.why: Expectations are set too high or too low like a dial, so the word moves easily into mental planning.
senses.whyCN: 预期像旋钮一样会被设得过高或过低，所以这个词很容易进入心理规划。

senses.title: To calibrate an instrument
senses.definition: to set an instrument against a standard so that its readings are accurate
senses.definitionCN: 以标准为参照设置仪器，使读数准确
senses.example: The lab adjusted the scale before every experiment.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室在每次实验前都校准天平。
senses.why: Precision work needs exact alignment with a standard, which is adjustment at its most rigorous.
senses.whyCN: 精密工作需要与标准精确对齐，这是 adjust 最严格的形式。

senses.title: To alter clothing for a better fit
senses.definition: to make small sewing changes so that a garment fits the wearer better
senses.definitionCN: 作小幅缝改，使衣服更贴合穿者
senses.example: The tailor adjusted the waist of the jacket.
senses.exampleCN: 裁缝调整了外套的腰围。
senses.why: Clothing is fitted to a body by small changes, the domestic origin of the same correcting act.
senses.whyCN: 衣服靠小改动去贴合身体，这是同一校正动作在家庭生活中的来源。

intro.en: Adjust reached English through French from a Latin phrase meaning to bring something near or set it right.
intro.cn: adjust 经由法语进入英语，源头是拉丁短语，意为「把某物带到近处、摆正」。

items.en: Iuxta meant near or beside, and it is also the source of juxtapose.
items.cn: iuxta 意为「靠近、在旁边」，也是 juxtapose 的来源。

items.en: A verb *adiuxtare, to bring near, is reconstructed as the source of the French family.
items.cn: 重构动词 *adiuxtare「使靠近」被认为是法语词族的来源。

items.en: Old French ajouster meant to join or fit; the modern form adjuster was influenced by Latin ad and justus.
items.cn: 古法语 ajouster 意为「连接、使合适」；现代形式 adjuster 受到拉丁语 ad 与 justus 的影响。

items.en: The verb is recorded in Middle English; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个动词在中古英语中已有记录，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Insurance gave the word its claim-settling sense and the job title adjuster.
items.cn: 保险业赋予这个词「理算索赔」的含义以及 adjuster 这一职位名。

items.en: The word now covers devices, prices, expectations, instruments and clothing.
items.cn: 如今这个词涵盖设备、价格、预期、仪器与衣物。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers adjust-family words and near spellings; the near-meaning group gathers change verbs with different scope.
note.cn: 形近组收 adjust 词族与拼写相近词；近义组收改动类动词，范围不同。

entries.definition: The noun for a small change made to fit or correct.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「调整」，指为合适或纠正而作的小改动。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning able to be changed or set.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可调整的」。

entries.definition: A person who assesses insurance claims, or a device that makes adjustments.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「理算员」或「调整器」。

entries.definition: To adjust again after a change.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「重新调整」。

entries.definition: To judge a case; it looks like adjust but comes from judex, a judge.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「裁决」，拼写像 adjust，但来自 judex「法官」，词源不同。

entries.definition: To change to fit a new use or condition; often broader and more structural than adjust.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使适应、改编」，常比 adjust 更大、更结构性。

entries.definition: To change something, often more substantially than a small adjustment.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「修改」，改动常比 adjust 的小幅调整更大。

entries.definition: To set an instrument or engine to its best working state.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「调音、调校」，把乐器或发动机调到最佳工作状态。

entries.definition: To make something different; it does not imply fitting or correctness.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「改变」，不必然含有「合适或正确」的意思。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real iuxta root and the device, insurance and tailoring phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的 iuxta 词根，以及这个词实际出现的设备、保险与裁衣搭配。

normal.en: Iuxta means near, and juxtapose comes from the same root.
normal.cn: iuxta 意为「靠近」，juxtapose 也来自同一词根。

normal.en: Adjust is a small correction: bring the thing near the right line.
normal.cn: adjust 是小幅校正：把东西挪到正确的线上。

normal.en: An insurance adjuster settles a claim into an exact figure.
normal.cn: 保险理算员把索赔调成一个准确数字。

normal.en: Adjustable means the setting can be moved; adjustment is the change itself.
normal.cn: adjustable 表示设置可以移动；adjustment 则是改动本身。

normal.en: Adjudicate looks similar but belongs to judge, not to adjust.
normal.cn: adjudicate 看起来相似，却属于 judge 词族，与 adjust 不同源。

abstract.en: Picture a crooked picture frame moved a centimetre until it is level.
abstract.cn: 想象歪掉的画框被挪动一厘米，直到水平。

abstract.en: Adjustment is the space between almost right and right.
abstract.cn: 调整就是「差不多对」与「对」之间的那段距离。

abstract.en: A dial can be turned both ways, and so can expectations.
abstract.cn: 旋钮可以两边转，预期也可以两边调。

examples.en: He adjusted his seat before the long drive.
examples.cn: 长途驾驶前，他调整了座椅。

examples.en: The team adjusted its plan after the first results came in.
examples.cn: 首批结果出来后，团队调整了计划。

examples.en: It takes time to adjust to a new language and a new city.
examples.cn: 适应一门新语言和一座新城市需要时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿卓斯特」——阿卓把画框挪一挪，正好摆正：调整

root: 拉丁语 iuxta「靠近、在旁边」经晚期拉丁语重构动词 *adiuxtare「使靠近」，再经古法语 ajouster 进入英语为 adjust；现代拼写受拉丁语 ad 与 justus 影响。iuxta 也是 juxtapose 的词源。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all make a small correction toward a right line: a fit, a new situation, a device, a price, a claim, an expectation, an instrument, or a garment.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都朝一条「正确的线」作小幅校正：合适度、新处境、设备、价格、索赔、预期、仪器，或衣物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crooked frame is moved a centimetre until it hangs level.
core.cn: 核心意象：歪掉的画框被挪动一厘米，挂平了。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL FIT: a chair or a garment is brought to the body.
branches.cn: 物理贴合线：椅子或衣服被调到身体上。

branches.en: THE INNER FIT: habits and expectations are set to new facts.
branches.cn: 内在贴合线：习惯与预期被调到新事实上。

branches.en: THE INSTRUMENT: a dial or a scale is aligned with a standard.
branches.cn: 仪器线：旋钮或天平被对准标准。

branches.en: THE FIGURE: prices and claims are corrected into exact amounts.
branches.cn: 数字线：价格与索赔被校正成准确数额。

branches.en: THE CORE: all senses keep the idea of a small move toward right.
branches.cn: 核心线：所有义项都保留「朝正确方向小幅移动」的理念。

intro.en: Adjust joins a Latin near-word with a verb ending, then collects English suffixes for its family.
intro.cn: adjust 把拉丁语「靠近」词与动词词尾结合，再用英语后缀扩展词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin iuxta is recorded; the verb *adiuxtare behind Old French ajouster is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 iuxta 有记录；古法语 ajouster 背后的动词 *adiuxtare 属重构形式。

items.example: It directs the movement toward a line.
It is the near root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这一词族的「靠近」词根。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ment 构成，义为「调整」
由动词加 -able 构成，义为「可调整的」
由动词加 -er 构成，义为「理算员；调整器」
由 re- 加本词构成，义为「重新调整」

definition_zh: 管理；施行；给予（药物、援助）；主持（誓言）；执行
definition_en: to manage an organization, or to put into effect and give out something such as a drug, justice or an oath
core_image: 一个人站在桌前，把事务一项项分派下去
scene: 诊所里，护士先在记录本上写下给药时间，然后才动手。The nurse administered the medicine at the correct hour.
sceneCN: 这里 administer 是「施用（药物）」（第 1 个义项：把药物给予病人）；句意为护士在正确的时间施用了药物。

pos.zh: 动词：管理；施行；给予；主持

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ation 构成，义为「管理；行政；政府」
由 administration 加 -ive 构成，义为「行政的；管理的」
由动词加 -ator 构成，义为「管理者；行政人员」
由动词加 -able 构成，义为「可管理的；可施用的」

senses.title: To manage an organization
senses.definition: to run the daily business of an organization, office or institution
senses.definitionCN: 经营组织、办公室或机构的日常事务
senses.example: She administers a small foundation with only three staff.
senses.exampleCN: 她管理一个只有三名员工的小型基金会。
senses.why: Administrare meant to serve, and managing an office is serving its work by directing it, so the word begins with service.
senses.whyCN: administrare 意为「服务」，管理办公室就是通过指挥来服务这项工作，所以这个词从「服务」开始。

senses.title: To administer justice
senses.definition: to carry out the law by hearing cases and giving lawful decisions
senses.definitionCN: 通过审理案件与作出合法裁决来执行法律
senses.example: The court administers justice for the whole district.
senses.exampleCN: 这家法院为整个地区执行司法。
senses.why: Justice is not merely discussed but delivered, and the word names the delivery of a public good.
senses.whyCN: 司法不只是讨论，而是被交付；这个词命名的正是公共善的交付。

senses.title: To give a drug or treatment
senses.definition: to give medicine or medical treatment to a patient in a controlled way
senses.definitionCN: 以受控方式把药物或治疗给予病人
senses.example: The doctor administered the vaccine to the child.
senses.exampleCN: 医生给孩子接种了疫苗。
senses.why: Medical giving must be exact and authorised, which is why the word is so common in clinical instructions.
senses.whyCN: 医疗给予必须精确且获授权，所以这个词在临床指示中非常常见。

senses.title: To administer an oath
senses.definition: to formally ask a person to swear or affirm something in a legal or official setting
senses.definitionCN: 在法律或官方场合正式要求某人宣誓或确认
senses.example: The clerk administered the oath before the hearing began.
senses.exampleCN: 听证开始前，书记员主持了宣誓。
senses.why: An oath is a formal act that must be delivered by an authorised person, so the word marks official giving.
senses.whyCN: 宣誓是需要由获授权者交付的正式行为，所以这个词标记「官方给予」。

senses.title: To administer a test
senses.definition: to organize and carry out an examination or assessment under controlled conditions
senses.definitionCN: 在受控条件下组织并实施考试或评估
senses.example: Teachers administer the reading test every September.
senses.exampleCN: 教师每年九月实施阅读测试。
senses.why: A test is a procedure that must be run properly, so the managing sense extends to assessment.
senses.whyCN: 测试是需要被正确运行的流程，于是「管理」义延伸到评估。

senses.title: To administer aid
senses.definition: to give help, relief or first aid to people who need it
senses.definitionCN: 向需要的人提供帮助、救济或急救
senses.example: Volunteers administered first aid at the roadside.
senses.exampleCN: 志愿者在路边实施急救。
senses.why: Aid is something handed out to those in need, which is the charitable branch of the same giving verb.
senses.whyCN: 援助是分发给有需要者的东西，这是同一个「给予」动词的慈善分支。

senses.title: To administer an estate
senses.definition: in law, to manage and settle the property of a deceased person or a trust
senses.definitionCN: 法律上指管理和清算死者财产或信托财产
senses.example: The lawyer administered the estate for eighteen months.
senses.exampleCN: 律师管理这份遗产达十八个月。
senses.why: An estate must be accounted for and distributed, so legal administration is a long, formal kind of management.
senses.whyCN: 遗产必须被核算并分配，所以法律上的管理是一种长期而正式的管理。

senses.title: To give a blow or rebuke
senses.definition: to deliver a physical blow or a sharp reprimand to someone
senses.definitionCN: 对某人施加身体打击或严厉斥责
senses.example: The coach administered a sharp rebuke after the missed practice.
senses.exampleCN: 队员缺席训练后，教练给予了严厉斥责。
senses.why: Even punishment is something delivered to a person, so the giving verb reaches into the language of discipline.
senses.whyCN: 连惩罚也是「递送到某人身上」的东西，所以这个「给予」动词延伸进了惩戒语言。

intro.en: Administer comes from Latin administrare, literally to serve toward something, from minister, a servant.
intro.cn: administer 来自拉丁语 administrare，字面为「朝向某事服务」，源自 minister「仆人」。

items.en: Minus meant less or lesser; it is the root behind minister and minor.
items.cn: minus 意为「较少、较小」，是 minister 与 minor 背后的词根。

items.en: Minister meant a servant or attendant, one who is lesser and therefore serves.
items.cn: minister 意为「仆人、侍从」，地位较低因而提供服务的人。

items.en: Ad plus ministrare formed administrare, to serve, manage or carry out.
items.cn: ad 与 ministrare 构成 administrare，意为「服务、管理、执行」。

items.en: Old French aministrer carried the verb into English with the managing and giving senses together.
items.cn: 古法语 aministrer 把这个动词带入英语，管理义与给予义一同进入。

items.en: The verb is recorded in Middle English; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个动词在中古英语中已有记录，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Medicine, law and government each developed their own fixed phrases, such as administer a drug and administer justice.
items.cn: 医学、法律与政府各自发展出固定搭配，如 administer a drug 与 administer justice。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the administer family; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of managing and giving with different objects.
note.cn: 形近组收 administer 词族；近义组收管理与给予类动词，对象不同。

entries.definition: The noun for managing an organization, or for a government in office.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「管理、行政」，也指在任的一届政府。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning relating to management or office work.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「行政的、管理的」。

entries.definition: A person who manages an organization or system.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「管理者、行政人员」。

entries.definition: A senior government official or a religious servant; the source noun of the family.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「部长」或「牧师」，是这一词族的来源名词。

entries.definition: A short informal form for administration or an administrator.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「管理、管理员」，是 administration 或 administrator 的口语缩略。

entries.definition: To run or control something; the everyday word for the first sense of administer.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「管理、经营」，是 administer 第一个义项的日常说法。

entries.definition: To give out medicine or goods in measured amounts; close to the drug sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「配发、分发」，按量发放药物或物品，接近「施用药物」义。

entries.definition: To make a law or rule take effect; close to administering justice.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「执行、强制实施」，使法律或规则生效，接近「执行司法」义。

entries.definition: To hand over or carry out; the general giving verb behind many administer phrases.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「交付、实施」，是许多 administer 搭配背后的通用「给予」动词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real minister root and the medical, legal and exam phrases the word appears in.
