normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的 minister 词根，以及这个词实际出现的医疗、法律与考试搭配。

normal.en: Administrare is ad plus ministrare, to serve toward; the manager is a servant of the work.
normal.cn: administrare 是 ad 加 ministrare「朝向服务」；管理者是这项工作的仆人。

normal.en: Minister, minor and minus all share the lesser root.
normal.cn: minister、minor、minus 都共享「较小」词根。

normal.en: Administer a drug means give it in a controlled way.
normal.cn: administer a drug 意为以受控方式给予药物。

normal.en: Administer justice means deliver the law, not merely discuss it.
normal.cn: administer justice 意为交付法律，而不只是讨论法律。

normal.en: Administration, administrator and admin all grow from this one verb.
normal.cn: administration、administrator、admin 都从这一个动词生长出来。

abstract.en: Picture a desk with a tray of tasks, each handed out one by one.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子，上面一托盘的事务被一项项分发出去。

abstract.en: The word's secret is service: to administer is to serve the work by directing it.
abstract.cn: 这个词的秘密是「服务」：管理就是通过指挥来服务工作。

abstract.en: Medicine, justice and oaths all arrive through the same hand: something is formally given.
abstract.cn: 药物、司法与誓言都经同一只手抵达：某物被正式给予。

examples.en: Only a doctor may administer this drug.
examples.cn: 只有医生才可以施用这种药物。

examples.en: The committee administers the fund for local schools.
examples.cn: 委员会管理这笔用于本地学校的基金。

examples.en: The judge administered the oath to the new officer.
examples.cn: 法官为新警官主持了宣誓。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德米尼斯特」——阿德像小仆人一样，把每件事一项项送出去：管理、施行

root: 拉丁语 minus「较少」构成 minister「仆人」，加 ad- 与 ministrare 成 administrare「服务、管理、执行」，经古法语 aministrer 进入英语为 administer。核心由「服侍」引申为管理与给予。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all hand something out under authority: an organization's work, justice, a drug, an oath, a test, aid, an estate, or even a rebuke.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在权威之下把某物交付出去：组织的工作、司法、药物、誓言、考试、援助、遗产，甚至斥责。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a desk tray of tasks is handed out one item at a time.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上的事务托盘被一项项分发出去。

branches.en: THE ORGANIZATION: an office or an estate is run and accounted for.
branches.cn: 组织线：办公室或遗产被经营与核算。

branches.en: THE LAW: justice is delivered, not merely debated.
branches.cn: 法律线：司法被交付，而不只是辩论。

branches.en: THE CARE: drugs and aid are given in measured, authorised ways.
branches.cn: 照护线：药物与援助以受控、获授权的方式给予。

branches.en: THE PROCEDURE: oaths and tests are formally conducted by an authority.
branches.cn: 程序线：誓言与考试由权威正式主持。

branches.en: THE DISCIPLINE: even a rebuke is something delivered to a person.
branches.cn: 惩戒线：连斥责也是递送到某人身上的东西。

intro.en: Administer is a Latin prefix, a serving root and a verb ending; the family then adds English noun and adjective suffixes.
intro.cn: administer 是拉丁语前缀、服务词根与动词词尾的组合；词族随后再加英语名词与形容词后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin minus, minister, ministrare and administrare are recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 minus、minister、ministrare、administrare 均有记录。

items.example: It directs service toward the work.
It is the root of minister.

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ation 构成，义为「管理；行政；政府」
由 administration 加 -ive 构成，义为「行政的」
由动词加 -ator 构成，义为「管理者；行政人员」
由动词加 -able 构成，义为「可管理的；可施用的」

definition_zh: 管理；行政；政府；施行；管理部门
definition_en: the work of managing an organization, the government in office, or the act of putting something such as justice or a drug into effect
core_image: 一间办公室的墙上贴满流程表
scene: 办公室里每面墙都贴着流程表，谁负责哪一步写得清清楚楚。The administration of the programme took more time than the teaching.
sceneCN: 这里 administration 是「管理」（第 1 个义项：组织事务的经营管理）；句意为这个项目的管理工作比教学本身花的时间还多。

pos.zh: 名词：管理；行政；政府；施行

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词基础，义为「管理；施行；给予」
由本词加 -ive 构成，义为「行政的；管理的」
由动词加 -ator 构成，义为「管理者；行政人员」
由本词逆构而成的动词，义为「管理；经营」

senses.title: The work of managing an organization
senses.definition: the daily work of planning, organizing and running an office, school or company
senses.definitionCN: 规划、组织并运营办公室、学校或公司的日常工作
senses.example: The school's administration handles budgets, timetables and staff records.
senses.exampleCN: 学校的行政部门负责预算、课表与员工档案。
senses.why: Administrare meant to serve and direct, and -tion names the activity, so administration is the work of directing an organization's service.
senses.whyCN: administrare 意为「服务并指挥」，-tion 表示活动，所以 administration 就是指挥组织运作的工作。

senses.title: The government in office
senses.definition: the group of people currently governing a country or region, especially after an election
senses.definitionCN: 当前治理国家或地区的一群人，尤指选举后上台的一届
senses.example: The new administration promised to cut waiting times.
senses.exampleCN: 新政府承诺缩短等待时间。
senses.why: Governing is the largest form of managing public business, so the word names the whole team in power.
senses.whyCN: 治理是管理公共事务的最大形式，所以这个词指掌权的整个团队。

senses.title: The executive branch in American usage
senses.titleCN: 美式用法中的行政部门
senses.definition: in American English, the President and the departments under his or her authority
senses.definitionCN: 美式英语中指总统及其管辖下的各政府部门
senses.example: The Administration sent a budget proposal to Congress.
senses.exampleCN: 行政部门向国会提交了预算提案。
senses.why: A specific constitutional system needs a short name for its executive side, and administration supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 特定的宪政体制需要为行政一侧提供一个简短名称，administration 正好承担这个角色。

senses.title: The administration of justice
senses.definition: the process by which courts and officials apply the law to cases
senses.definitionCN: 法院与官员把法律适用于案件的过程
senses.example: Fair administration of justice requires independent judges.
senses.exampleCN: 公正的司法执行需要独立的法官。
senses.why: Justice must be delivered through procedures, which is the administering sense applied to law.
senses.whyCN: 司法必须通过程序被交付，这是「施行」义被用到法律上。

senses.title: The administering of a drug
senses.definition: the act of giving medicine or treatment to a patient in a controlled manner
senses.definitionCN: 以受控方式把药物或治疗给予病人的行为
senses.example: The administration of the drug must be recorded every hour.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药物的施用必须每小时记录一次。
senses.why: The same noun names the giving action itself, especially where dosage and timing matter.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词也指给予动作本身，尤其在剂量与时间重要的场合。

senses.title: A school administration office
senses.definition: the department or office that handles enrolment, records and daily school business
senses.definitionCN: 负责招生、档案与学校日常事务的部门或办公室
senses.example: Parents should collect the forms from the administration.
senses.exampleCN: 家长应到行政办公室领取表格。
senses.why: The abstract work becomes a concrete place where the paperwork is done.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的工作变成了一个具体地点，文书工作在那里完成。

senses.title: Business administration as a field of study
senses.definition: the academic subject that teaches how to manage companies and organizations
senses.definitionCN: 教授如何管理公司与组织的学科
senses.example: She took a degree in business administration.
senses.exampleCN: 她取得了工商管理学位。
senses.why: Managing can be studied systematically, so the activity also becomes a named academic discipline.
senses.whyCN: 管理可以被系统研究，于是这项活动也成了一个有名称的学科。

senses.title: The paperwork side of an organization
senses.definition: the routine clerical side of an organization, such as forms, records and internal rules
senses.definitionCN: 组织内例行的文书侧面，如表单、记录与内部规章
senses.example: The staff complained that administration was taking up their teaching time.
senses.exampleCN: 员工抱怨文书事务占用了他们的教学时间。
senses.why: In everyday speech administration often means the paperwork rather than the grand work of governing.
senses.whyCN: 在日常口语中，administration 常指文书杂务，而不是宏大的治理工作。

intro.en: Administration is the noun of the Latin verb administrare, to serve and manage, built with the action suffix -tion.
intro.cn: administration 是拉丁动词 administrare「服务、管理」的名词形式，以动作后缀 -tion 构成。

items.en: Minus meant lesser, and it is the root of minister, a servant.
items.cn: minus 意为「较小」，是 minister「仆人」的词根。

items.en: Ad plus ministrare formed administrare, to serve, manage or carry out.
items.cn: ad 与 ministrare 构成 administrare，意为「服务、管理、执行」。

items.en: Administratio named the work of managing or carrying something out.
items.cn: administratio 表示管理或执行某项事务的工作。

items.en: Old French administration carried the noun into English with both the managing and the government senses.
items.cn: 古法语 administration 把这个名词带入英语，管理义与政府义同时进入。

items.en: The word is recorded in Middle English; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词在中古英语中已有记录，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Modern politics fixed the capitalized Administration for the American executive, while other fields kept the general sense.
items.cn: 现代政治把首字母大写的 Administration 固定指美国行政部门，其他领域则保留一般含义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the administer family; the near-meaning group gathers words for management and government with different scope.
note.cn: 形近组收 administer 词族；近义组收管理与政府类词，范围不同。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to manage or to give out something such as a drug.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「管理」或「给予药物等」。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning relating to management or paperwork.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「行政的、管理的」。

entries.definition: A person who manages an organization or system.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「管理者、行政人员」。

entries.definition: A government department; it shares the servant root minister.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「部、政府部门」，共享 minister「仆人」词根。

entries.definition: An informal short form for administration or an administrator.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「管理、管理员」，是口语缩略形式。

entries.definition: The act of running a business or team; often more commercial than administration.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「管理、经营」，常比 administration 更偏商业。

entries.definition: The system and process of governing; more abstract and more political.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「治理」，更抽象、更政治化。

entries.definition: The institution that governs a state; administration can mean one particular team in office.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「政府」，指治理国家的机构；administration 可指在任的一届团队。

entries.definition: The administrative system of a large organization, often with a negative tone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「官僚体系」，指大型组织的行政系统，常带贬义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real minister root and the school, hospital and government phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的 minister 词根，以及这个词实际出现的学校、医院与政府搭配。

normal.en: Administrare is ad plus ministrare, to serve toward; administration is the work of that service.
normal.cn: administrare 是 ad 加 ministrare「朝向服务」，administration 就是这项服务的工作。

normal.en: Ministry shares the minister root, because a department also serves the state.
normal.cn: ministry 共享 minister 词根，因为部门也是为国家服务的。

normal.en: The administration of justice is law being delivered through courts.
normal.cn: the administration of justice 是法律通过法院被交付。

normal.en: Business administration is management studied as a degree subject.
normal.cn: business administration 是把管理作为学位科目来研究。

normal.en: In American English the capitalized Administration means the President's team.
normal.cn: 在美式英语中，首字母大写的 Administration 指总统团队。

abstract.en: Picture a wall of flow charts, each arrow assigning a task to a person.
abstract.cn: 想象一墙的流程图，每个箭头都把任务指派给某个人。

abstract.en: Administration is the invisible floor under an organization: nobody notices it until it cracks.
abstract.cn: 管理是组织脚下看不见的地板：直到裂开才有人注意。

abstract.en: The word began with service, and good administration still serves the work rather than itself.
abstract.cn: 这个词始于「服务」，而好的管理至今仍在服务工作本身，而不是服务自己。

examples.en: The administration of the fund requires clear records.
examples.cn: 这笔基金的管理需要清晰的记录。

examples.en: She works in administration at a large hospital.
examples.cn: 她在一家大医院的行政部门工作。

examples.en: The administration of justice cannot depend on public opinion.
examples.cn: 司法执行不能依赖公众舆论。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德米尼斯吹申」——阿德把一墙流程表吹得整整齐齐：管理、行政

root: 拉丁语 minus「较少」构成 minister「仆人」，加 ad- 与 ministrare 成 administrare「服务、管理、执行」，名词 administratio；经古法语 administration 进入英语。核心仍是「为事务服务并指挥」。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all direct an organization's work: management itself, a government team, the American executive, justice, a drug, a school office, a degree subject, or the paperwork that fills the day.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在指挥一个组织的工作：管理本身、政府团队、美国行政部门、司法、药物、学校办公室、学位学科，或填满一天的文书事务。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wall of flow charts assigns every step to a responsible person.
core.cn: 核心意象：一墙流程图把每一步指派给负责人。

branches.en: THE OFFICE: management work, its physical office and its paperwork.
branches.cn: 办公室线：管理工作、其办公地点与文书事务。

branches.en: THE GOVERNMENT: a team in power and the American executive branch.
branches.cn: 政府线：在任团队与美国行政部门。

branches.en: THE LAW: justice is delivered through courts and officials.
branches.cn: 法律线：司法通过法院与官员被交付。

branches.en: THE BODY: a drug is given under controlled rules.
branches.cn: 身体线：药物在受控规则下被给予。

branches.en: THE STUDY: management becomes a taught academic subject.
branches.cn: 学科线：管理成为被教授的学术科目。

intro.en: Administration joins a Latin serving root to an action noun suffix; the same root also gives ministry and minister.
intro.cn: administration 把拉丁语「服务」词根与动作名词后缀结合；同一词根还给出 ministry 与 minister。

latinIntro.en: Latin minister, ministrare, administrare and administratio are recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 minister、ministrare、administrare、administratio 均有记录。

items.example: It directs service toward the work.
It is the root of minister.

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词基础，义为「管理；施行；给予」
由本词加 -ive 构成，义为「行政的」
由动词加 -ator 构成，义为「管理者」
由本词逆构而成的动词，义为「管理、经营」

definition_zh: 行政的；管理的；后勤事务的
definition_en: relating to the management and routine paperwork of an organization, rather than its main work
core_image: 文件柜与盖了章的表格
scene: 开学第一天，走廊尽头那间办公室排起长队，桌上堆满表格。Administrative work kept the whole school running behind the scenes.
sceneCN: 这里 administrative 是「行政的」（第 1 个义项：与管理事务有关的）；句意为行政工作让整所学校在幕后运转。

pos.zh: 形容词：行政的；管理的；后勤事务的

derivatives.zh: 本词的基础名词，义为「管理；行政；政府」
本词对应的动词，义为「管理；施行」
由动词加 -ator 构成，义为「管理者」
由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「在行政上」

senses.title: Relating to management
senses.definition: concerned with organizing and running an institution rather than its core activity
senses.definitionCN: 关涉机构的组织与运营，而不是其核心业务
senses.example: The new post is administrative rather than teaching.
senses.exampleCN: 这个新职位属于行政岗，而不是教学岗。
senses.why: Administration names the managing work, and -ive turns it into a describing word for anything belonging to that work.
senses.whyCN: administration 表示管理工作，-ive 把它变成描述「属于该工作」的形容词。

senses.title: Paperwork and routine office tasks
senses.definition: describing the forms, records and routine tasks that support an organization
senses.definitionCN: 形容支撑组织的表单、记录与例行任务
senses.example: Administrative tasks fill most of her Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 行政事务占用了她周五的大部分时间。
senses.why: The adjective often points at the humble paper side of management, not the big decisions.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词常指管理里朴素的纸张一面，而不是重大决策。

senses.title: Administrative law
senses.definition: the branch of law governing the actions of government agencies and officials
senses.definitionCN: 规范政府机构与官员行为的法律分支
senses.example: The case turned on a point of administrative law.
senses.exampleCN: 这个案件的关键在于一个行政法问题。
senses.why: Government acts through agencies, so law needs a named field for the rules that control those acts.
senses.whyCN: 政府通过机构行事，所以法律需要一个有名目的领域来规范这些行为。

senses.title: Administrative costs
senses.definition: the money spent on running an organization, such as salaries, offices and records
senses.definitionCN: 用于运行组织的开支，如工资、办公场所与档案
senses.example: The charity keeps administrative costs below ten percent.
senses.exampleCN: 这家慈善机构把行政成本控制在百分之十以下。
senses.why: Support work has a price, and the adjective marks spending that keeps the organization alive rather than delivers its service.
senses.whyCN: 支撑性工作也有成本，这个形容词标记维持组织运转、而非直接交付服务的开支。

senses.title: Administrative staff
senses.definition: the employees who handle records, scheduling and internal procedures
senses.definitionCN: 负责档案、排期与内部程序的员工
senses.example: Administrative staff processed every application by hand.
senses.exampleCN: 行政人员逐份手工处理了所有申请。
senses.why: People who do the managing work are marked by the same adjective, which separates them from front-line staff.
senses.whyCN: 做管理工作的人用同一个形容词标记，从而与一线人员区分开。

senses.title: Administrative leave
senses.definition: a period during which an employee is removed from duties while an issue is investigated
senses.definitionCN: 员工在问题被调查期间被暂时解除职务的一段时间
senses.example: The officer was placed on administrative leave pending review.
senses.exampleCN: 该官员被停职待查，等待复核。
senses.why: The measure is an internal management action rather than a punishment, so it carries the administrative label.
senses.whyCN: 这项措施是内部管理行动而非惩罚，所以带着 administrative 的标签。

senses.title: An administrative error
senses.definition: a mistake made in records, procedures or office processing rather than in the main work
senses.definitionCN: 发生在档案、程序或办公处理中的错误，而非主要业务中的错误
senses.example: An administrative error sent the letter to the wrong address.
senses.exampleCN: 一处行政差错把信寄到了错误的地址。
senses.why: Blaming the office side rather than the profession, the adjective precisely locates where the mistake happened.
senses.whyCN: 把责任归于办公环节而非专业环节，这个形容词精确指出了错误发生的位置。

senses.title: Administrative detention
senses.definition: holding a person in custody by government order without a criminal trial
senses.definitionCN: 依政府命令在没有刑事审判的情况下拘押某人
senses.example: The report criticised the use of administrative detention.
senses.exampleCN: 报告批评了使用行政拘留的做法。
senses.why: When custody is ordered by an agency rather than a court, the adjective marks the administrative rather than judicial route.
senses.whyCN: 当拘押由机构而非法院下令，这个形容词标记的是行政路径而非司法路径。

intro.en: Administrative is the adjective of administration, built on the Latin serving verb with the -ive suffix.
intro.cn: administrative 是 administration 的形容词，建立在拉丁语「服务」动词上，加 -ive 后缀。

items.en: Minus meant lesser, the root behind minister, a servant.
items.cn: minus 意为「较小」，是 minister「仆人」背后的词根。

items.en: Ad plus ministrare formed administrare, to serve, manage or carry out.
items.cn: ad 与 ministrare 构成 administrare「服务、管理、执行」。

items.en: Late Latin administrativus meant pertaining to management; the exact first record is uncertain.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 administrativus 意为「与管理有关的」，确切最早记录不确定。

items.en: French administratif carried the adjective into modern European usage.
items.cn: 法语 administratif 把这个形容词带入现代欧洲用法。

items.en: The English adjective appears in records of the seventeenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语形容词在十七世纪的记录中出现，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Law and public service fixed phrases such as administrative law and administrative leave.
items.cn: 法律与公共服务固定了 administrative law、administrative leave 等搭配。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the administer family; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for management and officialdom.
note.cn: 形近组收 administer 词族；近义组收管理与官方性质的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun for management, government or the act of administering.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「管理、行政、政府」或「施行」。

entries.definition: A person who manages an organization or system.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「管理者、行政人员」。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to manage or give out.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「管理」或「给予」。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning in administrative terms.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在行政上」。

entries.definition: Relating to a minister or government department; it shares the serving root.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「部长的、部门的」，共享「服务」词根。

entries.definition: Relating to managing people or business; often more about leadership than paperwork.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「管理层的」，常更强调领导而非文书。

entries.definition: Relating to office clerks and routine written work; narrower than administrative.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「文书员的、事务性的」，范围比 administrative 窄。

entries.definition: Relating to a large administrative system, often with a tone of excessive rules.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「官僚的」，指大型行政体系，常带规则过度的语气。

entries.definition: Approved by an authority; it stresses status rather than office work.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「官方的」，强调权威认可，而非办公事务。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real minister root and the law, cost and staffing phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的 minister 词根，以及这个词实际出现的法律、成本与人事搭配。

normal.en: Administrative is the -ive adjective of administration, the managing work.
normal.cn: administrative 是 administration「管理工作」的 -ive 形容词。

normal.en: Administrative costs are the price of keeping the organization running.
normal.cn: administrative costs 是维持组织运转的代价。

normal.en: Administrative law controls what government agencies may do.
normal.cn: administrative law 规范政府机构可以做什么。

normal.en: Administrative leave removes a person from duty while a matter is reviewed.
normal.cn: administrative leave 是在事项复核期间让人离岗。

normal.en: Ministerial shares the same serving root as administrative.
normal.cn: ministerial 与 administrative 共享同一个「服务」词根。

abstract.en: Picture a filing cabinet with every drawer labelled, and a stamp ready on the desk.
abstract.cn: 想象一个每个抽屉都贴了标签的文件柜，桌上还放着一枚印章。

abstract.en: Administrative work is the scaffolding around the main performance: invisible, but load-bearing.
abstract.cn: 行政工作是主演出周围的脚手架：看不见，却承重。

abstract.en: The adjective marks the line between doing the work and keeping the work possible.
abstract.cn: 这个形容词标记的是「做工作」与「让工作得以进行」之间的界线。

examples.en: She spends two days a week on administrative duties.
examples.cn: 她每周有两天用于行政事务。

examples.en: The university reduced administrative costs by merging offices.
examples.cn: 大学通过合并办公室降低了行政成本。

examples.en: The employee was placed on administrative leave during the inquiry.
examples.cn: 调查期间，这名员工被停职待查。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德米尼斯吹提夫」——阿德桌上堆满盖了章的表格：行政的

root: 拉丁语 minus「较少」构成 minister「仆人」，加 ad- 与 ministrare 成 administrare「服务、管理」，晚期拉丁语 administrativus 表示「与管理有关的」，经法语 administratif 进入英语为 administrative。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all mark the support side of an institution: management itself, paperwork, law, costs, staff, leave, errors, or detention.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都标记机构的支撑面：管理本身、文书、法律、成本、人员、休假、差错，或拘留。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a labelled filing cabinet and a stamp waiting on the desk.
core.cn: 核心意象：贴满标签的文件柜与桌上待用的印章。

branches.en: THE WORK: managing and handling the routine paper side.
branches.cn: 工作线：管理与处理日常文书的一面。

branches.en: THE LAW: rules that control government agencies.
branches.cn: 法律线：规范政府机构的规则。

branches.en: THE COST: support work has a measurable price.
branches.cn: 成本线：支撑工作有可测量的代价。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE: staff who do the work, and leave taken while matters are reviewed.
branches.cn: 人员线：做这些工作的员工，以及事项复核期间的离岗。

branches.en: THE FAILURE: office mistakes and agency-ordered custody.
branches.cn: 失当线：办公差错与机构下令的拘押。

intro.en: Administrative is the adjective form of administration, built with the Latin serving root and the -ive suffix.
intro.cn: administrative 是 administration 的形容词形式，由拉丁「服务」词根与 -ive 后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin minister, administrare and administrativus are recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 minister、administrare、administrativus 均有记录。

items.example: It directs service toward the work.

derivatives.zh: 本词的基础名词，义为「管理；行政；政府」
本词对应的动词，义为「管理；施行」
由动词加 -ator 构成，义为「管理者」
由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「在行政上」

definition_zh: 管理者；行政人员；遗产管理人；系统管理员
definition_en: a person who manages an organization, system or estate, or who handles its official procedures
core_image: 一个人坐在桌后，面前是三摞文件
scene: 医院走廊里，行政人员抱着文件夹快步走过，后面跟着两位医生。The administrator approved the new schedule before the ward opened.
sceneCN: 这里 administrator 是「管理者」（第 1 个义项：负责组织运营的人）；句意为这位管理者在病房开放前批准了新排班。

pos.zh: 名词：管理者；行政人员；系统管理员

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词基础，义为「管理；施行」
由动词加 -ation 构成，义为「管理；行政」
由 administration 加 -ive 构成，义为「行政的」
由本词截短的口语形式，义为「管理员」

senses.title: A manager of an organization
senses.definition: a person responsible for running the daily operations of an institution
senses.definitionCN: 负责机构日常运营的人
senses.example: The administrator met every department head on Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 管理者在周一见了每个部门的负责人。
senses.why: The -ator suffix marks the person who performs administrare, so the administrator is the one who does the serving and directing.
senses.whyCN: -ator 后缀标记执行 administrare 的人，所以 administrator 就是从事服务与指挥的那个人。

senses.title: A public administrator
senses.definition: a government official who runs public programmes and agencies
senses.definitionCN: 运营公共项目与政府机构的官员
senses.example: Public administrators must answer to elected officials.
senses.exampleCN: 公共行政官员必须对民选官员负责。
senses.why: Public business needs career managers distinct from politicians, and the word supplies that role.
senses.whyCN: 公共事务需要与政客不同的职业管理者，这个词正好提供这一角色。

senses.title: A hospital administrator
senses.definition: a person who manages the non-medical operations of a hospital, such as staffing and budgets
senses.definitionCN: 管理医院非医疗运营的人，如人员与预算
senses.example: The hospital administrator reorganized the outpatient queue.
senses.exampleCN: 医院管理者重新安排了门诊排队流程。
senses.why: Care is delivered inside a complex organization, so a manager is needed beside the clinicians.
senses.whyCN: 照护在复杂组织内部交付，所以临床人员身边需要一位管理者。

senses.title: A school administrator
senses.definition: a person who handles enrolment, discipline, records and daily school operations
senses.definitionCN: 负责招生、纪律、档案与学校日常运营的人
senses.example: The school administrator called every parent personally.
senses.exampleCN: 学校行政人员亲自给每位家长打了电话。
senses.why: Schools separate teaching from management, and the manager carries the administrative title.
senses.whyCN: 学校把教学与管理分开，管理者承担行政头衔。

senses.title: A system administrator
senses.definition: a person who maintains computers, networks and accounts in an organization
senses.definitionCN: 维护组织内计算机、网络与账户的人
senses.example: The system administrator reset every password after the breach.
senses.exampleCN: 泄露事件后，系统管理员重置了所有密码。
senses.why: Digital systems also need someone to keep accounts and permissions in order, which extends the managing role to machines.
senses.whyCN: 数字系统也需要有人维护账户与权限，这把管理角色扩展到机器。

senses.title: A database administrator
senses.definition: a specialist who controls access, backups and performance of a database
senses.definitionCN: 控制数据库访问、备份与性能的专门人员
senses.example: The database administrator restored the table from a backup.
senses.exampleCN: 数据库管理员从备份中恢复了那张表。
senses.why: Data must be governed like an office, so the word appears in a precise technical job title.
senses.whyCN: 数据必须像办公室一样被治理，所以这个词出现在精确的技术职位名中。

senses.title: An estate administrator
senses.definition: in law, a person appointed to collect, manage and distribute a deceased person's estate
senses.definitionCN: 法律上被指定收集、管理与分配死者遗产的人
senses.example: The court appointed an administrator for the estate.
senses.exampleCN: 法院为这份遗产指定了一名管理人。
senses.why: Property left behind must be accounted for, and law gives the managing person a formal name.
senses.whyCN: 留下的财产必须被核算，法律便为这位管理者给出正式名称。

senses.title: A bankruptcy administrator
senses.definition: a person appointed to manage the property and affairs of a bankrupt business or person
senses.definitionCN: 被指定管理破产企业或个人财产与事务的人
senses.example: The bankruptcy administrator sold the factory to pay creditors.
senses.exampleCN: 破产管理人卖掉工厂以偿还债权人。
senses.why: When a business fails, its remaining assets need orderly management, which is administration under legal supervision.
senses.whyCN: 企业失败时，剩余资产需要有序管理，这是法律监督下的行政。

intro.en: Administrator is the Latin agent noun of administrare, the person who serves and directs.
intro.cn: administrator 是 administrare 的拉丁施事名词，指服务并指挥的那个人。

items.en: Minus meant lesser, the root behind minister, a servant.
items.cn: minus 意为「较小」，是 minister「仆人」背后的词根。

items.en: Ad plus ministrare formed administrare, to serve, manage or carry out.
items.cn: ad 与 ministrare 构成 administrare「服务、管理、执行」。

items.en: Administrator was the recorded agent noun, the person who manages or carries out.
items.cn: administrator 是有记录的施事名词，指管理或执行的人。

items.en: Old French administrateur carried the role name into English.
items.cn: 古法语 administrateur 把这个角色名带入英语。

items.en: The English word is recorded in the fifteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语词在十五世纪已有记录，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Computing created system administrator and database administrator as precise job titles.
items.cn: 计算机领域造出 system administrator 与 database administrator 等精确职位名。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the administer family; the near-meaning group gathers managers and officials with different authority.
note.cn: 形近组收 administer 词族；近义组收管理者与官员，权威来源不同。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to manage or give out.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「管理」或「给予」。

entries.definition: The noun for management or government.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「管理、行政、政府」。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning relating to management.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「行政的、管理的」。

entries.definition: A short informal form of administrator or administration.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「管理员、管理」，是口语缩略。

entries.definition: A rare older word for a servant or provider; it shares the same serving root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，较旧且少见，义为「服务者、提供者」，共享同一「服务」词根。

entries.definition: A person who runs a team or business; common in commercial settings.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「经理、管理者」，常用于商业场景。

entries.definition: A senior manager with decision-making power; higher in rank than many administrators.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「高管」，拥有决策权，级别常高于一般行政人员。

entries.definition: A person holding public office; the authority comes from office, not from management.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「官员」，权威来自职位，而非管理职能。

entries.definition: A person who oversees workers; narrower and more hands-on than administrator.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「主管」，负责监督员工，范围更窄、更贴近一线。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real -ator agent suffix and the hospital, school and computing phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的 -ator 施事后缀，以及这个词实际出现的医院、学校与计算机搭配。

normal.en: The -ator ending marks the person who does the administering.
normal.cn: -ator 结尾标记执行管理工作的人。

normal.en: A system administrator manages accounts and permissions, not people.
normal.cn: 系统管理员管理的是账户与权限，而不是人。

normal.en: An estate administrator is appointed by law to settle property.
normal.cn: 遗产管理人由法律指定来处理财产。

normal.en: A public administrator runs programmes, while politicians set direction.
normal.cn: 公共行政官员运营项目，政客则设定方向。

normal.en: Admin is simply the clipped, everyday form of administrator.
normal.cn: admin 只是 administrator 的截短日常形式。

abstract.en: Picture a desk with three stacks of files and a name plate on the front edge.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子，三摞文件，前缘还有一块姓名牌。

abstract.en: The administrator is the person who keeps the machine oiled so others can work.
abstract.cn: 管理者是给机器上油的人，好让别人能工作。

abstract.en: Power here is procedural: it comes from keeping records straight, not from giving orders.
abstract.cn: 这里的权力是程序性的：来自把记录理清，而不是发号施令。

examples.en: The administrator signed the contract on behalf of the school.
examples.cn: 管理者代表学校签署了合同。

examples.en: Contact the system administrator if you cannot log in.
examples.cn: 如果无法登录，请联系系统管理员。

examples.en: The estate administrator distributed the property according to the will.
examples.cn: 遗产管理人按遗嘱分配了财产。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德米尼斯吹特」——阿德坐在三摞文件后面，一件件签字：管理者

root: 拉丁语 administrare「服务、管理、执行」的施事名词 administrator，经古法语 administrateur 进入英语。词根仍为 minister「仆人」，核心是「为事务服务并指挥的人」。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all name a person who keeps an institution in order: an organization manager, public official, hospital manager, school officer, system or database keeper, estate manager, or bankruptcy manager.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在命名「让机构保持秩序的人」：组织管理者、公共官员、医院管理者、学校行政、系统或数据库维护者、遗产管理人，或破产管理人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person behind three stacks of files with a name plate on the desk.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人坐在三摞文件后面，桌上有姓名牌。

branches.en: THE INSTITUTION: a manager runs an organization or a school.
branches.cn: 机构线：管理者运营组织或学校。

branches.en: THE STATE: public administrators run programmes under elected officials.
branches.cn: 国家线：公共行政官员在民选官员之下运营项目。

branches.en: THE HOSPITAL: non-medical operations need their own manager.
branches.cn: 医院线：非医疗运营需要自己的管理者。

branches.en: THE MACHINE: systems and databases have named keepers.
branches.cn: 机器线：系统与数据库有具名的维护者。

branches.en: THE LAW: estates and failed businesses are placed under a manager.
branches.cn: 法律线：遗产与破产企业被置于管理人之下。

intro.en: Administrator is a Latin verb stem plus the agent suffix -ator, the person who carries out the work.
intro.cn: administrator 是拉丁动词词干加施事后缀 -ator，指执行这项工作的人。

latinIntro.en: Latin administrare and administrator are recorded; the agent noun is classical.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 administrare 与 administrator 均有记录，施事名词属古典拉丁语。

items.example: It directs service toward the work.
It is used in computing job titles.
items.exampleCN: 它用于计算机职位名中。

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词基础，义为「管理；施行」
由动词加 -ation 构成，义为「管理；行政」
由 administration 加 -ive 构成，义为「行政的」
由本词截短的口语形式，义为「管理员」

definition_zh: 准许进入；入场费；承认；入院；录取；接纳
definition_en: permission to enter a place or institution, the fee paid for entry, or a statement admitting that something is true
core_image: 门口检票员撕下一角门票
scene: 剧院门口，观众把票递过去，检票员熟练地撕下一角。Admission to the exhibition is free for students.
sceneCN: 这里 admission 是「入场许可」（第 1 个义项：获准进入某场所）；句意为学生参观该展览可以免费入场。

pos.zh: 名词：准许进入；入场费；承认；录取

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词基础，义为「准许进入；承认」
由 admit 加 -ance 构成，义为「进入权；进入」
由 admit 加 -ible 构成，义为「可采纳的；可进入的」
由 admitted 加 -ly 构成，义为「诚然；无可否认」

senses.title: Permission to enter
senses.definition: the right or permission to enter a place, event or institution
senses.definitionCN: 进入某场所、活动或机构的权利或许可
senses.example: Admission is limited to members and their guests.
senses.exampleCN: 仅限会员及其宾客入场。
senses.why: Admittere means to send in, and -sion names the result, so admission is the state of being let in.
senses.whyCN: admittere 意为「送进去」，-sion 表示结果，所以 admission 就是「被放进去」的状态。

senses.title: The entrance fee
senses.definition: the money charged for entering a museum, cinema or other venue
senses.definitionCN: 进入博物馆、影院或其他场所所收取的费用
senses.example: The admission for adults is twelve pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 成人入场费是十二英镑。
senses.why: Permission to enter can be sold, so the word shifts from the permission itself to its price.
senses.whyCN: 进入许可可以被出售，于是这个词从「许可本身」转到「许可的价格」。

senses.title: Admitting that something is true
senses.definition: a statement in which a person accepts that something is true, often reluctantly
senses.definitionCN: 某人接受某事属实的陈述，常带不情愿
senses.example: His admission that he had forgotten surprised no one.
senses.exampleCN: 他承认自己忘了，这并不让人意外。
senses.why: To admit is also to let a fact into the mind, so the word covers the mental version of opening a door.
senses.whyCN: admit 也是让一个事实进入头脑，所以这个词涵盖「开门」的心理版本。

senses.title: Admission to hospital
senses.definition: the formal process of being received into a hospital for treatment or observation
senses.definitionCN: 被医院接收以接受治疗或观察的正式流程
senses.example: Her admission to hospital was arranged for the next morning.
senses.exampleCN: 她的入院安排在第二天上午。
senses.why: Hospitals are institutions with doors, so being received for care is described as being let in.
senses.whyCN: 医院是有门的机构，所以被接收接受照护就被描述为「被放进去」。

senses.title: University admission
senses.definition: the process or decision by which a school or university accepts a student
senses.definitionCN: 学校或大学接收学生的过程或决定
senses.example: Admission to the programme depends on two essays.
senses.exampleCN: 能否被这个项目录取取决于两篇文章。
senses.why: Education is an institution with limited places, and admission is the formal act of letting a student in.
senses.whyCN: 教育机构名额有限，admission 就是正式把学生放进去的行为。

senses.title: An admission of guilt
senses.definition: in law, a statement by an accused person that accepts a fact or acknowledges guilt
senses.definitionCN: 法律上指被指控者接受某事实或承认罪责的陈述
senses.example: The court treated the letter as an admission of guilt.
senses.exampleCN: 法院把这封信视为认罪陈述。
senses.why: A legal admission lets a damaging fact into the record, which is the courtroom form of opening the door.
senses.whyCN: 法律上的承认让一个不利事实进入记录，这是法庭版本的「开门」。

senses.title: An admission ticket
senses.definition: a physical or digital ticket that proves the holder may enter
senses.definitionCN: 证明持票人可以进入的实体或电子票
senses.example: Keep your admission ticket until the end of the show.
senses.exampleCN: 请保留入场券直到演出结束。
senses.why: The abstract permission needs a portable proof, so the word attaches to the ticket that carries it.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的许可需要可携带的凭证，于是这个词附着在承载它的票上。

senses.title: Admission of evidence
senses.definition: in law, the acceptance of evidence by a court so that it may be considered
senses.definitionCN: 法律上指法院接受证据并允许其被考虑
senses.example: The judge ruled on the admission of the recording.
senses.exampleCN: 法官就这段录音的采纳作出了裁定。
senses.why: Courts also let things into a proceeding, so evidence can be admitted or refused at the door.
senses.whyCN: 法院也让东西进入程序，所以证据可以在门口被接纳或被拒绝。

intro.en: Admission comes from the Latin verb admittere, to send in, with the noun suffix naming the letting-in.
intro.cn: admission 来自拉丁动词 admittere「送进去」，名词后缀表示「放进去」这一结果。

items.en: Mittere meant to send or let go; it is also the source of mission, missile and transmit.
items.cn: mittere 意为「送、放」，也是 mission、missile、transmit 的来源。

items.en: Ad plus mittere formed admittere, to send in, let in or allow.
items.cn: ad 与 mittere 构成 admittere，意为「送进去、放进去、允许」。

items.en: Admissio named the act of letting someone in or receiving them.
items.cn: admissio 表示让人进入或接待某人的行为。

items.en: Old French admission carried the noun into English with the entry and acceptance senses.
items.cn: 古法语 admission 把这个名词带入英语，进入义与接受义一同进入。

items.en: The word is recorded in Middle English; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词在中古英语中已有记录，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Schools, hospitals and courts each developed fixed admission phrases, from admission fee to admission of evidence.
items.cn: 学校、医院与法院各自发展出固定搭配，从 admission fee 到 admission of evidence。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the admit family and near spellings; the near-meaning group gathers words for entry, confession and acceptance.
note.cn: 形近组收 admit 词族与拼写相近词；近义组收进入、承认与接纳类词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to let in or to accept a fact.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「准许进入」或「承认」。

entries.definition: The right to enter, often used on notices such as no admittance.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「进入权」，常用于「禁止入内」一类告示。

entries.definition: Able to be accepted, especially as evidence in court.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可采纳的」，尤指法庭证据。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning it must be admitted or granted.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「诚然、无可否认」。

entries.definition: Evidence a court may legally consider; the direct counterpart of admission of evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 名词短语，义为「可采纳的证据」，与 admission of evidence 直接对应。

entries.definition: The act of going in or the right to go in; broader and less formal than admission.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「进入」或「进入权」，范围更宽、正式度更低。

entries.definition: A statement admitting wrongdoing, often formal or religious; stronger than admission.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「供认、忏悔」，常更正式或带宗教色彩，语气比 admission 更重。

entries.definition: The act of accepting that something is true or received.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「承认、确认」，指接受某事为真或已收到。

entries.definition: The act of registering as a member or student; the administrative side of admission.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「注册、入学」，是 admission 的行政一侧。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real mittere root and the ticket, hospital and court phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的 mittere 词根，以及这个词实际出现的门票、医院与法庭搭配。

normal.en: Admittere is ad plus mittere, to send in; admission is the result of being sent in.
normal.cn: admittere 是 ad 加 mittere「送进去」，admission 就是被送进去的结果。

normal.en: Mission and transmit share the mittere root.
normal.cn: mission 与 transmit 共享 mittere 词根。

normal.en: Admission fee is the price of the permission to enter.
normal.cn: admission fee 是进入许可的价格。

normal.en: An admission of guilt lets a damaging fact into the record.
normal.cn: 认罪让一个不利事实进入记录。

normal.en: University admission is a school formally letting a student in.
normal.cn: 大学录取是学校正式把一名学生放进去。

abstract.en: Picture a ticket being torn at the door, leaving a small corner in the hand.
abstract.cn: 想象门票在门口被撕下一角，手里留下小小的一截。

abstract.en: Admission is a door with conditions: a fee, a ticket, a test score or a confession.
abstract.cn: admission 是一扇有条件的门：费用、门票、分数或坦白。

abstract.en: The same word opens buildings and minds: both require letting something in.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既打开建筑也打开头脑：两者都需要让某物进入。

examples.en: Admission to the gallery is free on Sundays.
examples.cn: 周日进入美术馆免费。

examples.en: The patient's admission to hospital was delayed by a day.
examples.cn: 病人的入院被推迟了一天。

examples.en: His admission that he had lied changed the case.
examples.cn: 他承认自己撒了谎，这改变了案件走向。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德米申」——阿德在门口递票，检票员撕下一角让他进去：准许进入

root: 拉丁语 mittere「送、放」加 ad- 构成 admittere「送进去、允许进入」，名词 admissio；经古法语 admission 进入英语。mittere 也是 mission 与 transmit 的词源。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all describe letting something in: a person, a paying visitor, a fact, a patient, a student, a legal acknowledgement, a ticket, or a piece of evidence.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述「让某物进入」：人、付费参观者、事实、病人、学生、法律承认、门票，或一件证据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ticket is torn at the door and the holder is let through.
core.cn: 核心意象：门票在门口被撕下一角，持票人被放行。

branches.en: THE DOOR: permission to enter and the ticket that proves it.
branches.cn: 门线：进入许可与证明许可的门票。

branches.en: THE PRICE: permission is sold as an entrance fee.
branches.cn: 价格线：许可被作为入场费出售。

branches.en: THE MIND AND LAW: facts and guilt are let into the record.
branches.cn: 心智与法律线：事实与罪责被放进记录。

branches.en: THE INSTITUTION: hospitals and schools formally receive people.
branches.cn: 机构线：医院与学校正式接收人。

branches.en: THE EVIDENCE: a court decides what may enter the proceeding.
branches.cn: 证据线：法院决定什么可以进入程序。

intro.en: Admission is a Latin prefix plus a sending root, turned into a noun with -sion.
intro.cn: admission 是拉丁语前缀加「送」词根，用 -sion 变成名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin mittere, admittere and admissio are recorded; the noun reached English through French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mittere、admittere、admissio 均有记录；名词经法语进入英语。

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词基础，义为「准许进入；承认」
由 admit 加 -ance 构成，义为「进入权」
由 admit 加 -ible 构成，义为「可采纳的」
由 admitted 加 -ly 构成，义为「诚然」

definition_zh: 承认；准许进入；准许加入；容纳；容许；收治
definition_en: to agree that something is true, or to let a person or thing come into a place, group, or record
core_image: 一扇门被推开，人和事实都被放了进来
scene: 面试室里，年轻人攥着简历，沉默了很久才说出自己抄袭的事。He finally admitted that he had copied the report from a colleague.
sceneCN: 这里 admit 是「承认（事实或错误）」（第 1 个义项：不情愿地承认某事为真）；句意为他终于承认自己抄了同事的报告。图中可辨识物件：简历、桌面、半开的门。

pos.zh: 承认；准许进入；接纳；容纳
承认；容许（常与 of 连用）

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -sion 构成，义为「承认；进入许可；入场费」
由动词加 -ance 构成，义为「进入权；入场许可」
由过去分词加 -ly 构成，义为「诚然；无可否认地」
由动词加 -ible 构成，义为「可接受的；可采纳的」
由动词加 -able 构成，义为「可准许进入的；可承认的」

senses.title: To agree that something is true
senses.definition: to agree, often unwillingly, that something is true, especially something you would rather hide
senses.definitionCN: 承认某事为真，常带有不情愿，尤指本想隐瞒的事
senses.example: She admitted that she had forgotten the appointment.
senses.exampleCN: 她承认自己忘了那个约会。
senses.why: The core is letting something in: a fact you kept outside is finally allowed through the door of your account.
senses.whyCN: 核心是「放进来」：一直被你挡在外面的事实，终于被放进自己的说法里。

senses.title: To allow someone to enter a place
senses.definition: to allow a person or thing to enter a building, room, or other place
senses.definitionCN: 允许某人或某物进入建筑、房间或其他场所
senses.example: The guard admitted us through the side gate.
senses.exampleCN: 守卫让我们从侧门进去。
senses.why: This is the physical core made literal: ad- means toward, and the person is sent toward the inside.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心意象的字面用法：ad- 表示「朝向」，人被送向里面。

senses.title: To accept someone into a group or institution
senses.titleCN: 准许加入（学校、组织、医院）
senses.definition: to allow someone to join a school, hospital, club, or other institution
senses.definitionCN: 允许某人进入学校、医院、俱乐部等机构
senses.example: He was admitted to the university on a full scholarship.
senses.exampleCN: 他获得全额奖学金被这所大学录取。
senses.why: An institution is a building with a membership; admitting someone opens both the door and the list.
senses.whyCN: 机构既是一栋楼，也是一份名单；admit 同时打开门和名单。

senses.title: To have room for
senses.definition: to have enough space for a number of people or things
senses.definitionCN: 有足够的空间容纳一定数量的人或物
senses.example: The hall admits only two hundred people.
senses.exampleCN: 这个大厅只能容纳两百人。
senses.why: The door can only let in as much as the room behind it can hold; here the limit is space itself.
senses.whyCN: 门能放进多少人，取决于门后房间能装下多少；这里的限制来自空间本身。

senses.title: To allow something to be possible
senses.definition: to allow a particular interpretation, possibility, or course of action, chiefly in the phrase admit of
senses.definitionCN: 容许某种解释、可能性或做法，主要用于短语 admit of
senses.example: The evidence admits of only one explanation.
senses.exampleCN: 这些证据只容许一种解释。
senses.why: A possibility is treated like a visitor: the case either has room for it or shuts it out.
senses.whyCN: 可能性被当作来访者：这件事要么给它留了位置，要么把它关在门外。

senses.title: To confess a wrongdoing
senses.definition: to state formally or under pressure that you did something wrong or illegal
senses.definitionCN: 正式或在压力下声明自己做了错事或违法的事
senses.example: The suspect admitted stealing the car.
senses.exampleCN: 嫌疑人供认偷了那辆车。
senses.why: Law turns the everyday door into a formal one: the truth is let into the record, not just into a conversation.
senses.whyCN: 法律把日常的门变成正式的门：事实被放进记录，而不仅是放进一次谈话。

senses.title: To accept evidence or an argument
senses.definition: to accept evidence, testimony, or an argument as valid and allow it into a case
senses.definitionCN: 承认证据、证词或论点的有效性，并允许其进入案件审理
senses.example: The court refused to admit the recording as evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 法院拒绝将该录音作为证据采纳。
senses.why: The courtroom is a room with strict entry rules; to admit is to let a piece of proof through those rules.
senses.whyCN: 法庭是一间有严格进入规则的房间；admit 就是让一份证据通过规则进门。

senses.title: To receive a patient into hospital
senses.definition: to take a patient into a hospital for treatment, usually in the passive
senses.definitionCN: 接收病人入院治疗，通常用被动形式
senses.example: She was admitted to hospital with severe chest pain.
senses.exampleCN: 她因严重胸痛被收治入院。
senses.why: The hospital door receives the patient; the passive voice keeps the focus on the person being let in.
senses.whyCN: 医院的门接收病人；被动语态把焦点放在被收进来的人身上。

intro.en: Admit is a Latin compound of a direction prefix and a verb of sending, and the whole family keeps the image of sending someone or something inward.
intro.cn: admit 是拉丁语中「方向前缀 + 送」构成的复合词，整个词族都保留着「把人或物送进去」的意象。

items.en: The send-verb is usually traced to a root of the form *mey-, but the reconstruction and its meaning are uncertain.
items.cn: 这个「送」的动词通常被追溯到 *mey- 一类词根，但构拟形式与含义都不确定。

items.en: Mittere meant 'to send, let go, release', and it also gives missile, mission and dismiss.
items.cn: mittere 意为「送、放、释放」，它还给出 missile、mission、dismiss。

items.en: Ad plus mittere formed admittere, 'to send to, let in, give access'. The prefix points the sending inward.
items.cn: ad 与 mittere 构成 admittere，意为「送到、放进去、给予进入」。前缀把「送」的方向指向内部。

items.en: Old French admetre carried the word toward English with both the entry sense and the sense of granting a claim.
items.cn: 古法语 admetre 把这个词带入英语，既带「进入」义，也带「认可某项主张」义。

items.en: The verb is recorded in the fifteenth century; the confession sense grows out of granting that a charge is true.
items.cn: 动词于十五世纪有记录；「供认」义从「认可某项指控为真」发展而来。

items.en: Institutional uses multiply: one is admitted to a school, a hospital, a bar, or a case record.
items.cn: 机构性用法不断增多：人被学校、医院、律师协会或案件记录接纳。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the noun and adjective forms built on the same Latin verb; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of confessing, conceding and allowing, which differ in willingness and formality.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁动词构成的名词与形容词形式；近义组收承认、让步与允许一类的动词，彼此在自愿程度与正式程度上不同。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of admitting, the right to enter, or a confession.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「准许进入、入场权、承认」。

entries.definition: The noun for the right to enter a place, narrower than admission.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「进入权」，比 admission 的适用范围窄。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning as one must concede.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「诚然、无可否认地」。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning allowed to be considered, especially in court.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可采纳的」，多用于法庭。

entries.definition: To state openly that you have done wrong, often formally and with full responsibility.
entries.definitionCN: 公开说明自己做了错事，常带正式与完全担责的意味，比 admit 更重。

entries.definition: To recognize that something is true without necessarily accepting blame.
entries.definitionCN: 承认某事为真，但不一定接受责任，语气比 admit 轻。

entries.definition: To accept a point only after resistance, often in an argument.
entries.definitionCN: 在争论中经过抵抗后才接受某一点，强调不情愿。

entries.definition: To permit something to happen or someone to enter, without the confessional sense.
entries.definitionCN: 允许某事发生或某人进入，不含「承认」义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin pieces of the word and the phrases it actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用这个词真实的拉丁构件，以及它实际出现的短语。

normal.en: ad- means toward and mittere means to send: admit is to send someone in.
normal.cn: ad- 表示「朝向」，mittere 表示「送」：admit 就是把某人送进去。

normal.en: The same send-root appears in mission, missile and dismiss.
normal.cn: 同一个「送」词根出现在 mission、missile、dismiss 里。

normal.en: Admit defeat is the phrase for conceding that you have lost.
normal.cn: admit defeat 是承认自己输了时用的短语。

normal.en: Be admitted to hospital means being received as a patient.
normal.cn: be admitted to hospital 意为作为病人被收治入院。

normal.en: A court admits evidence, and a school admits students: both are doors with rules.
normal.cn: 法庭采纳证据，学校录取学生：两者都是有规则的门。

abstract.en: Picture a door with a small ledger beside it: every person or fact that passes through is written down.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门旁边放着一本小册子：每个通过的人或事实都会被记下来。

abstract.en: A confession and an entrance are the same motion: something outside is brought inside and kept there.
abstract.cn: 供认与进入是同一种动作：外面的东西被带进里面，并留在那里。

abstract.en: What a door admits defines the room: a mind, a court and a hall are all shaped by what they let in.
abstract.cn: 一扇门放进什么，就定义了那间屋子：头脑、法庭与大厅都由它们允许进入的东西塑造。

examples.en: He admitted his mistake only after the evidence was shown.
examples.cn: 直到证据被摆出来，他才承认自己的错误。

examples.en: Only ticket holders will be admitted to the gallery.
examples.cn: 只有持票者才被允许进入画廊。

examples.en: The small clinic admits about thirty patients each day.
examples.cn: 这家小诊所每天收治约三十名病人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德米特」——阿德推门放人进：承认、准入

root: 拉丁语 ad-（朝向）+ mittere（送、放）构成 admittere，字面为「送进去、准许进入」，由「让人进门」引申出「让事实进入自己的说法」，即承认。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of admit all involve letting something pass a boundary: a fact into your account, a person into a place, a student into a school, a crowd into a hall, a possibility into a case, a crime into a confession, evidence into a record, a patient into a ward.
sensesIntro.cn: admit 的八个义项都涉及让某物越过一道边界：事实进入自己的说法、人进入场所、学生进入学校、人群进入大厅、可能性进入案件、罪行进入供词、证据进入记录、病人进入病房。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heavy door swings open and something waiting outside is brought through it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇厚重的门打开，等在门外的东西被带了进来。

branches.en: THE ENTRY LINE: a place, school, hospital or club lets a person through its door.
branches.cn: 进入线：场所、学校、医院或俱乐部让人通过它们的门。

branches.en: THE TRUTH LINE: a fact or a crime, once kept outside, is finally let into the speaker's account.
branches.cn: 真相线：原本被挡在外面的事实或罪行，最终被放进说话者的说法里。

branches.en: THE CAPACITY LINE: the door can only pass as much as the room behind it can hold.
branches.cn: 容量线：门只能放进门后房间装得下的那么多。

branches.en: THE PERMISSION LINE: a possibility or a piece of evidence is allowed inside a case.
branches.cn: 许可线：一种可能性或一份证据被允许进入案件。

branches.en: THE CARE LINE: a hospital receives a patient and keeps the person inside for treatment.
branches.cn: 照护线：医院接收病人，并把这个人留在里面接受治疗。

intro.en: Admit is built from a Latin prefix and a Latin send-verb; English adds ordinary noun and adjective suffixes to make the family.
intro.cn: admit 由拉丁语前缀与「送」动词构成；英语再用普通的名词、形容词后缀扩展出这一词族。

latinIntro.en: Mittere, admittere and admissio are all recorded in Latin, so only the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: mittere、admittere 与 admissio 在拉丁语中都有记录，只有更早的印欧词根属于重构形式。

items.example: The prefix directs the sending inward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「送」的方向指向内部。

items.example: It is the send-root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这一词族的「送」词根。

items.example: The compound is the direct source of the English verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词是英语动词的直接来源。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -sion 构成，义为「承认；准许进入；入场费」
由动词加 -ance 构成，义为「进入权」
由过去分词加 -ly 构成，义为「诚然」
由动词加 -ible 构成，义为「可采纳的」

definition_zh: 告诫；警告；责备；劝告；训诫
definition_en: to warn, advise, or criticize someone firmly, usually without anger, so that they avoid a mistake
core_image: 有人在耳边轻敲一下，提醒你别走错
scene: 训练结束后，教练把几名队员叫到一旁，低声说出迟到的问题。The coach admonished the players for arriving late to training.
sceneCN: 这里 admonish 是「责备、告诫」（第 2 个义项：因过失而温和地批评）；句意为教练因队员训练迟到而责备了他们。图中可辨识物件：训练场、秒表、队服。

pos.zh: 告诫；警告；责备；劝告

derivatives.zh: 由动词词干加 -ition 构成，义为「告诫；警告；责备」
由词干加 -ory 构成，义为「告诫的；警告性的」
由动词加 -ment 构成，义为「告诫；训诫」
由动词加 -er 构成，义为「告诫者」

senses.title: To warn someone firmly
senses.definition: to warn someone strongly about a danger or a likely mistake, so that they avoid it
senses.definitionCN: 就某种危险或可能的错误强烈提醒某人，使其避开
senses.example: The guide admonished us not to swim beyond the reef.
senses.exampleCN: 向导告诫我们不要游到礁石之外。
senses.why: The word carries a reminder that comes as a tap on the shoulder: the warning arrives before the harm, not after.
senses.whyCN: 这个词带着「肩头被轻敲一下」的提醒：警告在伤害之前到达，而不是之后。

senses.title: To rebuke mildly
senses.definition: to criticize someone for a fault in a quiet, corrective way rather than with anger
senses.definitionCN: 以平静、纠正性的方式批评某人的过失，而不是发怒
senses.example: The teacher admonished the boy for talking during the test.
senses.exampleCN: 老师责备那个男孩考试时讲话。
senses.why: A rebuke here is still a reminder: the fault is named so that it will not be repeated, not to humiliate.
senses.whyCN: 这里的责备仍是一种提醒：指出过失是为了不再重犯，而不是为了羞辱。

senses.title: To remind someone of a duty
senses.definition: to remind a person of a responsibility or an obligation they must not forget
senses.definitionCN: 提醒某人不要忘记某项责任或义务
senses.example: The judge admonished the jury to weigh the evidence carefully.
senses.exampleCN: 法官提醒陪审团仔细权衡证据。
senses.why: The oldest layer of the word is simply to put something into someone's mind, and a duty is exactly what must be kept there.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的一层就是「把事情放进某人心里」，而职责正是必须一直放在那里的东西。

senses.title: To urge earnestly
senses.definition: to urge someone seriously to do or avoid something, often in a formal setting
senses.definitionCN: 郑重敦促某人去做或避免某事，常用于正式场合
senses.example: The doctor admonished him to rest for a full week.
senses.exampleCN: 医生郑重劝他休息整整一周。
senses.why: Urging is a warning turned forward: instead of describing the danger, the speaker presses a course of action on the listener.
senses.whyCN: 敦促是把警告转向前方：说话者不再描述危险，而是把某个做法压到听者身上。

senses.title: To counsel morally
senses.definition: to give moral or religious counsel, often from a position of authority
senses.definitionCN: 从权威位置给出道德或宗教上的训导
senses.example: The elder admonished the young men to keep their promises.
senses.exampleCN: 长者训诫年轻人要守信。
senses.why: Authority gives the reminder weight: the same words from a stranger would be advice, but from an elder they are a charge.
senses.whyCN: 权威给提醒增加了分量：同样的话出自陌生人之口只是建议，出自长者之口便成了训诫。

senses.title: To caution against a consequence
senses.definition: to point out the bad consequence that will follow if a warning is ignored
senses.definitionCN: 指出若无视警告将会出现的坏后果
senses.example: The inspector admonished the company against ignoring the safety rules.
senses.exampleCN: 检查员警告该公司不要无视安全规定。
senses.why: The reminder is paired with a forecast: the door is still open, but the speaker describes what lies behind it.
senses.whyCN: 提醒配上了一个预报：门还开着，但说话者描述门后有什么。

senses.title: To issue an official reprimand
senses.definition: to record a formal reprimand, especially in law, employment, or a disciplinary process
senses.definitionCN: 记录正式申诫，多用于法律、雇佣或纪律程序
senses.example: The court admonished the witness for refusing to answer.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭就证人拒答一事对其予以申诫。
senses.why: Once the reminder is written down, a private tap becomes a public record, and the word enters official language.
senses.whyCN: 提醒一旦被写下来，私下的一记轻敲就变成公开记录，这个词也由此进入官方语言。

senses.title: To urge someone to do something
senses.definition: to press someone to carry out an action, in the pattern admonish someone to do something
senses.definitionCN: 以 admonish someone to do something 的结构催促某人采取行动
senses.example: She admonished her brother to call their mother more often.
senses.exampleCN: 她敦促弟弟多给母亲打电话。
senses.why: The reminder has a target: it is not only about what to avoid, but about the act that should now be performed.
senses.whyCN: 提醒有了目标：不只是要避开什么，还包括现在就应该去做的那件事。

intro.en: Admonish comes from a Latin verb of reminding, and its family is full of words about warning, memory and advice.
intro.cn: admonish 来自一个表示「提醒」的拉丁动词，它的词族里满是与警告、记忆和建议有关的词。

items.en: The warning root is often connected with *men-, 'to think, mind', but the reconstruction is not certain.
items.cn: 这个「警告」词根常与 *men-「思考、心智」联系起来，但构拟并不确定。

items.en: Monere meant 'to warn, remind, advise', and it also produced monitor and monument.
items.cn: monere 意为「警告、提醒、建议」，它还生出 monitor 与 monument。

items.en: Ad plus monere formed admonere, 'to remind, warn, urge'. The prefix adds direction rather than intensity.
items.cn: ad 与 monere 构成 admonere，意为「提醒、警告、敦促」。前缀加的是方向，而不是强度。

items.en: Old French amonester carried the word into English, where the Latin d was restored by later spelling.
items.cn: 古法语 amonester 把词带入英语，后来的拼写又恢复了拉丁语的 d。

items.en: The verb appears in the fourteenth century with the senses of warning, advising and reproving already together.
items.cn: 动词于十四世纪出现，警告、建议与责备三个义项当时已经并存。

items.en: Legal and workplace usage adds a formal reprimand, while everyday usage keeps the quiet corrective tone.
items.cn: 法律与职场用法增加了正式申诫一义，日常用法则保留平静纠正的语气。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same Latin warning root; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of warning and criticism, which differ in force and in who has the authority to speak.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「警告」词根构成的词；近义组收警告与批评类动词，彼此在力度和说话者权威上不同。

entries.definition: The noun for a warning or a mild rebuke.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「告诫、温和的责备」。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning serving as a warning.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「警告性的、告诫的」。

entries.definition: The noun for the act or result of admonishing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「告诫、训诫」这一行为或结果。

entries.definition: A noun or verb from the same warning root, now about watching rather than correcting.
entries.definitionCN: 同词根的名词或动词，现代义偏向「监测」而不是「纠正」。

entries.definition: To tell someone about a danger so that they can avoid it, without implying a fault.
entries.definitionCN: 告知危险以便对方避开，不暗示对方已有过失，语气更中性。

entries.definition: To criticize someone sharply because they have done something wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 因对方做错事而尖锐批评，力度比 admonish 强。

entries.definition: To give an official or formal scolding, especially in work or the armed forces.
entries.definitionCN: 给予正式或官方的斥责，多用于职场或军队。

entries.definition: To advise someone to be careful, usually before any fault has occurred.
entries.definitionCN: 建议对方小心，通常发生在过失之前，强调预防。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin warning root and the patterns the verb actually takes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁「警告」词根，以及这个动词实际采用的句型。

normal.en: monere means to warn or remind: admonish is a warning aimed at a particular person.
normal.cn: monere 意为「警告、提醒」：admonish 就是对准某个人的警告。

normal.en: The same root gives monitor and monument, both about keeping something in mind.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 monitor 与 monument，两者都与「把某事记在心里」有关。

normal.en: Admonish someone for a fault, and admonish someone against a danger.
normal.cn: 因过失用 admonish someone for，针对危险用 admonish someone against。

normal.en: The -ish here is not the English suffix meaning like; it came from an Old French verb ending.
normal.cn: 这里的 -ish 不是英语中表示「像……」的后缀，它来自古法语动词词尾。

normal.en: Admonish keeps a quiet tone: it corrects without shouting.
normal.cn: admonish 保持平静的语气：它纠正人，但不喊叫。

abstract.en: Picture a hand tapping a shoulder just before a step is taken, not after the fall.
abstract.cn: 想象一只的手在迈步之前轻拍肩膀，而不是在摔倒之后。

abstract.en: The tap is the same whether it warns, reminds or reproves: someone is being steered back to the right line.
abstract.cn: 这记轻拍无论是警告、提醒还是责备都一样：有人在被引回正确的线上。

abstract.en: A written admonition is that tap turned into ink, which is why courts and employers can use it.
abstract.cn: 书面的 admonition 就是那记轻拍变成了墨迹，所以法庭和雇主都能使用它。

examples.en: The ranger admonished the hikers to carry enough water.
examples.cn: 护林员告诫徒步者要带够水。

examples.en: She was admonished for leaving the laboratory unlocked.
examples.cn: 她因没锁实验室的门而受到责备。

examples.en: His letter admonished the committee against a hasty decision.
examples.cn: 他的信告诫委员会不要仓促作出决定。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德莫尼什」——阿德敲桌提醒：告诫、责备

root: 拉丁语 ad-（朝向）+ monere（警告、提醒）构成 admonere，字面为「对着某人提醒」，故有告诫、劝告与温和责备三义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of admonish all deliver the same reminder in different settings: a danger to avoid, a fault to correct, a duty to keep, a course to follow, a moral charge, a consequence, an official record, or an act to perform.
sensesIntro.cn: admonish 的八个义项都在不同场合递出同一份提醒：要避开的危险、要纠正的过失、要记住的职责、要遵循的做法、道德上的训导、不良后果、官方记录，或应当去做的事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand taps a shoulder at the edge of a wrong step and points back to the right line.
core.cn: 核心意象：在即将迈错的一步边上，一只手轻拍肩膀，把人指回正确的线。

branches.en: THE DANGER LINE: the reminder arrives before harm and describes what waits if it is ignored.
branches.cn: 危险线：提醒在伤害之前到达，并说明若被无视会有什么等着。

branches.en: THE FAULT LINE: a fault already committed is named calmly so that it is not repeated.
branches.cn: 过失线：已经犯下的过失被平静地点出，为的是不再重犯。

branches.en: THE DUTY LINE: authority keeps a responsibility or a moral charge in the listener's mind.
branches.cn: 职责线：权威把某项责任或道德训导留在听者心里。

branches.en: THE ACTION LINE: the warning turns forward and presses a particular act on the listener.
branches.cn: 行动线：警告转向前方，把某个具体行动压到听者身上。

branches.en: THE RECORD LINE: the private tap becomes a written reprimand inside an institution.
branches.cn: 记录线：私下的一记轻敲变成机构内部的书面申诫。

intro.en: Admonish is a Latin prefix plus a Latin warning verb, with an Old French verb ending; English adds the noun and adjective suffixes.
intro.cn: admonish 由拉丁语前缀、拉丁「警告」动词和古法语动词词尾构成；英语再加入名词与形容词后缀。

latinIntro.en: Monere, admonere and admonitio are recorded in Latin, so no part of the core is reconstructed except the deeper Indo-European root.
latinIntro.cn: monere、admonere 与 admonitio 在拉丁语中都有记录，除更早的印欧词根外，核心部分都不属重构。

items.example: It aims the warning at a particular person.
items.exampleCN: 它把警告对准某个具体的人。

items.example: It is the warning root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这一词族的「警告」词根。

items.example: The compound is the direct source of the English verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词是英语动词的直接来源。

items.example: It is not the English suffix meaning like.
items.exampleCN: 它并不是英语中表示「像……」的后缀。

derivatives.zh: 由词干加 -ition 构成，义为「告诫；警告」
由词干加 -ory 构成，义为「警告性的」
由动词加 -ment 构成，义为「训诫」
由动词加 -er 构成，义为「告诫者」

definition_zh: 土坯；土坯砖；土坯建筑；制坯黏土
definition_en: a building material made of clay mixed with straw and dried in the sun, or a structure built from it
core_image: 太阳下晒干的泥砖，一块块垒成墙
scene: 沙漠边上的老教堂立了百余年，墙体没有一块烧制的砖。They built the walls of the old mission from adobe bricks dried in the sun.
sceneCN: 这里 adobe 是「土坯砖」（第 1 个义项：用黏土和草料制成、经日晒定型的砖块）；句意为他们用晒干的土坯砖砌成了这座老传教站的墙。图中可辨识物件：泥砖、木模、烈日。

pos.zh: 土坯；土坯砖；土坯建筑
土坯做的（多作定语，如土坯房）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 brick 构成的复合词，义为「土坯砖」
由本词加 house 构成的复合词，义为「土坯房」
由本词加 wall 构成的复合词，义为「土坯墙」

senses.title: A sun-dried clay brick
senses.definition: a brick made of clay mixed with straw or dung, shaped in a mold and hardened by the sun rather than by fire
senses.definitionCN: 用黏土掺草或粪料、在模具中成型、靠日晒而非火烧变硬的砖
senses.example: The workers laid adobe bricks in rows to dry.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们把土坯砖成排摆开晾晒。
senses.why: The word names the single unit first: the brick you can pick up is the most concrete thing the term can point to.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最先指的是单个单位：能拿在手里的那块砖，是这个词能指的最具体的东西。

senses.title: The building material as a mass
senses.definition: the clay-and-straw mixture used as a building material, treated as an uncountable mass
senses.definitionCN: 用作建筑材料的黏土与草料混合物，作不可数物质名词
senses.example: The floor was packed with adobe taken from the riverbank.
senses.exampleCN: 地面用从河岸取来的土坯料夯成。
senses.why: From single bricks the word moves to the substance they are made of, the way brick can mean both one block and the material.
senses.whyCN: 从单块砖出发，这个词又指做砖的物质，正如 brick 既可指一块砖，也可指砖这种材料。

senses.title: A building made of adobe
senses.definition: a house or other structure whose walls are built of adobe
senses.definitionCN: 墙体用土坯砌成的房屋或其他建筑
senses.example: They restored the adobe at the end of the street.
senses.exampleCN: 他们修复了街尾那栋土坯房。
senses.why: A material can stand for the thing made from it; here the walls are so much the identity of the building that the substance becomes its name.
senses.whyCN: 材料可以代指用它做成的东西；在这里墙体几乎就是建筑的身份，于是材料名成了建筑名。

senses.title: The raw clay mixture
senses.definition: the wet clay mixture, before shaping and drying, from which adobe bricks are made
senses.definitionCN: 尚未成型晾干、用来制土坯砖的湿黏土混合物
senses.example: Straw was folded into the adobe to stop it cracking.
senses.exampleCN: 人们把草料揉进制坯黏土里，防止它开裂。
senses.why: This is the material one step earlier in time, still soft and shapeless, before the sun gives it a form.
senses.whyCN: 这是时间上更早一步的材料，还软着、没有形状，等着太阳给它一个形态。

senses.title: Adobe as an architectural style
senses.definition: the style of construction associated with adobe, common in dry regions of the Americas and the Middle East
senses.definitionCN: 与土坯相关的一种建造风格，常见于美洲干旱地区与中东
senses.example: The hotel imitates the adobe of the American Southwest.
senses.exampleCN: 这家旅馆模仿美国西南部的土坯建筑风格。
senses.why: When a material becomes regional, its name can label a whole way of building rather than a single wall.
senses.whyCN: 当一种材料带上了地域色彩，它的名字就能标记一整套建造方式，而不只是一面墙。

senses.title: The regional building tradition
senses.definition: the craft and tradition of building with earth, tied to dry climates and communities with limited timber
senses.definitionCN: 与干旱气候、木材匮乏的社区相联系的夯土建造技艺与传统
senses.example: Adobe is still a living tradition in many desert villages.
senses.exampleCN: 在许多沙漠村落，土坯建造仍是活着的传统。
senses.why: The word carries a climate behind it: where rain and fuel are scarce, sun and earth do the work of kiln and timber.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后带着一种气候：在雨水与燃料稀缺的地方，太阳和泥土代替了窑炉与木材。

senses.title: Unfired brick, as opposed to fired brick
senses.titleCN: 未经烧制的砖（区别于烧结砖）
senses.definition: brick hardened by air and sun alone, contrasted with brick fired in a kiln
senses.definitionCN: 仅靠空气与日晒变硬的砖，与窑中烧制的砖相对
senses.example: Adobe is cheaper than fired brick but far less resistant to rain.
senses.exampleCN: 土坯比烧结砖便宜，但耐雨性差得多。
senses.why: The defining contrast is the absence of fire: what makes the material adobe is exactly what has not been done to it.
senses.whyCN: 定义性的对照是「没有火」：这种材料之所以是土坯，正因为它没有被火烧过。

senses.title: A plain, earthy image
senses.definition: in figurative use, the quality of being plain, earthy, and close to the ground, as in an adobe-colored landscape
senses.definitionCN: 用于比喻时指朴素、土气、贴近大地的质感，如土坯色的风景
senses.example: The whole town seemed washed in adobe light at dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 黄昏时整座小镇仿佛被土坯色的光洗过。
senses.why: A material named after mud carries the feel of mud: warm, matte, low to the ground, and unpolished.
senses.whyCN: 以泥土得名的材料带着泥土的质感：温暖、哑光、贴近地面、不加修饰。

intro.en: Adobe is not a Latin word at all: it travelled from Egyptian through Coptic and Arabic into Spanish, and only then into English.
intro.cn: adobe 根本不是拉丁词：它从埃及语经科普特语、阿拉伯语进入西班牙语，最后才进入英语。

items.en: Egyptian recorded a word for brick written with the consonants db; the exact vowels are uncertain because the script omits them.
items.cn: 埃及语有一个表示「砖」的词，书写只留辅音 db；由于文字不标元音，确切读音不确定。

items.en: Coptic tōbe continued the Egyptian word and meant 'brick', the form that later speakers actually pronounced.
items.cn: 科普特语 tōbe 延续了埃及语的这个词，意为「砖」，这是后来使用者真正读出来的形式。

items.en: Arabic borrowed the word as ṭūb, and with the definite article it appears as al-ṭūb, 'the brick'.
items.cn: 阿拉伯语借入后作 ṭūb，加上定冠词则作 al-ṭūb，意为「那砖」。

items.en: Spanish took al-ṭūb and ran the article into the noun, giving adobe; the same thing happened to algebra and alcohol.
items.cn: 西班牙语借入 al-ṭūb 时把冠词并进了名词，得到 adobe；algebra 与 alcohol 也经历了同样的合并。

items.en: In Mexican Spanish adobe named the sun-dried brick of the region, and from there the building technique.
items.cn: 在墨西哥西班牙语中，adobe 指当地日晒而成的土砖，并由此指这种建造技术。

items.en: English adopted the word through American Spanish; early records describe the material in the American Southwest and Mexico.
items.cn: 英语经美洲西班牙语借入这个词；早期记录描述的是美国西南部与墨西哥的这种材料。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that resemble adobe in sound or spelling but come from unrelated sources; the near-meaning group gathers earth-building materials and their units.
note.cn: 形近组收读音或拼写与 adobe 相近、但来源无关的词；近义组收泥土类建材及其单位。

entries.definition: A dwelling or home, from the verb abide, with no connection to clay.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「住所、家」，来自动词 abide，与泥土无关。

entries.definition: A Philippine and Latin American dish or marinade, from Spanish adobar, to marinate.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指菲律宾与拉美的腌渍菜或腌料，来自西班牙语 adobar「腌」。

entries.definition: An informal Southwestern American shortening of adobe, used for the material or a building.
entries.definitionCN: 美国西南部的口语缩略形式，指土坯材料或土坯房。

entries.definition: The fine-grained earth that is the main ingredient of adobe, before straw or shaping.
entries.definitionCN: 细粒泥土，是土坯的主要原料，尚未加草或成型。

entries.definition: A rectangular block used in building, whether fired, concrete, or sun-dried.
entries.definitionCN: 用于建造的长方块，可烧制、混凝土制或日晒而成，是土坯砖的上位词。

entries.definition: A mixture of clay, sand and straw used in earth building, but shaped by hand rather than in molds.
entries.definitionCN: 黏土、沙与草的混合物，也用于泥土建造，但用手塑形而非模具成型。

entries.definition: Fired clay used in building and sculpture, the kiln-made opposite of adobe.
entries.definitionCN: 经窑火烧制的陶土，用于建筑与雕塑，是土坯的「窑制」对立面。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the word's real travel route and the terms it actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用这个词真实的传播路线，以及它实际出现的说法。

normal.en: The Arabic article al- is still inside the word: al-ṭūb became adobe, just as al-jabr became algebra.
normal.cn: 阿拉伯语冠词 al- 还留在词里：al-ṭūb 变成 adobe，正如 al-jabr 变成 algebra。

normal.en: The same brick word reached Spanish and then English through Mexico.
normal.cn: 同一个「砖」词经墨西哥进入西班牙语，再进入英语。

normal.en: Adobe is dried by the sun, never fired in a kiln.
normal.cn: 土坯靠太阳晒干，从不在窑里烧。

normal.en: Adobe brick, adobe wall and adobe house are the three common compounds.
normal.cn: adobe brick、adobe wall 与 adobe house 是三个常见复合词。

normal.en: The word is tied to dry lands, where timber is scarce and sun is plentiful.
normal.cn: 这个词与干旱地区相连，那里木材稀缺、日照充足。

abstract.en: Picture a brick lying on hot sand with no kiln in sight: the sun is the only tool.
abstract.cn: 想象一块砖躺在滚烫的沙上，四下没有窑：太阳是唯一的工具。

abstract.en: The same lump of earth can be a wall, a house, a tradition or a color, depending on how far you step back.
abstract.cn: 同一团泥土可以是墙、是房子、是传统，也可以是一种颜色，取决于你退后多远看。

abstract.en: A material that needs no fire is a material that remembers the place it came from.
abstract.cn: 一种不需要火的材料，就是一种记得自己来自何处的材料。

examples.en: The old church is made entirely of adobe.
examples.cn: 这座老教堂完全由土坯建成。

examples.en: They mixed straw into the adobe to keep the walls from cracking.
examples.cn: 他们在土坯里掺入草料，防止墙体开裂。

examples.en: An adobe house stays cool in the desert heat.
examples.cn: 土坯房在沙漠的酷热中能保持凉爽。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿兜比」——阿兜一捧泥，晒成砖：土坯

root: 经西班牙语 adobe 来自阿拉伯语 al-ṭūb（那砖），更早可追至科普特语 tōbe 与埃及语表示「砖」的词；冠词 al- 并入了名词，故英语词首看似前缀而非前缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of adobe move from the single sun-dried brick to the material, the building, the raw mixture, the regional style, the tradition, the unfired contrast with kiln brick, and finally the plain earthy image.
sensesIntro.cn: adobe 的八个义项从单块日晒砖出发，依次扩展到材料、建筑、湿坯、地域风格、建造传统、与窑砖相对的不烧制特征，最后落到朴素土质的意象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wet clay brick sits in a wooden mold under a hard sun, hardening without any fire.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块湿泥砖躺在木模里，烈日之下慢慢变硬，全程没有火。

branches.en: THE UNIT LINE: one brick, and specifically one that has dried in the sun rather than in a kiln.
branches.cn: 单位线：一块砖，且特指日晒而非窑烧而成的那一种。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL LINE: the mixture as a mass, first wet and shapeless, then set into a usable substance.
branches.cn: 材料线：作为物质的混合物，先是湿软无定形，后来定成可用的材料。

branches.en: THE BUILDING LINE: walls of adobe stand for the house they enclose.
branches.cn: 建筑线：土坯墙代指它所围起的房屋。

branches.en: THE REGION LINE: a material tied to dry climates becomes a style and a living craft.
branches.cn: 地域线：与干旱气候相连的材料，成为风格与活着的技艺。

branches.en: THE FEELING LINE: the color and texture of earth pass into a plain, unpolished image.
branches.cn: 质感线：泥土的颜色与质地转化为朴素、不加修饰的意象。

intro.en: Adobe has no English prefix or derivational suffix of its own: its parts are Arabic and Coptic, and English only adds a plural and compound nouns.
intro.cn: adobe 本身没有英语前缀或派生后缀：它的构件来自阿拉伯语与科普特语，英语只加了复数与复合名词。

latinIntro.en: Adobe has no Latin root at all; it reached English through Spanish from Arabic and Coptic, so this section lists no Latin relatives.
latinIntro.cn: adobe 完全没有拉丁词根；它经西班牙语来自阿拉伯语与科普特语，因此本栏不列拉丁同族词。

items.example: It was absorbed into the noun in Spanish.
items.exampleCN: 这个冠词在西班牙语中被并进了名词。

items.example: It is the Arabic form borrowed by Spanish.
items.exampleCN: 这是被西班牙语借入的阿拉伯语形式。

items.example: It continues the older Egyptian word.
items.exampleCN: 它延续了更早的埃及语词。

items.example: Egyptian writing gives the consonants only.

items.meaning: used before a noun to name an adobe thing
items.meaningCN: 用于名词前，表示土坯制成的
items.example: It forms adobe brick and adobe wall.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 adobe brick 与 adobe wall。

items.example: It is used in the American Southwest.
The compound names the single unit.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词指单个砖块。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 brick 构成，义为「土坯砖」
由本词加 house 构成，义为「土坯房」
由本词加 wall 构成，义为「土坯墙」

definition_zh: 青春期；青少年时期；青春；成长过渡期
definition_en: the period between childhood and adulthood, when the body and mind are still growing
core_image: 正在长高的身体，站在童年与成年之间
scene: 夏天的院子里，孩子一年蹿高了一头，声音也变了。Her adolescence was spent moving between three different towns.
sceneCN: 这里 adolescence 是「青少年时期」（第 2 个义项：童年与成年之间的年龄段）；句意为她的青少年时期是在三个不同小镇之间搬来搬去中度过的。图中可辨识物件：行李箱、身高刻度、院墙。

pos.zh: 青春期；青少年时期；青春

derivatives.zh: 由词干加 -ent 构成，义为「青少年；青春期的」
由词干加 -esce 构成的罕用动词，义为「进入青春期、渐渐长成」
由前缀 pre- 加 adolescent 构成，义为「青春期前的；青春期前的孩子」

senses.title: The physical stage of growing up
senses.definition: the stage of physical development when a child's body matures into an adult body
senses.definitionCN: 儿童身体发育为成年身体的生理阶段
senses.example: Rapid growth is one of the clearest signs of adolescence.
senses.exampleCN: 快速长高是青春期最明显的标志之一。
senses.why: The Latin verb underneath means to grow up, so the word begins as a description of the body changing size and shape.
senses.whyCN: 这个词底下的拉丁动词意为「长成」，所以它最初描述的是身体尺寸与形状的改变。

senses.title: The years between childhood and adulthood
senses.definition: the period of life, roughly the teenage years, between being a child and being an adult
senses.definitionCN: 人生中大致相当于十几岁、介于儿童与成年之间的那段时期
senses.example: He spent most of his adolescence in a small coastal town.
senses.exampleCN: 他的青少年时期大部分是在一座海边小镇度过的。
senses.why: Once the body's growth defines a span of years, the word naturally names that span as a chapter of a life.
senses.whyCN: 一旦身体的成长划定了一段年数，这个词自然就用来命名人生中的那一章。

senses.title: Youth as a quality
senses.definition: the quality or spirit associated with being young, especially energy, uncertainty and openness
senses.definitionCN: 与年轻相联系的气质或精神，尤其是活力、不确定与开放
senses.example: There was still something of adolescence in his enthusiasm.
senses.exampleCN: 他的热情里还留着一点青春的东西。
senses.why: A period of time can stand for the temper of that time; the word then describes a mood rather than a birthday.
senses.whyCN: 一段时间可以代指那段时间的心气；于是这个词描述的是心境，而不是年龄数字。

senses.title: A transitional period of growth
senses.definition: any transitional period in which something is developing toward its mature form
senses.definitionCN: 任何向成熟形态发展中的过渡阶段
senses.example: The project is still in its adolescence and needs patient support.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目仍处在成长期，需要耐心的支持。
senses.why: The core image of standing between two states can be lifted off the human body and applied to anything still forming.
senses.whyCN: 「站在两种状态之间」的核心意象可以从人的身体上摘下来，用在任何仍在成形的事物上。

senses.title: The emotional turbulence of the teens
senses.definition: the emotional instability and identity-seeking often associated with the teenage years
senses.definitionCN: 常与十几岁相联系的情绪不稳与自我寻找
senses.example: Her adolescence was full of sudden moods and long silences.
senses.exampleCN: 她的青春期充满突如其来的情绪和长久的沉默。
senses.why: Because the body is between two shapes, the mind is heard as between two selves, and the word picks up that turmoil.
senses.whyCN: 因为身体处在两种形态之间，心灵也被听成处在两个自我之间，这个词便带上了那层动荡。

senses.title: The state of being adolescent
senses.definition: the condition or fact of being adolescent, considered as a state rather than a period
senses.definitionCN: 作为状态而非时间段来看的「处于青春期」这一事实
senses.example: Adolescence, for him, was a condition rather than a number of years.
senses.exampleCN: 对他来说，青春期是一种状态，而不是若干年。
senses.why: The -ence ending turns the growing person into a state; the same root can name a condition as well as a stage.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ence 把「正在长成的人」变成一种状态；同一词根既能命名阶段，也能命名境况。

senses.title: The demographic age group
senses.definition: the population cohort defined by adolescence, used in statistics, policy and medicine
senses.definitionCN: 以青春期界定的统计人口群体，用于统计、政策与医学
senses.example: The clinic has a separate ward for adolescence.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所为青少年设有单独病区。
senses.why: Institutions need a countable group, so a stage of life is frozen into a category with numbers attached.
senses.whyCN: 机构需要一个可计数的群体，于是一段人生阶段被固定成带数字的分类。

senses.title: The early stage of anything
senses.definition: in literary or figurative use, the early, unformed stage of an institution, art form or idea
senses.definitionCN: 用于文学或比喻时，指机构、艺术形式或观念的早期、未定型阶段
senses.example: Film was still in its adolescence when sound arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 声音出现时，电影仍处在它的成长期。
senses.why: The human life course is the readiest template for any growth story, so the word can lend its stages to things that never had a body.
senses.whyCN: 人的生命历程是任何成长故事最现成的模板，于是这个词能把自己的阶段借给从未有过身体的事物。

intro.en: Adolescence is built on a Latin verb for growing up, and its family includes adult and a set of words about nourishment.
intro.cn: adolescence 建立在一个表示「长成」的拉丁动词上，它的词族包括 adult 以及一组与滋养有关的词。

items.en: The nourishment root is generally reconstructed as *al-, 'to nourish, grow', though its wider connections are debated.
items.cn: 这个「滋养」词根一般被构拟为 *al-「滋养、生长」，但它更广的联系仍有争论。

items.en: Alere meant 'to nourish, feed', and it also stands behind aliment and alimony.
items.cn: alere 意为「滋养、喂养」，aliment 与 alimony 也出自它。

items.en: The inchoative form alescere meant 'to begin to grow, grow up', naming growth as a process that starts.
items.cn: 表示「开始」的 alescere 意为「开始生长、长成」，把生长命名为一个起步的过程。

items.en: Ad plus alescere formed adolescere, 'to grow up'. The same verb gives adultus, the past participle behind adult.
items.cn: ad 与 alescere 构成 adolescere「长成」；同一动词的过去分词 adultus 就是 adult 的来源。

items.en: Adolescentia named the state of growing up; English took the stem and added its own -ence.
items.cn: adolescentia 指「正在长成的状态」；英语取其词干，再加上自己的 -ence。

items.en: The English noun is recorded in the fifteenth century, first in medical and then in general use.
items.cn: 英语名词于十五世纪有记录，先用于医学，后进入一般用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same Latin growth verb; the near-meaning group gathers terms for the same life stage, which differ in register and in what they measure.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「生长」动词构成的词；近义组收同一人生阶段的说法，彼此在语体与衡量对象上不同。

entries.definition: A noun or adjective for a person in adolescence, or for the stage itself.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，指处于青春期的少年，或指这一阶段本身。

entries.definition: A person who has finished growing up, from the past participle of the same Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 已经长成的人，来自同一拉丁动词的过去分词。

entries.definition: A rare verb meaning to enter or pass through adolescence.
entries.definitionCN: 罕用动词，义为「进入或经历青春期」。
