entries.definition: The physical process of sexual maturation, narrower and more biological than adolescence.
entries.definitionCN: 性成熟的生理过程，比 adolescence 更窄、更偏生物学。

entries.definition: The period or quality of being young, often extending beyond the teenage years.
entries.definitionCN: 年轻的时期或气质，范围常超出十几岁。

entries.definition: The years from thirteen to nineteen, a looser everyday label for the same span.
entries.definitionCN: 十三到十九岁这几年，是同一阶段的日常宽松说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin growth root and the words the term actually partners with.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁「生长」词根，以及这个词实际搭配的说法。

normal.en: alere means to nourish, and alescere means to begin growing: adolescence is growth that has started.
normal.cn: alere 意为「滋养」，alescere 意为「开始生长」：adolescence 就是已经起步的生长。

normal.en: The past participle adultus became adult, so adolescence is the road and adult is the arrival.
normal.cn: 过去分词 adultus 变成 adult，所以 adolescence 是路，adult 是到达。

normal.en: Adolescence is the period; adolescent is the person.
normal.cn: adolescence 指时期，adolescent 指人。

normal.en: Early adolescence and late adolescence split the same stage into two ends.
normal.cn: early adolescence 与 late adolescence 把同一阶段分成前后两端。

normal.en: The same nourishment root appears in aliment, food that feeds growth.
normal.cn: 同一个「滋养」词根出现在 aliment 里，那是喂养生长的食物。

abstract.en: Picture a body drawn between two outlines, the child's and the adult's, not yet filling either.
abstract.cn: 想象一个身体被画在两条轮廓之间，一条是孩子的，一条是成人的，哪条都还没填满。

abstract.en: Growth is a verb before it is a stage: the word names something still happening, never something completed.
abstract.cn: 生长先是动作，然后才是阶段：这个词命名的是仍在发生的事，而不是已经完成的事。

abstract.en: Give the same template to a film or a project and adolescence becomes any early, awkward, unfinished becoming.
abstract.cn: 把同一模板套到电影或项目上，adolescence 就成了任何早期、笨拙、尚未完成的成形过程。

examples.en: Adolescence brings rapid changes in both body and mood.
examples.cn: 青春期带来身体与情绪上的急速变化。

examples.en: She spent her adolescence in a house full of books.
examples.cn: 她的青少年时期是在一座满是书的房子里度过的。

examples.en: The industry is still in its adolescence and makes mistakes.
examples.cn: 这个行业仍处在成长期，还会犯错误。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德莱森斯」——阿德一天天拔高：青春期

root: 拉丁语 ad-（朝向）+ alescere（开始生长，源自 alere「滋养」）构成 adolescere「长成」，其名词 adolescentia 指正在长成的状态；同一动词的过去分词 adultus 即 adult 的来源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of adolescence move from the physical maturation of the body to the years it occupies, the mood of youth, any transitional growth, the emotional storms, the state itself, a counted population, and finally the early stage of anything.
sensesIntro.cn: adolescence 的八个义项从身体的发育成熟出发，依次到所占的那段年岁、青春的心气、任何过渡性的成长、情绪的风暴、状态本身、可计数的人群，最后到一切事物的初期阶段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body stands between a child's outline and an adult's outline, still filling out.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个身体站在孩子的轮廓与成人的轮廓之间，还在慢慢长满。

branches.en: THE BODY LINE: the word begins as a description of physical maturation.
branches.cn: 身体线：这个词最初描述的是身体的发育成熟。

branches.en: THE CALENDAR LINE: a stage of growth becomes a span of years and then a countable group.
branches.cn: 日历线：一个生长阶段变成一段年数，再变成可计数的群体。

branches.en: THE MOOD LINE: youth's energy and its storms are read as the temper of the stage.
branches.cn: 心境线：青春的活力与风暴被读成这个阶段的心气。

branches.en: THE TEMPLATE LINE: the same shape is lent to projects, industries and art forms in their early forming.
branches.cn: 模板线：同一形状被借给仍在早期成形中的项目、行业与艺术形式。

branches.en: THE STATE LINE: the -ence ending lets the growing person be named as a condition, not only a period.
branches.cn: 状态线：后缀 -ence 让「正在长成的人」被命名为一种境况，而不只是时间段。

intro.en: Adolescence is a Latin prefix plus a Latin growth verb, with a Latin noun ending replaced in English by -ence; the same stem yields adolescent.
intro.cn: adolescence 由拉丁语前缀与拉丁「生长」动词构成，拉丁名词词尾在英语里被替换成 -ence；同一词干还给出 adolescent。

latinIntro.en: Alere, alescere, adolescere and adolescentia are all recorded in Latin, so the core is documented rather than reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: alere、alescere、adolescere 与 adolescentia 在拉丁语中都有记录，核心部分有文献可查，不属重构。

items.example: It points growth toward its end.
It is the nourishment root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这一词族的「滋养」词根。

items.example: Its inchoative ending marks growth as starting.
items.exampleCN: 它的「起始」词尾标志生长开始。

items.example: It appears in alescere and adolescere.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 alescere 与 adolescere 中。

items.example: It appears in aliment, food that feeds growth.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 aliment 中，指喂养生长的食物。

derivatives.zh: 由词干加 -ent 构成，义为「青少年；青春期的」
由词干加 -esce 构成的罕用动词，义为「进入青春期」
由前缀 pre- 加 adolescent 构成，义为「青春期前的」

definition_zh: 青少年；青春期的；青少年的；不成熟的
definition_en: a young person who is between being a child and being an adult, or the stage such a person is in
core_image: 还没长满的身体，站在孩子与成人两条轮廓之间
scene: 操场边的长椅上，几个刚换过声的少年挤在一起，低头研究新手机。The adolescent boys on the bench kept comparing their new phones.
sceneCN: 这里 adolescent 是「青春期的（形容词）」（第 2 个义项：与青春期这一阶段相关的）；句意为长椅上的那几个青春期男孩一直在比较新手机。图中可辨识物件：长椅、手机、校服外套。

pos.zh: 青少年（处于童年与成年之间的人）
青春期的；青少年的；不成熟的

derivatives.zh: 由词干加 -ence 构成，义为「青春期；青少年时期」
由词干加 -esce 构成的罕用动词，义为「进入青春期」
由前缀 pre- 加本词构成，义为「青春期前的；青春期前的孩子」

senses.title: A young person between child and adult
senses.definition: a person who is no longer a child but not yet an adult, roughly in the teenage years
senses.definitionCN: 已不是儿童但尚未成年的人，大致处在十几岁的年纪
senses.example: The programme offers free advice to adolescents.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目为青少年提供免费咨询。
senses.why: The Latin participle behind the word means one who is growing up, so the person is named by an action still in progress.
senses.whyCN: 这个词背后的拉丁分词意为「正在长成的人」，所以这个人是被一个仍在进行的动作命名的。

senses.title: Relating to the teenage stage
senses.definition: of or relating to the period between childhood and adulthood
senses.definitionCN: 属于或关于童年与成年之间这段时期的
senses.example: Adolescent sleep patterns differ sharply from adult ones.
senses.exampleCN: 青春期的睡眠模式与成年人的差别很大。
senses.why: As an adjective the word does not name a person but marks whatever belongs to that stretch of growing.
senses.whyCN: 作形容词时，这个词不指人，而是标记属于那段成长岁月的任何事物。

senses.title: Immature or not fully formed
senses.definition: used of behaviour or ideas that seem childish rather than fully grown
senses.definitionCN: 用于形容仍显得孩子气、尚未成熟的行为或想法
senses.example: His adolescent humour wore thin after the first hour.
senses.exampleCN: 过了一个小时，他那套幼稚的幽默就让人腻了。
senses.why: If the body is not yet grown, the mind can be accused of the same unfinished state; the word becomes a mild reproach.
senses.whyCN: 身体尚未长成，心智便也被指为同样未完成；这个词于是带上了一点轻微的责难。

senses.title: The physical traits of the stage
senses.definition: the bodily changes typical of the stage, such as growth spurts and voice change
senses.definitionCN: 这一阶段典型的身体变化，如猛长个子、变声
senses.example: Adolescent growth can outrun a child's coordination.
senses.exampleCN: 青春期的生长速度可能超过孩子协调能力的发展。
senses.why: The word's first layer is the body: limbs lengthen faster than the person learns to use them.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初的一层就是身体：四肢变长，快过人学会使用它们的速度。

senses.title: The emotional weather of the teens
senses.definition: the mood swings, self-consciousness and risk-taking often seen in teenagers
senses.definitionCN: 青少年常见的情绪起伏、自我意识与冒险倾向
senses.example: Adolescent mood swings can exhaust the whole family.
senses.exampleCN: 青少年的情绪起伏能把全家人都累垮。
senses.why: A body between two shapes is felt as a self between two shapes, and the adjective carries that instability.
senses.whyCN: 处在两种形态之间的身体，被感受为处在两种形态之间的自我，这个形容词便带着那份不稳。

senses.title: In health and policy language
senses.titleCN: 青少年的（医疗与政策语境）
senses.definition: the label used by medicine, education and policy for the age group
senses.definitionCN: 医学、教育与政策用来指这一年龄群体的标签
senses.example: Adolescent clinics treat patients from twelve to eighteen.
senses.exampleCN: 青少年门诊收治十二到十八岁的病人。
senses.why: Institutions need a stable category, so a stage of growth is frozen into an age band with services attached.
senses.whyCN: 机构需要一个稳定的分类，于是一个成长阶段被固定成带服务的年龄段。

senses.title: Still developing, of an institution or art
senses.definition: in figurative use, still in an early stage and not yet fully mature
senses.definitionCN: 用于比喻时，仍处在早期、尚未完全成熟的
senses.example: The industry remains adolescent in its safety practices.
senses.exampleCN: 这个行业在安全规范上仍显稚嫩。
senses.why: The human growth curve is the readiest model for any institution, so a young industry is called adolescent.
senses.whyCN: 人的成长曲线是任何机构最现成的模型，于是年轻的行业被称为 adolescent。

senses.title: The youthful spirit in literature
senses.definition: in literary writing, the openness, awkwardness and energy of youth as a quality
senses.definitionCN: 在文学写作中，指青春的开放、笨拙与活力这一气质
senses.example: There was an adolescent brightness in her first poems.
senses.exampleCN: 她的第一批诗里有一种少年的明亮。
senses.why: A stage of life can stand for a temper of mind; the word then describes a quality that can outlast the years.
senses.whyCN: 一段人生可以代指一种心气；这个词于是描述的是一种能活过那些年的气质。

intro.en: Adolescent is the present participle of a Latin verb meaning to grow up, so the word literally names someone in the middle of growing.
intro.cn: adolescent 是拉丁语「长成」动词的现在分词，字面上命名的是一个正处在生长之中的人。

items.en: The nourishment root is usually reconstructed as *al-, but its wider family ties remain debated.
items.cn: 这个「滋养」词根通常被构拟为 *al-，但它更广的词族联系仍有争论。

items.en: Alere meant 'to nourish, feed'; the same root appears in aliment and alimony.
items.cn: alere 意为「滋养、喂养」；同一词根出现在 aliment 与 alimony 中。

items.en: The inchoative alescere meant 'to begin to grow', marking growth at its starting point.
items.cn: 表示起始的 alescere 意为「开始生长」，标出生长的起点。

items.en: Ad plus alescere gave adolescere, 'to grow up'. Its present participle adolescens is the direct source of the English word.
items.cn: ad 与 alescere 构成 adolescere「长成」，其现在分词 adolescens 就是英语词的直接来源。

items.en: The accusative form adolescentem passed through French and into English as both noun and adjective.
items.cn: 宾格形式 adolescentem 经法语进入英语，同时作名词与形容词。

items.en: English records the word in the fifteenth century; the critical 'immature' sense develops much later.
items.cn: 英语于十五世纪记录该词；带有批评意味的「不成熟」义要到很久以后才发展出来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the same Latin growth verb; the near-meaning group gathers labels for young people and for immaturity, which differ in formality and in legal force.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「生长」动词的各种形式；近义组收指称年轻人与不成熟的词，彼此在正式程度与法律效力上不同。

entries.definition: The noun for the stage itself rather than the person in it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指这一阶段本身，而不是处于其中的人。

entries.definition: The grown person at the end of the same process, from the past participle.
entries.definitionCN: 同一过程终点处的成年人，来自过去分词。

entries.definition: A rare verb meaning to grow toward adulthood.
entries.definitionCN: 罕用动词，义为「向成年生长」。

entries.definition: An adjective labelling the years from thirteen to nineteen, based on the number rather than on growth.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，按十三到十九岁这一数字区间来标记，依据年龄而非生长过程。

entries.definition: A formal or legal term for a young person below the age of responsibility.
entries.definitionCN: 正式或法律用语，指未达责任年龄的未成年人。

entries.definition: An adjective describing the qualities of youth, which may be kept long after the years have passed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，描述青春的特质，这种特质可在年岁过去后仍保留。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin participle and the collocations the word actually forms.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁分词，以及这个词实际构成的搭配。

normal.en: Adolescent is a participle, not a label: it means growing up, still in progress.
normal.cn: adolescent 是个分词，不是标签：它的意思是「正在长成」，仍在进行。

normal.en: The noun is adolescence and the finished person is adult; all three share one Latin verb.
normal.cn: 名词是 adolescence，长成的人是 adult；三者共用一个拉丁动词。

normal.en: Adolescent health and adolescent development are the standard institutional phrases.
normal.cn: adolescent health 与 adolescent development 是机构里的标准说法。

normal.en: The -ent ending is the same participial ending seen in different and dependent.
normal.cn: 这里的 -ent 与 different、dependent 中的分词词尾相同。

normal.en: Used of adults, adolescent is a mild criticism meaning unfinished.
normal.cn: 用在成年人身上时，adolescent 是轻微的批评，意为「还没长成」。

abstract.en: Picture a photograph taken mid-stride: the foot is off the ground, neither here nor there.
abstract.cn: 想象一张在迈步中途拍下的照片：脚离了地，既不在这里，也不在那里。

abstract.en: The word names motion, so it fits a person, a mood, an industry or an art that has not arrived.
abstract.cn: 这个词命名的是运动，所以它既能用于人，也能用于情绪、行业或尚未到位的艺术。

abstract.en: To call something adolescent is to say it is still on the road, which is both an excuse and a warning.
abstract.cn: 说某事物 adolescent，等于说它还在路上，这既是开脱，也是警告。

examples.en: The survey questioned two thousand adolescents about sleep.
examples.cn: 这项调查就睡眠问题询问了两千名青少年。

examples.en: Adolescent behaviour can look reckless because the brain is still rewiring.
examples.cn: 青少年的行为看似鲁莽，是因为大脑仍在重新接线。

examples.en: The company's adolescent stage ended when it hired a real finance team.
examples.cn: 这家公司招到真正的财务团队后，它的稚嫩阶段就结束了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德莱森特」——阿德正长个儿：青少年

root: 拉丁语 ad-（朝向）+ alescere（开始生长，源自 alere「滋养」）→ adolescere「长成」，其现在分词 adolescens 即「正在长成的人」，英语作名词指青少年、作形容词指青春期的。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of adolescent keep one idea: something is still growing. It names the person, the stage, the unfinished mind, the changing body, the unstable mood, an age band, a young institution and a literary brightness.
sensesIntro.cn: adolescent 的八个义项共有一个意思：某物仍在生长。它可指人、指阶段、指未完成的心智、指变化中的身体、指不稳的情绪、指一个年龄段、指年轻的机构，也指文学里的明亮。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure caught mid-step between a child's outline and an adult's outline.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人被定格在孩子的轮廓与成人的轮廓之间，正迈着步子。

branches.en: THE PERSON LINE: the participle names the one who is growing, and the stage that person is in.
branches.cn: 人物线：分词命名正在生长的人，以及此人所处的阶段。

branches.en: THE UNFINISHED LINE: whatever is not yet formed can be called adolescent, in reproach or in description.
branches.cn: 未完成线：凡是尚未成形的事物都可称为 adolescent，既可责难，也可描述。

branches.en: THE BODY LINE: the word keeps the physical changes of the stage in view.
branches.cn: 身体线：这个词始终保留着这一阶段的身体变化。

branches.en: THE MOOD LINE: instability and brightness are two readings of the same youthful weather.
branches.cn: 心境线：不稳与明亮是对同一种青春气候的两种读法。

branches.en: THE CATEGORY LINE: institutions turn the growing stage into an age band.
branches.cn: 分类线：机构把这一生长阶段变成一个年龄段。

intro.en: Adolescent is a Latin compound seen through its participle ending; English keeps -ent and builds adolescence and pre-adolescent from the same stem.
intro.cn: adolescent 是透过分词词尾看到的拉丁复合词；英语保留 -ent，并用同一词干构成 adolescence 与 pre-adolescent。

latinIntro.en: Alere, alescere, adolescere and the participle adolescens are all attested in Latin, so only the Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: alere、alescere、adolescere 与分词 adolescens 在拉丁语中都有文献，只有印欧词根属重构。

items.example: It adds the idea of starting.
The participle of this verb is the English word's source.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词的分词就是英语词的来源。

items.example: It marks the start of growth.

derivatives.zh: 由词干加 -ence 构成，义为「青春期」
由词干加 -esce 构成的罕用动词，义为「进入青春期」
由前缀 pre- 加本词构成，义为「青春期前的」

definition_zh: 收养；采纳；采用；采取；正式通过
definition_en: to take a child into your family legally, or to take up and start using an idea, method, name, or policy
core_image: 把原本不属于自己的人或做法接过来，当成自己的
scene: 民政窗口前，一对夫妻签完最后一份文件，把一个小女孩牵回了家。They adopted a five-year-old girl from a local orphanage.
sceneCN: 这里 adopt 是「收养」（第 1 个义项：依法把别人的孩子接为自己家庭的孩子）；句意为他们从当地孤儿院收养了一个五岁女孩。图中可辨识物件：签字笔、文件、孩子的小书包。

pos.zh: 收养；采纳；采用；采取；正式通过

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -tion 构成，义为「收养；采纳；通过」
由动词加 -ive 构成，义为「收养的；采用的」
由动词加 -er 构成，义为「收养人；采用者」
由动词加 -ee 构成，义为「被收养者」
由动词加 -able 构成，义为「可收养的；可采用的」

senses.title: To take a child legally as one's own
senses.definition: to take another person's child into your family and make that child your own in law
senses.definitionCN: 把别人的孩子接进自己的家庭，并在法律上使其成为自己的孩子
senses.example: The couple adopted a baby from the same city.
senses.exampleCN: 这对夫妻收养了同城的一个婴儿。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to choose for oneself: a child who was not born to you is chosen and brought into your line.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「为自己挑选」：不是自己亲生的孩子被选中，并接进自己的家系。

senses.title: To take up an idea or method
senses.definition: to decide to use an idea, method, plan, or system that came from elsewhere
senses.definitionCN: 决定使用来自别处的想法、方法、计划或制度
senses.example: The school adopted a new way of teaching reading.
senses.exampleCN: 学校采纳了一种新的阅读教学法。
senses.why: Choosing is the core: the idea existed before you, and you pick it up and make it yours by using it.
senses.whyCN: 核心是「挑选」：这个想法先于你存在，你把它拿起来，通过使用使它成为自己的。

senses.title: To take over a word or name
senses.definition: to begin to use a word, spelling, name, or title that belongs to another language or source
senses.definitionCN: 开始使用属于另一语言或来源的词、拼写、名称或头衔
senses.example: English adopted the word from French in the Middle Ages.
senses.exampleCN: 英语在中世纪从法语中采用了这个词。
senses.why: A borrowed word is like an adopted child of the language: it arrives from outside and is raised as one's own.
senses.whyCN: 借词就像语言收养的孩子：它从外面来，被当成自己的孩子养大。

senses.title: To take on an attitude or stance
senses.definition: to choose a particular attitude, position, or policy and act according to it
senses.definitionCN: 选择某种态度、立场或政策并据此行动
senses.example: The government adopted a firm line on the dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 政府在这场争端中采取了强硬立场。
senses.why: An attitude is not a physical child, but it is still taken up and worn, the way a stance is put on.
senses.whyCN: 态度不是有形的孩子，但它同样被拿起来、穿上，就像摆出一个姿势。

senses.title: To approve a text formally
senses.definition: to accept and approve a resolution, report, or set of rules in a formal meeting
senses.definitionCN: 在正式会议中接受并通过决议、报告或一套规则
senses.example: The committee adopted the report without amendment.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会未经修正即通过了这份报告。
senses.why: What a body formally takes into its own authority is adopted; approval is the institutional form of choosing.
senses.whyCN: 一个机构正式纳入自己权限的东西就是被 adopt；通过是「挑选」在制度上的形态。

senses.title: To take over a custom or practice
senses.definition: to take a custom or practice from another group and begin to follow it
senses.definitionCN: 从另一群体接过某种风俗或做法并开始遵循
senses.example: The village adopted the festival from its neighbours.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子从邻村承袭了这个节庆。
senses.why: A practice can be inherited sideways, not only downward; the word covers what a community chooses to take in.
senses.whyCN: 做法也能横向继承，而不只是向下传；这个词涵盖了社群选择接纳的东西。

senses.title: To select as a candidate
senses.definition: to choose a person as a candidate or representative, especially in politics
senses.definitionCN: 选定某人作为候选人或代表，多用于政治
senses.example: The party adopted her as its candidate for the seat.
senses.exampleCN: 该党选定她为该选区的候选人。
senses.why: Here the choosing is done by a group, and the chosen person is taken up as the group's own face.
senses.whyCN: 这里的挑选由群体完成，被选中的人被接过来，成为群体的面孔。

senses.title: To take on an identity or role
senses.definition: to accept and begin to live by a new identity, role, or set of beliefs
senses.definitionCN: 接受并开始按照新的身份、角色或信念生活
senses.example: He adopted a calm tone even when the room was angry.
senses.exampleCN: 即使满屋人都很愤怒，他也采用了一种平静的语气。
senses.why: The verb lets a person put on something new the way clothing is put on, and then be seen in it.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词让人像穿衣一样穿上一件新东西，然后以那个样子被看见。

intro.en: Adopt is built from a Latin verb of choosing, and the whole family keeps the idea of taking something as one's own.
intro.cn: adopt 建立在一个表示「挑选」的拉丁动词上，整个词族都保留着「把某物当作自己的」这一观念。

items.en: The choosing root is often linked to *op-, 'to choose, prefer', but the reconstruction is not settled.
items.cn: 这个「挑选」词根常与 *op-「挑选、偏好」相联系，但构拟尚未定论。

items.en: Optare meant 'to choose, wish for', and it also gives option and opt.
items.cn: optare 意为「挑选、希望」，它还给出 option 与 opt。

items.en: Ad plus optare formed adoptare, 'to choose for oneself, take as one's own'. The legal adoption sense is already Roman.
items.cn: ad 与 optare 构成 adoptare，意为「为自己挑选、当作自己的」。法律上的收养义在罗马时期已经存在。

items.en: Old French adopter carried the word into English with both the family and the general senses.
items.cn: 古法语 adopter 把这个词带入英语，家庭义与一般义同时带入。

items.en: English records the verb in the fifteenth century; the sense of adopting an opinion grows in the sixteenth.
items.cn: 英语于十五世纪记录该动词；「采纳意见」义在十六世纪发展起来。

items.en: The word spreads into committee language, where a body adopts a report or a resolution.
items.cn: 这个词扩展进委员会语言，机构由此「通过」报告或决议。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers nouns and adjectives from the same choosing verb; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of taking something up, which differ in whether the thing is a practice, a belief, or a person.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「挑选」动词构成的名词与形容词；近义组收「接过来」类动词，彼此在被接过之物是做法、信念还是人上不同。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of adopting a child, an idea, or a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「收养；采纳；通过」。

entries.definition: The adjective describing a relationship formed by adoption.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，描述通过收养形成的关系。

entries.definition: The noun for a person who adopts, whether a child or a method.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指收养孩子或采用方法的人。

entries.definition: The noun for the person who is adopted.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指被收养的人。

entries.definition: To accept an idea or change willingly and with approval.
entries.definitionCN: 自愿并赞同地接受某种观念或变化，带有热情。

entries.definition: To take on a role, duty, or quality, often without choosing it eagerly.
entries.definitionCN: 承担角色、职责或性质，常不带主动挑选的热情。

entries.definition: To raise a child in your home temporarily, without the legal permanence of adoption.
entries.definitionCN: 在家中临时抚养孩子，不具备收养的法律永久性。

entries.definition: To support and follow a belief or cause, usually in formal writing.
entries.definitionCN: 支持并奉行某种信念或事业，多用于正式书面语。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin choosing root and the collocations the verb actually takes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁「挑选」词根，以及这个动词实际构成的搭配。

normal.en: optare means to choose: adopt is to choose something and make it your own.
normal.cn: optare 意为「挑选」：adopt 就是选中某物并把它变成自己的。

normal.en: Option shares the root, which is why adopting is always picking one thing over another.
normal.cn: option 共享这个词根，所以采纳总是在若干选项中挑一个。

normal.en: You adopt a child, a policy, a name, an approach or a resolution.
normal.cn: 你可以收养孩子，也可以采纳政策、名称、方法或通过决议。

normal.en: Adoptive parents are the ones who adopt; the adoptee is the one adopted.
normal.cn: adoptive parents 是收养的一方，adoptee 是被收养的一方。

normal.en: A committee adopts a report, which means it formally takes it in.
normal.cn: 委员会 adopt 一份报告，意思是正式把它纳进来。

abstract.en: Picture a hand reaching across a fence and lifting something over to your side.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸过篱笆，把一样东西拿到自己这一边。

abstract.en: What is adopted changes sides: it belonged to another family, language, party or tradition, and now belongs here.
abstract.cn: 被 adopt 的东西换了边：它原本属于另一个家庭、语言、党派或传统，现在属于这里。

abstract.en: The word is about choice before it is about love: you adopt because you picked this thing out.
abstract.cn: 这个词先说的是选择，然后才说爱：你收养，是因为你把它挑了出来。

examples.en: They adopted their son when he was three months old.
examples.cn: 他们的儿子三个月大时被他们收养。

examples.en: The firm adopted stricter rules after the accident.
examples.cn: 事故之后，这家公司采用了更严格的规定。

examples.en: Many languages have adopted this word unchanged.
examples.cn: 许多语言都原样采用了这个词。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿道普特」——阿道把孩子抱回家：收养、采纳

root: 拉丁语 ad-（朝向）+ optare（挑选）构成 adoptare，意为「为自己挑选、当作自己的」；由「收养孩子」扩展到「采纳想法、采用词语、通过决议」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of adopt all describe choosing something from outside and making it your own: a child, an idea, a word, a stance, a text, a custom, a candidate, or an identity.
sensesIntro.cn: adopt 的八个义项都描述从外面挑中某物并据为己有：孩子、想法、词语、立场、文本、风俗、候选人，或一种身份。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaches over a boundary, picks something up and brings it to its own side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手越过边界，拿起一样东西，把它带到自己这一边。

branches.en: THE FAMILY LINE: a child from outside is chosen and given a permanent place in the family.
branches.cn: 家庭线：来自外面的孩子被选中，并在家庭中获得永久的位置。

branches.en: THE CULTURE LINE: ideas, words and customs are taken from elsewhere and put to use.
branches.cn: 文化线：想法、词语与风俗从别处接来，并投入使用。

branches.en: THE STANCE LINE: an attitude, tone or identity is put on and then worn.
branches.cn: 姿态线：态度、语气或身份被穿上，然后一直穿着。

branches.en: THE INSTITUTION LINE: a body formally takes a text into its own authority.
branches.cn: 机构线：一个机构把文本正式纳入自己的权限。

branches.en: THE POLITICAL LINE: a group chooses one person to be its public face.
branches.cn: 政治线：一个群体选出一个人作为对外的面孔。

intro.en: Adopt is a Latin prefix plus a Latin verb of choosing; English adds noun, adjective and agent suffixes to build the family.
intro.cn: adopt 由拉丁语前缀与表示「挑选」的拉丁动词构成；英语加入名词、形容词与施事后缀扩展词族。

latinIntro.en: Optare and adoptare are recorded in Latin; optio and adoptio are their nouns, so the core needs no reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: optare 与 adoptare 在拉丁语中有记录，optio 与 adoptio 是对应名词，核心部分无需重构。

items.example: It turns choosing into taking for oneself.
items.exampleCN: 它把「挑选」变成「为自己拿取」。

items.example: It is the choosing root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这一词族的「挑选」词根。

items.example: The compound is the direct source of the English verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词是英语动词的直接来源。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -tion 构成，义为「收养；采纳」
由动词加 -ive 构成，义为「收养的」
由动词加 -er 构成，义为「收养人；采用者」
由动词加 -ee 构成，义为「被收养者」

definition_zh: 可爱的；讨人喜欢的；惹人怜爱的
definition_en: so lovable or charming that people want to hold, protect, or admire the person or thing
core_image: 让人忍不住想伸手抱一下的小东西
scene: 沙发旁，小狗把头搁在孩子的膝盖上，眼睛一眨一眨地看人。The puppy looked so adorable that everyone stopped to watch.
sceneCN: 这里 adorable 是「可爱的」（第 1 个义项：外貌或举止惹人喜爱）；句意为那只小狗看起来太可爱了，所有人都停下来看。图中可辨识物件：沙发、膝盖、小狗的项圈。

pos.zh: 可爱的；讨人喜欢的；值得爱慕的

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词基础，义为「爱慕；喜爱；敬拜」
由动词加 -ation 构成，义为「爱慕；敬拜」
由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「可爱地」
由本词加 -ness 构成，义为「可爱；惹人喜爱」

senses.title: Cute and lovable
senses.definition: so cute or charming in appearance or manner that people feel affection at once
senses.definitionCN: 外貌或举止非常可爱、讨喜，让人立刻生出喜爱
senses.example: The baby's first smile was utterly adorable.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿的第一个笑容可爱极了。
senses.why: The word once meant worthy of worship; the affection of worship has been scaled down to the affection of a passing smile.
senses.whyCN: 这个词原本意为「值得敬拜」；敬拜的深情被缩小成了对一个微笑的喜爱。

senses.title: Charming in personality
senses.definition: pleasing in character, especially in a warm and harmless way
senses.definitionCN: 性格上令人愉快，尤其是一种温暖而无害的方式
senses.example: He is an adorable old man who remembers every neighbour's name.
senses.exampleCN: 他是位讨人喜欢的老人，记得每位邻居的名字。
senses.why: When affection moves from the face to the person, adorable describes a temperament rather than a look.
senses.whyCN: 当喜爱从脸孔移到整个人，adorable 描述的便是性情而不是长相。

senses.title: Worthy of adoration
senses.definition: in formal or literary use, deserving deep love or reverence
senses.definitionCN: 在正式或文学用法中，值得深切爱慕或敬重
senses.example: The old hymn calls the saint adorable above all others.
senses.exampleCN: 那首古老的赞美诗称这位圣徒在众人之上，值得敬拜。
senses.why: This is the word's oldest sense kept intact: what deserves adoration, not merely a hug.
senses.whyCN: 这是词最古老的一层，完整保留：值得敬拜，而不只是值得一个拥抱。

senses.title: Endearing, of small creatures
senses.titleCN: 惹人怜爱的（小动物、婴儿）
senses.definition: used of small animals, babies, or small things in a way that invites care and protection
senses.definitionCN: 用于小动物、婴儿或小物件，带有想照顾、想保护的意味
senses.example: The kitten had an adorable way of falling asleep mid-step.
senses.exampleCN: 那只小猫走到一半就睡着的样子很惹人怜爱。
senses.why: Smallness and helplessness pull the word toward tenderness: the object is not only pretty but in need of care.
senses.whyCN: 幼小与无助把词拉向温柔：对象不只是好看，还需要被照顾。

senses.title: Ironic: absurdly charming
senses.definition: used ironically of something childish, awkward, or unreasonable, as if it were charming
senses.definitionCN: 反讽地用于幼稚、别扭或不合理的事物，仿佛它们很迷人
senses.example: He offered the most adorable excuse for missing the deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 他为错过截止日期给出了一个荒唐得好笑的借口。
senses.why: Many fond words can be turned against their object; calling a bad excuse adorable means it is too childish to be taken seriously.
senses.whyCN: 许多亲昵的词都能反转来用；说一个糟糕的借口 adorable，意思是它幼稚到无法当真。

senses.title: In the speech of children and adults to children
senses.titleCN: 儿童用语里的「太可爱了」
senses.definition: a frequent exclamation in talk addressed to or about children and pets
senses.definitionCN: 在面向儿童或谈论儿童、宠物时常用的感叹说法
senses.example: Look at his tiny boots. Adorable!
senses.exampleCN: 看他那双小靴子。太可爱了！
senses.why: A word used constantly around children becomes part of that register, a quick signal of warm approval.
senses.whyCN: 一个总在孩子身边使用的词，会进入那个语域，成为温暖赞许的快速信号。

senses.title: The archaic religious sense
senses.definition: in older religious writing, describing what is worthy of worship and divine honour
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的宗教文本中，描述值得敬拜与神圣尊崇者
senses.example: The prayer addresses the adorable name with reverence.
senses.exampleCN: 祷词以敬畏之心称呼那个值得敬拜的名。
senses.why: Adore began as a verb of prayer; the adjective kept a religious sense long after everyday speech turned it toward cuteness.
senses.whyCN: adore 原本是祈祷的动词；日常语把它转向「可爱」很久之后，形容词仍保留着宗教义。

senses.title: An affectionate form of address
senses.definition: used as a tender way of addressing a loved person, especially a child
senses.definitionCN: 用作称呼所爱之人的亲昵说法，尤用于孩子
senses.example: Come here, my adorable one, and let me see that bruise.
senses.exampleCN: 过来，我的小可爱，让我看看那块淤青。
senses.why: A descriptive adjective can become a name when affection is spoken directly to the person.
senses.whyCN: 当喜爱直接对着那个人说出时，描述性的形容词就成了称呼。

intro.en: Adorable comes from a Latin verb of prayer, and its meaning slid from worship to affection without losing the intensity.
intro.cn: adorable 来自一个表示「祈祷」的拉丁动词，它的意义从敬拜滑向喜爱，却没有丢掉那份强度。

items.en: The speaking root is often connected with *or-, 'to speak', but the wider reconstruction is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个「说话」词根常与 *or-「说」相联系，但更广的构拟并不确定。

items.en: Orare meant 'to speak, plead, pray', and it also gives oral, orator and oracle.
items.cn: orare 意为「说话、恳求、祈祷」，它还给出 oral、orator 与 oracle。

items.en: Ad plus orare formed adorare, 'to speak to, pray to, worship'. The prefix turns speech toward its object.
items.cn: ad 与 orare 构成 adorare，意为「对……说话、向……祈祷、敬拜」。前缀把说话指向对象。

items.en: Adorabilis meant 'worthy of adoration'; the suffix -abilis marks what deserves the action.
items.cn: adorabilis 意为「值得敬拜的」；后缀 -abilis 标记值得承受这一动作者。

items.en: Old French and later English kept the religious sense first, applying the word to persons and things worthy of reverence.
items.cn: 古法语与后来的英语先保留宗教义，用它形容值得敬重的人与物。

items.en: The modern 'cute' sense is a later softening: what is loved intensely comes to be called adorable in everyday affection.
items.cn: 现代「可爱」义是后来软化的结果：被深深喜爱的东西在日常亲昵里被称为 adorable。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same Latin prayer verb; the near-meaning group gathers praise words for charm and cuteness, which differ in intensity and in how childish they sound.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「祈祷」动词构成的词；近义组收称赞迷人、可爱的词，彼此在强度与孩子气程度上不同。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to love intensely or, in older use, to worship.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「深爱」，旧时也指「敬拜」。

entries.definition: The noun for deep love or worship.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「爱慕；敬拜」。

entries.definition: The adjective describing a look or manner full of love.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，描述充满爱意的目光或举止。

entries.definition: Attractive in a pretty or endearing way, the most everyday word for the same impression.
entries.definitionCN: 以漂亮或惹人喜爱的方式吸引人，是表达同一印象最日常的词。

entries.definition: Deserving love because of character rather than appearance.
entries.definitionCN: 因性格而非外貌而值得被爱，比 adorable 更重心性。

entries.definition: Pleasing and attractive in a social way, often of manner rather than looks.
entries.definitionCN: 在社交上令人愉快、有吸引力，多指举止而非长相。

entries.definition: Kind and pleasing in a gentle, unassuming way.
entries.definitionCN: 温和、不张扬地令人愉快。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin prayer root and the phrases the adjective actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁「祈祷」词根，以及这个形容词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: orare means to pray: adore began as worship, and adorable began as worthy of worship.
normal.cn: orare 意为「祈祷」：adore 起初是敬拜，adorable 起初是「值得敬拜」。

normal.en: The same root gives oral and orator, both about speaking.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 oral 与 orator，两者都与说话有关。

normal.en: Adorable is the adjective, adorably the adverb, adorableness the noun.
normal.cn: adorable 是形容词，adorably 是副词，adorableness 是名词。

normal.en: Look adorable and absolutely adorable are the everyday intensifiers.
normal.cn: look adorable 与 absolutely adorable 是日常的搭配与强调。

normal.en: Used of a bad excuse, adorable turns ironic and means childish.
normal.cn: 用在糟糕的借口上，adorable 转为反讽，意思是幼稚。

abstract.en: Picture a very old word kneeling in prayer, then standing up to tickle a puppy.
abstract.cn: 想象一个很古老的词先跪着祈祷，然后站起来去逗小狗。

abstract.en: The intensity never left: we still say adorable when affection is stronger than reason.
abstract.cn: 那份强度从未离开：当喜爱超过理智时，我们仍说 adorable。

abstract.en: Anything small and defenseless borrows the word, and anything absurd can borrow it as a joke.
abstract.cn: 任何幼小无助的东西都能借走这个词，任何荒唐的东西也能借它来开玩笑。

examples.en: Their new puppy is absolutely adorable.
examples.cn: 他们新养的小狗可爱极了。

examples.en: She has an adorable habit of humming while she works.
examples.cn: 她工作时哼歌的习惯很讨人喜欢。

examples.en: The old hymn still calls the saint adorable.
examples.cn: 那首古老的赞美诗仍称这位圣徒值得敬拜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿多勒伯」——阿多伸手想抱：可爱得让人爱

root: 拉丁语 ad-（朝向）+ orare（说话、祈祷）构成 adorare「向……祈祷、敬拜」，加 -abilis「值得……的」构成 adorabilis，本义「值得敬拜的」，现代日常语中软化为「可爱的」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of adorable run from plain cuteness through charm, formal reverence, tender smallness, irony, child talk, the archaic religious sense and a lover's form of address.
sensesIntro.cn: adorable 的八个义项从单纯的可爱，经讨喜的性格、正式的敬慕、惹人怜爱的幼小、反讽、儿童用语、古老的宗教义，一直到亲昵的称呼。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something small looks up at you and your hand reaches out before you decide to.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个小东西抬头看你，你的手在决定之前就已经伸出去了。

branches.en: THE WORSHIP LINE: the oldest layer keeps the word pointed at what deserves reverence.
branches.cn: 敬拜线：最古老的一层让这个词仍指向值得敬重之物。

branches.en: THE AFFECTION LINE: reverence scaled down becomes warm liking of a face or a character.
branches.cn: 喜爱线：敬重被缩小，成了对一张脸或一种性情的温暖喜欢。

branches.en: THE TENDERNESS LINE: smallness and helplessness invite care and protection.
branches.cn: 温柔线：幼小与无助唤起照顾与保护。

branches.en: THE IRONY LINE: the same fond word can mock what is childish or absurd.
branches.cn: 反讽线：同一个亲昵的词可以嘲弄幼稚或荒唐之物。

branches.en: THE SPEECH LINE: constant use around children turns the adjective into an exclamation and a pet name.
branches.cn: 言语线：在孩子身边的频繁使用，把这个形容词变成感叹与昵称。

intro.en: Adorable is a Latin prefix and prayer verb plus the suffix -able; English adds -ly and -ness, and the verb adore stands at the base.
intro.cn: adorable 由拉丁语前缀、祈祷动词与后缀 -able 构成；英语再加 -ly 与 -ness，动词 adore 是它的基础。

latinIntro.en: Orare, adorare and adorabilis are all recorded in Latin, so the core is documented rather than reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: orare、adorare 与 adorabilis 在拉丁语中都有记录，核心部分有文献可查，不属重构。

items.example: It turns speech toward the one addressed.
items.exampleCN: 它把说话指向被称呼者。

items.example: It is the speaking root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这一词族的「说话」词根。

items.example: The compound is the source of adore.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词是 adore 的来源。

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词基础，义为「爱慕；敬拜」
由动词加 -ation 构成，义为「爱慕；敬拜」
由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「可爱地」
由本词加 -ness 构成，义为「可爱」

definition_zh: 成年人；成年的；成熟的；成虫；成体
definition_en: a person or animal that has finished growing and is fully developed, or something suitable for such people
core_image: 已经长成的人，站在成长的终点
scene: 深夜的厨房里，父亲把家里的账本推到女儿面前，她刚拿到第一份工资。Now that she is an adult, she pays her own rent.
sceneCN: 这里 adult 是「成年人」（第 1 个义项：已经长大、在法律与生活中自立的人）；句意为既然她已是成年人，就自己付房租。图中可辨识物件：账本、工资单、厨房台面。

pos.zh: 成年人；成虫；成体
成年的；成熟的；适合成年人的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -hood 构成，义为「成年；成年期」
由本词加 -ing 构成的口语名词，义为「承担成年人的日常责任」
由本词加 -like 构成，义为「像成年人的」

senses.title: A fully grown person
senses.definition: a person who has finished growing and is considered fully developed, usually from about eighteen
senses.definitionCN: 已经结束生长、被视为完全发育的人，通常从十八岁左右起算
senses.example: Every adult in the room had signed the form.
senses.exampleCN: 屋里的每位成年人都签了那张表。
senses.why: The Latin word is a past participle: the adult is the one who has grown, growth now behind rather than ahead.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁词是过去分词：adult 是「已经长成」的人，生长已在身后而不是在前方。

senses.title: Fully grown, as an adjective
senses.definition: having reached full physical growth, used of people or animals
senses.definitionCN: 已达到完全的体格发育，用于人或动物
senses.example: An adult male of this species weighs about ten kilos.
senses.exampleCN: 这个物种的成年雄性体重约十公斤。
senses.why: As an adjective the participle points at a state of completion: nothing more is expected to grow.
senses.whyCN: 作形容词时，这个分词指向一种完成状态：不再预期还会长什么。

senses.title: Mature in behaviour
senses.definition: behaving in a sensible, responsible way expected of a grown person
senses.definitionCN: 以成年人应有的明智、负责方式行事
senses.example: It was an adult response to a very childish provocation.
senses.exampleCN: 面对十分幼稚的挑衅，那是一个成熟的回应。
senses.why: Growing up is not only body but conduct; the word can praise someone for acting as a grown person should.
senses.whyCN: 长大不只是身体，也是举止；这个词可以称赞某人按成年人的样子行事。

senses.title: Intended for adults only
senses.titleCN: 适宜成年人的；成人限定的
senses.definition: describing material, entertainment, or content considered suitable only for grown people
senses.definitionCN: 形容只适合成年人观看或使用的材料、娱乐或内容
senses.example: The film was given an adult rating and barred to children.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影被定为成人级，禁止儿童观看。
senses.why: Once a group is defined by age, the market splits, and adult becomes a label on the shelf rather than a description of a person.
senses.whyCN: 一旦一个群体按年龄被界定，市场就分开了，adult 便成了货架上的标签，而不是对人的描述。

senses.title: The adult insect
senses.definition: the final, reproductive stage of an insect after metamorphosis
senses.definitionCN: 昆虫变态后具有繁殖能力的最终阶段
senses.example: The adult moth lives only a few days.
senses.exampleCN: 这种蛾的成虫只活几天。
senses.why: Biology borrows the human word for the finished form: the stage that no longer changes shape.
senses.whyCN: 生物学借用了人的说法来指完成形态：那个不再改变形状的阶段。

senses.title: A fully developed organism
senses.definition: a fully developed plant or animal, as opposed to a larva, seedling, or juvenile
senses.definitionCN: 完全发育的植物或动物，与幼虫、幼苗、幼体相对
senses.example: The adult coral cannot move once it settles.
senses.exampleCN: 这种珊瑚的成体一旦定居就不能移动。
senses.why: In every life cycle there is a last form, and the word marks the point where development stops changing shape.
senses.whyCN: 每个生命周期都有一个最后的形态，这个词标记发育不再改变形状的那一刻。

senses.title: Legally of age
senses.definition: having reached the age at which the law grants full rights and duties
senses.definitionCN: 已达到法律授予完全权利与义务的年龄
senses.example: In this country a person is adult at eighteen.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个国家，人到十八岁即为成年。
senses.why: Law draws a line where nature draws a curve, and the word is used to mark that line.
senses.whyCN: 自然画出的是曲线，法律画出的是一条线，这个词被用来标记那条线。

senses.title: A mature stage of anything
senses.definition: in figurative use, the settled, fully developed stage of an institution, art, or idea
senses.definitionCN: 用于比喻时，指机构、艺术或观念稳定、充分发展的阶段
senses.example: The movement had reached its adult form by the late century.
senses.exampleCN: 到那个世纪末，这场运动已进入它的成熟形态。
senses.why: Any growth story can borrow the human life span, so what has stopped changing shape is called adult.
senses.whyCN: 任何成长故事都能借用人的生命周期，于是不再改变形状的东西被称为 adult。

intro.en: Adult is the past participle of the same Latin verb that gives adolescence: one word is the growing, the other the grown.
intro.cn: adult 与 adolescence 出自同一个拉丁动词，前者是过去分词；一个词说「正在长」，另一个说「已长成」。

items.en: The nourishment root is usually reconstructed as *al-, though its broader connections are debated.
items.cn: 这个「滋养」词根通常被构拟为 *al-，但它更广的联系仍有争论。

items.en: Alere meant 'to nourish, feed', and it stands behind aliment and alimony.
items.cn: alere 意为「滋养、喂养」，aliment 与 alimony 也出自它。

items.en: The inchoative alescere meant 'to begin to grow'; growth is marked at its start.
items.cn: 表示起始的 alescere 意为「开始生长」，生长在这里被标在起点。

items.en: Ad plus alescere formed adolescere, 'to grow up'.
items.cn: ad 与 alescere 构成 adolescere，意为「长成」。

items.en: The past participle adultus meant 'having grown up'. Latin also used adultus as a noun for a grown person.
items.cn: 过去分词 adultus 意为「已经长成的」；拉丁语也用它作名词，指成年人。

items.en: English adopts adult in the seventeenth century; the adjective and noun uses spread together in the eighteenth and nineteenth.
items.cn: 英语于十七世纪借入 adult；形容词与名词用法在十八、十九世纪一同扩展。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same growth verb; the near-meaning group gathers words for grown people and maturity, which differ in register, age reference and legal weight.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「生长」动词构成的词；近义组收指成年人及成熟的词，彼此在语体、年龄所指与法律效力上不同。

entries.definition: The period of growing up that ends where adulthood begins.
entries.definitionCN: 成长的那段时期，其终点正是成年期的起点。

entries.definition: The person or stage still on the way to being adult.
entries.definitionCN: 尚未到达成年的人或阶段。

entries.definition: The noun for the state or period of being adult.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成年；成年期」。

entries.definition: An everyday or child's word for an adult, warmer and less technical.
entries.definitionCN: 日常或儿童用语，指成年人，比 adult 更温暖、更不正式。

entries.definition: Fully developed in body or behaviour, stressing the quality rather than the age line.
entries.definitionCN: 身体或行为上充分发展，强调素质而非年龄界线。

entries.definition: A phrase meaning having reached the legal age of full rights.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，意为已达享有完全权利的法定年龄。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin participle and the phrases adult actually forms.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁分词，以及 adult 实际构成的搭配。

normal.en: Adult is a past participle: the growing is finished, and the person is the result.
normal.cn: adult 是过去分词：生长已经结束，人就是那个结果。

normal.en: Adolescent is still on the road; adult has arrived.
normal.cn: adolescent 还在路上，adult 已经到达。

normal.en: Young adult, adult education and adult supervision are standard phrases.
normal.cn: young adult、adult education 与 adult supervision 都是标准说法。

normal.en: In biology the adult is the final stage, after larva and juvenile.
normal.cn: 在生物学里，adult 是幼虫与幼体之后的最终阶段。

normal.en: Adulthood adds -hood, the suffix for a state or period, as in childhood.
normal.cn: adulthood 加的是 -hood，表示状态或时期的后缀，正如 childhood。

abstract.en: Picture a road that ends at a gate: the gate is adult, the road was adolescence.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路终止在一道门前：门是 adult，路是 adolescence。

abstract.en: The same word can describe a body, a behaviour, a film rating, a moth and an institution.
abstract.cn: 同一个词可以描述身体、行为、电影分级、一只蛾和一个机构。

abstract.en: Being adult is a shape that has stopped changing, which is both a relief and a limitation.
abstract.cn: 成年是一种停止改变形状的状态，这既是解脱，也是限制。

examples.en: Two adults and three children were waiting at the gate.
examples.cn: 两个成年人和三个孩子在门口等着。

examples.en: The adult bird has completely different feathers from the young one.
examples.cn: 成鸟的羽毛与幼鸟完全不同。

examples.en: He handled the complaint in a calm, adult way.
examples.cn: 他以平静、成熟的方式处理了这起投诉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿达特」——阿达长到头了：成年人

root: 拉丁语 adolescere（长成）的过去分词 adultus，意为「已经长成的」；与 adolescence 同源，一个指生长的过程，一个指生长完成的状态。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of adult all mark a finished form: a grown person, a full-grown animal, mature conduct, adult-only material, an insect's final stage, a developed organism, a legal age line, and the settled stage of anything.
sensesIntro.cn: adult 的八个义项都标记一种完成的形态：长成的人、完全发育的动物、成熟的举止、成人限定的内容、昆虫的最终阶段、发育完全的生物、法定年龄线，以及任何事物的稳定阶段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure stands at the end of a growth curve, outline complete and no longer stretching.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在成长曲线的末端，轮廓完整，不再被拉长。

branches.en: THE BODY LINE: the person or animal has reached full physical growth.
branches.cn: 身体线：人或动物已达到完全的体格发育。

branches.en: THE BEARING LINE: maturity shows in conduct and in institutions that have stopped changing shape.
branches.cn: 举止线：成熟体现在行为，也体现在不再改变形状的机构上。

branches.en: THE MARKET LINE: age defines a group, and adult becomes a label on content.
branches.cn: 市场线：年龄界定出群体，adult 成了内容上的标签。

branches.en: THE LIFE-CYCLE LINE: biology uses the word for the final stage of an organism.
branches.cn: 生命周期线：生物学用这个词指生物的最终阶段。

branches.en: THE LAW LINE: a legal age draws a clear line across a gradual process.
branches.cn: 法律线：法定年龄在渐进的过程中画出一道清晰的线。

intro.en: Adult is a Latin participle used as a base; English adds -hood, -ing and -like to extend it into a small family.
intro.cn: adult 是作基础使用的拉丁分词；英语加 -hood、-ing 与 -like 把它扩展成一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: Alere, alescere, adolescere and adultus are all recorded in Latin, so the base is attested rather than reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: alere、alescere、adolescere 与 adultus 在拉丁语中都有记录，基础部分有文献可查，不属重构。

items.example: It marks the start of growth.

items.exampleCN: adult 就是它的过去分词。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -hood 构成，义为「成年期」
由本词加 -ing 构成的口语名词，义为「承担成年责任」
由本词加 -like 构成，义为「像成年人的」

definition_zh: 通奸；婚外性行为（尤指一方已婚）
definition_en: sex between a married person and someone who is not that person's husband or wife
core_image: 婚姻围栏上被悄悄打开的一道缺口，只有两个人知道
scene: 老城旅馆的走廊里，一份离婚诉状摊在桌上，理由栏写得极短。The divorce petition cited adultery as the ground for the marriage's collapse.
sceneCN: 这里 adultery 是「通奸」（第 1 个义项：已婚者与配偶以外的人发生性关系）；句意为这份离婚诉状把通奸列为婚姻破裂的理由。图中可辨识的物件：诉状、钢笔、旅馆房牌。

pos.zh: 通奸；婚外性行为（不可数）

derivatives.zh: 由词干加 -er 构成，指「通奸的男子」
由 adultere 加 -ess 构成的旧式阴性形式，指「通奸的女子」，今多含贬义、渐少用
由词干加 -ous 构成，义为「通奸的；不忠的」

senses.title: The act of sex outside marriage
senses.definition: the act of a married person having sex with someone who is not his or her spouse
senses.definitionCN: 已婚者与配偶以外的人发生性关系的行为
senses.example: The village treated adultery as a private shame and a public fact.
senses.exampleCN: 村里把通奸既当作私下的耻辱，也当作公开的事实。
senses.why: Latin adulterare meant to go to another, and the noun names precisely that act, so this is the plainest sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 adulterare 意为「走向另一个」，名词命名的正是这一行为，这是最本义的义项。

senses.title: A legal ground for divorce
senses.definition: the act as a recognised reason on which a court may dissolve a marriage
senses.definitionCN: 作为法院可以据以解除婚姻的公认理由的这一行为
senses.example: In this jurisdiction adultery remains a fault-based ground for divorce.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个司法辖区，通奸仍是过错离婚的一项理由。
senses.why: Because marriage is a legal contract, the same act becomes a recognised ground on which the contract may be ended.
senses.whyCN: 婚姻是一份法律契约，因此同一行为成为契约可以据以终止的公认事由。

senses.title: A breach of the marriage vow
senses.definition: the act understood as breaking a promise made before God rather than as a legal fact
senses.definitionCN: 被理解为在神面前毁掉承诺、而非法律事实的这一行为
senses.example: The church called adultery a sin against the wedding vow.
senses.exampleCN: 教会把通奸称为对婚礼誓言的罪。
senses.why: In religious framing the same act is not a legal fact but a broken vow, so the word shifts from deed to sin.
senses.whyCN: 在宗教框架里，同一行为不是法律事实而是被撕毁的誓言，于是这个词从行为转向罪。

senses.title: An accusation brought against someone
senses.definition: the word as a charge that one person lays against another
senses.definitionCN: 一个人加在另一个人头上的这一指控
senses.example: He denied the adultery allegation and demanded proof.
senses.exampleCN: 他否认通奸的指控，并要求拿出证据。
senses.why: Once a name exists for the act, it can be attached to a person as an accusation, and the word enters court language.
senses.whyCN: 行为一旦有了名字，就能安到某个人头上成为指控，这个词于是进入法庭语言。

senses.title: A word weighted by gender
senses.titleCN: 带有性别偏见的旧用法
senses.definition: the historically uneven use of the term, applied far more harshly to wives than to husbands
senses.definitionCN: 这个词在历史上用法不均，对妻子的责难远重于丈夫
senses.example: Old novels punish adulteresses far more severely than adulterers.
senses.exampleCN: 旧小说对通奸女子的惩罚远重于通奸男子。
senses.why: Historically the word was applied far more harshly to women, so its use carries an uneven moral weight.
senses.whyCN: 历史上这个词对女性的责难远重于男性，所以它的使用带着不均衡的道德重量。

senses.title: Betrayal of a pledged loyalty
senses.definition: in figurative use, the breaking of any loyalty or trust that was solemnly pledged
senses.definitionCN: 用于比喻时，指撕毁任何曾郑重立下的忠诚或信任
senses.example: They accused the party of adultery toward its own founding ideals.
senses.exampleCN: 他们指责该政党背叛了自己立党的理想。
senses.why: Any pledged loyalty can be broken in the same shape, so the word extends to betraying a cause or a trust.
senses.whyCN: 任何立誓的忠诚都能以同样的形状被破坏，于是这个词延伸到对事业或信任的背叛。

senses.title: The concealed affair as a plot engine
senses.definition: in literature, the hidden relationship used to drive suspense and revelation
senses.definitionCN: 在文学中，被用来推动悬念与真相揭露的隐秘关系
senses.example: The play turns on adultery discovered through a misplaced letter.
senses.exampleCN: 这出戏靠一封放错地方的信揭出通奸，情节由此转动。
senses.why: A hidden affair is a ready-made engine of suspense, so literature borrows the word for its plots.
senses.whyCN: 隐秘的私情是现成的悬念发动机，文学于是借这个词来推动情节。

senses.title: The public shame of discovery
senses.definition: the scandal that follows when the private act becomes known
senses.definitionCN: 私下的行为被人知道之后随之而来的丑闻
senses.example: The adultery became a scandal that cost him his ministry.
senses.exampleCN: 这桩通奸变成丑闻，使他丢掉了牧师职位。
senses.why: The act only becomes scandal when it is exposed, and the word then names the public noise rather than the private deed.
senses.whyCN: 这一行为只有被揭露才成为丑闻，此时这个词命名的是公开的喧哗，而非私下的行为。

intro.en: Adultery descends from a Latin verb built on alter, the word for other, so its oldest sense is going to someone else.
intro.cn: adultery 源自一个以 alter（另一个）为核心构成的拉丁动词，最古老的意思就是「走向别人」。

items.en: Alter meant the other of two, and it still survives in English alternation and alternative.
items.cn: alter 意为两者中的另一个，至今仍活在英语的 alternation 与 alternative 里。

items.en: Ad plus alter gave adulterare, to go to another and so to commit adultery; it also meant to corrupt.
items.cn: ad 加 alter 构成 adulterare，义为「走向另一个」，因此指通奸，同时也表示「玷污」。

items.en: The noun adulterium named the act itself, and this form is the direct source of the English noun.
items.cn: 名词 adulterium 命名这一行为本身，这一形式正是英语名词的直接来源。

items.en: Old French carried the word as avoutrie and later adulterie, with the spelling unsettled for centuries.
items.cn: 古法语把这个词带作 avoutrie，后来又作 adulterie，拼写数百年间并不固定。

items.en: English borrowed the noun in the fourteenth century, first in religious and legal texts.
items.cn: 英语于十四世纪借入这个名词，最早见于宗教与法律文本。

items.en: The modern word keeps both the religious tone and the legal force, though criminal penalties have largely disappeared.
items.cn: 现代英语的这个名词同时保留了宗教语气与法律效力，尽管刑事处罚已大多废除。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same alter family, including one that means to corrupt rather than to stray; the near-meaning group gathers blunter, softer and more clinical labels for the same territory.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 alter 词族的词，其中包括表示「玷污」而非「越界」的一个；近义组收指同一片领域的更直白、更委婉与更临床的说法。

entries.definition: The person who commits the act, formed with the agent suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 实施这一行为的人，由施事后缀构成。

entries.definition: The adjective describing the act or the person, formed with -ous.
entries.definitionCN: 描述行为或人的形容词，由 -ous 构成。

entries.definition: From the same Latin verb but with the idea of corrupting a substance by mixing in something inferior.
entries.definitionCN: 来自同一拉丁动词，但取「掺入次货使物质变劣」之意，与私情无关。

entries.definition: A softer, vaguer word for a romantic relationship outside marriage.
entries.definitionCN: 更委婉含糊的说法，指婚外的感情关系。

entries.definition: A formal term for breaking faith with a partner, broader than the single act.
entries.definitionCN: 正式用语，指对伴侣不忠，范围比单次行为更广。

entries.definition: The everyday word for the same behaviour, carrying no legal or religious weight.
entries.definitionCN: 日常口语说法，指同样的行为，不带法律或宗教分量。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin alter, the real word family and the legal phrases the noun actually forms.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用拉丁语 alter、真实的词族，以及这个名词实际构成的短语。

normal.en: Adulterare is ad plus alter: to go to another. The word is built into the meaning.
normal.cn: adulterare 就是 ad 加 alter：走向另一个。词义被写进了构词里。

normal.en: Alter also gives alternative and alter ego, all about a second version.
normal.cn: alter 还给出 alternative 与 alter ego，都与「另一个版本」有关。

normal.en: The family runs adulterer, adulteress and adulterous, so the noun has three ready relatives.
normal.cn: 词族里有 adulterer、adulteress 与 adulterous，这个名词因此有三个现成亲戚。

normal.en: The verb that goes with it is commit, as in commit adultery, not do adultery.
normal.cn: 与它搭配的动词是 commit，说 commit adultery，而不说 do adultery。

normal.en: Legal writing prefers grounds of adultery, a fixed phrase in divorce statutes.
normal.cn: 法律写作偏爱 grounds of adultery，这是离婚法条里的固定说法。

abstract.en: Picture a second key cut for the same door, made quietly and kept out of sight.
abstract.cn: 想象有人悄悄配了同一扇门的第二把钥匙，藏在看不见的地方。

abstract.en: The word names a relationship, but its force comes from the promise it breaks.
abstract.cn: 这个词命名一段关系，但它的力量来自被它撕毁的那个承诺。

abstract.en: Every exposure story repeats the same shape: a private gap, then public light.
abstract.cn: 每个曝光的故事都重复同一个形状：私下的缺口，然后是公开的光。

examples.en: In many countries adultery is no longer a criminal offence.
examples.cn: 在许多国家，通奸已不再是刑事犯罪。

examples.en: The church treated adultery as a breach of the wedding vow.
examples.cn: 教会把通奸视为对婚礼誓言的违背。

examples.en: Novelists have long used adultery to set a plot in motion.
examples.cn: 小说家早就用通奸来推动情节。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德尔特里」——德尔另开一扇门：通奸

root: 拉丁语 ad-（朝向）+ alter（另一个）→ adulterare「走向另一个、玷污」，名词 adulterium 经古法语进入英语，义为通奸。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of adultery all turn on one gap opened in a pledged bond: the act itself, its legal force, its religious weight, the charge, the uneven blame, the figurative betrayal, the literary engine and the public scandal.
sensesIntro.cn: adultery 的八个义项都围绕一个在誓约上打开的缺口：行为本身、法律效力、宗教重量、指控、不均的责难、比喻性的背叛、文学里的情节引擎，以及公开的丑闻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gap quietly opened in the fence around a marriage.
core.cn: 核心意象：婚姻围栏上被悄悄打开的一道缺口。

branches.en: THE DEED LINE: the act and the broken vow are two readings of the same private step.
branches.cn: 行为线：行为与被撕毁的誓言，是对同一个私下举动的两种读法。

branches.en: THE COURT LINE: the deed becomes a ground and then a charge once lawyers take it up.
branches.cn: 法庭线：一旦律师介入，行为先成为事由，再成为指控。

branches.en: THE BLAME LINE: the same word has weighed more heavily on wives than on husbands.
branches.cn: 责难线：同一个词压在妻子身上的分量历来重于丈夫。

branches.en: THE STORY LINE: the shape of a broken pledge can be borrowed for causes and for plots.
branches.cn: 故事线：被毁誓约的形状可以被借去说事业，也可以被借去写情节。

branches.en: THE SCANDAL LINE: exposure turns the private gap into public noise.
branches.cn: 丑闻线：曝光把私下的缺口变成公开的喧哗。

intro.en: Adultery is a Latin noun in -ium built on the verb adulterare, whose core is alter, the other; English keeps the stem and adds English agent and adjective endings.
intro.cn: adultery 是以 -ium 结尾的拉丁名词，建于动词 adulterare 之上，其核心是 alter（另一个）；英语保留词干，并加上英语的施事与形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Alter, adulterare and adulterium are all attested in Latin, so nothing here is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: alter、adulterare 与 adulterium 在拉丁语中均有文献，此处没有构拟形式。

items.example: It turns alter into a motion toward the other.
items.exampleCN: 它把 alter 变成「朝另一个而去」的动作。

items.example: It is the semantic heart of the word.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个词的意义核心。

items.meaning: to commit adultery, also to corrupt
items.example: Its noun is the source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 它的名词形式是英语词的来源。

items.example: It carries the Latin noun into English.
items.exampleCN: 它把拉丁名词带入英语。

items.example: It forms the old word adulteress.

derivatives.zh: 由词干加 -er 构成，义为「通奸的男子」
由词干加 -ess 构成的旧式阴性形式，义为「通奸的女子」
由词干加 -ous 构成，义为「通奸的；不忠的」

definition_zh: 前进；推进；促进；提前；预付；进展；进步
definition_en: to move forward, to make progress, to help something grow, or to pay money before it is due
core_image: 一支队伍或一枚指针整体向前挪了一格
scene: 清晨的工地上，推土机把土堆一寸寸向前压平，进度牌又翻了一页。The crew advanced the earthworks by thirty metres before noon.
sceneCN: 这里 advance 是「推进；使向前」（第 1 个义项：把某物向前移动）；句意为施工队到中午前把土方工程向前推进了三十米。图中可辨识的物件：推土机、土堆、进度牌。

pos.zh: 前进；推进；促进；提前；预付
前进；进展；进步；预付款
预先的；提前的（多用于名词前）

derivatives.zh: 由 advance 加 -ment 构成，义为「推进；提升；进步」
由过去分词转作形容词，义为「先进的；高级的」
由现在分词转作形容词，义为「前进的；不断推进的」

senses.title: To move something forward
senses.definition: to move a person, force or object forward in space
senses.definitionCN: 把人、队伍或物体在空间中向前移动
senses.example: The army advanced two kilometres along the valley road.
senses.exampleCN: 部队沿谷底公路向前推进了两公里。
senses.why: The oldest image is physical motion, because the source verb meant to put something in front.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意象是物理移动，因为源动词的意思就是「把某物放到前面」。

senses.title: To make progress
senses.definition: to move forward in knowledge, work or a process rather than in space
senses.definitionCN: 在知识、工作或进程上向前，而不是在空间里向前
senses.example: Research has advanced faster than the regulations.
senses.exampleCN: 研究进展得比监管更快。
senses.why: Once forward motion is the image, any process can be said to move forward along its own line.
senses.whyCN: 一旦以「向前移动」为意象，任何进程都可以说是在自己的线上向前走。

senses.title: To help a cause develop
senses.definition: to help an idea, cause or interest to gain ground
senses.definitionCN: 帮助某个想法、事业或利益获得地盘
senses.example: The scholarship fund advanced the careers of many village teachers.
senses.exampleCN: 这项奖学金推动了许多乡村教师的职业发展。
senses.why: To push something forward is also to push it up in the world, so the verb takes on the sense of promoting.
senses.whyCN: 把某物向前推，也是在世间把它往上推，于是这个动词带上「促进」的含义。

senses.title: To pay money before it is due
senses.definition: to pay part or all of a sum earlier than the agreed date
senses.definitionCN: 在约定日期之前支付一笔款项的部分或全部
senses.example: The publisher advanced her a year's royalties.
senses.exampleCN: 出版商向她预付了一年的版税。
senses.why: Money handed over ahead of time is money moved forward on the calendar, so the spatial sense becomes financial.
senses.whyCN: 提前交出的钱，是在日历上被向前挪动的钱，空间义于是变成财务义。

senses.title: To bring an event earlier
senses.definition: to move a planned date or time to an earlier point
senses.definitionCN: 把预定的日期或时间挪到更早的时点
senses.example: They advanced the meeting by two days.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把会议提前了两天。
senses.why: If forward is the metaphor, then forward on a timetable means sooner, and the sense follows naturally.
senses.whyCN: 既然「向前」是比喻，那么时间表上的向前就意味着更早，这一义项便自然跟上。

senses.title: To raise someone in rank
senses.definition: to promote a person to a higher position or grade
senses.definitionCN: 把某人提拔到更高的职位或等级
senses.example: He was advanced to head of the department after ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 十年后他被提升为部门主管。
senses.why: Rank is pictured as a ladder, and moving up it is moving forward in one's career.
senses.whyCN: 等级被想象成一架梯子，沿梯子向上就是在职业生涯中向前。

senses.title: Forward movement as a noun
senses.definition: the noun for the act of moving forward, especially of an army or a group
senses.definitionCN: 名词，指向前移动的动作，尤指军队或队伍的前进
senses.example: The advance halted at the river.
senses.exampleCN: 前进在河边停了下来。
senses.why: English routinely turns a verb of motion into a noun, and the noun keeps the same forward picture.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把表示运动的动词直接用作名词，这个名词保留着同一幅向前的画面。

senses.title: Progress or improvement as a noun
senses.definition: a development or improvement seen as a step forward in a field
senses.definitionCN: 在某一领域被视为向前一步的发展或改进
senses.example: Recent advances in battery design have cut charging times.
senses.exampleCN: 电池设计上的近期进展缩短了充电时间。
senses.why: The countable noun turns each step forward into a separate item that can be counted and reported.
senses.whyCN: 可数名词把每一个向前的步子变成一个可以计数、可以报道的独立条目。

intro.en: Advance comes from Old French avancier, to move forward, built on the Latin phrase abante, from before.
intro.cn: advance 来自古法语 avancier「向前移动」，其基础是拉丁短语 abante「从前面」。

items.en: Ante meant before or in front of, and it survives in English in ante-room and in the prefix ante-.
items.cn: ante 意为「在……之前」或「在……前面」，在英语的 ante-room 与前缀 ante- 中仍有留存。

items.en: Ab plus ante formed the phrase abante, from before, which passed into Vulgar Latin as a verb stem.
items.cn: ab 加 ante 构成短语 abante「从前面」，并以动词词干的形式进入通俗拉丁语。

items.en: Old French avancier meant to move forward or to promote, and English borrowed it with both senses.
items.cn: 古法语 avancier 意为「向前移动」或「提拔」，英语借入时把两个意思一并带来。

items.en: The verb appears in Middle English in military and legal contexts before it spreads to money and time.
items.cn: 这个动词先在中古英语的军事与法律语境中出现，之后才扩展到金钱与时间。

items.en: The financial sense of an early payment and the noun sense of a step forward both settle in the modern period.
items.cn: 预付这一财务义与「向前一步」的名词义，都在现代时期稳定下来。

note.en: The look-alike group is the English family grown from the same stem; the near-meaning group gathers verbs and nouns of forward motion, which differ in how physical or how official they are.
note.cn: 形近组是同一词干长出的英语词族；近义组收表示向前运动的动词与名词，差别在于它们有多具体、多正式。

entries.definition: The noun of progress or promotion, formed with -ment.
entries.definitionCN: 表示进展或提升的名词，由 -ment 构成。

entries.definition: The participle used as an adjective for something far along, as in advanced mathematics.
entries.definitionCN: 分词转作的形容词，指程度很靠前的事物，如「高等数学」。

entries.definition: A related noun from the same avant stem, but meaning a favourable position rather than forward motion.
entries.definitionCN: 同一 avant 词干的相关名词，但义为有利位置，而非向前运动。

entries.definition: Movement toward a better state, usually without the military or financial overtones of advance.
entries.definitionCN: 朝更好状态的运动，通常不带 advance 那样的军事或财务色彩。

entries.definition: To go on or move onward, often in a formal or procedural register.
entries.definitionCN: 继续前行，常用于正式或程序性语境。

entries.definition: To help something grow or to raise someone in rank, overlapping with two senses of advance.
entries.definitionCN: 帮助某物成长或提拔某人，与 advance 的两个义项重叠。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real etymological phrase abante, the word family and the fixed collocations of the verb and noun.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的词源短语 abante、这个词族，以及动词与名词的固定搭配。

normal.en: Abante means from before, so to advance is to put something in front of you.
normal.cn: abante 意为「从前面」，所以 advance 就是把某物放到你前面。

normal.en: The preposition ante is still visible in ante-room and antebellum.
normal.cn: 介词 ante 仍能在 ante-room 与 antebellum 中看见。

normal.en: The family splits neatly: advancement is the noun of progress, advanced is the adjective of degree.
normal.cn: 词族分工清楚：advancement 是进展的名词，advanced 是程度形容词。

normal.en: Money paid early is an advance payment, and time moved earlier is advanced by two days.
normal.cn: 提前付的钱是 advance payment，提前的时间则是 advanced by two days。

normal.en: In advance is the phrase for doing something ahead of the event.
normal.cn: in advance 是「在事情之前先做」的固定说法。

abstract.en: Picture a chess pawn that has just cleared one square and now sees the next.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚刚走过一格、现在看见下一格的棋子。

abstract.en: Forward in space, forward in time, forward in rank: one picture serves three calendars.
abstract.cn: 空间向前、时间向前、等级向前：一幅画同时服务三种日历。

abstract.en: An advance is a step someone can point to, which is why it is countable.
abstract.cn: 一次进展是一个能用手指出的步子，所以它可以计数。

examples.en: The troops advanced through the pass before dawn.
examples.cn: 部队在黎明前穿过山口向前推进。

examples.en: Please book the tickets in advance; the hall fills quickly.
examples.cn: 请提前订票，礼堂很快就坐满。

examples.en: Medical advances have added years to average life expectancy.
examples.cn: 医学上的进步让平均预期寿命延长了多年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德万斯」——万斯往前迈一步：前进

root: 拉丁语 abante（从前面，ab-「离开」+ ante「之前」）→ 古法语 avancier「向前移动」→ 英语 advance，由空间上的向前扩展到进展、提升、预付与提前。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of advance all carry the same forward step: in space, in knowledge, in a cause, in money, on a calendar, up a rank, and then as the noun for the step itself or for progress.
sensesIntro.cn: advance 的八个义项都带着同一个向前的步子：在空间里、在知识上、在事业上、在金钱上、在日历上、在等级上，最后又把这个步子本身或进步用作名词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of people or a needle moved one notch forward.
core.cn: 核心意象：一队人或一根指针整体向前挪了一格。

branches.en: THE MOTION LINE: the verb and the noun keep the plain picture of moving forward.
branches.cn: 运动线：动词与名词都保留着向前移动的朴素画面。

branches.en: THE PROGRESS LINE: a process or a field moves along its own line, and each step can be counted.
branches.cn: 进展线：进程或领域沿自己的线向前，每一个步子都可以计数。

branches.en: THE CAUSE LINE: pushing something forward becomes helping it gain ground.
branches.cn: 事业线：把某物向前推，变成帮助它获得地盘。

branches.en: THE LEDGER LINE: money and dates are moved forward on their own scales.
branches.cn: 账目线：金钱与日期在各自的刻度上被向前挪动。

branches.en: THE LADDER LINE: rank is pictured as a ladder, so promotion is advance.
branches.cn: 梯子线：等级被想象成梯子，所以提拔就是 advance。

intro.en: Advance rests on the Latin phrase abante and reaches English through Old French avancier; the endings -ance, -ment and -ed build the modern family.
intro.cn: advance 建立在拉丁短语 abante 之上，经古法语 avancier 到达英语；-ance、-ment 与 -ed 构成现代词族。

latinIntro.en: Ante and abante are attested in Latin, while the Vulgar Latin verb stem behind avancier is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: ante 与 abante 在拉丁语中有文献，而 avancier 背后的通俗拉丁动词词干属于构拟。

items.example: It supplies the idea of front.
It is the phrase behind the French verb.
items.exampleCN: 它是法语动词背后的短语。

items.example: It is the direct source of the English verb.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语动词的直接来源。

items.example: It appears in related nouns of forward movement.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在表示向前运动的相关名词中。

items.example: It forms advanced as an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它构成作形容词的 advanced。

items.example: It is the commonest adverbial use of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这是这个名词最常见的副词性用法。

derivatives.zh: 由 advance 加 -ment 构成，义为「推进；提升」
由过去分词转作形容词，义为「先进的；高级的」

definition_zh: 优势；有利条件；好处；利益
definition_en: a condition, quality or position that puts someone in a better situation than others
core_image: 站在坡上，比站在坡下多看见的一段路
scene: 网球场上，教练让队员站到发球线内侧，又指了指对手的反手位。Her left-handed serve gave her a clear advantage on the grass court.
sceneCN: 这里 advantage 是「优势」（第 1 个义项：使自己比别人处于更有利位置的条件）；句意为她的左手发球在草地球场上给了她明显的优势。图中可辨识的物件：球拍、发球线、草地上的白线。

pos.zh: 优势；有利条件；好处；利益

derivatives.zh: 由 advantage 加 -ous 构成，义为「有利的；有益的」
由 advantageous 加 -ly 构成，义为「有利地」
由否定前缀 dis- 加本词构成，义为「不利条件；劣势」

senses.title: A condition that puts you ahead
senses.definition: a circumstance or quality that makes you more likely to succeed than others
senses.definitionCN: 使你比别人更可能成功的处境或品质
senses.example: Smaller classes give students an advantage in discussion.
senses.exampleCN: 小班让学生在讨论中占有优势。
senses.why: The word's core is position before others, so any condition that puts you in front is an advantage.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的核心是「处在别人前面」，所以任何把你放到前面的条件都是 advantage。

senses.title: A benefit or profit
senses.definition: something useful or profitable that you gain from a situation
senses.definitionCN: 从某种处境中得到的有用或有利的东西
senses.example: The main advantage of the plan is its low cost.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方案的主要好处是成本低。
senses.why: If being in front is good, then whatever produces that position can be counted as a gain.
senses.whyCN: 既然处在前面是好事，那么任何产生这一位置的东西都可以算作收益。

senses.title: Superiority in a contest
senses.definition: the upper hand held by one side in a game or struggle
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛或较量中一方所占的上风
senses.example: The home side held the advantage for most of the second half.
senses.exampleCN: 主队在大部分下半场时间里占着上风。
senses.why: Contests are pictured as positions on a field, and the higher or forward position is the winning one.
senses.whyCN: 较量被想象成场地上的位置，更高或更靠前的位置就是取胜的位置。

senses.title: To make good use of an opportunity
senses.definition: in the phrase take advantage of, to use a chance or a resource for your own benefit
senses.definitionCN: 在短语 take advantage of 中，指为自己利益而利用机会或资源
senses.example: She took advantage of the quiet morning to finish the report.
senses.exampleCN: 她利用清晨的安静完成了报告。
senses.why: An advantage is a forward position, and taking it is simply occupying that position while it is open.
senses.whyCN: advantage 是一个靠前的位置，take 就是趁它还空着时把这个位置占下来。

senses.title: To treat someone unfairly
senses.definition: in the same phrase, to exploit a person's weakness or good nature
senses.definitionCN: 在同一短语中，指利用某人的弱点或善良占其便宜
senses.example: He took advantage of her trust and borrowed money he never returned.
senses.exampleCN: 他利用了她的信任，借走一笔从没还的钱。
senses.why: The same forward position can be seized at another's expense, which turns use into exploitation.
senses.whyCN: 同一个靠前的位置也可以踩着别人占下，于是「利用」变成了「占便宜」。

senses.title: A head start
senses.definition: an early gain in time or preparation over competitors
senses.definitionCN: 在时间或准备上先于竞争者取得的领先
senses.example: Firms that tested the software early had an advantage over rivals.
senses.exampleCN: 早早测试这款软件的公司比对手占了先手。
senses.why: Being before others in time is the same picture as being before them in space.
senses.whyCN: 在时间上先于别人，与在空间上先于别人是同一幅画面。

senses.title: The tennis scoring term
senses.definition: the point scored after deuce that puts a player one point from winning the game
senses.definitionCN: 平分之后拿下的一分，使球员离赢下这一局只差一分
senses.example: At advantage, the server chose a wide slice.
senses.exampleCN: 占先时，发球方选择了一记外角切削。
senses.why: The scoring term is a literal instance of the core sense: one player now stands ahead of the other.
senses.whyCN: 这个计分术语是核心义的字面实例：一方此刻站在另一方前面。

senses.title: A favourable point in an argument
senses.definition: a fact or argument that supports one side of a case
senses.definitionCN: 支持某一方主张的事实或论据
senses.example: The advantage of this reading is that it explains the missing page.
senses.exampleCN: 这一解读的有利之处在于它解释了缺失的那一页。
senses.why: An argument is a contest of positions, so a point that strengthens your side is an advantage.
senses.whyCN: 论证是位置的较量，所以能加强你这一方的论点就是 advantage。

intro.en: Advantage comes from Old French avantage, built on avant, before, which descends from the Latin phrase abante.
intro.cn: advantage 来自古法语 avantage，建于 avant「在前面」之上，而 avant 又源自拉丁短语 abante。

items.en: Ante meant before or in front, and it remains visible in English in ante-room and antebellum.
items.cn: ante 意为「在……之前」或「在前面」，在英语的 ante-room 与 antebellum 中仍可见。

items.en: Ab plus ante formed abante, from before, the phrase behind the whole family.
items.cn: ab 加 ante 构成 abante「从前面」，这是整个词族背后的短语。

items.en: Avant meant before or ahead, and it still survives in English phrases such as avant-garde.
items.cn: avant 意为「在……之前」或「在前」，至今仍活在英语的 avant-garde 等说法里。

items.en: Avantage named the state of being ahead, and English took the noun with the sense of a favourable position.
items.cn: avantage 命名「处于前面」的状态，英语借入这个名词时取「有利位置」之义。

items.en: The noun is recorded in English in the fourteenth century, first in military and legal writing.
items.cn: 这个名词在十四世纪的英语文献中出现，最早见于军事与法律写作。

items.en: The phrase take advantage of splits into a neutral sense of using and a darker sense of exploiting.
items.cn: 短语 take advantage of 分化为中性的「利用」与更阴暗的「占便宜」两种意思。

note.en: The look-alike group is the avant family in English; the near-meaning group gathers words for being ahead, which differ in whether they name a position, a gain or a plain good.
note.cn: 形近组是英语里的 avant 词族；近义组收表示「领先」的词，差别在于它们说的是位置、收益，还是单纯的好处。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning productive of an advantage.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「能带来优势的」的形容词。

entries.definition: The negated form, naming a condition that holds you back.
entries.definitionCN: 加否定前缀的形式，指拖住你的不利条件。

entries.definition: A related word from the same avant stem, but centred on forward motion rather than on position.
entries.definitionCN: 同一 avant 词干的相关词，但核心是向前运动而非位置。

entries.definition: A slight lead or superiority, often the everyday word for a small advantage.
entries.definitionCN: 轻微的领先或优势，常是 advantage 的口语小词。

entries.definition: A good effect or profit, stressing the gain rather than the position.
entries.definitionCN: 良好的效果或收益，强调所得而非位置。

entries.definition: The state of being better or higher, a stronger and more abstract claim than advantage.
entries.definitionCN: 更好或更高的状态，比 advantage 更强、更抽象。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the French avant, the real verb phrases and the family that grows with -ous and dis-.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用法语 avant、真实的动词短语，以及由 -ous 与 dis- 生长的词族。

normal.en: Avant means before, and avant-garde is the guard that goes first; an advantage is the place that goes first.
normal.cn: avant 意为「在前」，avant-garde 是走在前面的卫队；advantage 就是走在前面的那个位置。

normal.en: The standard verb is take: take advantage of a chance, or take advantage of a person.
normal.cn: 标准动词是 take：take advantage of 既可以接机会，也可以接人。

normal.en: Have an advantage over someone is the fixed comparative phrase.
normal.cn: have an advantage over someone 是固定的比较说法。

normal.en: The negative is disadvantage, and the adjective is advantageous; both are regular.
normal.cn: 否定形式是 disadvantage，形容词是 advantageous，两者都很规则。

normal.en: In tennis, advantage is the point right after deuce, the clearest picture of being one step ahead.
normal.cn: 网球里的 advantage 是平分后的那一分，是「领先一步」最清楚的画面。

abstract.en: Picture two runners on a slope: the higher one sees the turn before the lower one.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人在斜坡上跑：高处的那个先看见弯道。

abstract.en: An advantage is not a thing you own but a position you occupy, which is why it can be taken.
abstract.cn: 优势不是你拥有的东西，而是你占据的位置，所以它可以被 take。

abstract.en: The same word covers a fair head start and an unfair squeeze, and context decides the tone.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指公平的先手，也指不公平的挤压，语气由语境决定。

examples.en: Living near the campus is a real advantage for a first-year student.
examples.cn: 对一年级学生来说，住在校园附近是实实在在的优势。

examples.en: The firm took advantage of the tax break to modernise its plant.
examples.cn: 这家公司利用税收减免把厂房现代化了。

examples.en: We should weigh the advantages against the risks before we sign.
examples.cn: 签字之前，我们应当把好处与风险权衡一下。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德万提吉」——万提吉，先提一步占上风：优势

root: 拉丁语 abante（从前面）→ 古法语 avant「在前」→ avantage「处于前面的状态」→ 英语 advantage，义为优势、有利条件与好处。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of advantage all describe standing ahead of others: a condition, a gain, the upper hand, the chance you seize, the person you exploit, a head start, a tennis point, and a strong point in an argument.
sensesIntro.cn: advantage 的八个义项都在描述「站在别人前面」：一个条件、一份收益、上风、被你抓住的机会、被你占便宜的人、先手、网球的一分，以及论证里的一处强点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a view from higher up the slope, seeing more of the road.
core.cn: 核心意象：从坡上更高的位置看见更多一段路。

branches.en: THE POSITION LINE: being ahead in place or in time is the root of every other sense.
branches.cn: 位置线：在空间或时间上靠前，是其余各个义项的根。

branches.en: THE GAIN LINE: whatever secures the forward position can be counted as a benefit.
branches.cn: 收益线：任何能保住靠前位置的东西，都可以算作好处。

branches.en: THE CONTEST LINE: games make the position literal, down to the tennis point after deuce.
branches.cn: 较量线：比赛把这个位置变成字面事实，一直到网球平分后的那一分。

branches.en: THE SEIZURE LINE: the open position can be taken fairly, or taken at someone else's cost.
branches.cn: 抢占线：空着的位置可以被公平占下，也可以踩着别人的代价占下。

branches.en: THE ARGUMENT LINE: a debate is a field of positions, so a strong point is an advantage.
branches.cn: 论证线：辩论是一片位置的场地，所以一处强点就是 advantage。

intro.en: Advantage is an Old French noun in -age built on avant, before; English adds -ous and the negating dis- to make the rest of the family.
intro.cn: advantage 是以 -age 结尾的古法语名词，建于 avant「在前」之上；英语加上 -ous 与否定前缀 dis- 造出词族其余成员。

latinIntro.en: Ante and abante are attested in Latin; avant and avantage are attested in Old French, so only the earliest link is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: ante 与 abante 在拉丁语中有文献；avant 与 avantage 在古法语中有文献，只有最早的连接属于构拟。

items.example: It is the oldest layer of the word.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个词最古老的一层。

items.example: It combines with ante in abante.
items.exampleCN: 它与 ante 组合成 abante。

items.example: It is the direct stem of the English noun.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语名词的直接词干。

items.example: It is the immediate source of advantage.
items.exampleCN: 它是 advantage 的直接来源。

items.example: It carries the French noun into English.
items.exampleCN: 它把法语名词带入英语。

derivatives.zh: 由 advantage 加 -ous 构成，义为「有利的」
由 dis- 加本词构成，义为「劣势；不利条件」

definition_zh: 有利的；有益的；有好处的
definition_en: producing a benefit or a better position; helpful to a plan or a person
core_image: 一股风正好推在你背后，让你省下半程力气
scene: 帆船赛前，老水手抬头看云，把舵柄交给徒弟。A steady offshore wind was advantageous for the smaller boat.
sceneCN: 这里 advantageous 是「有利的」（第 1 个义项：能带来好处或更好处境的）；句意为稳定的离岸风对小船有利。图中可辨识的物件：帆、舵柄、海面上的白浪。

pos.zh: 有利的；有益的；有好处的

derivatives.zh: 本形容词的名词基础，义为「优势；有利条件」
由 advantageous 加 -ly 构成，义为「有利地；有益地」
由否定前缀 dis- 加本词构成，义为「不利的」

senses.title: Producing a benefit
senses.definition: bringing a gain or making a situation better
senses.definitionCN: 带来收益或使处境变得更好
senses.example: Early planting is advantageous in a short growing season.
senses.exampleCN: 在生长季短的地方，早播是有利的。
senses.why: The adjective simply turns the noun advantage into a quality: whatever yields an advantage is advantageous.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是把名词 advantage 变成一种性质：凡能带来优势的，就是 advantageous。

senses.title: Favourable to a particular person
senses.definition: helpful to one side in a specific situation, usually followed by to
senses.definitionCN: 在具体情形中对某一方有帮助，通常后接 to
senses.example: The ruling was advantageous to small landowners.
senses.exampleCN: 这项裁决对小地主有利。
senses.why: A position is always someone's position, so the adjective naturally asks who is being helped and takes the preposition to.
senses.whyCN: 位置总是某人的位置，所以这个形容词自然会问「谁受了益」，并接上介词 to。

senses.title: Favourable in business terms
senses.definition: used of prices, terms or contracts that favour the buyer or the holder
senses.definitionCN: 用于对买方或持有人有利的价格、条款或合同
senses.example: They secured advantageous terms on the lease.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在租约上争取到了优惠条件。
senses.why: Commerce is the modern arena where being ahead is measured in money, so the adjective attaches to terms and prices.
senses.whyCN: 商业是现代社会用金钱衡量「领先」的场域，于是这个形容词常挂在条款与价格上。

senses.title: Giving a positional edge
senses.definition: describing ground, height or placement that gives an edge in a contest
senses.definitionCN: 形容在较量中带来优势的地形、高度或位置
senses.example: The regiment held an advantageous ridge above the road.
senses.exampleCN: 这个团占据着公路旁一处有利的山脊。
senses.why: The literal image of the word is higher or better ground, and military writing keeps that image alive.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的字面意象就是更高或更好的地势，军事写作让这幅画面一直活着。

senses.title: Good for both sides
senses.definition: in the phrase mutually advantageous, beneficial to each party in an arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 在 mutually advantageous 这一说法中，指对安排中的每一方都有益
senses.example: The two ports signed a mutually advantageous customs agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 两个港口签署了一份互利的海关协议。
senses.why: If advantage can be shared, the adjective can be pluralised in meaning, and diplomacy uses it to soften bargaining.
senses.whyCN: 既然优势可以共享，这个形容词在意义上就能复数化，外交语言便用它来柔化讨价还价。

senses.title: A polite word for self-serving
senses.definition: used politely of an arrangement that mainly serves the speaker's interest
senses.definitionCN: 礼貌地用于一项主要服务于说话者自身利益的安排
senses.example: He called the rezoning advantageous, though only his land gained value.
senses.exampleCN: 他称这次重新分区是有利的，尽管只有他自己的地涨了价。
senses.why: Because the adjective is neutral in form, it can dress a private gain in public language, which is why it often sounds evasive.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个形容词形式上中立，它能用公共语言包装私人收益，所以常听起来像在回避。

senses.title: An adaptive edge in biology
senses.definition: in biology, describing a trait that improves an organism's chance of survival
senses.definitionCN: 在生物学中，形容能提高生物存活机会的性状
senses.example: A thicker coat proved advantageous during the cold snap.
senses.exampleCN: 寒潮期间，更厚的毛皮被证明是有利的。
senses.why: Evolution is a long contest, and any inherited edge is an advantage written into a body.
senses.whyCN: 演化是一场漫长的较量，任何遗传上的优势都是写进身体里的 advantage。

senses.title: A recommended option in formal prose
senses.definition: in formal writing, describing a course of action that is worth choosing
senses.definitionCN: 在正式写作中，形容值得选取的做法
senses.example: It would be advantageous to settle the matter before the audit.
senses.exampleCN: 在审计之前把这件事解决掉会更为可取。
senses.why: Formal prose prefers the adjective over the blunt phrase good for you, so it becomes a polite recommendation.
senses.whyCN: 正式文字偏爱这个形容词，而不直说「对你有好处」，于是它成了一种礼貌的推荐。

intro.en: Advantageous is advantage plus the Latin adjective ending -ous; the noun beneath it comes from Old French avantage, from avant, before.
intro.cn: advantageous 是 advantage 加上拉丁形容词词尾 -ous；其下层的名词来自古法语 avantage，而 avantage 又来自 avant「在前」。

items.en: Ante meant before or in front, the oldest layer shared by the whole family.
items.cn: ante 意为「在……之前」或「在前面」，是整个词族共享的最古一层。

items.en: Avant meant before or ahead, and it survives in English in avant-garde.
items.cn: avant 意为「在前」，至今仍活在英语的 avant-garde 里。
