items.en: Avantage named a position ahead; English borrowed it as advantage.
items.cn: avantage 命名「靠前的位置」，英语借作 advantage。

items.en: The noun advantage settles in English, and the adjective is soon formed on it.
items.cn: 名词 advantage 在英语中稳定下来，形容词很快就在它上面构成。

items.en: French had its own adjective avantageux, and English -ous attaches to the borrowed stem in parallel.
items.cn: 法语本有形容词 avantageux，英语的 -ous 则平行地接在借来的词干上。

items.en: The adjective spreads into commerce, law and biology, keeping the same core of a better position.
items.cn: 这个形容词扩展到商业、法律与生物学，核心始终是「更好的位置」。

note.en: The look-alike group is the advantage family with its negation and adverb; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of benefit, which differ in formality and in whether they imply comparison.
note.cn: 形近组是 advantage 词族及其否定式与副词；近义组收表示「有好处」的形容词，差别在于正式程度以及是否隐含比较。

entries.definition: The noun this adjective is built on.
entries.definitionCN: 这个形容词所依附的名词。

entries.definition: The adverb, describing how something is done to one's benefit.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，描述某事如何被做得对己有利。

entries.definition: The negated adjective, naming what holds a person back.
entries.definitionCN: 加否定前缀的形容词，指拖住人的因素。

entries.definition: Producing a good effect, often used of health, policy or learning.
entries.definitionCN: 产生良好效果，常用于健康、政策或学习。

entries.definition: Showing approval or giving good conditions, broader than advantageous.
entries.definitionCN: 表示赞许或提供良好条件，范围比 advantageous 更广。

entries.definition: The plain everyday word for giving assistance, with no sense of competition.
entries.definitionCN: 日常口语里表示「有帮助」的朴素说法，不含竞争意味。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the avant stem, the -ous ending and the prepositions and collocations the adjective actually takes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用 avant 词干、-ous 词尾，以及这个形容词实际接的介词与搭配。

normal.en: Avant means before, -age makes a state, -ous makes a quality: the state of being ahead becomes a describable quality.
normal.cn: avant 意为「在前」，-age 造成状态，-ous 造成性质：处于前面的状态变成可描述的性质。

normal.en: The adjective takes to: advantageous to the buyer, advantageous to both sides.
normal.cn: 这个形容词接 to：advantageous to the buyer、advantageous to both sides。

normal.en: Business writing likes advantageous terms and advantageous prices.
normal.cn: 商业写作偏爱 advantageous terms 与 advantageous prices。

normal.en: Mutually advantageous is the diplomatic phrase for a deal both sides can defend.
normal.cn: mutually advantageous 是外交上形容「双方都能交代的交易」的说法。

normal.en: The comparatives are more and most advantageous, not advantageouer.
normal.cn: 比较级与最高级是 more advantageous 与 most advantageous，而不是 advantageouer。

abstract.en: Picture a tailwind that costs nothing and shortens the whole race.
abstract.cn: 想象一股不花分文、却缩短整场比赛的顺风。

abstract.en: The word always implies a comparison: something is better for someone than the alternative.
abstract.cn: 这个词总隐含比较：对某人来说，某事比另一种选择更好。

abstract.en: Its neutral tone is exactly what makes it useful when a private gain needs a public word.
abstract.cn: 它的中性语气，正是私人收益需要一个公共说辞时它好用的原因。

examples.en: A later start would be advantageous for the students who commute.
examples.cn: 对需要通勤的学生来说，晚一点开课会更有利。

examples.en: The treaty was advantageous to both coastal provinces.
examples.cn: 这项条约对两个沿海省份都有利。

examples.en: Reviewers found the proposal advantageous but poorly costed.
examples.cn: 评审者认为这个提案有利，但成本核算很差。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德万泰杰斯」——万泰皆得，占尽便宜：有利的

root: advantage（优势，源自拉丁 abante「从前面」经古法语 avantage）+ 形容词词尾 -ous → advantageous，义为「有利的；有益的」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of advantageous all describe something that improves your position: a plain benefit, a favour to one side, good commercial terms, higher ground, a deal good for both, a polite name for self-interest, an adaptive trait and a formal recommendation.
sensesIntro.cn: advantageous 的八个义项都描述「改善你的处境」：单纯的好处、对某一方的偏助、优惠的商业条件、更高的地势、对双方都好的交易、对私利的礼貌称呼、适应性的性状，以及正式的推荐。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wind at your back that shortens the distance.
core.cn: 核心意象：一股推在背后的风，把距离缩短。

branches.en: THE BENEFIT LINE: the adjective names what yields a gain, and asks for whom.
branches.cn: 收益线：这个形容词命名能带来收益之物，并追问对谁而言。

branches.en: THE MARKET LINE: prices and terms are the modern measure of a better position.
branches.cn: 市场线：价格与条款是现代衡量「更好位置」的尺度。

branches.en: THE EDGE LINE: from a ridge to an inherited trait, an edge is an edge.
branches.cn: 优势线：从一道山脊到一种遗传性状，优势就是优势。

branches.en: THE INTEREST LINE: advantage can be shared honestly or dressed up politely.
branches.cn: 利益线：优势可以被诚实地共享，也可以被礼貌地包装。

branches.en: THE DISCOURSE LINE: formal prose uses the adjective to recommend without insisting.
branches.cn: 话语线：正式文字用这个形容词来推荐，而不把话说死。

intro.en: Advantageous is advantage plus -ous; the noun itself is French in -age on avant, and the negating dis- and the adverb -ly complete the set.
intro.cn: advantageous 是 advantage 加 -ous；名词本身是建于 avant 之上的法语 -age 名词，否定前缀 dis- 与副词词尾 -ly 补全了这一组。

latinIntro.en: Ante and abante are attested in Latin; avant and avantage in Old French. The English endings -ous, -ly and dis- are all productive.
latinIntro.cn: ante 与 abante 在拉丁语中有文献，avant 与 avantage 在古法语中有文献；英语的 -ous、-ly 与 dis- 都仍能产。

items.example: It is the oldest layer of the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个词族最古老的一层。

items.example: It is the source of advantage.

items.exampleCN: 它把 advantage 变成 advantageous。

items.example: It forms the phrase mutually advantageous.

derivatives.zh: 由 advantageous 加 -ly 构成，义为「有利地」
由 dis- 加本词构成，义为「不利的」

definition_zh: 到来；出现；（首字母大写）基督降临节
definition_en: the arrival or first appearance of something important, especially after a long wait
core_image: 远处的地平线上终于出现一个正在靠近的黑点
scene: 天文台的观测窗前，一群人守到后半夜，屏幕上的光点终于开始变大。The advent of cheap sensors changed amateur astronomy completely.
sceneCN: 这里 advent 是「到来」（第 1 个义项：重要事物经过漫长等待后出现）；句意为廉价传感器的到来彻底改变了业余天文。图中可辨识的物件：望远镜、屏幕、保温杯。

pos.zh: 到来；出现；（大写）基督降临节

forms.label: 不可数（固定于 the advent of）

derivatives.zh: 由 Advent 加 -ist 构成，指「相信基督再临的教派成员」
由同一拉丁词根加 -itious 构成，义为「偶然外来的；非本位的」
由 Advent 加 -al 构成，义为「降临节的」

senses.title: The arrival of something long awaited
senses.definition: the arrival of an important event, thing or period after a period of waiting
senses.definitionCN: 重要的事件、事物或时期经过一段等待之后的到来
senses.example: The advent of the printing press reshaped reading in Europe.
senses.exampleCN: 印刷机的到来重塑了欧洲的阅读方式。
senses.why: The Latin noun means an arrival, so the plainest sense is simply that something has come.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁名词本义就是「到达」，所以最朴素的义项就是某物已经来了。

senses.title: The first appearance of a technology
senses.definition: the point at which a new tool, product or system first becomes available
senses.definitionCN: 新的工具、产品或系统首次可供使用的时点
senses.example: The advent of streaming ended the video shop on the corner.
senses.exampleCN: 流媒体的出现终结了街角的录像店。
senses.why: When an invention arrives it divides time into before and after, so the word marks a boundary in history.
senses.whyCN: 一项发明到来时把时间分成前后两段，所以这个词标记的是历史上的一道分界。

senses.title: The Christian season before Christmas
senses.definition: the four weeks of preparation before Christmas in the Christian calendar
senses.definitionCN: 基督教历法中圣诞节前为期四周的准备期
senses.example: The church stays unlit during Advent until the fourth Sunday.
senses.exampleCN: 降临节期间，教堂直到第四个主日才点灯。
senses.why: The season is named for a coming, because it is spent waiting for a birth that has not yet happened.
senses.whyCN: 这个节期以「到来」命名，因为它整个是在等待一件尚未发生的诞生。

senses.title: The expected return of Christ
senses.definition: in theology, the promised second coming of Christ at the end of history
senses.definitionCN: 神学中，历史终结时基督应许的第二次来临
senses.example: The sermon dwelt on the advent of the Lord in judgement.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇讲道详述了主在审判中的再临。
senses.why: The same noun serves the liturgical calendar and the end of time, both being arrivals that the faithful wait for.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词既服务礼仪年历，也服务时间的终点，两者都是信徒等待的来临。

senses.title: The start of a new era
senses.definition: the beginning of a new period in a field or in society
senses.definitionCN: 某一领域或社会中一个新时期的开始
senses.example: Historians speak of the advent of the industrial age.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家谈到工业时代的到来。
senses.why: An arrival can be large enough to name an age, and the word then stands for the opening of a period.
senses.whyCN: 一次到来可以大到足以命名一个时代，此时这个词就代指一个时期的开端。

senses.title: A person's arrival in a role
senses.definition: in formal or literary use, the arrival of a notable person into a place or post
senses.definitionCN: 在正式或文学用法中，某位重要人物进入某地或某职
senses.example: The advent of a new coach lifted the whole squad.
senses.exampleCN: 新教练的到任提振了整支队伍。
senses.why: People also arrive, and formal prose borrows the grand noun to give an entrance some weight.
senses.whyCN: 人也会到达，正式文字借用这个庄重的名词，给一次登场添上分量。

senses.title: The onset of a condition
senses.definition: in medical writing, the point at which a disease or symptom begins
senses.definitionCN: 医学写作中，疾病或症状开始出现的时点
senses.example: Treatment works best before the advent of severe symptoms.
senses.exampleCN: 在严重症状出现之前治疗效果最好。
senses.why: A disease arrives on its own schedule, so medicine uses the same noun for the hour it first shows itself.
senses.whyCN: 疾病按自己的时间表到来，于是医学用同一个名词指它初次露面的时刻。

senses.title: The coming of a season
senses.definition: in literary description, the arrival of a season or a natural change
senses.definitionCN: 在文学描写中，季节或自然变化的来临
senses.example: The advent of spring brought colour back to the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 春天的来临让山谷重新有了颜色。
senses.why: Seasons come whether or not anyone waits, and poetry keeps the old noun for that quiet arrival.
senses.whyCN: 季节无论有没有人等待都会来，诗歌便用这个古老的名词指那种安静的来临。

intro.en: Advent is the Latin noun adventus, an arrival, from advenire, to come to, built on venire, to come.
intro.cn: advent 是拉丁名词 adventus「到达」，来自 advenire「来到」，其基础是 venire「来」。

items.en: Venire meant to come, and it also feeds English venue, avenue and prevent.
items.cn: venire 意为「来」，英语的 venue、avenue 与 prevent 也由它而来。

items.en: Ad plus venire gave advenire, to come to or arrive at a place.
items.cn: ad 加 venire 构成 advenire，意为「来到」或「抵达某地」。

items.en: The fourth-declension noun adventus named the arrival itself, whether of a person, a season or a god.
items.cn: 第四变格名词 adventus 命名到达本身，无论到的是人、季节还是神。

items.en: Old French took the word as avent, and English borrowed it first in ecclesiastical texts.
items.cn: 古法语把这个词带作 avent，英语最先在教会文本中借入。

items.en: The liturgical sense is the earliest in English; the general sense of any arrival develops later.
items.cn: 英语中最早的义项是礼仪上的节期，泛指的「任何到来」则发展得较晚。

items.en: Modern usage splits the lowercase general noun from the capitalised season, a distinction kept in print.
items.cn: 现代用法把小写的泛指名词与大写的节期分开，印刷中一直保留这一区别。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same venire family, two of which have drifted far from plain arrival; the near-meaning group gathers plainer words for coming, which differ in register and in what they name.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 venire 词族的词，其中两个已远离「到达」的本义；近义组收表示「来临」的更朴素说法，差别在于语体与所指。

entries.definition: From Latin adventura, things about to happen, but now meaning a risky journey rather than a coming.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁语 adventura「即将发生之事」，但今义是冒险旅程，而非到来。

entries.definition: A botanical and medical adjective meaning arriving from outside rather than by nature.
entries.definitionCN: 植物学与医学形容词，指从外部而非本性带来的。

entries.definition: A member of a church that centres on the expected second coming.
entries.definitionCN: 以期待基督再临为核心的教会成员。

entries.definition: The plain word for reaching a place, used of people and trains more often than of eras.
entries.definitionCN: 到达某地的朴素说法，多用于人与列车，而非时代。

entries.definition: A general noun for something approaching, without the formality or grandeur of advent.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指某物临近的名词，没有 advent 的正式或庄重感。

entries.definition: The beginning of something unpleasant, especially a disease or winter.
entries.definitionCN: 不愉快之事的开始，尤指疾病或冬季。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin verb venire, the word family and the fixed phrases the noun forms in English.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用拉丁动词 venire、这个词族，以及这个名词在英语中构成的固定短语。

normal.en: Venire means to come, and ad adds direction: advenire is to come toward, so advent is the coming.
normal.cn: venire 意为「来」，ad 加上方向：advenire 就是「朝这边来」，所以 advent 就是「到来」。

normal.en: Venire is also hiding in venue, avenue and prevent, all about coming or blocking a coming.
normal.cn: venire 还藏在 venue、avenue 与 prevent 里，都与「来」或「挡住来」有关。

normal.en: The standard frame is the advent of something: the advent of the internet, the advent of cheap sensors.
normal.cn: 标准框架是 the advent of 某物：the advent of the internet、the advent of cheap sensors。

normal.en: Capitalised, Advent is the four weeks before Christmas, counted with an Advent calendar.
normal.cn: 首字母大写时，Advent 是圣诞节前的四周，用降临节日历一天天倒数。

normal.en: Before the advent of is the phrase for the world that existed earlier.
normal.cn: before the advent of 是描述「更早那个世界」的固定说法。

abstract.en: Picture a ship sighted from a cliff: first a dot, then a mast, then a whole hull.
abstract.cn: 想象从悬崖上望见一艘船：先是黑点，然后是桅杆，最后是整个船身。

abstract.en: An advent cuts history in two, which is why the word can name an age as easily as a gadget.
abstract.cn: 一次到来把历史切成两段，所以这个词既能命名一个时代，也能命名一件小器具。

abstract.en: The liturgical sense survives because waiting is still the shape of the season.
abstract.cn: 礼仪上的义项之所以留存，是因为等待仍然是这个节期的形状。

examples.en: The advent of online banking closed hundreds of small branches.
examples.cn: 网上银行的到来让数百家小分行关门。

examples.en: Before the advent of the railway, the journey took three days.
examples.cn: 在铁路出现之前，这段路程要走三天。

examples.en: The choir rehearses throughout Advent for the midnight service.
examples.cn: 唱诗班在整个降临节期间为午夜礼拜排练。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德文特」——阿德闻声而至：到来

root: 拉丁语 ad-（朝向）+ venire（来）→ advenire「来到」→ 名词 adventus「到达」，英语作 advent，指重要事物的到来，也指圣诞节前的降临节。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of advent all describe something crossing the horizon: an awaited thing, a new technology, the church season, the final return, a new era, a person's arrival, the onset of illness and the coming of spring.
sensesIntro.cn: advent 的八个义项都描述某物越过地平线：被等待的事物、新技术、教会的节期、最终的再临、新时代、某人的到任、病症的发作，以及春天的来临。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dot on the horizon growing until it is unmistakably here.
core.cn: 核心意象：地平线上的黑点不断变大，直到它确凿无疑地到了。

branches.en: THE ARRIVAL LINE: the plain coming and the first appearance of a tool are the same event seen close up.
branches.cn: 到来线：朴素的来临与一件工具的首次出现，是同一事件被拉近观看。

branches.en: THE SACRED LINE: the season and the second coming both turn waiting into a calendar.
branches.cn: 神圣线：节期与再临都把等待变成一份日历。

branches.en: THE EPOCH LINE: a large enough arrival becomes the name of an age.
branches.cn: 时代线：一次足够大的到来会变成时代的名字。

branches.en: THE ENTRANCE LINE: people and diseases alike make their entrance on the same noun.
branches.cn: 登场线：人与疾病都用同一个名词完成自己的登场。

branches.en: THE SEASON LINE: spring arrives without waiting, and the old noun still fits.
branches.cn: 季节线：春天并不等待谁就来了，而这个古老名词依然合用。

intro.en: Advent is a Latin fourth-declension noun from advenire; English keeps the -vent stem and builds -ist, -itious and -al on it.
intro.cn: advent 是来自 advenire 的拉丁第四变格名词；英语保留 -vent 词干，并在其上构成 -ist、-itious 与 -al。

latinIntro.en: Venire, advenire and adventus are all attested in Latin, so the chain needs no reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: venire、advenire 与 adventus 在拉丁语中均有文献，这条链条无需构拟。

items.example: It turns venire into a coming toward.
items.exampleCN: 它把 venire 变成「朝这边来」。

items.example: It is the semantic core of the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个词族的意义核心。

items.example: It is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: It appears in advent, event and prevent.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 advent、event 与 prevent 中。

derivatives.zh: 由 Advent 加 -ist 构成，指「期待基督再临的教派成员」
由同一词根加 -itious 构成，义为「偶然外来的」

definition_zh: 冒险；奇遇；冒险经历；冒险活动
definition_en: an exciting and sometimes dangerous experience or journey, especially one with an uncertain outcome
core_image: 踏出熟悉边界的那一步，前面没有地图
scene: 码头边的旧酒馆里，几个水手围着桌子摊开一张缺角的海图。The crossing to the island was an adventure none of them would forget.
sceneCN: 这里 adventure 是「冒险经历」（第 1 个义项：令人兴奋又带危险的经历）；句意为前往那座岛的横渡是他们谁都忘不掉的一次冒险。图中可辨识的物件：海图、酒杯、桌角的地图钉。

pos.zh: 冒险；奇遇；冒险经历

derivatives.zh: 由 adventure 加 -ous 构成，义为「爱冒险的；充满危险的」
由 adventure 加 -er 构成，义为「冒险者」，也指靠冒险谋利的人
由前缀 mis- 加本词构成，义为「不幸的意外；事故」

senses.title: An exciting and risky experience
senses.definition: an experience that is exciting because it involves risk and uncertainty
senses.definitionCN: 因涉及风险与不确定而令人兴奋的经历
senses.example: Their first night in the desert was a real adventure.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在沙漠里的第一夜是真正的冒险。
senses.why: The Latin source means things about to happen, so an adventure is an experience whose ending is still unknown.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源意为「即将发生之事」，所以一次冒险就是结局仍未可知的经历。

senses.title: A journey into the unknown
senses.definition: a journey to a place where the route or the outcome is not known in advance
senses.definitionCN: 前往路线或结果事先并不知晓之地的旅行
senses.example: They set out on an adventure across the northern ice.
senses.exampleCN: 他们出发去北方冰原探险。
senses.why: A journey is the commonest shape of the unknown, so the word attaches naturally to travel.
senses.whyCN: 旅行是「未知」最常见的形状，所以这个词自然挂在远行上。

senses.title: A commercial venture of risk
senses.definition: in older commercial language, a trading venture in which merchants risked their goods
senses.definitionCN: 较早的商业用语中，商人以货物承担风险的一次贸易行动
senses.example: The merchants funded an adventure to the spice ports.
senses.exampleCN: 商人们出资经营一项前往香料港口的风险事业。
senses.why: Sea trade once carried the same uncertainty as exploration, so the same noun served the counting house.
senses.whyCN: 海上贸易曾经与探险承担同样的不确定，于是同一个名词也服务于账房。

senses.title: A romance episode in literature
senses.definition: in medieval and later romance, a knight's series of marvelous undertakings
senses.definitionCN: 在中世纪及后世传奇中，骑士一系列奇异的功业
senses.example: The tale strings together one adventure after another.
senses.exampleCN: 这个故事把一次又一次传奇经历串在一起。
senses.why: Romance narrative is built from episodes of risk and marvel, and English borrowed the word to name them.
senses.whyCN: 传奇叙事由风险与奇异的片段搭成，英语借这个词来命名这些片段。

senses.title: A designed thrill for visitors
senses.definition: a commercial attraction or activity built to give paying visitors a safe thrill
senses.definitionCN: 为付费游客提供安全刺激而建的商业游乐项目或活动
senses.example: The park sells a night adventure with ropes and headlamps.
senses.exampleCN: 这个乐园卖一项带绳索与头灯的夜间探险。
senses.why: Modern leisure manufactures the shape of risk without its cost, and keeps the old word for the product.
senses.whyCN: 现代休闲制造出风险的形状而不付风险的代价，并沿用旧词来称呼这个产品。

senses.title: An unexpected episode
senses.definition: a striking or unusual episode that happens without being sought
senses.definitionCN: 并非刻意追寻却发生的引人注目或不寻常的插曲
senses.example: Losing his wallet in Lisbon turned into an adventure of its own.
senses.exampleCN: 在里斯本丢钱包，本身变成了一段意外的插曲。
senses.why: Anything that unfolds unpredictably can be called an adventure, even when nobody chose it.
senses.whyCN: 任何不可预测地展开的事都能被称为 adventure，哪怕没人主动选择它。

senses.title: The appetite for risk itself
senses.definition: as a mass noun, the taste for novelty and risk rather than for safety
senses.definitionCN: 作不可数名词时，指偏爱新奇与风险而非安稳的胃口
senses.example: There is still adventure in her, even at seventy.
senses.exampleCN: 即使到了七十岁，她身上仍有冒险精神。
senses.why: English lets a countable noun become a quality, so a series of deeds turns into a disposition.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许可数名词变成一种气质，于是一连串行为就转成一种性情。

senses.title: A discreet word for an escapade
senses.definition: in literary or ironic use, a romantic or sexual escapade spoken of as a journey
senses.definitionCN: 在文学或反讽用法中，被说成一段旅程的浪漫或情色韵事
senses.example: The novel treats his Paris adventure as a chapter, not a scandal.
senses.exampleCN: 这本小说把他的巴黎韵事当作一章，而不当作丑闻。
senses.why: Calling an affair a journey borrows the innocence of travel, which is exactly the irony intended.
senses.whyCN: 把一段私情说成旅程，借用了旅行的无害感，而这正是反讽所在。

intro.en: Adventure comes from Latin adventura, the things about to happen, a future participle of advenire, to come to.
intro.cn: adventure 来自拉丁语 adventura「即将发生之事」，它是 advenire「来到」的将来分词。

items.en: Venire meant to come, and it also lies behind venue and avenue.
items.cn: venire 意为「来」，英语的 venue 与 avenue 也由它而来。

items.en: Ad plus venire meant to come to, to arrive, or to fall to someone's lot.
items.cn: ad 加 venire 意为「来到」「抵达」，也指「落到某人头上」。

items.en: The future participle adventura named what is going to happen, a word full of open endings.
items.cn: 将来分词 adventura 命名「将要发生的事」，这个词里满是未定的结局。

items.en: Old French aventure carried both chance and a knight's dangerous enterprise.
items.cn: 古法语 aventure 同时带着「机缘」与「骑士的危险功业」两种意思。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the middle ages, first in romances and later in trade.
items.cn: 英语在中世纪借入这个词，最早见于传奇，后来也用于贸易。

items.en: Modern English adds the leisure sense of adventure travel and the theme-park adventure.
items.cn: 现代英语又添上探险旅行与主题乐园探险这类休闲义。

note.en: The look-alike group is the English family from the same stem; the near-meaning group gathers words for risky undertakings, which differ in scale, in formality and in whether danger is real.
note.cn: 形近组是同一词干长出的英语词族；近义组收表示风险行动的词，差别在于规模、正式程度，以及危险是否真实。

entries.definition: The adjective for a person or journey that seeks risk.
entries.definitionCN: 形容人或旅程寻求风险的形容词。

entries.definition: The person who seeks adventure, sometimes with a hint of recklessness.
entries.definitionCN: 寻求冒险的人，有时带一丝鲁莽的暗示。

entries.definition: An unfortunate chance event, literally a bad coming.
entries.definitionCN: 不幸的偶然事件，字面上是「坏的到来」。

entries.definition: A risky undertaking, often financial, sharing the same Latin root but stressing exposure.
entries.definitionCN: 风险行动，常指财务上的，词源相同但更强调风险暴露。

entries.definition: An organised journey with a stated purpose, more planned than an adventure.
entries.definitionCN: 有明确目的的组织化远行，比冒险更有计划。

entries.definition: A reckless or mischievous episode, smaller and often disapproved of.
entries.definitionCN: 鲁莽或顽皮的插曲，规模更小，且常受非议。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin future participle, the real word family and the collocations adventure forms with travel and story.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用拉丁将来分词、真实词族，以及 adventure 与旅行、故事构成的搭配。

normal.en: Adventura means things about to happen, so an adventure is a story whose next page is blank.
normal.cn: adventura 意为「即将发生之事」，所以一次冒险就是下一页还空着的故事。

normal.en: The family runs adventurer, adventurous and misadventure, one person, one quality, one bad outcome.
normal.cn: 词族里有 adventurer、adventurous 与 misadventure，分别是一个人、一种性质、一个坏结果。

normal.en: English says embark on an adventure and set out on an adventure, both journey verbs.
normal.cn: 英语说 embark on an adventure 与 set out on an adventure，两个都是启程动词。

normal.en: Sense of adventure is the mass-noun phrase for the appetite itself.
normal.cn: sense of adventure 是形容这股胃口本身的不可数短语。

normal.en: Adventure travel and adventure park are the modern commercial uses.
normal.cn: adventure travel 与 adventure park 是现代的商业用法。

abstract.en: Picture a map with its corner torn off, so the last stretch must be guessed.
abstract.cn: 想象一张被撕掉一角的地图，最后一段路只能靠猜。

abstract.en: The word began as a statement about the future, which is why it suits anything with an open ending.
abstract.cn: 这个词最初是一句关于将来的话，所以它适合任何结局未定之事。

abstract.en: Risk sold as leisure keeps the shape of danger and removes the bill.
abstract.cn: 被当作休闲出售的风险，保留了危险的形状，却把账单拿走了。

examples.en: The whole trip was an adventure from the first train to the last ferry.
examples.cn: 整趟旅行从第一班火车到最后一班渡轮都是一场冒险。

examples.en: He has a sense of adventure that his desk job slowly smothered.
examples.cn: 他有冒险精神，而这份坐办公室的工作慢慢把它闷死了。

examples.en: The old romance tells of an adventure in a forest full of signs.
examples.cn: 那部古老传奇讲述了一场发生在满是预兆的森林里的冒险。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德文彻」——文彻背着包远行：冒险

root: 拉丁语 advenire（来到）的将来分词 adventura「即将发生之事」→ 古法语 aventure「机缘、骑士功业」→ 英语 adventure，指充满未知与风险的经历。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of adventure all keep an open ending: a risky experience, an unknown journey, a trading venture, a romance episode, a paid thrill, an accidental episode, the appetite for risk and a discreet name for an escapade.
sensesIntro.cn: adventure 的八个义项都保留着未定的结局：危险经历、未知远行、风险贸易、传奇片段、付费刺激、意外插曲、对风险的胃口，以及对风流韵事的委婉称呼。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a step past the edge of the map.
core.cn: 核心意象：跨出地图边缘的那一步。

branches.en: THE JOURNEY LINE: the experience and the journey are one shape, risk met on the move.
branches.cn: 旅程线：经历与远行是同一个形状，都是在移动中遭遇风险。

branches.en: THE LEDGER LINE: sea trade took the same word because it took the same risk.
branches.cn: 账本线：海上贸易取用同一个词，因为它承担同一种风险。

branches.en: THE EPISODE LINE: romance and accident both produce a story worth telling.
branches.cn: 片段线：传奇与意外都产出一个值得讲的故事。

branches.en: THE APPETITE LINE: leisure sells the thrill, and the noun turns into a disposition.
branches.cn: 胃口线：休闲出售刺激，而这个名词转成一种性情。

branches.en: THE IRONY LINE: calling an affair a journey borrows the innocence of travel.
branches.cn: 反讽线：把私情说成旅程，借用了旅行的无害感。

intro.en: Adventure is a Latin future participle turned noun; English keeps the -ure ending and builds -ous, -er and the negating mis- on the stem.
intro.cn: adventure 是由拉丁将来分词转成的名词；英语保留 -ure 词尾，并在词干上构成 -ous、-er 与否定前缀 mis-。

latinIntro.en: Venire, advenire and the future participle adventura are attested in Latin, so no step of the chain is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: venire、advenire 与将来分词 adventura 在拉丁语中均有文献，这条链上没有任何一步属于构拟。

items.example: It gives the verb its direction.
It is the core of the family.
It is the direct source of adventure.
items.exampleCN: 它是 adventure 的直接来源。

items.example: It carried the word into English.

derivatives.zh: 由 adventure 加 -ous 构成，义为「爱冒险的」
由 adventure 加 -er 构成，义为「冒险者」
由 mis- 加本词构成，义为「不幸的意外」

definition_zh: 爱冒险的；大胆的；充满危险的
definition_en: eager to try new and risky things, or full of risk and excitement
core_image: 背包里塞着绳索，眼睛却盯着没有足迹的方向
scene: 山谷入口的木牌上写着禁止通行，一个年轻人却已经在解背包的扣子。An adventurous hiker ignored the sign and took the old goat path.
sceneCN: 这里 adventurous 是「爱冒险的」（第 1 个义项：乐于尝试新鲜而带风险之事的）；句意为一名爱冒险的徒步者无视告示，走上了那条旧羊道。图中可辨识的物件：木牌、背包、绳索。

pos.zh: 爱冒险的；大胆的；充满危险的

derivatives.zh: 本形容词的名词基础，义为「冒险；奇遇」
由 adventurous 加 -ly 构成，义为「冒险地；大胆地」
由 adventurer 的词干加 -ism 构成，义为「冒险主义」，多含贬义

senses.title: Eager for new and risky experience
senses.definition: describing a person who actively seeks novelty and risk
senses.definitionCN: 形容主动寻求新奇与风险的人
senses.example: She was adventurous enough to move abroad with no job lined up.
senses.exampleCN: 她够爱冒险，没找好工作就搬到了国外。
senses.why: The -ous ending turns adventure into a trait, so the adjective describes a person's appetite rather than an event.
senses.whyCN: -ous 词尾把 adventure 变成一种特质，所以这个形容词描述的是人的胃口，而不是事件。

senses.title: Full of risk and excitement
senses.definition: describing a journey or undertaking that contains real danger
senses.definitionCN: 形容包含真实危险的旅程或行动
senses.example: The descent through the gorge was an adventurous route.
senses.exampleCN: 穿过峡谷下行的路线充满冒险。
senses.why: The same adjective can look outward at the journey, where the risk belongs to the road rather than to the person.
senses.whyCN: 同一个形容词也可以朝外看旅程，此时风险属于道路，而不属于人。

senses.title: Unconventional in method
senses.definition: describing an approach that departs from the safe or standard way
senses.definitionCN: 形容偏离稳妥或标准做法的办法
senses.example: The director took an adventurous approach to a familiar play.
senses.exampleCN: 导演对一出熟悉的戏采取了大刀阔斧的处理。
senses.why: Departing from the standard route is the mental version of leaving the marked path.
senses.whyCN: 偏离标准路线，是「离开标记好的小路」在思维层面的版本。

senses.title: Bold in taste
senses.definition: describing choices in food, fashion or design that risk being disliked
senses.definitionCN: 形容在饮食、时装或设计上敢于冒被厌恶之险的选择
senses.example: The menu is adventurous, with fermented fruit and raw fish.
senses.exampleCN: 这份菜单很大胆，有发酵水果和生鱼。
senses.why: Taste is a small arena of risk, where trying the strange dish is the everyday form of adventure.
senses.whyCN: 口味是一个小型的风险场，尝试怪菜就是冒险的日常形式。

senses.title: Risky in financial terms
senses.definition: describing an investment or portfolio that accepts high risk for high return
senses.definitionCN: 形容为求高回报而接受高风险的投资或组合
senses.example: Analysts warned that the fund was too adventurous for retirees.
senses.exampleCN: 分析师警告说，这只基金对退休者来说过于激进。
senses.why: Finance reuses the travel metaphor: a portfolio can take an unmarked route too.
senses.whyCN: 金融沿用旅行的比喻：一份投资组合也可以走没有标记的路。

senses.title: Marvellous in the manner of romance
senses.definition: in literary description, full of marvels and unlikely turns
senses.definitionCN: 在文学描写中，充满奇观与不大可能的转折
senses.example: The memoir reads like an adventurous romance.
senses.exampleCN: 这本回忆录读起来像一部传奇冒险故事。
senses.why: Romance is the genre where adventure was first a literary shape, and the adjective still carries that glow.
senses.whyCN: 传奇是 adventure 最初获得文学形状的体裁，这个形容词仍带着那层光。

senses.title: Physically bold, of a child
senses.definition: describing a child who climbs, explores and tests limits
senses.definitionCN: 形容爱攀爬、爱探索、不断试探界限的孩子
senses.example: An adventurous toddler will find every unlocked door.
senses.exampleCN: 一个胆大的幼儿会找到每一扇没锁的门。
senses.why: The trait appears early, before any journey, as a body testing the edges of a room.
senses.whyCN: 这种特质很早就出现，还在任何远行之前，表现为一具身体在试探房间的边缘。

senses.title: Recklessly bold, with disapproval
senses.definition: used with disapproval of boldness that ignores sensible limits
senses.definitionCN: 带不赞同地形容无视合理界限的胆大
senses.example: Critics called the plan adventurous rather than innovative.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者称这个计划是鲁莽，而不是创新。
senses.why: A trait praised in one context is blamed in another, so the adjective can slide from courage to recklessness.
senses.whyCN: 同一种特质在此处受赞、在彼处受责，所以这个形容词能从勇气滑向鲁莽。

intro.en: Adventurous is adventure plus -ous; the noun goes back through Old French aventure to Latin adventura, things about to happen.
intro.cn: adventurous 是 adventure 加 -ous；名词经古法语 aventure 上溯到拉丁语 adventura「即将发生之事」。

items.en: Venire meant to come, the root shared by venue, avenue and event.
items.cn: venire 意为「来」，venue、avenue 与 event 共享这个词根。

items.en: The future participle adventura named what is about to happen, a word of open endings.
items.cn: 将来分词 adventura 命名「将要发生的事」，是一个结局未定的词。

items.en: Aventure meant chance or a risky enterprise, and it carried both into English.
items.cn: aventure 意为「机缘」或「风险功业」，并把两者一并带进英语。

items.en: French formed the adjective aventureux, meaning given to risk, and English followed with its own -ous form.
items.cn: 法语构成形容词 aventureux，意为「爱冒险的」，英语随后用自己的 -ous 形式跟上。

items.en: The English adjective settles in the sixteenth century, first describing travellers and tales.
items.cn: 英语形容词在十六世纪稳定下来，最早用于描述旅行者与故事。

items.en: Modern use extends the adjective to cuisine, finance and child behaviour, keeping the same risk at its centre.
items.cn: 现代用法把这个形容词扩展到饮食、金融与儿童行为，中心始终是同一份风险。

note.en: The look-alike group is the adventure family; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of boldness, which differ in whether the risk is physical, social or merely stylistic.
note.cn: 形近组是 adventure 词族；近义组收表示胆大的形容词，差别在于风险是身体上的、社交上的，还是仅仅风格上的。

entries.definition: The noun this adjective describes.
entries.definitionCN: 这个形容词所描述的名词。

entries.definition: The person, often with a hint that the risk is taken for gain.
entries.definitionCN: 冒险的人，常暗示其冒险带有图利目的。

entries.definition: A rarer synonym built with -some instead of -ous.
entries.definitionCN: 用 -some 而非 -ous 构成的较少见同义词。

entries.definition: Willing to take great risks, stressing courage in the moment rather than a lasting trait.
entries.definitionCN: 愿意承担大风险，强调当下的勇气而非持久的特质。

entries.definition: Confident and unafraid, a broader word that need not involve physical danger.
entries.definitionCN: 自信而不惧，范围更广，不一定涉及身体危险。

entries.definition: Inclined to take chances, a formal and slightly old-fashioned synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 倾向于碰运气，正式而略显过时的同义词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the aventure stem, the -ous ending and the collocations the adjective actually forms.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用 aventure 词干、-ous 词尾，以及这个形容词实际构成的搭配。

normal.en: Adventure plus -ous makes a trait: a person who carries adventure inside.
normal.cn: adventure 加 -ous 造出一种特质：把冒险装在身体里的人。

normal.en: The same adjective describes the traveller and the road, the appetite and the danger.
normal.cn: 同一个形容词既描述旅行者，也描述道路；既描述胃口，也描述危险。

normal.en: Be adventurous with food is the everyday invitation to try something strange.
normal.cn: be adventurous with food 是邀请人尝试怪东西的日常说法。

normal.en: The comparatives are more and most adventurous, never adventurouer.
normal.cn: 比较级与最高级是 more 与 most adventurous，绝不用 adventurouer。

normal.en: Adventurism is the noun for the disapproved version, risk taken for its own sake.
normal.cn: adventurism 是带贬义的名词，指为冒险而冒险。

abstract.en: Picture a boot print just outside the rope that marks the safe path.
abstract.cn: 想象安全小路的绳索之外，正好有一个靴印。

abstract.en: The word lives on a sliding scale: curiosity at one end, recklessness at the other.
abstract.cn: 这个词活在一条滑动刻度上：一端是好奇，另一端是鲁莽。

abstract.en: Small risks rehearse big ones, which is why a child and a fund manager can share the word.
abstract.cn: 小风险是巨大风险的排练，所以一个孩子和一位基金经理能共用这个词。

examples.en: The more adventurous students chose the mountain route.
examples.cn: 更爱冒险的学生选择了山路。

examples.en: An adventurous menu can frighten a tired traveller.
examples.cn: 一份大胆的菜单会吓到疲惫的旅人。

examples.en: She was adventurous with colour, and her paintings showed it.
examples.cn: 她用色大胆，她的画作看得出这一点。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德文彻勒斯」——彻勒斯敢往没路的地方走：爱冒险的

root: adventure（冒险，源自拉丁 adventura「即将发生之事」）+ 形容词词尾 -ous → adventurous，义为爱冒险的、充满危险的。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of adventurous all measure appetite for risk: a person, a journey, a method, a taste, a portfolio, a romance, a child and a criticised boldness.
sensesIntro.cn: adventurous 的八个义项都在衡量对风险的胃口：一个人、一段旅程、一种方法、一种口味、一份投资、一部传奇、一个孩子，以及一种受批评的胆大。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pack of rope carried toward ground with no footprints.
core.cn: 核心意象：背着绳索，走向没有足迹的地面。

branches.en: THE PERSON LINE: the appetite for risk shows first in a body, then in a character.
branches.cn: 人物线：对风险的胃口先在身体上显露，然后在性格上显露。

branches.en: THE JOURNEY LINE: the road and the romance both carry the danger outside the traveller.
branches.cn: 旅程线：道路与传奇都把危险放在旅行者之外。

branches.en: THE METHOD LINE: leaving the marked path becomes leaving the standard method.
branches.cn: 方法线：离开标记好的小路，变成离开标准的做法。

branches.en: THE TASTE LINE: food and money are small arenas where the same risk is tried.
branches.cn: 口味线：饮食与金钱是同一份风险被尝试的小型场地。

branches.en: THE LIMIT LINE: the same boldness is praised or blamed depending on who pays for it.
branches.cn: 界限线：同一份胆大是受赞还是受责，取决于谁为它买单。

intro.en: Adventurous is aventure plus -ous; the noun behind it is a Latin future participle, and English adds -ly and -ism to the same stem.
intro.cn: adventurous 是 aventure 加 -ous；其后的名词是拉丁将来分词，英语又在同一词干上加 -ly 与 -ism。

latinIntro.en: Venire, advenire and adventura are attested in Latin; the French adjective aventureux is attested too, so only the earliest link is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: venire、advenire 与 adventura 在拉丁语中有文献；法语形容词 aventureux 也有文献，只有最早的连接属于构拟。

items.example: It is the seed of adventure.
It brought the noun into English.
items.exampleCN: 它把这个名词带进英语。

derivatives.zh: 由 adventurous 加 -ly 构成，义为「冒险地」
由 adventurer 的词干加 -ism 构成，义为「冒险主义」

definition_zh: 不利的；有害的；相反的；对立的
definition_en: having a harmful or negative effect, or pointing in the opposite direction
core_image: 迎面顶来的风，把人和车都往回推
scene: 山口的天气预报牌闪着红光，货车司机把车速降了一半。Adverse weather forced the convoy to spend the night in the pass.
sceneCN: 这里 adverse 是「不利的」（第 1 个义项：产生有害或负面影响的）；句意为恶劣的天气迫使车队在山口过夜。图中可辨识的物件：预报牌、货车、山口的路标。

pos.zh: 不利的；有害的；相反的；对立的

derivatives.zh: 由 adverse 加 -ly 构成，义为「不利地；有害地」
由 adverse 的词干加 -ity 构成，义为「逆境；厄运」
由词干加 -ative 构成，语法术语，指「表示转折的（词）」

senses.title: Producing a harmful effect
senses.definition: causing harm or a negative result, especially of a drug or a condition
senses.definitionCN: 造成伤害或负面结果，尤用于药物或状况
senses.example: The drug's adverse effects included dizziness and nausea.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药的不良反应包括头晕与恶心。
senses.why: Adversus meant turned against, and anything turned against you works against your good.
senses.whyCN: adversus 意为「转向对立面」，任何转向你对立面的事物都在对抗你的好处。

senses.title: Unfavourable conditions
senses.definition: describing weather, markets or circumstances that work against success
senses.definitionCN: 形容阻碍成功的天气、市场或境况
senses.example: Adverse market conditions delayed the sale for a year.
senses.exampleCN: 不利的市场行情让出售推迟了一年。
senses.why: Conditions are pictured as forces that can face you or follow you, and adverse ones face you.
senses.whyCN: 外部条件被想象成可以迎面或顺身的力量，adverse 就是迎面而来的那种。

senses.title: Opposite in direction
senses.definition: pointing or flowing in the opposite direction to one's course
senses.definitionCN: 指向或流向与行进方向相反
senses.example: An adverse current held the boat below the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 一股逆向水流把小船压在桥下。
senses.why: The literal Latin picture is a force turned against you, so wind and water can be adverse in the plain physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语的字面画面是一股转向你的力量，所以风与水可以在纯物理意义上 adverse。

senses.title: Hostile or opposed in attitude
senses.definition: in formal use with to, opposed to or unfriendly toward something
senses.definitionCN: 正式用法中接 to，指对某事物持反对或不友好的态度
senses.example: The board was adverse to any change in the dividend.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会对红利的任何变动都持反对态度。
senses.why: A mind can turn against an idea just as a wind turns against a ship, so the adjective extends to attitudes.
senses.whyCN: 心思可以像风对着船那样对着一个想法，所以这个形容词延伸到态度。

senses.title: Against one's interest in law
senses.definition: in legal language, describing a claim or possession asserted against another's rights
senses.definitionCN: 法律用语中，形容针对他人权利提出的主张或占有
senses.example: The purchaser ignored an adverse claim on the land.
senses.exampleCN: 买主无视了针对这块地的一项不利主张。
senses.why: Law speaks of interests turned against each other, and the word marks the side that loses by the turn.
senses.whyCN: 法律讲的是彼此对立的各种利益，这个词标记的是因这一转向而吃亏的一方。

senses.title: A side effect in medicine
senses.definition: the standard label for an unwanted bodily response to treatment
senses.definitionCN: 治疗引起的不想要的机体反应的通行标签
senses.example: Report any adverse reaction to the clinic at once.
senses.exampleCN: 一旦出现任何不良反应，立刻向诊所报告。
senses.why: Medicine needs a neutral word for harm done by a remedy, and adverse supplies it without implying blame.
senses.whyCN: 医学需要一个中性的词来描述治疗造成的伤害，adverse 正好提供，而不含指责。

senses.title: A risk in selection
senses.definition: in economics and insurance, describing the tendency of the riskiest cases to seek cover most
senses.definitionCN: 在经济学与保险中，形容风险最高者最积极寻求保障的倾向
senses.example: Adverse selection raised the average cost of the policy.
senses.exampleCN: 逆向选择抬高了这份保单的平均成本。
senses.why: The market turns against the seller when the worst cases arrive first, which is the same turn seen from the other side.
senses.whyCN: 最坏的案例先到时，市场就转向卖方，这是从另一面看到的同一个转向。

senses.title: Unkind fortune in literature
senses.definition: in literary writing, describing fate or fortune that works against a character
senses.definitionCN: 在文学写作中，形容与人物作对的命运或运势
senses.example: He blamed adverse fate for the loss of the estate.
senses.exampleCN: 他把产业的丧失归咎于不济的命运。
senses.why: Fortune was once a power that could face a person, and the old adjective survives in that fatalistic tone.
senses.whyCN: 命运曾被想象成一种能迎面而来的力量，这个古老的形容词便活在那份宿命语气里。

intro.en: Adverse is Latin adversus, turned against, the past participle of adversari, from ad and vertere, to turn.
intro.cn: adverse 是拉丁语 adversus「转向对立面」，为 adversari 的过去分词，由 ad 与 vertere「转」构成。

items.en: Vertere meant to turn, and it also gives English convert, reverse and vertigo.
items.cn: vertere 意为「转」，英语的 convert、reverse 与 vertigo 也由它而来。

items.en: Ad plus versum, toward turned, described a thing placed facing you.
items.cn: ad 加 versum「转向」，描述一个被摆到你面前的事物。

items.en: The participle adversus meant turned against or hostile, and it served both weather and opponents.
items.cn: 分词 adversus 意为「转向对立」或「敌对」，既用于天气，也用于对手。

items.en: Old French took the word as avers, and English borrowed it in legal and medical writing.
items.cn: 古法语把它带作 avers，英语最早在法律与医学写作中借入。

items.en: English records the adjective in the fourteenth century with the sense of contrary or unfavourable.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪记录这个形容词，义为「相反的」或「不利的」。

items.en: Modern usage fixes the phrase adverse effect and keeps adverse to for formal opposition.
items.cn: 现代用法固定了 adverse effect 这一短语，并保留 adverse to 表示正式反对。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same vertere family, including the classic trap averse, which means unwilling rather than harmful; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of harm and opposition.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 vertere 词族的词，其中包括经典陷阱 averse，它意为「不情愿」而非「有害」；近义组收表示伤害与对立的形容词。

entries.definition: Unwilling or reluctant, usually with to; same vertere root but a different prefix and a personal feeling rather than an external harm.
entries.definitionCN: 意为不情愿、反感，通常接 to；与 adverse 同出 vertere 词根但前缀不同，说的是人的感受而非外部的伤害。

entries.definition: The noun for misfortune, the state that adverse conditions create.
entries.definitionCN: 指厄运的名词，即不利条件造成的处境。

entries.definition: An opponent, literally one who turns against you.
entries.definitionCN: 对手，字面上是「转向你的人」。

entries.definition: Not helpful or not approving, a broader word than adverse.
entries.definitionCN: 不有帮助或不表赞同，范围比 adverse 更广。

entries.definition: Causing damage, the everyday word for what adverse says in formal contexts.
entries.definitionCN: 造成损害，是 adverse 在正式语境中所说的内容的日常说法。

entries.definition: Openly unfriendly or aggressive, stronger and more personal than adverse.
entries.definitionCN: 公开不友好或带攻击性，比 adverse 更强、更针对人。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin vertere, the real word family and the medical and legal phrases adverse appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用拉丁语 vertere、真实词族，以及 adverse 出现的医学与法律短语。

normal.en: Adversus is turned against: ad plus vertere. Whatever faces you and pushes back is adverse.
normal.cn: adversus 就是「转向对立」：ad 加 vertere。任何迎面顶你、把你往回推的东西都是 adverse。

normal.en: Keep adverse and averse apart: adverse weather is bad weather, but averse to risk means unwilling to take it.
normal.cn: 把 adverse 与 averse 分开：adverse weather 是坏天气，而 averse to risk 是不愿承担风险。

normal.en: The fixed medical phrase is adverse reaction or adverse effect.
normal.cn: 医学上的固定说法是 adverse reaction 或 adverse effect。

normal.en: Adversity is the noun, and an adversary is the person who turns against you.
normal.cn: adversity 是名词，adversary 是转向你的那个人。

normal.en: Adverse to is the formal phrase for opposing an idea or a change.
normal.cn: adverse to 是正式地反对某个想法或变动的说法。

abstract.en: Picture a headwind so strong that the cyclist has to stand on the pedals to stay still.
abstract.cn: 想象一股强到让骑手必须站着踩踏板才能原地不动的逆风。

abstract.en: The word always implies a direction: something is turned toward you, and that is why it is against you.
abstract.cn: 这个词总暗含方向：某物转向你，正因为它对着你，所以它才不利于你。

abstract.en: Formal language prefers adverse to plain bad because it names the mechanism instead of the blame.
abstract.cn: 正式语言偏爱 adverse 而不直说坏，因为它命名的是机制，而非责难。

examples.en: Adverse weather delayed every flight out of the northern airport.
examples.cn: 恶劣天气让北部机场的每一班航班都延误了。

examples.en: The trial was stopped after two patients had an adverse reaction.
examples.cn: 两名患者出现不良反应后，试验被中止。

examples.en: The court weighed the adverse impact on the fishing village.
examples.cn: 法院权衡了这一项目对渔村的负面影响。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德沃斯」——沃斯逆风顶回来：不利的

root: 拉丁语 ad-（朝向）+ vertere（转）→ adversus「转向对立面的」→ 英语 adverse，义为不利的、有害的、逆向的、持反对态度的。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of adverse all describe a force turned against you: a harmful effect, bad conditions, an opposing current, a hostile attitude, a legal claim, a medical reaction, a selection risk and unkind fate.
sensesIntro.cn: adverse 的八个义项都描述一股转向你的力量：有害影响、恶劣条件、逆向水流、敌对态度、法律主张、医学反应、选择风险，以及不济的命运。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wind in the face that pushes every step backward.
core.cn: 核心意象：迎面顶来的风，把每一步都往回推。

branches.en: THE HARM LINE: what is turned against you works against your good, in medicine and in markets.
branches.cn: 伤害线：转向你的事物在医学与市场里都对抗你的好处。

branches.en: THE CURRENT LINE: wind and water give the adjective its literal body.
branches.cn: 水流线：风与水给这个形容词以字面的躯体。

branches.en: THE OPPOSITION LINE: minds and legal interests can both be turned against something.
branches.cn: 对立线：心思与法律利益都能转向某物的对立面。

branches.en: THE RISK LINE: medicine and insurance need a neutral label for harm and for the wrong side of a market.
branches.cn: 风险线：医学与保险都需要一个中性的标签，用来指伤害与市场的不利一面。

branches.en: THE FATE LINE: fortune itself can be imagined as facing a person.
branches.cn: 命运线：命运本身也可以被想象成迎面站在一个人面前。

intro.en: Adverse is the Latin participle adversus; English keeps the -verse stem and builds -ly, -ity and -ative on it, while averse sits nearby with a different prefix.
intro.cn: adverse 是拉丁分词 adversus；英语保留 -verse 词干，并在其上构成 -ly、-ity 与 -ative，而 averse 带着不同前缀待在旁边。

latinIntro.en: Vertere, adversus and adversari are attested in Latin, so the chain is documented rather than reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: vertere、adversus 与 adversari 在拉丁语中有文献，这条链有据可查，而非构拟。

items.example: It directs the turning toward an opponent.
It is the shared root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个词族共享的词根。

items.example: It is the direct source of adverse.
items.exampleCN: 它是 adverse 的直接来源。

items.example: It also appears in reverse and converse.
items.exampleCN: 它也出现在 reverse 与 converse 中。

items.example: It makes the neighbouring word averse, with a different sense.
items.exampleCN: 它造出邻近的 averse，意义与 adverse 不同。

derivatives.zh: 由 adverse 加 -ly 构成，义为「不利地」
由词干加 -ity 构成，义为「逆境」

definition_zh: 逆境；厄运；苦难；不幸
definition_en: a difficult or unpleasant situation, especially one caused by misfortune
core_image: 车轮陷进泥里，越用力反而越往下沉
scene: 暴雨后的乡道上，一辆卡车陷在泥里，司机蹲在轮胎旁抽烟。He learned patience in adversity, not in comfort.
sceneCN: 这里 adversity 是「逆境」（第 1 个义项：由不幸造成的困难处境）；句意为他在逆境中学会了耐心，而不是在安逸里。图中可辨识的物件：泥浆、轮胎、烟头。

pos.zh: 逆境；厄运；苦难（可数或不可数）

derivatives.zh: 本名词的形容词基础，义为「不利的；有害的」
由 adverse 加 -ly 构成，义为「不利地」
由同一词干加 -ative 构成，语法术语，指「表示转折的（词）」

senses.title: A difficult situation caused by misfortune
senses.definition: a hard or unfavourable situation brought about by bad luck or misfortune
senses.definitionCN: 由坏运气或不幸造成的一种艰难或不利处境
senses.example: The family stayed together through years of adversity.
senses.exampleCN: 这一家人历经多年逆境仍守在一起。
senses.why: The noun is built on adverse, turned against, so adversity is the condition of living with things turned against you.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词建于 adverse「转向对立」之上，所以 adversity 就是生活在「事物都与你作对」的处境里。

senses.title: Hardship as a continuing condition
senses.definition: as a mass noun, prolonged suffering and difficulty rather than one event
senses.definitionCN: 作不可数名词时，指长期的煎熬与艰难，而非单一事件
senses.example: Adversity had worn the patience of the whole village thin.
senses.exampleCN: 苦难把整个村子的耐心都磨薄了。
senses.why: When the turned-against condition lasts, it stops being an incident and becomes a climate.
senses.whyCN: 当「与你作对」的处境持续下去，它就不再是一件事，而变成一种气候。

senses.title: A particular calamity
senses.definition: a specific misfortune that can be counted among others
senses.definitionCN: 可以和其他不幸并列计数的一次具体灾祸
senses.example: They survived three adversities in a single winter.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在同一个冬天里扛过了三场灾祸。
senses.why: The countable use treats each misfortune as a separate blow, which is why the plural is possible.
senses.whyCN: 可数用法把每一次不幸当作单独的一击，所以这个词可以有复数。

senses.title: Financial distress
senses.definition: an older use for poverty or a lack of money and means
senses.definitionCN: 较旧的用法，指贫困或缺少钱财与生计手段
senses.example: The letters describe the adversity of a family without rent money.
senses.exampleCN: 这些书信描述了一个连房租都拿不出的家庭的困窘。
senses.why: Money is the commonest form in which things turn against a household, so the word often means plain poverty.
senses.whyCN: 金钱是一个家庭最常遭遇的「作对」形式，所以这个词常直接指贫困。

senses.title: The emotional strain of hardship
senses.definition: the inner strain produced by living through difficult conditions
senses.definitionCN: 在艰难处境中生活所产生的内心压力
senses.example: Adversity can isolate a person even in a crowded room.
senses.exampleCN: 逆境能让人即使身处满屋人也感到孤立。
senses.why: External conditions are also felt inside, so the noun can name the weight rather than the circumstance.
senses.whyCN: 外部处境也会被从内部感受到，所以这个名词能命名那份重量，而非处境本身。

senses.title: A test of character
senses.definition: hardship understood as a trial that reveals what a person is made of
senses.definitionCN: 被理解为揭示一个人本性的试炼的艰难
senses.example: Adversity shows which friendships are merely convenient.
senses.exampleCN: 逆境会显出哪些友谊只是图方便。
senses.why: A force turned against you also tests you, and moral writing has long used the word for that examination.
senses.whyCN: 一股对着你的力量也在考验你，道德文章早就用这个词来指那场考试。

senses.title: Hostile opposition
senses.definition: in formal or older writing, active hostility or opposition from others
senses.definitionCN: 在正式或较旧的文字中，指他人主动的敌意或阻挠
senses.example: The reform met adversity from every landed interest.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革遭到每一个地主利益的阻挠。
senses.why: Adversity can be people rather than events, because people are the ones who turn against a cause.
senses.whyCN: 逆境可以是人，而不只是事件，因为正是人转向一项事业的对立面。

senses.title: The measure of true friends
senses.definition: in proverbial style, the condition in which loyalty is proved or exposed
senses.definitionCN: 在谚语式表达中，忠诚被证明或暴露出来的那种处境
senses.example: A friend in adversity is worth ten at the feast.
senses.exampleCN: 逆境中的一个朋友，胜过宴席上的十个。
senses.why: Proverbs compress the test sense into a social lesson, and the word becomes a yardstick for people.
senses.whyCN: 谚语把「试炼」义压缩成一句人情教训，这个词于是成了衡量人的尺子。

intro.en: Adversity is the Latin noun adversitas, from adversus, turned against, itself the participle of advertere.
intro.cn: adversity 是拉丁名词 adversitas，来自 adversus「转向对立面的」，而 adversus 又是 advertere 的分词。

items.en: Vertere meant to turn, the root shared by reverse, convert and vertigo.
items.cn: vertere 意为「转」，reverse、convert 与 vertigo 共享这个词根。

items.en: The participle adversus meant turned against, facing you as an obstacle or an enemy.
items.cn: 分词 adversus 意为「转向对立」，作为障碍或敌人面对着你。

items.en: The abstract noun adversitas named the state of having things turned against one.
items.cn: 抽象名词 adversitas 命名「事物都与自己作对」的状态。

items.en: Old French carried the abstract noun toward English as aversete and later adversite.
items.cn: 古法语把这个抽象名词带向英语，先作 aversete，后作 adversite。

items.en: English records the noun in the fourteenth century, mostly in moral and religious writing.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪记录这个名词，多见于道德与宗教写作。

items.en: Modern usage keeps both the mass sense of prolonged hardship and the countable sense of a calamity.
items.cn: 现代用法同时保留「长期苦难」的不可数义与「一场灾祸」的可数义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same vertere family, including the trap averse, which describes reluctance rather than hardship; the near-meaning group gathers nouns for hard times.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 vertere 词族的词，其中包括陷阱词 averse，它说的是不情愿而非苦难；近义组收表示艰难时世的名词。

entries.definition: The adjective for what works against you, from which the noun is formed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容与你作对之物的形容词，这个名词正是由它构成。

entries.definition: An opponent, the personified form of what is turned against you.
entries.definitionCN: 对手，是「转向你之物」的人格化形式。

entries.definition: Unwilling or reluctant, a personal feeling with a different prefix, not a condition of hardship.
entries.definitionCN: 意为不情愿、反感，是带不同前缀的个人感受，并非苦难处境。

entries.definition: Suffering caused by difficult living conditions, often material and practical.
entries.definitionCN: 艰难生活条件造成的苦，常偏物质与实际层面。

entries.definition: Bad luck or a single unlucky event, usually shorter than adversity.
entries.definitionCN: 坏运气或单次不幸事件，通常比 adversity 更短促。

entries.definition: A great trial or suffering, with a strong religious or literary tone.
entries.definitionCN: 巨大的试炼或苦难，带浓厚的宗教或文学语气。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the adversus root, the abstract -ity ending and the phrases adversity actually forms.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用 adversus 词根、抽象名词词尾 -ity，以及 adversity 实际构成的短语。

normal.en: Adversus is turned against; add -ity and you get the state of being turned against.
normal.cn: adversus 是「转向对立」；加上 -ity，就得到「被转向对立」的状态。

normal.en: The adjective is adverse, the noun is adversity, and the person is an adversary.
normal.cn: 形容词是 adverse，名词是 adversity，而那个人是 adversary。

normal.en: The standard phrases are in adversity and overcome adversity.
normal.cn: 标准短语是 in adversity 与 overcome adversity。

normal.en: Do not confuse adversity with averse: one is hardship, the other is reluctance.
normal.cn: 不要把 adversity 与 averse 混了：一个是苦难，一个是不情愿。

normal.en: The plural adversities counts separate blows, as in three adversities in one winter.
normal.cn: 复数 adversities 数的是分开的打击，如「一个冬天里的三场灾祸」。

abstract.en: Picture a wheel spinning in mud: effort and sinking increase together.
abstract.cn: 想象一只在泥里空转的车轮：越用力，陷得越深。

abstract.en: Adversity is not one event but a direction, which is why it can also name a mood.
abstract.cn: 逆境不是一个事件，而是一个方向，所以它也能命名一种心境。

abstract.en: The proverb makes the word a test: what survives adversity is what was real.
abstract.cn: 谚语把这个词变成一场考试：熬过逆境的，才是真的。

examples.en: The company survived the adversity of two lost seasons.
examples.cn: 这家公司熬过了两个失收季节的逆境。

examples.en: In adversity she discovered who would actually answer the phone.
examples.cn: 在逆境中，她看清了谁会真的接电话。

examples.en: The memoir treats adversity as a teacher rather than a punishment.
examples.cn: 这本回忆录把逆境当作老师，而不是惩罚。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德沃西提」——沃西提陷在泥里越挣越深：逆境

root: 拉丁语 adversus（转向对立面的）+ 抽象名词词尾 -itas → adversitas，经古法语进入英语作 adversity，义为逆境、厄运与苦难。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of adversity all come from things turned against a person: a hard situation, lasting hardship, a single calamity, poverty, inner strain, a moral test, human hostility and the proverb's yardstick for friends.
sensesIntro.cn: adversity 的八个义项都来自「事物转向一个人」：艰难处境、长期苦难、单场灾祸、贫困、内心重压、品格试炼、他人的敌意，以及谚语里衡量朋友的尺子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wheel sinking deeper the harder it turns.
core.cn: 核心意象：越用力转，陷得越深的一只车轮。

branches.en: THE CONDITION LINE: one hard situation, a lasting climate and a counted calamity are three scales of the same thing.
branches.cn: 处境线：一个艰难处境、一种持续气候、一场可数的灾祸，是同一事物的三种尺度。

branches.en: THE POVERTY LINE: lack of money is the oldest concrete form of hardship.
branches.cn: 贫困线：缺钱是苦难最古老的具体形态。

branches.en: THE INNER LINE: the outer condition is also felt as weight.
branches.cn: 内心线：外部处境也被感受为一种重量。

branches.en: THE TEST LINE: hardship reveals character and sorts friends.
branches.cn: 试炼线：苦难既显露品格，也筛出朋友。

branches.en: THE HUMAN LINE: sometimes the force turned against you is other people.
branches.cn: 人事线：有时转向你的那股力量，就是别的人。

intro.en: Adversity is adversus plus the abstract -ity; the family also gives adverse, adversely and adversary, all from the same vertere root.
intro.cn: adversity 是 adversus 加抽象词尾 -ity；词族还给出 adverse、adversely 与 adversary，全部来自同一 vertere 词根。

latinIntro.en: Vertere, adversus and adversitas are attested in Latin, so the derivation is documented.
latinIntro.cn: vertere、adversus 与 adversitas 在拉丁语中有文献，这条派生有据可查。

items.example: It turns the root toward an opposing direction.
items.exampleCN: 它把这个词根转向对立的方向。

items.example: It is the shared root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个词族共享的词根。

items.example: It supplies the adjective and the noun stem.
items.exampleCN: 它提供形容词与名词词干。

items.example: It is the direct source of adversity.
items.exampleCN: 它是 adversity 的直接来源。
它把 adversus 变成 adversity。

derivatives.zh: 由同一词干构成，义为「不利的」
由 adverse 加 -ly 构成，义为「不利地」

definition_zh: 宣传；做广告；登广告；公告；招揽
definition_en: to tell the public about a product, service, event or vacancy in order to attract buyers or applicants
core_image: 把一件商品举到人群头顶，让所有眼睛都看见
scene: 夜市入口的喇叭反复喊着同一句话，摊主把灯箱举过头顶。The stallholder advertised her noodles with a hand-painted sign.
sceneCN: 这里 advertise 是「为……做广告」（第 1 个义项：向公众宣传商品以吸引购买）；句意为摊主用手绘招牌给自己的面条做广告。图中可辨识的物件：灯箱、招牌、喇叭。

pos.zh: 宣传；做广告；登广告；公告；招揽

derivatives.zh: 由 advertise 加 -ment 构成，义为「广告；公告」
由 advertise 加 -er 构成，义为「广告主；登广告的人」
由现在分词转作名词，义为「广告业；广告活动」

senses.title: To promote goods or services
senses.definition: to draw public attention to something for sale in order to increase demand
senses.definitionCN: 把待售之物引起公众注意，以提高需求
senses.example: The bakery advertised its new rye loaf on the window.
senses.exampleCN: 面包店在橱窗上为新的黑麦面包做广告。
senses.why: The word once meant to inform; commerce narrowed it to informing with the aim of selling.
senses.whyCN: 这个词曾经只是「告知」，商业把它收窄为「带着销售目的去告知」。

senses.title: To place a notice in the media
senses.definition: to buy space or time in a newspaper, broadcast or website for a message
senses.definitionCN: 在报纸、广播或网站上购买版面或时段来刊登信息
senses.example: They advertised in three local papers for a month.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在三家本地报纸上登了一个月广告。
senses.why: Once a notice must reach strangers, it needs a medium, and the verb follows the notice into print and broadcast.
senses.whyCN: 当告示必须触达陌生人，它就需要一个媒介，这个动词便跟着告示进了印刷与广播。

senses.title: To recruit by public notice
senses.definition: to announce a job vacancy so that applicants come forward
senses.definitionCN: 公布职位空缺，让申请人前来应征
senses.example: The hospital advertised for two night nurses.
senses.exampleCN: 医院登广告招两名夜班护士。
senses.why: A vacancy is a need made public, and the same verb serves the employer as it serves the seller.
senses.whyCN: 空缺是一种公开出去的需求，这个动词既服务雇主，也服务卖家。

senses.title: To announce an event publicly
senses.definition: to give public notice of a meeting, performance or gathering
senses.definitionCN: 公开告知一场会议、演出或聚会
senses.example: The society advertised the lecture on every noticeboard.
senses.exampleCN: 学会在每一块布告栏上公告了这场讲座。
senses.why: The oldest sense was simply to notify, and public events still use the verb in that plain way.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思只是「通知」，公共活动至今仍以这种朴素方式使用这个动词。

senses.title: To make a fact visible
senses.definition: to make something known or obvious, sometimes unintentionally
senses.definitionCN: 使某事为人所知或变得明显，有时并非有意
senses.example: His careful silence advertised that the question had hit home.
senses.exampleCN: 他小心翼翼的沉默暴露出这个问题戳到了痛处。
senses.why: Anything that makes a fact public advertises it, even when no product is involved.
senses.whyCN: 任何把事实公开出来的举动都在 advertise 它，哪怕其中没有商品。

senses.title: To claim a quality in marketing
senses.definition: in the passive, to be presented as having a particular quality
senses.definitionCN: 在被动态中，指被呈现为具有某种性质
senses.example: The pills were advertised as free of artificial colour.
senses.exampleCN: 这些药片被宣传为不含人工色素。
senses.why: Marketing does not only name a product; it attaches claims to it, and the passive carries those claims.
senses.whyCN: 营销不只是说出产品名字，还把各种说法挂在它身上，被动式承载的正是这些说法。

senses.title: To draw attention to oneself
senses.definition: to call attention to one's own abilities or deeds, often with disapproval
senses.definitionCN: 引起别人对自己能力或功绩的注意，常带不赞同
senses.example: He advertised his contacts at every dinner party.
senses.exampleCN: 他在每场晚宴上都标榜自己的人脉。
senses.why: A person can be treated like a product, and self-promotion borrows the commercial verb with a sour taste.
senses.whyCN: 人也可以被当作商品来对待，自我推销借来这个商业动词，便带上了酸味。

senses.title: To warn or inform, in older usage
senses.definition: in older texts, to give notice or warning of something rather than to sell it
senses.definitionCN: 在较旧的文本中，指就某事给出通知或提醒，而非推销
senses.example: The magistrate advertised the town of the coming flood.
senses.exampleCN: 地方官向全镇告知洪水将至。
senses.why: This is the original sense, preserved in old records after commerce took over the everyday use.
senses.whyCN: 这是本义，在商业接管日常用法之后，仍保留在旧档案里。

intro.en: Advertise comes from Old French advertir, to turn attention to, from Latin advertere, ad plus vertere, to turn.
intro.cn: advertise 来自古法语 advertir「把注意力转向」，其源是拉丁语 advertere，即 ad 加 vertere「转」。

items.en: Vertere meant to turn; English keeps it in convert, reverse and vertigo.
items.cn: vertere 意为「转」，英语在 convert、reverse 与 vertigo 中保留它。

items.en: Ad plus vertere meant to turn the mind toward something, hence to notice or to heed.
items.cn: ad 加 vertere 意为「把心思转向某物」，因此指注意或留意。

items.en: Old French advertir meant to warn or inform, and this sense came into English first.
items.cn: 古法语 advertir 意为「警告」或「告知」，这个意思最先进入英语。

items.en: English first uses advertise in the sense of giving notice, with no commercial colour at all.
items.cn: 英语最初使用 advertise 时只有「发出通知」的意思，毫无商业色彩。

items.en: The commercial sense of promoting goods becomes dominant, and the older sense retreats to old records.
items.cn: 推销商品的商业义取得主导，较旧的意思退回到旧档案里。

items.en: Modern English adds media-specific uses such as advertise online and be advertised as.
items.cn: 现代英语又加上「在线投放」与「被宣传为」这类媒介特定用法。

note.en: The look-alike group is the advertise family with its noun and agent forms; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of making something publicly known, which differ in whether money and persuasion are involved.
note.cn: 形近组是 advertise 词族及其名词与施事形式；近义组收「使某事公开」的动词，差别在于是否涉及金钱与说服。

entries.definition: The noun naming the notice or film that results from the act.
entries.definitionCN: 命名这一行为所产出的告示或片子的名词。

entries.definition: The person or company that pays for the promotion.
entries.definitionCN: 出资做宣传的个人或公司。

entries.definition: The activity or industry as a whole, used as a mass noun.
entries.definitionCN: 整个行业或活动，作不可数名词使用。

entries.definition: To help something grow or sell, broader than advertise and not tied to paid notices.
entries.definitionCN: 帮助某物成长或销售，范围比 advertise 更广，也不限于付费告示。

entries.definition: To make something widely known, with no necessary aim of selling.
entries.definitionCN: 使某事广为人知，不一定以销售为目的。

entries.definition: To plan and carry out the selling of a product, of which advertising is one part.
entries.definitionCN: 策划并执行产品的销售，做广告只是其中一环。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the advertere root, the older sense of giving notice and the phrases the verb actually forms.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用 advertere 词根、较旧的「发出通知」义，以及这个动词实际构成的短语。

normal.en: Advertere is to turn attention toward something, which is exactly what an advertisement does.
normal.cn: advertere 就是「把注意力转向某物」，这正是广告所做的事。

normal.en: The verb is regular: advertises, advertised, advertising.
normal.cn: 这个动词很规则：advertises、advertised、advertising。

normal.en: British English uses advert for the noun, American English prefers ad.
normal.cn: 英式英语用 advert 指广告，美式英语更爱用 ad。

normal.en: Advertise for staff and advertise a vacancy are the recruitment phrases.
normal.cn: advertise for staff 与 advertise a vacancy 是招聘用语。

normal.en: Be advertised as is the passive frame for marketing claims.
normal.cn: be advertised as 是营销说法的被动框架。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp held above a crowd, doing nothing but making one object impossible to miss.
abstract.cn: 想象把一盏灯举到人群上方，它什么都不做，只让一件东西无法被忽视。

abstract.en: The word began as a warning and became a sales pitch, which is a short history of public speech.
abstract.cn: 这个词从警告变成叫卖，这本身就是一段公共言论的小史。

abstract.en: To advertise a fact is to put it under the same lamp, whether or not anyone is selling.
abstract.cn: advertise 一个事实，就是把它放到同一盏灯下，无论有没有人在卖东西。

examples.en: The council advertised the road closure two weeks ahead.
examples.cn: 市政会提前两周公告了封路。

examples.en: Small farms cannot afford to advertise on national television.
examples.cn: 小农场负担不起在全国电视上做广告。

examples.en: The job was advertised as part-time but ran full-time hours.
examples.cn: 这份工作被宣传为兼职，实际工时却是全职。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德沃泰兹」——沃泰兹把灯箱举过头：做广告

root: 拉丁语 advertere（ad-「朝向」+ vertere「转」，意为把注意力转向）→ 古法语 advertir「告知、警告」→ 英语 advertise，由「通知」扩展为「做广告」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of advertise all turn attention toward something: a product, a media notice, a vacancy, an event, an exposed fact, a marketing claim, a self-promotion and the old sense of warning.
sensesIntro.cn: advertise 的八个义项都把注意力转向某物：商品、媒体告示、职位空缺、活动、被暴露的事实、营销说法、自我标榜，以及古老的「警告」义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp raised above a crowd so one object cannot be missed.
core.cn: 核心意象：把一盏灯举过人群，让一件东西无法被忽视。

branches.en: THE MARKET LINE: informing becomes selling once a medium and a price are attached.
branches.cn: 市场线：一旦接上媒介与价格，告知就变成销售。

branches.en: THE NOTICE LINE: vacancies and events are needs and dates made public.
branches.cn: 告示线：职位空缺与活动，是被公开出去的需求与日期。

branches.en: THE EXPOSURE LINE: facts and people can be put under the same lamp.
branches.cn: 暴露线：事实与人可以被放到同一盏灯下。

branches.en: THE CLAIM LINE: marketing attaches promises to a product.
branches.cn: 说法线：营销把承诺挂在产品身上。

branches.en: THE WARNING LINE: the oldest sense survives in old records.
branches.cn: 警告线：最古老的意思仍留在旧档案里。

intro.en: Advertise is a Latin verb in English form; the stem advertere also gives advertisement, advertiser and advertising, while -ise marks the verb.
intro.cn: advertise 是以英语形式出现的拉丁动词；词干 advertere 还给出 advertisement、advertiser 与 advertising，而 -ise 标记动词。

latinIntro.en: Vertere, advertere and the French verb advertir are all attested, so the chain is documented.
latinIntro.cn: vertere、advertere 与法语动词 advertir 均有文献，这条链有据可查。

items.example: It turns attention toward an object.
items.exampleCN: 它把注意力转向某个对象。

items.example: It carried the word into English.
It marks the English verb, also spelled -ize.
items.exampleCN: 它标记这个英语动词，也拼作 -ize。

derivatives.zh: 由 advertise 加 -ment 构成，义为「广告」
由 advertise 加 -er 构成，义为「广告主」

definition_zh: 广告；宣传；公告
definition_en: a public notice, image or short film that promotes a product, service, event or job
core_image: 夹在报纸页缝里、被一眼扫过却记住了的那块彩色
scene: 凌晨的地铁车厢里，一个上班族盯着手机屏幕，手指跳过一段十几秒的短片。The advertisement lasted fifteen seconds and sold nothing.
sceneCN: 这里 advertisement 是「广告」（第 1 个义项：为推销商品或服务而制作的公开宣传物）；句意为这则广告只有十五秒，什么也没卖出去。图中可辨识的物件：手机屏幕、车厢扶手、耳机。

pos.zh: 广告；宣传；公告

derivatives.zh: 本名词的动词基础，义为「做广告；宣传」
由 advertise 加 -er 构成，义为「广告主」
由 advertise 加 -ing 构成，义为「广告业；广告活动」

senses.title: A paid promotion of goods
senses.definition: a paid public message designed to persuade people to buy a product or service
senses.definitionCN: 为说服人们购买产品或服务而付费制作的公开信息
senses.example: The advertisement promised a cleaner floor in one wipe.
senses.exampleCN: 这则广告承诺一抹就能让地板干净。
senses.why: The noun is the product of the verb to advertise, so it names the finished message rather than the act.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词是动词 advertise 的产物，所以它命名的是完成的信息，而非动作。

senses.title: A vacancy notice
senses.definition: a notice announcing a job and inviting applications
senses.definitionCN: 公布一个职位并邀请应征的告示
senses.example: The advertisement asked for a driver with a clean licence.
senses.exampleCN: 这则招聘广告要求一名无违章记录的司机。
senses.why: A job is offered like a product, and the recruitment notice takes the same noun.
senses.whyCN: 职位像商品一样被提供，招聘告示便使用同一个名词。

senses.title: A public announcement
senses.definition: a formal notice about an event, a rule or a meeting, not necessarily for sale
senses.definitionCN: 关于活动、规定或会议的正式告示，不一定为了销售
senses.example: An advertisement in the parish paper announced the harvest fair.
senses.exampleCN: 教区小报上的一则公告宣告了丰收集市。
senses.why: The oldest sense of the verb was to give notice, and this noun keeps that neutral, non-commercial use.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词最古老的意思是「发出通知」，这个名词保留了那一中性、非商业的用法。

senses.title: A short film or clip
senses.definition: a produced film or clip made for broadcast or streaming
senses.definitionCN: 为广播或网络播放而制作的片子或短片
senses.example: The advertisement was shot in one unbroken take.
senses.exampleCN: 这则广告片是用一个长镜头拍成的。
senses.why: As media changed, the noun followed the message into sound and moving image.
senses.whyCN: 随着媒介变化，这个名词跟着信息进入了声音与活动影像。

senses.title: An online banner or pop-up
senses.definition: a display slot on a website or app that carries a promotional message
senses.definitionCN: 网站或应用上承载推广信息的展示位
senses.example: The advertisement covered the button I needed to press.
senses.exampleCN: 那个网络广告挡住了我要按的按钮。
senses.why: A slot is a page's rented space, and the noun moves from paper to pixels unchanged.
senses.whyCN: 广告位是页面被租出去的空间，这个名词从纸面移到像素上，意思未变。

senses.title: Something that argues for a thing
senses.definition: in figurative use, a person or thing that visibly recommends a quality or a place
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法中，指明显为某种品质或地方作推荐的人或物
senses.example: The garden is an advertisement for patience.
senses.exampleCN: 这座花园就是耐心的活广告。
senses.why: Anything that makes a case visibly can be read as an advertisement, even without a buyer.
senses.whyCN: 任何能显眼地为某事说项的东西都可被读作广告，哪怕没有买家。

senses.title: A notice of warning in older use
senses.definition: in older texts, a formal notice giving information or warning
senses.definitionCN: 在较旧文本中，给出信息或警告的正式告示
senses.example: An advertisement on the gate warned of deep water.
senses.exampleCN: 门上的一则告示警示此处水很深。
senses.why: Before commerce took the word, an advertisement was simply something brought to public attention.
senses.whyCN: 在商业接管这个词之前，advertisement 只是「被带到公众注意之下的事物」。

senses.title: The craft or industry as a whole
senses.definition: in uncountable or attributive use, the business of producing such messages
senses.definitionCN: 在不可数或定语用法中，指制作这类信息的行业
senses.example: She moved from newspaper layout into advertisement design.
senses.exampleCN: 她从报纸排版转去做广告设计。
senses.why: A countable product can be abstracted into an industry, which is why the noun can modify design or campaign.
senses.whyCN: 可数的产品可以被抽象成一个行业，所以这个名词能修饰设计或宣传活动。

intro.en: Advertisement is the noun of advertise, which came from Old French advertir, to give notice, from Latin advertere, to turn toward.
intro.cn: advertisement 是 advertise 的名词，而 advertise 来自古法语 advertir「发出通知」，其源是拉丁语 advertere「把注意力转向」。

items.en: Vertere meant to turn, the common root of convert, reverse and advertise.
items.cn: vertere 意为「转」，是 convert、reverse 与 advertise 的共同词根。

items.en: Ad plus vertere meant to turn one's attention toward something.
items.cn: ad 加 vertere 意为「把注意力转向某物」。

items.en: Advertir meant to warn or inform, and the noun advertissement named the notice itself.
items.cn: advertir 意为「警告」或「告知」，名词 advertissement 则命名告示本身。

items.en: English borrowed the noun first as a plain notice, with no commercial meaning.
items.cn: 英语先借入这个名词，只作朴素的「告示」，没有商业含义。

items.en: Paid notices for goods become common, and the commercial sense takes over the noun.
items.cn: 为商品付费的告示变得常见，商业义接管了这个名词。

items.en: Film, broadcast and the web add new kinds of advertisement without changing the core meaning.
items.cn: 电影、广播与网络添加了新种类的广告，却没有改变核心含义。

note.en: The look-alike group is the advertise family; the near-meaning group gathers words for promotional messages, which differ in length, register and whether money changes hands.
note.cn: 形近组是 advertise 词族；近义组收表示推广信息的词，差别在于长度、语体，以及是否涉及金钱。

entries.definition: The verb whose product this noun names.
entries.definitionCN: 这个名词所命名的产物对应的动词。

entries.definition: The party that pays for the message to appear.
entries.definitionCN: 为信息出现而付费的一方。

entries.definition: The activity or industry rather than a single message.
entries.definitionCN: 活动或行业本身，而非单条信息。

entries.definition: A paid spot on television or radio, the broadcast cousin of the print advertisement.
entries.definitionCN: 电视或广播上付费的时段，是平面广告的广播表亲。

entries.definition: The short British noun for the same thing, common in speech and in classified pages.
entries.definitionCN: 英式英语里指同一事物的短名词，常见于口语与分类广告页。

entries.definition: A campaign or special offer meant to boost sales, broader than one notice.
entries.definitionCN: 为提升销量而做的活动或优惠，比单则告示范围更广。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the advertere root, the media collocations and the family that shares the same verb.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用 advertere 词根、媒介搭配，以及共用同一动词的词族。

normal.en: An advertisement is the finished product of advertise, just as a payment is the product of pay.
normal.cn: advertisement 是 advertise 的成品，正如 payment 是 pay 的成品。

normal.en: The family is neat: advertise the verb, advertisement the thing, advertiser the payer, advertising the industry.
normal.cn: 词族很整齐：advertise 是动词，advertisement 是东西，advertiser 是出钱的人，advertising 是行业。

normal.en: Place an advertisement is the standard verb phrase in print and online.
normal.cn: place an advertisement 是平面与网络上的标准动词短语。

normal.en: British speech shortens it to advert, and American speech to ad.
normal.cn: 英式口语缩成 advert，美式口语缩成 ad。

normal.en: Job advertisement and television advertisement name the two commonest kinds.
normal.cn: job advertisement 与 television advertisement 命名最常见的两类。

abstract.en: Picture a colour block in a grey newspaper that your eye finds before your mind reads it.
abstract.cn: 想象灰暗报纸里的一块彩色，你的眼睛先于头脑找到它。

abstract.en: The word started as a notice on a gate and grew into an industry, keeping the same shape.
abstract.cn: 这个词从门上的一则告示长成一个行业，形状始终未变。

abstract.en: An advertisement is a message that has been paid for, which is why it can never be fully neutral.
abstract.cn: 广告是一条付过费的信息，所以它永远不可能完全中立。

examples.en: The advertisement ran during the final and cost more than the prize.
examples.cn: 这则广告在决赛期间播出，花费比奖金还高。

examples.en: She answered an advertisement for a part-time archivist.
examples.cn: 她应征了一则招聘兼职档案员的广告。

examples.en: An advertisement on the ferry warned passengers about the tide.
examples.cn: 渡轮上的一则告示提醒乘客注意潮水。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德弗提斯门特」——门上贴出的告示：广告

root: advertise（做广告，源自拉丁 advertere「把注意力转向」）+ 名词词尾 -ment → advertisement，指为推销或告知而制作的公开信息。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of advertisement all name a message put in front of the public: a product pitch, a vacancy, an announcement, a film, an online slot, a figurative recommendation, an old warning notice and the industry itself.
sensesIntro.cn: advertisement 的八个义项都命名「摆到公众面前的信息」：商品推销、职位空缺、公告、广告片、网络广告位、比喻性的推荐、旧时的警示告示，以及行业本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coloured block in a grey page that the eye finds first.
core.cn: 核心意象：灰色页面上一块先被眼睛找到的彩色。

branches.en: THE MEDIUM LINE: the same message takes paper, film or pixels as its body.
branches.cn: 媒介线：同一条信息以纸面、胶片或像素为躯体。

branches.en: THE VACANCY LINE: a job is offered with the same noun as a product.
branches.cn: 招聘线：职位与商品用同一个名词被提供。

branches.en: THE NOTICE LINE: the neutral and warning uses preserve the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 告示线：中性的与警示的用法保存着最古老的意思。

branches.en: THE FIGURE LINE: anything visibly recommending something becomes an advertisement.
branches.cn: 比喻线：任何明显为某物说项的东西都成了广告。

branches.en: THE INDUSTRY LINE: a countable product is abstracted into a trade.
branches.cn: 行业线：可数的产品被抽象成一门生意。

intro.en: Advertisement is advertise plus -ment; the verb itself rests on the Latin advertere, and the family adds -er and -ing.
intro.cn: advertisement 是 advertise 加 -ment；动词本身建于拉丁 advertere 之上，词族又加上 -er 与 -ing。

latinIntro.en: Vertere, advertere and the French advertir are attested, so the chain is fully documented.
latinIntro.cn: vertere、advertere 与法语 advertir 均有文献，这条链完全有据可查。

items.example: It directs attention toward the message.
It is the root of the whole family.
It is the ancestor of advertise.

items.exampleCN: 它给英语提供了这个动词。

items.example: It marks advertise, also spelled with -ize.

derivatives.zh: 本名词的动词基础，义为「做广告」
由 advertise 加 -er 构成，义为「广告主」

definition_zh: 建议；忠告；劝告；（商业）通知
definition_en: an opinion or suggestion offered to someone about what they should do
core_image: 有人把一张写满字的小纸条塞进你手里
scene: 毕业典礼后，老教授把学生叫到走廊尽头，递过去一张折好的纸。The advice on the paper was shorter than the ceremony.
sceneCN: 这里 advice 是「建议」（第 1 个义项：就某人该怎么做而给出的意见）；句意为纸上的建议比整场典礼还短。图中可辨识的物件：折好的纸、走廊、学位帽。

pos.zh: 建议；忠告；劝告；（商业）通知

derivatives.zh: 与本名词同源的动词，义为「建议；劝告；通知」
由 advise 加 -er 构成，义为「顾问；提出建议者」
由 advise 加 -able 构成，义为「可取的；适当的」

senses.title: An opinion about what to do
senses.definition: an opinion offered to help someone decide how to act
senses.definitionCN: 为帮助某人决定怎么行动而给出的意见
senses.example: Her advice was to wait a year before buying.
senses.exampleCN: 她的建议是等一年再买。
senses.why: The word descends from a phrase meaning it seems to me, so advice is an opinion offered rather than a command.
senses.whyCN: 这个词源自「在我看来」这一说法，所以 advice 是提出来的意见，而不是命令。

senses.title: Professional counsel
senses.definition: guidance given by a trained professional in law, medicine or finance
senses.definitionCN: 由法律、医学或金融方面的专业人士给出的指导
senses.example: You should get legal advice before signing the lease.
senses.exampleCN: 签租约之前你应当取得法律意见。
senses.why: When the opinion carries expertise and liability, the ordinary noun becomes a professional service.
senses.whyCN: 当意见带着专业能力与责任时，这个普通名词就变成一项专业服务。

senses.title: A counted item of guidance
senses.definition: a single suggestion, counted with the phrase a piece of advice
senses.definitionCN: 单条建议，用 a piece of advice 来计数
senses.example: He gave me three pieces of advice and one warning.
senses.exampleCN: 他给了我三条建议和一个警告。
senses.why: English keeps advice uncountable, so individual items are counted through piece rather than through a plural.
senses.whyCN: 英语把 advice 当作不可数，所以单条建议用 piece 计数，而不用复数。

senses.title: A commercial notice
senses.definition: in trade, a formal notification such as an advice of shipment or of payment
senses.definitionCN: 在贸易中，装运通知或付款通知这类正式告知
senses.example: The bank sent an advice of credit to the exporter.
senses.exampleCN: 银行向出口商发出了一份信用证通知。
senses.why: Commerce kept the oldest sense of informing, and the plural advices survives in shipping and banking.
senses.whyCN: 商业保留了「告知」这一最古老的意思，复数 advices 仍在航运与银行业中使用。

senses.title: A recommendation against something
senses.definition: guidance that warns a person away from a course of action
senses.definitionCN: 警告某人不要采取某种做法的指导
senses.example: The doctor's advice against long flights was ignored.
senses.exampleCN: 医生不要长途飞行的告诫被忽视了。
senses.why: An opinion can lean either way, and advice against is the negative form of the same offer.
senses.whyCN: 意见可以偏向任何一边，advice against 正是同一种提议的否定形式。

senses.title: Confidential counsel
senses.definition: guidance given privately, as in diplomatic or government advice
senses.definitionCN: 私下给出的指导，如外交或政府内部意见
senses.example: The minister's advice to the cabinet remained unpublished.
senses.exampleCN: 部长给内阁的意见始终没有公开。
senses.why: Some opinions are too sensitive to be public, and the noun then names a document as much as an opinion.
senses.whyCN: 有些意见过于敏感而不宜公开，此时这个名词既指意见，也指文件。

senses.title: Deliberation, in older usage
senses.definition: in older texts, the act of considering a matter before acting
senses.definitionCN: 在较旧文本中，指行动之前对一件事的考虑
senses.example: The council took advice on the matter for a full week.
senses.exampleCN: 议会就此事商议了整整一周。
senses.why: To take advice once meant to take thought, because an opinion must be weighed before it can guide.
senses.whyCN: take advice 曾经意为「加以考虑」，因为意见必须先被权衡才能起指导作用。

senses.title: Moral exhortation
senses.definition: in literary or parental use, moral guidance offered with authority
senses.definitionCN: 在文学或家长式用法中，带着权威给出的道德指导
senses.example: His father's advice filled a notebook he never opened again.
senses.exampleCN: 父亲的训导写满了一本他再也没打开过的笔记本。
senses.why: Advice offered from above carries obligation as well as opinion, which is why it can feel like instruction.
senses.whyCN: 自上而下给出的建议既带意见也带义务，所以它读起来像训令。

intro.en: Advice comes from Old French avis, an opinion, generally traced to Latin visum, what seems, from videre, to see; the role of the prefix ad- is debated.
intro.cn: advice 来自古法语 avis「意见」，一般认为上溯到拉丁语 visum「看来如此」，源于 videre「看见」；前缀 ad- 的作用存在争议。

items.en: Videre meant to see, and it also gives English vision, evident and video.
items.cn: videre 意为「看见」，英语的 vision、evident 与 video 也由它而来。

items.en: The neuter past participle visum meant what has been seen, and so what seems to be the case.
items.cn: 中性过去分词 visum 意为「被看见的东西」，因此指「看来如此的情形」。

items.en: Old French avis developed the sense of opinion, as in the phrase ce m'est a vis, it seems to me.
items.cn: 古法语 avis 发展出「意见」之义，见于短语 ce m'est a vis「在我看来」。

items.en: English borrows the noun as advice, while the related verb arrives separately as advise.
items.cn: 英语把这个名词借作 advice，而相关动词则另以 advise 的形式进入英语。

items.en: Print fixes the spelling split advice and advise, a classic trap for learners.
items.cn: 印刷固定了 advice 与 advise 的拼写分工，这成了学习者的经典陷阱。

items.en: Trade keeps the older sense of a formal notice, which survives in an advice of shipment.
items.cn: 商业保留了「正式通知」这一较旧的意思，存留于装运通知等说法中。

note.en: The look-alike group is the advice family, including the verb that differs by one letter; the near-meaning group gathers words for guidance, which differ in authority and in formality.
note.cn: 形近组是 advice 词族，其中包括只差一个字母的动词；近义组收表示指导的词，差别在于权威性与正式程度。

entries.definition: The verb, spelled with s and pronounced with a voiced ending; advice is the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 同源的动词，拼作 s 并以浊音收尾；advice 是名词。

entries.definition: The person who gives the advice, formed from the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 给出建议的人，由动词构成。
